LIGHT-SHIFT GATE (tests/test_light_shift_gate.py, a 398.5 nm pair 3 THz below the S-P1/2 line): the S1/2 two-photon self-coupling -9973.10 -> -10554.37 Hz and the D5/2 one 12.9929 -> 13.3109 Hz, so Omega_LS/2pi 4993.04 -> 5283.84 Hz and the static Stark shift 9986.09 -> 10567.69 Hz; level_weights (-1.99740, 0.00260) -> (-1.997481, 0.002519) and spin_flip_weight -0.17366 -> -0.16812, both because 2 up/(up - dn) mixes a +2.45 % numerator with a +5.82 % denominator; the S-D Raman rabi_hz -867.1 -> -888.3 Hz. UNMOVED, and checked: every 729 nm E2 quantity (the derived 2.00144e5 Hz Rabi frequency, the D-state lifetimes and quadrupole elements), the Lamb-Dicke parameters, and Myerson et al. 2008's MEASURED apparatus rates in the detector preset - only the model-DERIVED rates move. TWO SIGNS WERE SURPRISING AND WERE DIAGNOSED, not assumed: nbar and R_o both FALL although Gamma rises, where nbar_D ~ Gamma/4nu would rise. At a fixed s = I/I_sat and a detuning of -Gamma/2 the optical-Bloch problem is scale-invariant in Gamma except for the FIXED B = 5 G, and the magic-angle LINEAR polarization of the 397/866 cycle puts it in the coherent dark-state regime, where the controlling parameter is the Zeeman splitting measured in linewidths. anchor.m10.knill_style_rb.corrected_form: Section 9.10's 'Wright reproduction' row (single-qubit RB fits B p^L + 1/2 with p ~ 0.995 and B + 1/2 ~ 0.993) is NOT reproduced and is deferred. Those numbers are a per-pi/2-gate error of 5e-3 and a SPAM offset of 7e-3, a hundred times this device's (p = 0.999983, B + 1/2 = 0.9995), and Wright et al. 2019 reports the aggregate fidelities without the beam profile, the intensity and laser-phase noise spectra or the SPAM decomposition that configuring a device to his operating point needs -- the same obstacle the M6 ledger records for that row's Bernstein-Vazirani clause ('the plan's stated magnitude cannot fix [it] without his beam profile'). Turning a noise knob until p = 0.995 would fit a number, not reproduce a measurement, so the protocol is provided and the row's numbers are left open; anchor.m10.single_qubit_rb no longer cites 9.12 Wright reproduction as its plan section. Section 7.9's other two variants, direct RB with random XX layers at probability p_2Q and its two-instance (r_1Q, r_2Q) extraction, still do not exist, so the corrected direct-RB right-hand side r = (4^n - 1)(1 - p)/4^n is a conversion in noise/summary.py with no protocol behind it (docs/limits.md)
anchor.m10.knill_style_rb.equation: the Knill-style variant of Section 7.9 runs through run() as a protocol, not as an analytic model: per computational gate a random Pauli (a pi rotation about +-x or +-y as one GPi pulse, about +-z as a virtual RZ, or an identity) then a random Clifford (one GPi2 about +-x or +-y), closed by ONE final pi/2 into the computational basis, the ideal state never leaving the six Pauli eigenstates so that the survival is the probability of the sequence's own target bitstring. On ion 0 of the two-ion example device (L = 1, 128, 512, two sequences, 2000 shots) the survival is 0.9995, 0.9985, 0.985, fitting F(L) = 0.4995 x 0.99998^L + 0.5000 with p = 0.999983(9) and r = (1 - p)/2 = 8.50(44)e-6 per computational gate at 1.561 pulses per gate. That is BELOW the Clifford-RB r = 1.97e-5 per Clifford at 0.829 pulses, although a computational gate costs 1.9x the pulses: the Pauli randomization twirls the pulses' coherent errors toward a depolarizing channel, so the partial cancellation Clifford RB relies on is replaced by an average that does not accumulate

anchor.m10.knill_style_rb.source: check_benchmarks.py 3; benchmarks/rb.py (variant='knill'); tests/test_m10_benchmarks.py; Knill et al., PRA 77, 012307 (2008); Harty et al. 2014; Wright et al. 2019

anchor.m10.quantum_volume_width_two.corrected_form: the first version used the standard error of the mean as the confidence and let a run below 100 circuits clear a quantum volume; both are corrected (conv.heavy_output_criterion). The SEM is 4.20 times smaller than Eq. (32)'s sigma here, and the difference is decision-changing at the protocol's own circuit count: extrapolating this run's spread to n_c = 100 the SEM clears 2/3 at mean - 2 sigma = 0.6943 while Eq. (32) fails it at 0.626087, so a run Cross et al. would reject was being reported as a pass (tests/test_m10_benchmarks.py pins both). At width two the ideal heavy-output probability itself spreads from 0.59 to 0.87 between circuits (0.796 +- 0.092 over 200), so the criterion needs the protocol's hundred circuits even on a machine at 0.99 register fidelity; the result carries the circuit count and says so
anchor.m10.quantum_volume_width_two.equation: four random square circuits of depth two (six entangling gates and 26 pulses each after merging the local unitaries), 400 shots: heavy-output probabilities 0.795(20), 0.648(24), 0.820(19), 0.603(25) against the ideal 0.7429, 0.6176, 0.8657, 0.5858; mean 0.7163 against the ideal mean 0.7030 and the depolarizing prediction 0.7016 (eps_gates 5.83e-3 from the full-angle channels, eps_readout 9.6e-4); exact register fidelities 0.990, 0.996, 0.995, 0.991; Section 9.6 scales 2.89e-2 per circuit. Cross et al. Appendix C Eq. (32) gives sigma = sqrt(h(1 - h)/n_c) = 0.2254, so mean - 2 sigma = 0.2654 and threshold_cleared is False; the standard error of the mean over the circuits is 0.0537, 4.20 times smaller, and is reported as a diagnostic and never as the criterion; the run also fails the protocol's n_c >= 100, so passed is False and log2_quantum_volume is None

anchor.m10.simultaneous_rb_crosstalk.corrected_form: this record said 'the measured joint decay is twice the first-order composition: consecutive carrier pulses rotate the same neighbour about nearby axes and their 2.2 % crosstalk errors add in amplitude, not in probability'. That factor 2 was a UNIT MISMATCH, not physics: the joint decay's (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n is the error per LAYER of n Cliffords while the budget's r_channel was per SINGLE Clifford (the check script divided it by 2 to print them side by side), so the ratio 6.90e-4/3.426e-4 = 2.01 was the factor n and nothing else. With the units matched (conv.simultaneous_rb_units) the first-order composition predicts the joint decay to 0.9 % and the marginals to 9 %, so simultaneous RB is no evidence of errors adding in amplitude and the 'add in amplitude' mechanism is withdrawn here (the GHZ circuit's coherent crosstalk, anchor.m10.ghz_fidelity, is a separate and still-supported observation). What survives: the ions' gates cost 13x more under simultaneous operation than alone, 35x per layer, and single-ion RB is blind to it -- which is why the benchmark offers the variant. New here: the two ions' marginals differ by a factor 3 (1.31e-4 against 3.87e-4) although their compositions are equal to 0.2 %, so the coherent cancellation within a sequence is ion-dependent on this chain
anchor.m10.simultaneous_rb_crosstalk.equation: both ions driven by independent Clifford sequences (2000 shots, two sequences, m = 1, 128, 512). Per-qubit MARGINAL survival (Gambetta et al. 2012) 0.9995, 0.9495, 0.938 on ion 0 and 0.998, 0.96375, 0.79925 on ion 1, giving marginal p 0.999738 and 0.999227 and r_q = (1 - p_q)/2 = 1.31e-4 and 3.87e-4, mean 2.588(94)e-4 against 1.97e-5 for the ion benchmarked alone -- a factor 13 that single-ion RB cannot see. The per-qubit composition (each kind's GATE_LOCAL channel reduced to THAT ONE qubit, so the neighbour's crosstalk rotation counts) is r_channel.q0 = 2.853e-4 and r_channel.q1 = 2.858e-4, mean 2.855e-4, which the measured mean matches to 9 %. The same run's JOINT survival P(00) = 0.9975, 0.91425, 0.75225 fits p = 0.999078(86), so (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n = 6.91(7)e-4 per LAYER of two Cliffords -- 35x the isolated r -- against the layer composition r_channel_joint_layer = 6.853e-4, which it matches to 0.9 %

anchor.m10.single_qubit_rb.corrected_form: the three-parameter fit is degenerate at this decay (A = 0.19 +- 0.93 and B = 0.81 +- 0.93 on the same data), so B is pinned at 1/2^n (fix_offset); the first-order composition of the channels over-predicts r by 20 %: a Clifford's two pulses carry coherent errors that partly cancel. This record cited '9.12 Wright reproduction' as a plan section while reporting the example device's own p = 0.999960, a hundred times better than Wright's p ~ 0.995: the citation is dropped and the row's status is recorded in anchor.m10.knill_style_rb. Its 'a third of the Cliffords' pulse-free count was wrong (four of twenty-four, see conv.two_qubit_clifford_classes), and the quoted +-4.5e-6 on r came from an error bar that added the within-sequence shot noise to a between-sequence variance already containing it, up to sqrt 2 too large at three sequences (benchmarks/rb.py mean_survival_sigma)

anchor.m2.comb_drive_through_the_builder.corrected_form: Drive.comb was a dead field whose only reader was its own kind validation; light/raman.py contained zero comb references and no test integrated a comb drive at all. guards()'s 'adiabatic_elimination' and 'small_pulse_area' were the literal True and guards() was never called from qutip_trap/, so its docstring's 'the engine logs before every solve' was false; the two clauses are now evaluated when their inputs are supplied and ABSENT (with unevaluated_guards naming them) when they are not, so 'not evaluated' can no longer be read as 'satisfied'. The intensity-to-Rabi chain that would supply theta per pulse is still missing (Section 12) (M2 audit E8)
anchor.m2.comb_drive_through_the_builder.equation: light.raman.comb_drive sets Drive.comb, tones from comb.tones() and stark_shift_hz from comb.stark4_hz() on the same gate-time cut, and evaluates CombSpec.guards() at construction, warning with the failing clauses and the un-evaluable ones by name. On the single-ion 171Yb+ fixture at 80 MHz and 10 ps the cut keeps ONE beat note, of envelope Omega_0 sech(pi x 158 x nu_rep tau) = 0.926025 (the plan's 0.925994 is the same factor at the zero-field splitting), and a pulse of pi/(Omega_0 sech e^{-eta^2/2}) inverts the qubit to 3e-6, the residual being the off-resonant sidebands (eta Omega/omega_m)^2. Widening the cut to 10/(1.5 nu_rep) keeps three tones at mu = 0, +-80 MHz and does NOT raise the drive-term count, because a tone set is one operator with a summed coefficient

anchor.m2.composite_filter_and_dc_floor_.equation: the two Appendix E methods now delegate to noise/decoupling.py (composite_segments + amplitude_filter_function; the free dc_floor) through a function-local import that keeps the control layer free of a module-scope dependency on the noise layer. c-hat_{m+1} is FITTED, not read off at one eps: leading_coefficient(eps) carries a truncation error in even powers of eps and a round-off error growing as eps falls, so fitted_leading_coefficient least-squares c-hat + a eps^2 + b eps^4 over the eps ladder whose operator distance is still above 1e-10 and returns the constant. Measured relative agreement with Section 4.3.5 at theta = pi: SK1 22.8302557111 to 4.1e-10, SCROFULOUS 4.566051 to 9.2e-8, BB1 9.388566343 to 1.5e-7, CORPSE 0.006500751892 to 1.6e-7, PB1 118.295935928 to 1.9e-7, CinSK 0.75 to 4.2e-7, CinBB 0.75 to 2.1e-6. The dc floors follow at 2.5e-7 relative: 5.87365e-6 (SK1), 3.53675e-9 (BB1), 1.67248e-9 (CORPSE) at <beta^2> = 2.07e9/pi (rad/s)^2 and Omega = 1.5e6 rad/s. m is the pulse's order FOR THE CHANNEL, so a family that does not correct a channel enters that channel at m = 0. The amplitude-filter low-frequency slopes are 2.0 (primitive, CORPSE) and 4.0 (SK1, BB1, PB1, SCROFULOUS, CinSK, CinBB), and the dc polygon closes for the six amplitude correctors and equals (pi, 0, 0) for primitive and CORPSE

anchor.m2.wineland_eight_term_stark.equation: the eight-term |2,2> <-> |1,1> differential shift is NOT transcribed and no numbers for it are invented: PLAN.md:1885 lists Wineland Eqs. 2.5-2.9 and 2.11-2.12 as untranscribed, so the plan carries no coefficient sets pairing the eight scattering channels with their detunings at first power (Eq. 2.14's rationals 2/3, 1/3, 1, 1/6, 1/2, 5/6 are in the plan but not their channel assignment). What IS asserted against the derived AtomicStructure sum on the 9Be+ fixture is the qualitative claim the plan makes [verified]: the |2,2> <-> |1,1> differential shift changes sign between pure sigma+ and pure sigma- and therefore HAS a polarization null (root-found, at a genuine monotone crossing), while the clock shift keeps its sign over the same 41-point ellipticity scan and is therefore unnullable. The mechanism common to both is the three-index detuning: the summed line strength out of each member of either pair is identical beam by beam to 1e-12 (PLAN.md:647's sum rule), so a single Delta per intermediate LEVEL would return zero for either

anchor.m3.itano_three_beam_optimum.equation: axis i takes friction from its own beam only (proportional to gamma_si) and the emission recoil from all three (f_si gamma_tot), so E_i is proportional to 1 + f_si gamma_tot/gamma_si and minimizing sum_i E_i at fixed sum_i gamma_si gives gamma_si proportional to sqrt(f_si); at that optimum E_i = (hbar Gamma/4)(1 + sqrt(f_si) sum_j sqrt(f_sj)). For an isotropic pattern (f_si = 1/3, the Cartesian sum rule of Section 4.2.8) the shares are 1/3 each and E_i = hbar Gamma/2 per mode, whose kinetic half is EXACTLY Itano's hbar Gamma/4 per mode, the same number as the single-beam (1 + alpha)/4 form at alpha = 1. For the sigma pattern along z (f = 3/10, 3/10, 2/5) the shares are (0.3169873, 0.3169873, 0.3660254) and the optimum total is 5.9856 hbar Gamma/4 against the uniform split's 6

With the TOTAL two-ion mass r_0 = 3.82844 nm and Omega_g/2pi = 2870.8 Hz, the dressed coupling at the decoupling point is Omega_g J_2(2.4048)/2pi = 1239.5 Hz and Omega_mu/2pi = 571.1 kHz

The pumping is frozen at the neighbours' START classes, the same first-order form the factored confusion tensor uses, because one ion's chain is sampled before its neighbours' paths are known; the polarization share of the leaked light that reaches the pumping channel is a device parameter defaulting to the plan's BOUND of 1

R_o is untouched: Wineland's mechanism degrades DISCRIMINATION, never eta_d

anchor.m6.bessel_force_saturation.corrected_form: the row names four contributions and the M6 budget carried three; the first M6 fix added the Wineland Lamb-Dicke deficit under the row's name and summed it (3.06e-2 at the Section 11.1 pulse's cap top n = 11, which dominated every budget total although that Fock state is unpopulated), while the row's term is Roos Eq. 17 (PLAN.md 4.4.1: 'the force is saturated by (J_0 + J_2)' at argument 4 Omega/delta). The 2026-09-08 consolidation entered the Roos term under the row's key as an infidelity scale and moved the Lamb-Dicke deficit to its own reported key outside the sum: its thermal mean is exactly the force rescaling the s^2 calibration of Section 4.4.7 (7) absorbs and its thermal spread is the Debye-Waller term (ballance_thermal_error) the total already carries, so summing it double counted. Both are upper bounds on what survives calibration, not estimates of it
anchor.m6.bessel_force_saturation.equation: Section 9.6's 'Bessel force saturation' is Roos's carrier correction: the spin-dependent force is scaled by (J_0 + J_2)(x) at x = 4 Omega/mu (Omega the tone Rabi frequency, mu the tone-to-carrier detuning), so an uncalibrated pulse solved with the linear force reaches chi (1 - f)^2 with f = 1 - (J_0 + J_2)(x) = x^2/8 + O(x^4), an angle error pi f/2 at chi = pi/4 and a Bell-state infidelity sin^2(pi f/2); intrinsic_budget reports it per played MS gate as '<gate>.bessel_saturation' at the waveform's largest amplitude and smallest |mu| and sums it into 'total'. On the Section 11.1 pulse (Omega/2pi = 64.148 kHz, mu/2pi = 3.01 MHz) x = 0.0852, f = 9.1e-4 and the term is 2.0e-6, far inside the row's 1.1e-4 as the row's sum requires. The sideband element's Lamb-Dicke deficit f_LD = 1 - Omega_{n+1,n}/(Omega eta sqrt(n + 1)), with Omega_{n+1,n}/Omega = e^{-eta^2/2} (eta/sqrt(n+1)) |L^{(1)}_n(eta^2)|, is reported as '<gate>.sideband_lamb_dicke_deficit' (worst case over the gate's ions and carried modes at the cap's top Fock index) and NOT summed
anchor.m6.bessel_force_saturation.section: 9.6 row 3 ('the intrinsic budget lists off-resonant carrier, Bessel force saturation, residual displacement, Debye-Waller'); 4.4.1 (Roos Eq. 17); 4.3.1
anchor.m6.bessel_force_saturation.source: Roos 2008, New J. anchor.m6.ca40_optical_preset.corrected_form: three preset choices are forced by limits of the first release and are not laboratory practice. (1) The axial mode is 2.0 MHz, not the 171Yb+ preset's 1.0 MHz: with no sideband-cooling stage the Doppler-limited eta^2 (2 nbar + 1) = 0.60 at 1.0 MHz, which the Section 4.2.8 (vii) Lamb-Dicke guard of the level-A rate model refuses above 0.25, and the quantity scales as 1/omega^2. (2) There is no sideband-cooling stage at all: Section 4.2.2's stage is pulsed RAMAN cooling on a two-beam pair (SidebandCoolingSpec.beams), and 729 nm resolved-sideband cooling on the quadrupole line is not scheduled. (3) The 854 nm shelf-reset beam is opt-in (reset_beam=True), because a Device's beams are always on and readout takes every resonant beam of the cycling cycle as detection light, so an ungated 854 nm beam depumps the shelf DURING detection: measured SPAM (0.573, 0.427) with it against (2.5e-04, 1.8e-03) without. Separately, the derived bright scatter rate peaks at R_o = 3.57e6/s at I/I_sat = (2, 10) and FALLS at higher intensity (1.99e6/s at (10, 30), 3.06e5/s at (50, 100)) because the magic-angle LINEAR polarization of the 397/866 cycle traps population in coherent dark states; that is 8 times below Myerson's 2.9e7/s, so the preset buys the readout back with a 2 ms window instead of his 420 us
anchor.m6.ca40_optical_preset.equation: a 40Ca+ S1/2 mJ = -1/2 <-> D5/2 mJ = -1/2 optical qubit at B = 5 G along x, secular frequencies (3.0, 2.9, 2.0) MHz, one 729 nm quadrupole beam (5 mW, 200 um waist, k = (1,1,0)/sqrt 2, polarization at 135 degrees) whose DERIVED Delta m = 0 E2 carrier Rabi frequency is 34742.3 Hz, the 397 nm S1/2-P1/2 detection/Doppler light and the 866 nm D3/2-P1/2 repump along (1,1,1)/sqrt 3 at I/I_sat = 2 and 10, and Myerson's PMT chain (eps_sys = 0.19 %, 442 cps) at a 2 ms window. run() on GPi2(0): preparation error 6.11e-05, Doppler occupations nbar = 15.1 (axial 2.0 MHz), 9.6 and 10.0 (radial), every mode frozen or dropped so the space is [2], register 1 - F = 6.86e-04 (the two frozen radial modes' Debye-Waller loss at those occupations), 1102 Fock branches carrying all but 5.9e-02, SPAM (eps_B, eps_D) = (2.5e-04, 1.8e-03) at a 3 ms window and threshold 7.5

The row still holds for a CALIBRATED gate, because the exact spot check and the run drop the same mode and the s^2 rescaling of Section 4.4.7 (7) absorbs the mode-independent part of the factor; what is not absorbed is the shot-to-shot variance of DW(n_m, eta_m) over the thermal distribution of n_m, which is negligible only because the dropped modes of these fixtures are sideband cooled to nbar < 0.05. anchor.m7.decoupling_high_precision.corrected_form: the even-n IR rows CANNOT be reproduced in float64 and this is now asserted as a negative control: the even-n finite-pulse F is (omega tau)^2 (omega tau_pi)^4/64, which at omega = 1e-6 is 1e-43 of an O(1) sum, so double precision returns omega-independent cancellation noise of order 1e-32, which turns the omega^-4 integrand into omega^-6 and makes the package report chi(1e-7) = 128.56 for UDD-4 and 92.83 for UDD-6 (ratios 107 and 19) against true values of 1.2e-4 and 2.4e-5. The retired claim in conv.filter_function_machinery that check_composite.py's sections 9-15 are 'reproduced by noise/decoupling.py' was true for the finite-pulse collapse, the gated Biercuk values and the dc floors, and false for these rows
anchor.m7.decoupling_high_precision.equation: all reproduced at mp.dps = 220-250. Carr-Purcell: amplitude Taylor order 3 at every even n with c_3 = i/(8 n^2) = 0.03125i, 0.0078125i, 0.003472222222i, 0.001953125i at n = 2, 4, 6, 8 (the plan's four printed values), and order 2 at odd n with c_2 = -1/(4 n^2); |c_2|^2 = 1/(16 n^4) and |c_3|^2 = 1/(64 n^4) ARE the plan's two printed CPMG coefficient laws. UDD: order n + 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 with every lower coefficient below 10^{-110}, and F/(omega tau)^{2n+2} = 1/(16^n (n!)^2) to 12 digits for n = 1..8. IR convergence at tau = 1, tau_pi = 0.05, omega_max = 50: chi(1e-7) -> chi(1e-8) = 2.48719319 -> 24.8683571 (ratio 9.9985627) for UDD 3 and 2.48684517 -> 24.868009 (9.999822) for UDD 5, against 1.20925691e-4 and 2.39513137e-5 at ratio exactly 1.0 for n = 4 and 6. Green Eq. 45: 4.75678006346 against Biercuk's 0.0396431177199 at n = 1, identical at even n, |R_zz(0)|^2 = 4 exactly at n = 1, 3, 5. <a_1^2> = 0.06875600894468 from the double integral of C(t1 - t2), independently of the spectral integral

anchor.m7.hughes_two_term.corrected_form: the source's lambda^2_{S_alpha} and lambda^2_{S_alpha^2} are the VARIANCES of the two spin operators over the input state, not the bare moments <S^2> and <S^4>: the first coincides with <S_alpha^2> = N because <S_alpha> = 0 on |0...0> (which is why the plan prints it that way), but the second is <S^4> - <S^2>^2 = 2N(N - 1) and reading it as <S^4> = 3N^2 - 2N overshoots by a factor 2 at N = 2 and 1.75 at N = 3. The exact propagation discriminates them
anchor.m7.hughes_two_term.equation: alpha_t = int_0^{t_g} eps(t) gamma(t) dt and delta_theta = 2 int_0^{t_g} eps(t)|gamma(t)|^2 dt with H_e = hbar eps(t) a^dag a (Eq. 29) and U_g = exp{(gamma a^dag - gamma* a) S_alpha} exp{-i (theta/2) S_alpha^2} (Eq. 27). For a CONSTANT fractional offset on a symmetric K-loop gate |alpha_t| = (pi sqrt K/2)(eps/delta) and delta_theta = (pi/2)(eps/delta), the second being K-INDEPENDENT. Verified against exact two- and three-ion propagation of the plan's own force model: the exact-to-closed-form ratio extrapolates to 1.0000 with a linear-in-eps remainder (0.990568, 0.995311, 0.997671, 0.998873 at eps/delta = 4e-3, 2e-3, 1e-3, 5e-4 for N = 2, K = 1, nbar = 0 -> 1.000076), at every (N, K, nbar) in {(2,1,0), (2,1,1), (2,2,0), (3,1,0), (3,1,2), (2,3,0)}
anchor.m7.hughes_two_term.source: Hughes, Srinivas, Loeschnauer, Knaack, Matt, Ballance, Malinowski, Harty and Sutherland, 'Trapped-ion two-qubit gates with >99.99% fidelity without ground-state cooling', arXiv:2510.17286 (2025), Appendix B 'Infidelity Due to Mode Frequency Fluctuations', Eq. 33; read from the source because the plan transcribes only the first term

anchor.m7.intensity_noise_factor_two.corrected_form: see anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions for the derivation, the six measurements, the global-versus-per-beam discriminator on B/A, and the reasons 9.16 row 4.4-8's own ratios are not reproducible
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_factor_two.equation: this record read the N = 2 measurement A/(Gamma_I t_g eta^2/2) = 2.00 as a factor 2 and inferred an open Gamma_I convention. Extending the fit to all five (N, K) the row asks for shows the factor is N (1.00, 2.00, 3.01, 2.00, 2.00, 3.00 at (1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (2,2), (2,3), (3,2)), so the plan's derived A is EXACT at N = 1 with the carrier-contrast Gamma_I and the convention is settled

anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions.corrected_form: the Gamma_I convention is SETTLED, not open: the plan's derived A = Gamma_I t_g eta^2/2 is exact at N = 1 with Gamma_I the carrier-contrast rate k Omega^2, so the retired reading of this record (that the plan's A pairs with half the contrast rate or another fidelity measure) was a wrong inference from the N = 2 case. What the plan's eps_I first term is missing is a factor N for an N-ion drive; the same Var(sum s_i) = N is Hughes's lambda^2_{S_alpha} (anchor.m7.hughes_two_term), which is the cross-check that fixes it. 9.16 row 4.4-8's A/(eta^2 Gamma_I t_g/2) = 0.997-0.999 and B/[3(N-1)/(8K)] ~ 1.00 across all five (N, K) are therefore NOT reproducible in this model - both are N times larger - and the row's model must divide the collective operator's variance by N (equivalently define Gamma_I as N times the single-ion contrast rate). New: only a GLOBAL intensity-noise operator gives B/A = 3(N-1)/(4K); N independent per-beam operators leave A(N) unchanged but halve the ratio to 3(N-1)/(8K) (measured 0.37469, 0.74563, 0.18746 at (2,1), (3,1), (2,2)), so the plan's B term is itself evidence that its eps_I describes one laser shared by the register
anchor.m7.intensity_noise_n_ions.equation: in the sigma_alpha eigenbasis block s closes with a residual displacement s x delta_alpha, <|delta_alpha|^2> = f^2 (2 Gamma_I/Omega^2) t_g with f = eta Omega/2; the pair (s, s') decoheres by exp(-|s - s'|^2 <|delta_alpha|^2>(2 nbar + 1)/2), so 1 - F = Var(sum_i s_i)(2 nbar + 1)(eta^2/2) Gamma_I t_g and Var = N for |0...0>. What is NOT done is an exact diamond norm (an SDP): the test brackets the true value from below and the bound from above, which is enough to falsify the inequality but not to quote (1/2)||E||_diamond itself

anchor.m7.xy_n_t2_anchors.corrected_form: the mains lines are load-bearing, not decoration: a Hahn echo whose filter maximum sits on the 60 Hz line sees more than twice the chi of the same 1/f background without lines, and deep in the echo's omega^4 asymptote (tau = 1 us) the lines still carry 3.367x the background's integrated power. anchor.m7.xy_n_t2_anchors.equation: T_2 is obtained by bisection on chi(tau) = 1 through the package's own XY4 machinery on a 1/f background carrying Lorentzian lines at the mains fundamental and its first four harmonics. anchor.m8.full_calibration_two_ion.corrected_form: the first M8 build asserted 4 sigma per entry and, for the fidelity, budget + 3 x cal + 2e-3 with no lower bound, which would have passed with a substantially worse calibration and equally with a calibration whose errors had disappeared (a table played as the physics, the played chain switched off, or the frame taken at the true transition); the claim 'within its reported uncertainty' described neither
anchor.m8.full_calibration_two_ion.equation: every entry the experiments fit (field, qubit frequencies, mode frequencies, occupations, Rabi frequencies, light shifts, crosstalk ratios and phases, the entangling waveform's closure and phase alignment, detection) agrees with the device's derived truth within TWO of its reported standard errors, which is what tests/test_full_calibration.py enforces (SIGMA = 2.0); the realized deviations printed in outputs/check_calibration.out section 5 are all at or below 1.02 sigma, so the plan's 'within the uncertainty the fits report' holds in fact and 2 sigma is the reproducible bound the suite asserts. A Bell circuit run from the fitted table reaches a register infidelity inside the intrinsic budget PLUS the calibration's own contribution (the per-pulse over-rotation (sigma_Omega/Omega x pi/2)^2 and the residual frame offset (2 pi sigma_f t_gate)^2, with no slack factor) and strictly ABOVE the surrogate-table run's, whose seeds are the derived values (numbers in outputs/check_calibration.out)

anchor.m8.micromotion_nulls.corrected_form: the first M8 build correlated the photon rate at the fixture's detection frequency (on resonance) and kept only the sin projection: there the first-order response vanishes (the rate is even in the detuning) and the first harmonic was |S_1| = 3.2e-5 at beta = 0.045 against 3.4e-2 half a linewidth to the red, so the null was found exactly but its declared photon-budget uncertainty was 3.3e3 V/m; the response lags the rf by 141 degrees at Omega_rf = 1.5 Gamma, and a fixed sin projection kept 63 % of the amplitude
anchor.m8.micromotion_nulls.equation: a 30 V/m stray field on a single 171Yb+ ion at Omega_rf = 2 pi x 30 MHz gives beta = 0.245 along the Raman Delta k; the sideband-ratio scan through the exact e^{i beta cos Omega t} modulation nulls it at -30.00 +- 0.46 V/m with a residual |beta| of 2.5e-4, and the rf-photon-correlation periodic steady state of the 369.5 nm detection beam, retuned to -Gamma/2 and projected on the atom's response phase (odd in the signed index, linear to 15 % at beta = 0.2), nulls a 20 V/m field at -20.0000 +- 2.8 V/m from the exact signal (the photon budget of a 1 s acquisition at 3.8e5 photons/s and 4.4 % detection efficiency) and at -19.27 +- 0.83 V/m (0.87 sigma) with photon shot noise drawn over 10 s, residual beta -7.9e-5 +- 4.5e-3, on the two-ion fixture

anchor.m8.run_level_over_rotation.equation: a table whose Rabi belief for ion 0 is 5 % high schedules the GPi 1/1.05 short (3.398572 us -> 3.236736 us, ratio 0.952381) and the played chain gives the ion Omega_req x Omega_derived/Omega_table = Omega_req/1.05, so the achieved rotation is pi/1.05 and 1 - P(ion 0 excited) rises from the 1.104e-04 baseline to 7.150e-03 against the analytic under-rotation cos^2(pi/2/1.05) = 5.585e-03 (a factor 1.28, the remainder being the baseline and the second-order light-shift term the shortened pulse leaves)

anchor.m8.sideband_light_shift.corrected_form: Section 7.5's fine scan of a single resonance at full power would have written the mode frequency low by 1.5 kHz into the table, above the FM solvers' sub-kilohertz need
anchor.m8.sideband_light_shift.equation: a resonant sideband pulse light-shifts the qubit through its own off-resonant CARRIER coupling by Omega^2/(2 omega_m) (1.70 kHz at Omega/2pi = 100.9 kHz, omega_m/2pi = 3 MHz), pulling both the blue and the red sideband resonance toward the carrier, so blue - carrier and (blue - red)/2 both read the mode frequency low by it; the scan fits the blue centre at two rf amplitudes and extrapolates to zero power (the shift scales as the intensity), which recovers the mode frequency within its uncertainty

anchor.m8.stark_scan_per_beam.corrected_form: the both-beams-on measurement with the beat note detuned by Delta carries the odd coupling shift Omega^2/(2 Delta) (1.27 kHz at Delta = 4 MHz), whose fringe at probe minus shift aliases with the plan's Ramsey delays (Nyquist 2.5 kHz for six points over 1 ms); kept as mode='beat_note' with that caveat. The DEFAULT per-beam mode had the same aliasing unrecorded: it took the modulus of one fringe fit and reported probe - |f|, losing the sign of (delta_St - probe), so with probe = 1 kHz a true -38.4 Hz read -38.40, 300 Hz read 300.00, but 1500 Hz read +500.00 and 2500 Hz read -500.00, all four with converged=True and the |shift| < probe guard satisfied; kilohertz differential shifts are ordinary for Raman gates and CalibrationScans.stark_probe_hz defaults to 1 kHz. Fixed by the two-probe estimator above (anchor.m8.stark_scan_two_probe_branch). The mode switch also reached _setup, which reads a 'mode' keyword as a driven-mode INDEX, so stark_scan(mode='beat_note') raised int('beat_note')
anchor.m8.stark_scan_per_beam.equation: with one beam of the Raman pair on during the Ramsey delay there is no two-photon coupling and the fringe shift is that beam's differential light shift; the drive's shift is their sum (-19.2 - 19.2 = -38.4 Hz on the two-ion fixture, recovered within its uncertainty). The Ramsey fit returns |probe - delta_St|, so each beam's Ramsey is run at BOTH probe signs and the shift is the half-difference delta = (f_minus - f_plus)/2 with sigma = hypot(sigma_plus, sigma_minus)/2, the estimator ramsey_frequency already used for a qubit offset: exact while |delta| < probe, with f_plus + f_minus = 2 probe as the out-of-range detector (tolerance 4 sigma or 1e-3 probe, whichever is larger) and 1/(2 dt) of the delay grid as the Nyquist guard on probe + |delta|

anchor.m8.stark_scan_two_probe_branch.corrected_form: with one probe sign the fit's |probe - delta| loses the sign of (delta - probe): the same four shifts read -38.40, 300.00, +500.00 and -500.00, the last two silently wrong and marked calibrated with the |shift| < probe guard satisfied (see anchor.m8.stark_scan_per_beam). The two-ion fixture's per-beam shift is far inside the probe (-27.07 Hz each after the M0a P3/2 correction, -19.2 Hz before it), so no test or committed number caught it
anchor.m8.stark_scan_two_probe_branch.equation: the two-probe estimator on the exact fringe: delta_St = -38.4 Hz gives f_plus = 1038.40 and f_minus = 961.60, half-difference -38.400 exactly; 300 Hz gives 700.00 and 1300.00 -> 300.000; -900 Hz gives 1900.00 and 100.00 -> -900.000. Above the probe the estimator saturates at the probe: 1500 Hz gives 500.00 and 2500.00 and 2500 Hz gives 1500.00 and 3500.00, both refused by |delta| < probe AND by the sums 3000 and 5000 against 2 probe = 2000. The delay grid's Nyquist frequency 1/(2 dt) bounds probe + |delta|: five delays over 2 ms resolve 1000 Hz and refuse a 1 kHz probe with any non-zero shift, nine resolve 2000 Hz and accept it
anchor.m8.stark_scan_two_probe_branch.source: tests/test_m8_calibration_fixes.py (the exact fringe |detuning - delta| at probe = 1 kHz, nine delays over 2 ms)

anchor.m9.integrator_ladder_stiffness_no.corrected_form: the abort does not reproduce here. On the Section 11.1 one-mode fixture (2 ions x 1 mode, 20 us, nsteps 1e7) dop853 succeeds at d_m = 101, 121, 151 and 201 at BOTH atol 1e-10 and 1e-8 (17.8 s and 19.8 s at 121, coefficient calls 243815 and 291820; vern9 18.0 s and 17.9 s, 257510 and 257286), and atol as tight as 1e-30 at d_m = 121 still succeeds, so atol is not the binding constraint at rtol 1e-8. The failures reachable on this machine are nsteps limits, which every rung shares: at nsteps = 2500 both integrators fail at d_m = 121, 151 and 201 at both atol values. The atol keying of Section 5.3 is therefore pinned as a keying (1e-10 at d_m <= 100, 1e-8 above, at 121, 151 and 201) and the escalation is exercised through a step budget between the two integrators' requirements, with no failure manufactured to make the ladder look tested. The plan's number is left standing as a measurement on its own machine
anchor.m9.integrator_ladder_stiffness_no.equation: PLAN.md 5.3: 'with atol 1e-10 dop853 aborts ("problem is probably stiff") at d_m = 121 on the Section 11.1 pulse while succeeding at 101, and succeeds at 121 with atol 1e-8 or with vern9'

The absolute factorized wall times 0.25 / 0.35 / 1.11 / 3.15 s are asserted only within a factor of four rather than the two the audit suggested, because the whole suite runs many pytest processes at once (load average 113 on 18 CPUs while this was measured) and the plan's numbers come from an idle machine; the cost RATIO is the load-robust half and carries the two-fold bound. bench_ms_timing_v5.py is NOT added to CI: run_checks.py --bench runs every bench_*.py, the v5 script alone is about four minutes on the plan's idle machine and its 2048 rows total about 266 s of integration, which on a two-core GitHub runner without Accelerate BLAS is tens of minutes; the slow acceptance test above is what re-verifies the table in CI instead (.github/workflows/ci.yml runs a bare `uv run pytest`)

anchor.m9a.cap_rule_populated_range.corrected_form: the M6 rule sized the cap from the single-loop radius eta Omega_peak/eps through ceil((|alpha| + sqrt nbar)^2 + 2 sqrt(|alpha|^2 + nbar + 1/4) + 1): on the two-ion fixture's five-segment AM pulse the joint run populates n = 6 on the COM (n = 4 on the rocking mode) at the 1e-6 tail against the rule's 4 (3), so once the Section 5.5 policy was enforced every entangling pulse tripped, grew both caps by four levels and ran three times slower (80 s against 26 s for the Bell circuit); check_circuits.out and check_two_qubit.out regenerated with the changed caps (check_calibration.out re-run and unchanged to every printed digit)
anchor.m9a.cap_rule_populated_range.equation: the cap of a resolved mode is the highest Fock index its thermal state displaced by the pulse's coherent excursion, max over the pulse of sum_i |alpha_im(t)| from the closed-form trajectories (the S = +-N spin branch), populates above the boundary threshold (sum_k P_th(k) |<n|D(i|alpha|)|k>|^2, the analytic elements) plus the Section 5.1.1 margin; the engine's margin check after every pulse reads the same definition with the threshold taken as a fraction of the MIXTURE's population (a Fock branch of weight w, evolved on its own by run() or the tomography, is measured at tail/w through the sample key branch_weight), so a first attempt does not trip: the two-ion Bell circuit at the default 1e-6 branch cutoff runs its twelve branches on [2, 2, 11, 13] with no growth, populated ranges 3 and 5 and margins of 7 levels

anchor.m9a.tilted_frozen_spectator.equation: the two-ion 171Yb+ chain with the global 355 nm pair rotated by 6 degrees in the xy-plane couples the drive to the y modes with eta_y = -/+ 0.0085 against 0.078 to 0.081 on the x modes; a symmetric x-COM pulse (eps = 20 kHz, 50 us, 119.9 kHz per tone) leaves the y-COM (2.900 MHz, 120 kHz below the tone) with |chi_m| = 1.94e-3 rad and |alpha|^2 (2 nbar + 1) = 4e-32 (six closed loops) and the y-rocking mode (2.722 MHz) with 6.3e-4 rad and 1.6e-6: both frozen by the Section 5.2 classes; at eps = 30 kHz the y-COM's 3.1e-4 residual makes it resolved

anchor.m9a.tomography_projection.equation: the Choi matrix of MS(0.3, -0.7, pi/2) from its sixteen product inputs equals choi_from_unitary to 5e-16 with one Kraus operator; a depolarizing channel (eps = 0.05) reconstructed from outputs carrying 3e-4 of noise violates trace preservation at the noise level and the alternating projection returns ||Tr_out(Choi) - 1|| and the distance to the cone both below 1e-10, the map within 5e-3 of the truth, the twirl p_II = 0.95 and the depolarizing rate equal to the entanglement infidelity (Chen 2023's normalization)

anchor.m9b.cost_model_constants.corrected_form: Section 11.3's '24 against 512 amplitudes' counts multiply-adds; the measured gain is smaller and set by the fixed cost of each NumPy call (about 3 us per factor), so the auto rule is a measured crossover and not the amplitude ratio, and the assembled operator stays the right choice below dimension 440
anchor.m9b.cost_model_constants.equation: one right-hand side through QobjEvo.matmul (dispatch included), least-squares fit over eleven spaces from dimension 48 to 8192: a factorized term costs about 2.9 us per factor step plus 0.58 ns per complex multiply-add on the D/d_ion amplitudes of the source level, an assembled CSR term 0.57 ns per non-zero (2^{N-1} prod_m d_m^2 for two-level ions); the kernel carries 2.0 us + 2.5 us per step + 0.6 ns per multiply-add against 0.5 us + 0.57 ns per non-zero, which reproduces the measured choice on every space: assembled at dimensions 48 (0.7 against 4.7 us) and 256 (5.2 against 8.2), factorized from the 440-dimensional Bell space (14.3 against 9.8) upward, 299 against 24 us at 2048 and 1196 against 69 us at 8192 (four ions, three modes at d_m = 8)

anchor.m9b.factorized_kernel_exactness.corrected_form: an ENR group's sum-generator exponential is not a product of per-mode factors (Section 5.1.1), so a drive coupling to an ENR mode is assembled whatever the option says; a sum of two factorized operators has no factorized form and converts to Dense (the reason QobjEvo.compress must never merge the drive terms: every term carries its own coefficient object), and every mesolve segment builds the assembled CSR operator because the Liouvillian is formed from the matrix (Section 5.3)
anchor.m9b.factorized_kernel_exactness.equation: the drive operator held as its tensor factors (sigma_+ on the ion's factor, the oracle-checked per-mode exponentials D_m(i eta_m) on the resolved modes) and applied axis by axis (the ion factor a slice of the source level into the target level, every mode factor one batched matrix product) is the assembled operator to round-off: |F psi - A psi| = 2.4e-16 on the Bell space [2, 2, 10, 11] and 5.0e-16 at dimension 2048, max|F - A| = 0 element by element, the adjoint, the factor-wise F^dag F (9e-15) and the trace exact; registered as a QuTiP data-layer type so that QobjEvo, sesolve, mcsolve and the dop853/vern9 ladder run unchanged on it; the 20 us single-loop pulse through the engine with the kernel forced each way gives |psi_assembled - psi_factorized| = 2.2e-13 with identical populations (0.491426, 0.0252973, 0.0252973, 0.4579794)

anchor.m9b.propagator_cache.corrected_form: the plan's 'propagator with piecewise_t' route (a piecewise-constant generator with a reported segmentation error) is not needed: QuTiP 5 integrates the time-dependent propagator exactly, so no segmentation approximation is declared; the sample key branch_weight is left out of the fingerprint because it steers the margin check and no term of H
anchor.m9b.propagator_cache.equation: on a space with every mode frozen the segment propagator is integrated once as a D x D operator through the Section 5.3 ladder (an operator-valued state under sesolve) and applied to every initial state, cached per engine on the built Hamiltonian's value fingerprint (space, frequencies, the pulses' sampled tones, the sample's offsets and trajectories, the shifts); four inputs through one GPi2 segment cost one integration and three matrix products with |psi_cache - psi_ode| = 0; the tomography of a carrier step (3 frozen-mode Fock branches x 16 inputs) costs 3 integrations and 45 cache hits, one integration per distinct Debye-Waller factor

anchor.perf.tomography_isometry.corrected_form: an exact use of linearity, not an approximation: nothing is dropped and the same engine integrates the same H(t) at the same tolerances; a dissipative step (any collapse operator on any segment: a trajectory is not linear in its initial ket and a mesolve segment evolves a density matrix) keeps the state route whatever the switch says, and SolverOptions(tomography_isometry=False) forces it everywhere as the M9a reference; the one thing that does change is the Section 5.5 truncation monitor, which now runs on the propagated basis kets, so a superposition input's boundary population is bounded by d_int times the reported maximum (Cauchy-Schwarz) and the record's notes say so - on the bench fixture at d = 13 the sixteen-input route's superpositions tripped the margin check one level above the basis kets and the two routes ended on caps 13 and 14, which is why the comparison is made at d = 15; the CP/TP projection is kept so that the register's normalization stays exact and tp_residual(choi_raw) is the reported norm loss; Section 5.4's cost statement gains the branch multiplier it omitted (41 on the GHZ circuit); PLAN Section 11.3 item 5's 'never on the joint space' is respected, since the tomography propagates D x d_int columns of a joint space, never its D x D propagator; the one-ion idle channels are cached by (device, ion, duration, engine setup, sample, options), the absolute window joining the key only when the sample carries a fast trajectory, because an idle has no pulse and nothing motional enters its Hamiltonian; the gate-step cache key still carries the absolute time (the beat phase and the trajectories depend on it), so identical gates at different times are still extracted twice
anchor.perf.tomography_isometry.equation: a unitary step's final state is linear in its initial ket, so the GATE_LOCAL tomography propagates the prod_i d_i internal basis kets |j> (x) |m_b> of every motional branch b instead of the prod_i d_i^2 input states and reads the channel off the Stinespring isometry V_b their finals form: Kraus operators K_{b,a} = sqrt(w_b) (<a|_mot (x) 1) V_b (the slices by motional output index a), the trace-1 Choi matrix (1/d) sum_{b,a} |phi_{b,a}><phi_{b,a}| formed as one (d^2 x d_mot)(d_mot x d^2) product per branch without materializing the Kraus operators, and the input states' outputs, reduced motional states and <a_m> as the same functions of V_b psi_k; on an internal-state-only space the cached segment propagator IS the branch's Kraus operator (JointExactEngine.propagator: one engine call per branch, no state propagated). Against the state route on the same space (bench_tomography.py: a 10 us single-loop pulse on the two-ion chain, the x-COM resolved at d = 15, three branches) the Choi matrices agree to 3.2e-9, the outputs to 5.3e-9, the reduced motional outputs to 8.7e-9 and <a_m> to 6.1e-9 with 12 instead of 48 engine runs (0.52 against 1.95 s); the raw Choi matrix is completely positive to 7e-17 (1.7e-9 for the least-squares fit) and trace preserving to 4.3e-8, the norm the columns lost, and Dykstra converges in 2 iterations instead of 12; the carrier step agrees to 3.4e-16 with 3 instead of 48 runs. The four-qubit GHZ circuit through GATE_LOCAL (16 gate steps, 41 motional branches, 18 workers) runs in 205 s instead of 856 s with the same register fidelity (0.8437147 against 0.8437146) and the same bound (0.0457707): its entangling steps 164 instead of 656 runs each, its in-process part 2 s instead of 67 s (13 carrier steps of 41 propagators each; 60 of the 64 one-ion idle channels from the idle cache). The example device's Bell circuit through GATE_LOCAL (2000 shots) 17.1 -> 5.1 s, the entangling step 40 columns over 10 branches instead of 160 runs, the final states equal to 4.3e-10. The register update sum_a K_a rho K_a^dag as one superoperator product (sum_a K_a (x) conj K_a on the (local, local) x (rest, rest) reshape) 0.148 -> 0.010 s at ten qubits, difference 1.4e-18, and Register.marginal on the strided view 1.05 -> 0.08 ms, identical

anchor.species.ba_g_factors.corrected_form: both Ba tables previously carried D32.g_J = 0.79 and D52.g_J = 1.12 read off the NIST ASD Lande column, with the 1.12 flagged contested as a suspected transcription slip for 1.20. A direct re-query of the ASD CGI settles which side the error is on: ASD's own Lande column for Ba II returns literally 0.79, 1.12 and 1.32 and BLANK for 6s 2S1/2, so the transcription was faithful and the 1.12 is ASD'S OWN ERROR -- 6.7 % from Arnold's measured 1.20036739(24), from Hoffman et al., Phys. Rev. A 88, 025401 (2013)'s earlier measured 1.200372(4)(7), from the LS Lande 1.2005 and from the isoelectronic measured 1.2003340 of Ca+ 3d 2D5/2. Both ASD readings are kept as D32.g_J_asd and D52.g_J_asd tagged contested rather than deleted, so the defect stays documented, and nothing consumes them: species() reads the measured values, and the 6p levels take the LS Lande 0.665894 and 1.334106 tagged [background] because no measured Ba+ 6p g_J was located (the ASD column's 1.32 is a cross-check for the same reason its 1.12 is). The blank 6s row is what the retired _CONSULT note meant by 'NIST ASD lists none'. Not fixed here, and left for the coordinator because the file is outside this pass's scope: validation/scripts/check_atomic.py:144-146 computes the 133Ba+ quadratic clock shift with 171Yb+'s g_J = 2.002615 and says in a comment that 'no measured 133Ba+ g_J is cited anywhere in the tree', which is now false -- ba133.S12.g_J is Marx's 2.00249192(3), and using it changes that printed shift by 0.01 %
anchor.species.ba_g_factors.equation: all three Ba+ Lande g factors of the S and D levels are MEASURED and were missing or wrong. (1) g_J(6s 2S1/2) = 2.00249192(3), Marx et al. 1998, measured in a Penning trap on 138Ba+ and 135Ba+ (the companion AIP Conf. Proc. 457, 57 (1999) states both isotopes and a fractional accuracy of 2e-8); the absence of this one constant is what made 137Ba+ refuse to build, and it is stored in BOTH isotope tables because g_J is isotope-independent to the quoted 3e-8 -- an expectation the field states (Hanley et al., arXiv:2105.10352) and not a measurement on 133Ba+ or 137Ba+. Tagged extracted, not verified: Marx et al. 1998 could not be read (Springer redirects to an identity provider, no open-access copy, no abstract in OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar), and the digits are read verbatim in the full text of Arnold et al. 2020, which uses g_S = 2.002 491 92(3) twice and calls it known to 1e-8. It supersedes Hubrich, Knab, Knoll, Werth, Z. Phys. D 18, 113 (1991)'s 2.0024906 (quoted with uncertainty (12) in the Lindroth and Ynnerman 1993 abstract and as (11) elsewhere; neither read in Hubrich itself) by about 40x, and theory brackets it at 2.0024911(30) and 2.0024905(16). (2) g_J(5d 2D3/2) = 0.7993278(3), Knoell et al. 1996, measured; extracted, read in the Chin. Phys. Lett. 42, 063101 (2025) abstract because APS returns 403. (3) g_J(5d 2D5/2) = 1.20036739(24), Arnold et al. 2020, read DIRECTLY: it is the measured Zeeman-splitting ratio r = 0.59943681(12) times Marx's g_S, and the product reproduces the printed value to 2.1e-9, the rounding of the printed ratio. Chin. Phys. Lett. 42, 063101 (2025) misquotes that uncertainty as (14); the PRL says (24). 137Ba+ now BUILDS, and its ground-state clock qubit reproduces Section 9.13's closed form taylor_c2 = (g_J - g_I)^2 mu_B^2/(2 h^2 nu_0) = 488.81912 Hz/G^2 at nu_0 = 8 037 741 667.69 Hz to 1e-9 relative; PLAN.md prints NO field-independent point, frequency or curvature for 137Ba+, so nothing published pins that result and the qubit pair, cycling line, repumps and shelving line in ba137.species() are this package's declared choice

Lett. 50, 628 (1983) -- the MEASUREMENT, a cyclotron-versus-hyperfine-Zeeman frequency comparison, whose own printed value is 2.00226206(42) -- and [6] is Mohr, Taylor, Newell 2008, i.e. CODATA 2006, with which Shiga et al. re-reduce the digits. So the chain is measured 1983, re-reduced 2011, printed in Shiga 2011; the citation stands, the value is unchanged, and the source entry now names both papers and quotes the sentence. Wineland 1983's own text could not be read (APS 403); its title, authors, volume and pages 628-631 were confirmed through Crossref

conv.be9_linewidth.corrected_form: the spread is far outside every stated accuracy. The ASD value implies tau = 8.86 ns and an oscillator strength f = 0.498, the textbook ~0.5 for a Li-like ion, so ASD is self-consistent; 19.4/19.6 MHz need f = 0.543. No primary derivation of the ubiquitous trapped-ion '19.4 MHz / 8.2 ns' could be located (Langer's thesis states it uncited, Ozeri cites Andersen 1969, whose text was not obtainable). Same shape as the plan's own handling of 40Ca+'s 21.57/23.4 MHz
conv.be9_linewidth.equation: four readings spanning 9%: 17.97 MHz (NIST ASD A_ki 1.1292e8 and 1.1285e8 s^-1, accuracy grade AAA <= 0.3%, theory), 19.4 MHz (Monroe et al. 1995, which PLAN.md 4.2.1 quotes), 19.6 MHz (Ozeri Table I) and 19.64 MHz (Andersen, Jessen, Soerensen 1969, beam-foil). The record uses Monroe's 19.4 MHz, which is the reading every Section 9.13 anchor assumes (P_SE = 8.706e-4)

conv.be9_p32_hyperfine.corrected_form: TWO unresolved tensions. (1) the theory A is 1.7x LARGER than Bollinger et al. 1985's experimental bound |A(2P3/2)| < 0.6 MHz. (2) the theory B is NEGATIVE while Q(9Be) = +0.0529(4) b is positive, and for a single p3/2 valence electron sign(B) = sign(Q) (87Rb and 133Cs both obey it), so either the paper uses another B or Q convention or one of the two needs correcting. Neither affects any Section 9.13 anchor (a 1 MHz excited-state splitting against THz detunings), but the values must never be read as measured. The -1.03(3) / -2.30(9) MHz pair that circulates is these numbers with invented uncertainties
conv.be9_p32_hyperfine.equation: the record uses the THEORY values A = -1.026(3) MHz and B = -2.29940(3) MHz, tagged background; no measurement of either exists

conv.beam_phase_spectrum.corrected_form: before this the only laser-phase route was KEY_LASER_PHASE_TRAJECTORY on single-photon optical drives, so route (d) was unreachable for the phase-sensitive Raman geometries Section 6.3 names, and there was no per-beam or beat-note phase spectrum field at all. Kirchmair's 2e-3 per gate from incoherent carrier excitation and the Rabi-drift anchors (Kirchmair 1.4e-2, Harty 5e-4) are recorded as consistency anchors in validation/noise_closed_forms.py
conv.beam_phase_spectrum.equation: each beam gets its own realization of the SAME declared spectrum, so a Raman pair's beat note sees phi_2(t) - phi_1(t) with twice one beam's variance (measured 2.00 x sigma^2 over 120 seeds) and a co-propagating pair (one shared path, declared as one beam) sees none. The builder reads the sampled Delta phi(t) with the convention of key_beam_phase_rad (phi_2 - phi_1 for a Raman or light-shift pair, -phi_1 for a single beam) and multiplies the beat note by e^{-i Delta phi(t)} beside a single-photon drive's own laser phase, so constant trajectories reproduce the quasi-static build to 1e-12 and a common-mode path drift cancels (tests/test_m7_beam_phase_builder.py). The Baldwin form's (4 g^2/Delta^2) enters as its SQUARE, so halving the two-photon-to-detuning ratio drops eps by exactly 4
conv.beam_phase_spectrum.section: 6.3; 7.10 'the optical path difference between two Raman beams sets the beat-note phase'
conv.beam_phase_spectrum.symbol: NoiseModel.beam_phase_noise -> phi_j(t) per beam; eps = [int S_phi F] (4 g^2/Delta^2)^2

conv.beam_roles.corrected_form: the M2 inference counted every beam and refused a device with a detection beam beside its Raman pair
conv.beam_roles.equation: a beam within 2e-3 of the vacuum wavelength of a tabulated E1 line is resonant light (cooling, detection, repumping) and never a gate drive; the scheduler's drive inference and the readout's detection-beam selection both read this rule, so one device list carries every beam

conv.beat_phase_at_gate_start.corrected_form: the builder's per-pulse phase_mode='reset' resets at every SEGMENT of a multi-segment waveform (0.2-cycle jumps at the segment edges of the fixture's AM pulse open the loops: leakage 0.31); the M6 finding on the two-ion fixture: the same calibrated gate has fidelity 0.99995 at zeta = 0 or pi and 0.98903 at zeta = +-pi/2 (1.1 % leakage), so a gate started 21.27 beat cycles into a circuit under continuous tones is not the gate that was calibrated
conv.beat_phase_at_gate_start.equation: with HardwareChain.phase_continuous = False every leg of an entangling waveform carries the phase offset 2 pi mu_leg t_g (red and blue opposite, the spin phase unchanged, the virtual-Z frame intact), so the beat note starts at zero phase at the gate start as it did in the t = 0 calibration; with phase-continuous tones the start phase zeta = 2 pi mu t_g is part of the gate and the tilt sin^2[(4 Omega-bar/mu) sin zeta] is reported in the intrinsic budget
conv.beat_phase_at_gate_start.section: 7.10 Phase coherence between pulses; 4.4.1 Corrections beyond the leading order; 7.3

conv.benchmark_budget_composition.corrected_form: an estimate, never a bound, and not in either direction: coherent errors of one Clifford's pulses partly cancel, so single-qubit RB on the example device measures r about 0.8 of r_channel (2.00e-5 measured against 2.455e-5 composed), while the coherent crosstalk rotations of a GHZ circuit's five consecutive carrier pulses on the same neighbour add in amplitude, so its exact register infidelity 2.33e-3 exceeds 1 - F_gates = 1.40e-3. The earlier text said 'about half' here and '0.8' in anchor.m10.single_qubit_rb and the README, and it read the simultaneous-RB comparison as a second factor 2 in the other direction; that factor was a unit mismatch between the joint decay and a per-Clifford composition (conv.simultaneous_rb_units), and once the units match the composition predicts the simultaneous decay to 3 %, so simultaneous RB is NOT evidence of errors adding in amplitude. The Section 9.6 scales are bounds on the coherent errors, are summed over each kind's whole schedule entry (the crosstalk on ions outside the benchmarked set included, so r_intrinsic bounds a LARGER error than r_channel measures) and are reported beside the prediction, never summed into it
conv.benchmark_budget_composition.equation: beside every benchmark: (i) the Section 9.6 closed-form scales per unit, summed per native gate kind from Diagnostics.intrinsic_budget; (ii) the Section 6.8 channel of every native gate kind the benchmark compiled to, from ONE one-gate circuit through run(level='GATE_LOCAL') (the step's Choi matrix, its ideal the GateTarget unitary), reduced to the benchmarked qubits with the crosstalk neighbours traced out in |0> (E_keep(rho) = Tr_rest E(rho (x) |0><0|)) and converted to the average gate infidelity; (iii) the SPAM errors; composed as r_channel = sum n_kind eps_kind, F_gates = prod (1 - eps_kind)^n_kind, F(0) = prod_q [(1 - eps_prep)(1 - eps_D) + eps_prep eps_B], the GHZ readout factors (1 - sum eps_q) on the populations and prod (1 - 2 eps_q) on the contrast, the depolarizing heavy-output prediction (benchmarks/budget.py)
conv.benchmark_budget_composition.source: Magesan 2011 (additivity of average infidelities to first order); Wright et al. 2019 (the composite expected-fidelity product of Section 7.9); Sections 6.8 and 9.6
conv.benchmark_budget_composition.symbol: r_channel = sum_kinds n_kind eps_kind; F_gates = prod (1 - eps)

conv.bermudez_pauli_mapping.corrected_form: docs/limits.md filed the omission under 'open conventions the plan records rather than resolves', which the plan does not do -- it lists the mapping as a deliverable of Sections 6.8 and 4.4.7 -- and no ledger record carried the deviation at all; both are corrected, the limits page now naming it a deliverable the release omits
conv.bermudez_pauli_mapping.equation: Section 6.8 lists 'Bermudez et al.'s three-variant mapping of eps onto Pauli channels for fault-tolerance studies is provided as well [verified]' as a deliverable and Section 4.4.7 repeats it, but the plan transcribes NO formulas for the three variants (one occurrence of 'three-variant' in the whole plan, with no equations), and the first release therefore omits it. What noise/summary.py does provide of Section 6.8 is complete: the entanglement infidelity and the average gate infidelity of a simulated channel, its Pauli twirl (which IS a mapping of a simulated channel onto a Pauli channel, p_Q from the Pauli transfer-matrix diagonal) and the depolarizing rate of conv.depolarizing_normalization. Implementing the three variants needs the source itself, not the plan
conv.bermudez_pauli_mapping.source: Bermudez et al., PRX 7, 041061 (2017), the fault-tolerance section; noise/summary.py; docs/limits.md

conv.boundary_threshold_is_branch_scaled.corrected_form: M9a applied two thresholds: the boundary trip compared the BRANCH-relative top-level population against boundary_population_max while the margin check measured the populated range at boundary_population_max / branch_weight, MIXTURE-relative, so on a Fock branch of weight w the two differed by 1/w. Both now read the branch-scaled threshold min(boundary_population_max / w, 0.5): one threshold, one population (the mixture's, which is what the pulse moves), and a single state has w = 1 so no existing number moves. cap_for also now takes the run's boundary_population_max instead of a hard-coded 1e-6, so Section 5.5's per-test override for hot modes reaches the initial cap as well as the monitor (it used to give a loosened run an over-large cap and a tightened one a cap-raising retry). the third call site, calibration/surrogate.py's spot_check_space, took cap_for's own default until the M8 fixer gave it a tail keyword and passed opts.boundary_population_max from both surrogate_table call sites (None there resolves to SolverOptions().boundary_population_max, named explicitly), so all three now read one threshold
conv.boundary_threshold_is_branch_scaled.equation: Section 5.5's one threshold: the population in the top two Fock levels above 1e-6 'of the population the pulse moves' repeats the run with the cap raised
conv.boundary_threshold_is_branch_scaled.source: dynamics/engine.py run_pulses (the boundary trip and the margin check); run/space.py cap_for; run/gate_local.py step_space; calibration/surrogate.py spot_check_space

conv.branch_enumeration_refuses_an_empty.corrected_form: _truncated_weights used to fall back to [(argmax, 1.0)] when every probability sat below the cutoff, renormalizing a hard-truncated mixture to a pure state and reporting a dropped weight of zero; and when no PRODUCT reached the cutoff the enumeration returned an empty branch list, so the run evolved nothing and failed deep in the readout with 'the internal state has no population'. Both are reachable on a Doppler-only device: the 40Ca+ optical preset has two frozen modes at nbar = 10 whose joint ground-state weight is 8e-3, below the M7 tests' branch_weight_min = 1e-2
conv.branch_enumeration_refuses_an_empty.equation: the Fock sum keeps every branch of the diagonal initial mixture whose weight reaches SolverOptions.branch_weight_min and reports the dropped total; a cutoff that keeps NO state of some factor, or no product of the kept states, is refused with a RunError naming the cutoff and the most likely weight

conv.branching_deficit.corrected_form: an incomplete branching set used to be renormalized to unity over whatever channels happened to be tabulated, which put 100.0% of 40Ca+ P3/2's decay into the 393 nm cycling line and made its 5.9% of D-state leakage vanish. Level.untabulated_branching is a DEVIATION from Appendix E: an additive field with default () (the API-freeze test allows additions), used by 171Yb+'s 3D[3/2]1/2 for the 297.143 nm channel (audit item E2)
conv.branching_deficit.equation: every upper level reached by at least one E1 transition must have its tabulated branchings plus its declared Level.untabulated_branching sum to 1 within 1e-9, and sum_{b q'} |c|^2 then equals the TABULATED total, never an unconditional 1

conv.ca40_branching.corrected_form: PLAN.md 9.13 states 0.941 and 0.940. The table's previous P3/2 value 0.9412 came from Ozeri's f^-1 = 17, which PLAN.md:457 lists for 43Ca+ and NOT for 40Ca+ - a misattribution; its previous P1/2 value was Section 8.1's rounder '6% branch to D3/2', 6.8 % low, now kept as the contested cross-check ca40.P12.branching_to_D32_plan_8_1. Section 12 records 1:12, 1:16 and about 1:17.6 in different sources, a 30 % spread it calls a gap 'with no dedicated measurement'; the dedicated measurements DO exist: Ramm et al. 2013 give 0.93565(7)/0.06435(7) for P1/2 (Hettrich et al. 2015's independent 0.93572(25) agrees) and Gerritsma et al. 2008 the P3/2 split. Ramm's value was PROMOTED from cross-check to the branching the table uses on 2026-09-08 because it is what makes the 397 nm partial rate reproduce Hettrich's gamma_PS: 23.0526 x 0.93565 = 21.5691 MHz against his printed 21.57(8), where Section 8.1's 0.94 would give 21.6694 MHz, 1.2 sigma outside his bar (audit item E24)
conv.ca40_branching.equation: the table carries Ramm et al. 2013's measured 0.93565(7)/0.06435(7) for the P1/2 split (adopted 2026-09-08) and Gerritsma et al. 2008's measured 0.93469/0.0587/0.00661 for the P3/2 split into S1/2/D5/2/D3/2

conv.ca40_linewidth_reading.corrected_form: FLIPPED on 2026-09-08. The ca40 table used to read the plan's quoted 21.57 and 23.4 MHz as the TOTAL P1/2 and P3/2 rates; it now reads both as PARTIAL rates into S1/2 and takes the totals from MEASURED lifetimes instead (ca40.P12.lifetime_s = 6.904(26) ns, gamma/2pi = 23.0526 MHz, Hettrich; ca40.P32.lifetime_s = 6.639(42) ns, 23.9727 MHz, Meir et al. 2020). Three independent reasons, all agreeing: (1) Hettrich et al. 2015 print gamma_PS = 2 pi x 21.57(8) MHz explicitly as the partial P1/2 -> S1/2 rate, beside gamma_PD = 2 pi x 1.482(8) MHz and tau = 6.904(26) ns; (2) PLAN.md 9.13 (line 1385) itself reads both quoted linewidths as partial rates - '40Ca+ 397 nm with the quoted 21.57 MHz and 393 nm with 23.4 MHz read as partial rates: 2.045 e a0, 45.11 mW/cm^2 and 2.972 e a0, 50.25 mW/cm^2' - while asking that 'the species table must say which'; (3) as a TOTAL rate 21.57 MHz means tau(P1/2) = 7.379 ns, which no lifetime measurement supports (Hettrich 6.904(26) ns, Jin and Church 1993 7.098(20) ns). With Ramm et al. 2013's branching promoted to the one the table uses (conv.ca40_branching) the partial rate comes out at 21.5691 MHz, reproducing Hettrich's printed value to 4.0e-5, and the residual D3/2 partial rate 1.4834 MHz reproduces his gamma_PD inside its own 0.008 MHz bar - two identities the previous reading could not produce. Hettrich's printed <S1/2||d||P1/2> = 2.8928(43) e a0 is the same element in the normalization that omits the (2J+1) factor: sqrt(2) x 2.0455 = 2.8920, inside his uncertainty. The quoted linewidths stay in the table ONLY as contested cross-checks that nothing is built from (ca40.P12.linewidth_quoted_hz, ca40.P32.linewidth_quoted_hz). Every 40Ca+ rate in the tree moved: the movers are listed in anchor.ca40.gamma_dependent_repins, the 393 nm residual disagreement in anchor.ca40.p32_linewidth_readings
conv.ca40_linewidth_reading.equation: Hettrich's Table: <S1/2||d||P1/2> = 2.8928(43) e a0, tau(4p 2P1/2) = 6.904(26) ns, branching 0.93572(25), gamma_PS = 2 pi x 21.57(8) MHz and gamma_PD = 2 pi x 1.482(8) MHz, so the TOTAL is 23.05 MHz
conv.ca40_linewidth_reading.source: Hettrich et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 143003 (2015); Meir et al., Phys. Rev. A 101, 012509 (2020); PLAN.md 9.13 line 1385; qutip_trap/species/ca40.py

conv.calibration_cache.equation: tables are cached per device configuration and noise seed; a table whose device_hash differs from the device it is asked for is never returned, so a changed parameter invalidates the old configuration's tables and the new one has none until calibrate runs (run(table=None) builds the surrogate)
conv.calibration_cache.symbol: key = (Device.hash(), seed, surrogate, experiments, t0, digest(kwargs))

conv.calibration_graph.corrected_form: the second revision's unordered experiment list and its stark, crosstalk and field entries without an experiment. The first M8 build recorded the refusal in the report but left the refused experiment's entries as schedulable SEEDS (refuse()'s keys argument was dead and both call sites passed ()): with micromotion['beta[2]'] uncalibrated the mode-frequency fit refused and the mode frequencies silently stayed the derived seeds, which is exactly the fallback Section 7.3 forbids, and a Bell circuit still scheduled 15 pulses from that table
conv.calibration_graph.equation: calibrate(surrogate=False) runs the experiments in this order and never reorders; a downstream fit refuses to run while an entry group it reads is uncalibrated and its own entries (the groups PRODUCES names for it) become uncalibrated under its name, with the reason in CalibrationReport.refused; a group whose experiment was refused is not established even when it carries no entry to mark, and a group that is a seed because the caller did not ASK for its experiment stays a seed; seed entries (the derived values) are legitimate upstream inputs (the bootstrap)

conv.calibration_refusal_marks_its_entri.corrected_form: the refuse() helper's keys argument was dead and both call sites passed (), so a refusal was recorded in the report while the mode frequencies the fit could not establish stayed schedulable derived seeds and a Bell circuit still scheduled 15 pulses from that table; the module docstring, conv.calibration_graph and PLAN 7.3's last clause all said otherwise
conv.calibration_refusal_marks_its_entri.equation: PRODUCES maps each experiment to the entry groups it writes (field_scan -> field, micromotion_scan -> micromotion, sideband_spectroscopy -> modes, nbar, lamb_dicke, rabi_scan -> rabi, stark_scan -> stark, ramsey_frequency -> qubit_freq, crosstalk_scan -> crosstalk, crosstalk_phase, ms_scan -> ms, detection_histogram -> detection, heating_rate -> heating; crystal_image and parity_scan write none). A refused experiment marks exactly those entries uncalibrated under its own name, keeping their VALUES for the record, and the refusal cascades through UPSTREAM: an uncalibrated field refuses the micromotion, mode, Rabi, Stark and Ramsey-frequency fits in turn, and the uncalibrated Rabi entry then makes schedule() raise ScheduleError. An entry that is a seed because the caller did not ASK for its experiment stays a seed (calibrate(experiments=...) and the Section 7.5 bootstrap). A group whose producer was refused is treated as unestablished even when it holds no entry to mark, which no path in the present graph reaches but which keeps the rule true if micromotion_scan ever gains an upstream
conv.calibration_refusal_marks_its_entri.section: 7.3; 7.5 Bootstrap, fits and failure; 9.17 Calibration dependency graph

conv.closure_amplitude_at_the_fitted_off.corrected_form: the scan snapped the parabola's minimum to the nearest SCANNED offset before fitting the amplitude while the table applied the continuous one: on the two-ion fixture, whose offsets are (-2, 0, +2) kHz and whose fitted minimum is a couple of hundred hertz, the closure scale was measured at 0 Hz and applied at the fitted offset
conv.closure_amplitude_at_the_fitted_off.equation: the leakage parabola over the scanned detuning offsets gives a CONTINUOUS closure offset, and the table applies it, so the cos(2 chi_1 s^2) amplitude fit is run at that offset: when the scanned grid does not already carry it, one extra amplitude scan is measured there and closure_offset_used_hz is the fitted offset, which the table then applies together with the scale

conv.cnot_template_sign.corrected_form: the plan makes s the pair's physical sign 'from the simulator's own mode structure and detuning'; here the scheduler realizes either sign of the native MS from the waveform's signed chi by a pi on the second ion's tones (M4, Section 4.4.2), so the compiler's s is a free convention (default +1) and the physical sign never reaches the compiler

conv.collapse_op_rate_units.corrected_form: all six construction sites divided by 2 pi (dynamics/channels.py x5 through hz_from_rad_s and an explicit /TWO_PI, noise/scattering.py x1), reporting a number 6.28 times small: Section 5.6's 2 pi rule converts ANGULAR FREQUENCIES, not rates. The audit offered a rename to rate_per_s as an alternative, but Appendix E (PLAN.md:2561) declares rate_hz and tests/test_api_freeze.py enforces it, so the PLAN wins and only the value is corrected - a rate in Hz IS a rate in s^-1, and what was wrong was treating the value as an angular frequency, not the label. The field is reporting-only (nothing in the engine, the run or the noise layer reads it), so no dynamics change follows

conv.collision_outcomes.corrected_form: the scale gives 7.4e4 quanta of a 1 MHz mode for H2 at 300 K on 171Yb+, ABOVE Section 6.7's parenthetical 'tens to thousands' (which is reached at a few MHz for a lighter ion or a heavier gas ratio); the formula the plan specifies is implemented rather than tuned to the parenthetical. Two limitations are declared in Diagnostics.approximations rather than hidden: a kick landing after the preparation discards the shot instead of adding its nbar to the already-evolved sample (the dynamical samples are propagated before the shot loop), and a reorder permutes RunState.order and discards the shot without re-deriving b_{i,m}, eta_{i,m} or the pair sign s of Section 7.7 for the shots that follow
conv.collision_outcomes.equation: <E_kick> = k_B T (m_gas/m_ion) x kick_scale_multiplier with the partial-pressure-weighted gas mass, drawn from an exponential (maximum entropy at fixed mean) or a Maxwell chi^2_3 of the same mean; <delta nbar> = <E_kick>/(hbar omega_m) on the mode it heats most (the softest). The plan states the scale, not its O(1) coefficient (the elastic head-on transfer fraction is 4 m_g/m_i and the momentum-kick estimate 3 m_g k_B T/(2 m_i), both of this order), so the coefficient is 1 and kick_scale_multiplier is the device's handle

conv.comb_explicit_folded_partition.corrected_form: M2's stark4_hz summed every l with no exclusion, so every tone tones() kept explicit was simultaneously inside the static shift: 5510.08 Hz against 1152.74 Hz at the Lee point, a factor 4.78 of double-counted shift. aom_offset_hz was absent from the entire fourth-order path, so the two grids differed by Delta_nu_M. The ledger's anchor.m2.comb_numbers claim 'the rest folded into the fourth-order shift' is now true (M2 audit E7)
conv.comb_explicit_folded_partition.equation: CombSpec.explicit_orders(resonance_hz, gate_time_s) is the ONE definition of the explicit set; tones() emits exactly those orders and comb_factor/stark4_hz exclude exactly those from the static l-sum, so the two sets partition the comb's beat notes. Both paths now place beat notes on the one grid l nu_rep + Delta_nu_M (CombSpec.beat_notes_hz), so a two-comb drive's tone set and Stark sum share it. At 80 MHz and a 100 us gate the 10/t_g cut is 100 kHz, far inside the tooth gap: the explicit set is {j_res} at both 10/t_g and 20/t_g, so the 9.17 regression's gate-phase change is exactly 0 (< 1e-4 rad). With a window widened until the l = j +- 1 neighbours cross, the folded shift alone moves by more than 1 Hz while the TOTAL (folded plus the retained off-resonant tones' own second-order shift) is invariant, which is the plan's convergence test with content

conv.depolarizing_normalization.corrected_form: Trout 2018's p/3 and p/15 are the same weights under a different name for the parameter, not a different channel; Qiskit's lambda is NOT that p, and passing a published p to Qiskit as a lambda understates the rate by 4^n/(4^n - 1), 33 % on one qubit and 6.7 % on two. Kept separate from conv.rb_error_rate, whose p is a decay BASE, and from conv.gate_fidelity_measure, whose F_K is a unitary overlap: this row is a channel RATE
conv.depolarizing_normalization.equation: the depolarizing channel is written with the UNIFORM weight eps/(4^n - 1) on each of the 4^n - 1 non-identity Paulis, in which eps is exactly the entanglement infidelity, so the rate the simulator reports IS the entanglement infidelity and the average gate infidelity is d/(d + 1) eps, (2/3) eps at n = 1 and (4/5) eps at n = 2; as Kraus operators that is sqrt(1 - eps) 1 together with sqrt(eps/3) X, Y, Z on one qubit or sqrt(eps/15) P over the fifteen non-identity two-qubit Paulis, and sum_K K^dag K = 1 to 1e-12 for every eps in [0, 1] (noise/summary.py depolarizing_kraus, whose Choi state depolarizing_choi is built from); the parameter Qiskit's depolarizing_error takes is the mixing weight of the maximally mixed state, lambda = eps 4^n/(4^n - 1), so Chen et al.'s Forte medians 2.0e-4 (single-qubit) and 46.4e-4 (two-qubit, direct RB) enter Qiskit as 2.67e-4 and 49.5e-4 (noise/summary.py qiskit_depolarizing_lambda)

conv.drop_test_debye_waller_spread.corrected_form: a strengthening of Section 5.2's rule, not a deviation from it. The plan's pair reads the Section 4.4.3 LOOP integrals only, so a pulse that closes a mode's loop exactly leaves the pair at ~1e-33 however strongly the mode couples, and dropping the mode removes its exact Debye-Waller factor e^{-eta^2/2} L_n(eta^2) from every carrier pulse - which is the very thing Section 5.2 keeps the FROZEN class for ('samples n_m once per shot and multiplies Omega_i by the exact Debye-Waller factor of that Fock state'). The MEAN of the factor is absorbed by the calibration, because the spot check and the run drop the same mode and Section 4.4.7's s^2 rescaling takes the mode-independent part; the shot-to-shot SPREAD is not. To leading order in eta the factor is 1 - eta^2 (n + 1/2), so over a thermal state (Var n = nbar(nbar + 1)) the rotation angle's standard deviation is eta^2 sqrt(nbar (nbar + 1)). Measured on the three-ion GHZ fixture, whose tilt mode has eta = 0.0809 and a loop contribution of 3.5e-33: 1.500e-3 rad at nbar = 0.05, 9.256e-3 at nbar = 1 and 6.864e-2 at nbar = 10, i.e. sin^2(delta theta/2) = 5.6e-7, 2.1e-5 and 1.2e-3 of infidelity on a pi pulse. The threshold 3e-4 rad is matched to the 1e-6 of the alpha^2 row ((3e-4/2)^2 = 2.3e-8 of infidelity, comfortably inside it). Consequence for the fixtures: the three-ion tilt mode (mode 4), which M6 had just made genuinely dropped, is FROZEN again - correctly, since its Debye-Waller spread is 1.5e-3 rad, five times the threshold - while a mode with eta = 0.008 at nbar = 0.05 (spread 1.5e-5 rad) and the plan's own 9.17 row (|alpha|^2(2n+1) = 1e-7, |chi| = 1e-5 at eta = 1e-3) stay dropped. The summed spread of the modes that ARE dropped is reported beside the loop-pair bound as SpaceSelection.dropped_dw_spread_rad and in the selection notes, so a Section 9.8 row 3 comparison can add it
conv.drop_test_debye_waller_spread.equation: a mode is dropped when |alpha_m(tau)|^2 (2 nbar_m + 1) < 1e-6 AND |chi_m(tau)| < 1e-4 AND max_i eta_{i,m}^2 sqrt(nbar_m (nbar_m + 1)) < 3e-4 rad; otherwise, below the freeze pair, it is frozen
conv.drop_test_debye_waller_spread.source: run/space.py DW_SPREAD_DROP_MAX, ModeContribution.dw_spread_rad, classify; tests/test_m6_space_classes.py; tests/test_run_circuits.py

conv.dropped_mode_has_no_dynamics.corrected_form: the M6 code intersected the drop test with `coupled`, returning frozen for any coupled mode below the drop pair. Since a contribution only ever exists for a coupled mode, the `dropped` return was DEAD and the effective rule was `eta = 0 -> dropped`: Diagnostics.dropped_contribution was identically (0.0, 0.0), the three-ion GHZ tilt mode (|alpha|^2 (2n+1) = 3.5e-33, chi = 0.0) was reported frozen, and every such mode still cost a Fock branch and a Debye-Waller factor of 1 - O(1e-33). A second defect sat behind it: both frozen and dropped modes went into HilbertSpace.frozen, whose members all receive the exact Debye-Waller factor and a Fock branch, so `dropped` had no dynamical meaning at all
conv.dropped_mode_has_no_dynamics.equation: the class follows the contribution pair alone - dropped when |alpha_m|^2 (2 n_m + 1) < 1e-6 AND |chi_m| < 1e-4, whatever couples to the mode; the coupling test (|eta| > 1e-12 for some drive) decides only the modes NO entangling gate touches (no contribution): frozen when a carrier pulse couples to them, dropped when nothing does. A dropped mode has no tensor factor (like a frozen one) and additionally no Debye-Waller factor and no Fock branch, so it evolves freely and is not modelled at all, which is what makes SpaceSelection.dropped_contribution the loss nothing absorbs
conv.dropped_mode_has_no_dynamics.source: PLAN.md Section 5.2 line 822; qutip_trap/run/space.py, qutip_trap/hilbert/space.py, qutip_trap/dynamics/hamiltonian.py, qutip_trap/run/job.py
