conv.e2_ac_stark_shift.equation: the ac Stark shift of a driven |S, m>-|D, m'> component by the nine off-resonant components inside the Zeeman span, second order in the same Omega(m, m') table: Delta(m, m') = 2 pi[(E_D(m0') - E_S(m0)) - (E_D(m') - E_S(m))] is a pure Zeeman offset, a component shifts its lower level by +|Omega|^2/(4 Delta) and its upper by -|Omega|^2/(4 Delta), and the driven component is excluded because the Rabi dynamics treats it exactly

conv.e2_decay_weights.corrected_form: lambda_3j was referenced only by the drive and by tests; no decay operator used it and no lumped sqrt(A) sigma_- existed either (shelf decay appears only as readout/presets.py's shelf_lifetime_s inside the M5 Markov chain). quadrupole_collapse_operators is deliberately NOT wired into any engine: the noise layer of Section 4.5.7 chooses between it and the plan's own escape hatch, 'a lumped sqrt(A) sigma_- is adequate at A ~ 0.86 s^-1 for microsecond gates' (audit item E9, defect B8)
conv.e2_decay_weights.equation: the E2 collapse operators are sqrt(A w(m, m')) |S, m><D, m'| with the same A that fixed the Rabi frequency; the raw 3-j squares sum to 1/6 at every m' (so the normalization is a multiplication by 6) and the weights sum to 1 over m at fixed m', giving sum_m A w = A
conv.e2_decay_weights.section: 4.5.7 Dissipation, dephasing and crosstalk; 9.14 3-j table and mask

conv.effective_sample_size.corrected_form: the M6 code added the within-sample binomial term mean[p_s(1 - p_s)/M_s]/S on top of np.var(ps, ddof=1)/S, which already contains it: the error bars were up to sqrt(2) too large whenever more than one sample was drawn (measured on 200 replicates of i.i.d. Bernoulli shots: n_eff/shots = 0.547 at S = 8, 0.510 at S = 64, 0.640 at S = 2, where 1.0 is correct). The between-only ANOVA component would be s^2_total - mean[p_s(1 - p_s)/M_s], and adding the within term back to THAT returns s^2_total/S exactly
conv.effective_sample_size.equation: with S samples of M_s shots and per-sample frequencies p_s, the pooled estimate is p_hat = sum M_s p_s / sum M_s and Var(p_hat) = Var(p_s)/S, where Var(p_s) = sigma^2_between + p(1 - p)/M is the TOTAL per-sample variance; Var(p_s) is estimated by the shot-count-weighted sample variance sum_s M_s (p_s - p_hat)^2 / [(S - 1) sum_s M_s], which reduces to var(p_s, ddof=1)/S for equal M_s, and n_eff = p(1 - p)/Var(p_hat), the minimum over the bitstrings seen, capped at the shot count

conv.emission_collapse_operators.corrected_form: never one operator per excited sublevel (Berkeland's Eq. 12 as printed), never a coherent sum over recoil classes (Joshi Eq. A.3); QuTiP's auto-tidyup zeroes elements below 1e-12, so the rate prefactor must multiply the 1e-29 C m elements before the Qobj is built (M3a implementation finding)
conv.emission_collapse_operators.equation: one collapse operator per fine-structure decay line (lower, upper) and emitted polarization index q, the lower<-upper block of the dipole operator in C m times sqrt(g_LU); sum_q C_q^dag C_q = Gamma_{U->L} P_U by the Wigner-Eckart sum rule (residual 1e-16 in the tests); the excited-to-ground feeding term carries the product of two matrix elements that transfers excited coherence into ground coherence; with a mode each C_q is resolved over emission directions as C_q (x) D(-i eta_em u), entered INCOHERENTLY over directions; decay into excluded levels follows the leak policy include / sink / renormalize

conv.enr_factor_dims.corrected_form: until 2026-09-08 identity(), number(), annihilation(), embed() and the joint states of an ENR space came back labelled [..., n_exc + 1, n_exc + 1] while the factorized drive term (FactorizedOperator, built on HilbertSpace.dims) said [..., C(M+N_exc,N_exc)], so the first ENR run through run() (the M9 fixer's end-to-end test, 2026-09-08) failed inside QobjEvo with 'has dims [[2, 2, 11, 13, 6], ...] but previous terms had dims [[2, 2, 11, 13, 3, 3], ...]' - after building a 37752-dimensional space that took 20 GB, because an explicit JOINT_EXACT above the Section 11.5 guards was not refused (conv.space_declaration_before_allocation). The unit tests of the ENR construction (tests/test_scaling_modes.py) never combined an ENR motional term with a drive term in one QobjEvo, which is why the mismatch survived M9a and M9b
conv.enr_factor_dims.equation: every joint operator and state an ENR space hands out is relabelled with the space's own dims, in which the excitation-number-restricted group is ONE tensor factor of dimension C(M + N_exc, N_exc); QuTiP's enr_identity / enr_destroy / enr_fock / enr_thermal_dm label the group by its per-mode dims (n_exc + 1 each, product C(M+N_exc,N_exc) only by accident of small cases), and a QobjEvo refuses to combine terms whose dims differ. Data is shared, not copied. Marginals of the group remain index sums over the ENR basis (never ptrace)
conv.enr_factor_dims.section: 5.1.1 (the ENR option, 'dimensions from shape'); 13 (ENR row); 11.3 item 1
conv.enr_factor_dims.source: qutip_trap/hilbert/space.py (with_space_dims, applied by identity, embed, embed_many, product_state); tests/test_m9_scaling.py::test_every_joint_operator_and_state_of_an_enr_space_carries_the_spaces_dims
conv.enr_factor_dims.symbol: HilbertSpace.dims = [ions..., resolved d_m..., C(M + N_exc, N_exc)]

conv.entangling_angle.corrected_form: Choi's printed factor 2 holds only for proportional envelopes; Blumel's kernel with target pi/8 must be doubled; Roos's and Kirchmair's pi/8 comes from S without the 1/2 and must not be rescaled
conv.entangling_angle.equation: chi_ij = sum_m eta_im eta_jm int int [Omega_i(t) Omega_j(t') + Omega_j(t) Omega_i(t')] ... with the pair sum over i < j; maximally entangling at chi = pi/4; XX(chi) = exp(-i chi sigma_x sigma_x)

conv.entangling_scan_beliefs.corrected_form: full_calibration built both keyword arguments and neither reached anything: ms_scan called exact_gate_check with an explicit argument list that omitted qubit_shifts_hz, parity_after_analysis_pulse had no such parameter at all, and mode_frequencies_hz had no consumer on that path - both landed in **kw and were dropped. The entangling scans were therefore the only experiments of the whole calibration running with a PERFECT qubit frame, and the amplitude scan rigidly shifted and rescaled the surrogate's derived-mode solution, which is equivalent for one symmetric mode but not for a multi-segment AM pulse whose segment amplitudes depend on the mode spacing
conv.entangling_scan_beliefs.equation: the entangling scans run in the frame the machine programs (qubit_shifts_hz = nu_true - table.qubit_freq per ion, forwarded to exact_gate_check and to parity_after_analysis_pulse's engine) and build their GateModes at the frequencies the table believes (mode_frequencies_hz), so the spin-phase corrections they write carry the frame error run() will apply. Before the amplitude scan the pair's waveform is RE-SOLVED at the calibrated mode frequencies (surrogate_waveform(mode_frequencies_hz=...), keeping the surrogate's duration, beat-note placement rule and phase entries), which is PLAN 7.5 item 4's 'the closure amplitude the pulse solver predicts at the calibrated mode frequencies'; the scan then refines the closure offset and the amplitude. A supplied GateModes together with mode_frequencies_hz is refused rather than one of them discarded
conv.entangling_scan_beliefs.source: calibration/experiments.py (the entangling block, _resolved_at_calibrated_modes); experiments/entangling.py _entangling_setup, _frame_shifts; calibration/entangling.py parity_after_analysis_pulse; tests/test_m8_calibration_fixes.py

conv.entangling_sign.corrected_form: Waveform.chi_m is SIGNED and, after the exact spot check, carries the measured angle; a solver landing on -pi/4 is not a failure
conv.entangling_sign.equation: a pulse applies exp(+i chi sigma sigma) with chi = sum_m chi_m signed by the detuning side (tones inside the sidebands give chi > 0); XX(chi) = exp(-i chi sigma sigma), so a positive chi is played with a pi on the second ion's tones (GPi(phi + pi) = -GPi(phi)) and a partial angle rescales every amplitude by sqrt((theta/2)/|chi|)

conv.epsilon_d_split.corrected_form: the module's own P_Rayleigh comes from the elastic amplitude sum and does NOT contain the D-level Raman channel (the D-level finals are counted in leakage_per_s and hence in eps_S), so Section 4.5.5's 'overstating the elastic rate by f P_total' is reported as the amount by which OZERI'S CLOSED FORM exceeds this one (ozeri_rayleigh_overstatement), not as a correction subtracted from it - subtracting it would clamp at zero and hide the fact that the two P_Rayleigh definitions differ
conv.epsilon_d_split.equation: f is DERIVED from the species' tabulated D-level branchings, weighted by the 1/Delta_e^2 excitation of the reachable excited levels, never typed in; for 171Yb+ at 355 nm it is 9.69e-3, so eps_D sits two decades below eps_S
conv.epsilon_d_split.source: M7 audit E-16 (light/scattering.d_level_branching / epsilon_s_and_d, validation/noise_closed_forms.epsilon_d_from_p_total; tests/test_m7_closed_forms.py). The Table II power regression itself is M0a's validation/ozeri_closed_forms.py and tests/test_m0a_ozeri_closed_forms.py, reused rather than duplicated
conv.epsilon_d_split.symbol: eps_D = f P_total, reported beside eps_S = P_Raman

conv.factorized_isequal_is_structural.corrected_form: M9b compared a.scale * A_f against b.scale * B_f factor by factor, which multiplies the scale in once PER FACTOR: 2 (X (x) Y) and 1 ((2X) (x) (2Y)) differ by a factor two and passed that test, and a false 'equal' merges two distinct drive terms in QobjEvo.compress. The comparison is now the exact structural one above, over the union of the two factor sets with an omitted factor read as the identity, so a 'no' is a proof; the two-probe-vector fallback remains only for a factorized operator against another data type, where the exact answer would need one of the two assembled
conv.factorized_isequal_is_structural.equation: scale_a (x)_f A_f == scale_b (x)_f B_f iff A_f = c_f B_f for every factor f with scale_a prod_f c_f = scale_b

conv.filter_function_machinery.corrected_form: XY4, XY8, KDD, CDD and (XY)^N compose per-pulse blocks with Lambda^{(l-1)} (never the scalar (-1)^l), return to identity to 1e-12 and match brute-force propagation to 1e-8 with a second-order rule (the check script's mpmath quadrature reaches 4e-10); no source validates them [background]
conv.filter_function_machinery.equation: per segment M_l = e^{i omega t_{l-1}}[I_c 1 + (I_1 - I_c) n n^T + I_s [n]_x] with the elementary integrals of cos, sin and 1 against e^{i omega s} (removable poles at omega = +-Omega_l); R^P(theta) = cos theta 1 + (1 - cos theta) n n^T + sin theta [n]_x is the adjoint of U^dag; the gated option switches the noise off during pulses and reproduces Biercuk's (-1)^{n+1} form to 1e-15 at both parities; the ungated (physical) finite-pulse form keeps a first-order transverse term at odd n (F ~ omega^2)
conv.filter_function_machinery.section: 6.9; 13 'Filter-function normalization stack', 'Toggling-frame control matrix', 'Dynamical-decoupling filter function'

conv.filter_function_normalization.corrected_form: mixing a 1/(2 pi) prefactor with a one-sided integral is a factor 2 in chi; dropping the explicit 1/omega^2 is a factor omega^2; a 1/omega^4 weight appears nowhere
conv.filter_function_normalization.equation: four pieces pinned together: S two-sided in angular frequency with the e^{-i omega t} kernel (per rad/s); prefactor 1/(2 pi) two-sided or 1/pi one-sided; weight 1/omega^2; an explicit -i omega inside R_ij(omega) = -i omega int_0^tau dt R_ij(t) e^{+i omega t}, so only (F = omega^2 |FT[R]|^2, 1/omega^2) and (F = |FT[R]|^2, omega^0) are self-consistent

conv.filter_function_omega_min_fallback.corrected_form: the third fallback is the simulator's invention, not the plan's 2 pi/T_total: it exists because a Gaussian or OU band starts at dc and carries no infrared edge of its own, and it is always reported beside d ln chi/d ln omega_min so a divergence cannot pass unnoticed (Section 12's 'no source supplies an infrared cutoff, so omega_min is the simulator's choice')
conv.filter_function_omega_min_fallback.equation: the cutoff is, in order: the caller's omega_min_rad_s; the spectrum's own lowest positive tabulated frequency when its band starts above zero (the device declared it); 2 pi/experiment_duration_s (Appendix E and Section 12's rule); else three decades below the sequence, 2 pi/(1000 tau)
conv.filter_function_omega_min_fallback.symbol: omega_min = 2 pi/(1000 tau) when neither the band nor an experiment duration sets it

conv.floquet_branch_normalization.corrected_form: House's Eq. 7 sign; unitarity of Gamma^-1(0) as a check; the paper-literal inverted C_-2 step (the Floquet-Lyapunov modes themselves are not built in M1)
conv.floquet_branch_normalization.equation: omega_j = beta_j Omega/2 on the principal branch; companion matrix F = [[0, 1], [-(A - 2Q cos 2tau), 0]] with U(0) = 1 and monodromy at tau = pi; |tr M| < 2 for stability

conv.floquet_phase_origin.corrected_form: the RMP's quantum section, Wineland's trajectory and the plan's second revision use [1 + (q/2) cos], i nu (1 - q): the same physics half an rf period later
conv.floquet_phase_origin.equation: u_dot(0) = i nu (1 + q) at u(0) = 1 in the adopted sign; C0 = 1 + 3q^2/16 even in q
conv.floquet_phase_origin.section: 13 Floquet function and rf phase origin; 4.1.1
conv.floquet_phase_origin.symbol: u(t) ~ e^{i nu t}[1 - (q/2) cos omega_rf t]

conv.fm_closure_guard.corrected_form: measured on eta = {a: (0.08, 0), b: (0.07, 0.09)}: |alpha_{b,1}| fell from 0.0296 (eps_ent = 8.8e-4) to 6e-14 and every |alpha| is now below 1e-12; the same fix needed the least-squares gradient test disabled (gtol=None), since J^T r goes tiny long before the residual does and stopped the descent at |alpha| ~ 1e-6. On a real crystal the node eta is 1e-17 rather than an exact zero, which is why the defect was invisible outside a synthetic mode table
conv.fm_closure_guard.equation: the FM family holds Omega constant and equal on both ions, so alpha_{i,m} ~ eta_{i,m} and closing one ion closes the other; the solver drove the residual from ion a alone and SKIPPED every mode with eta_a = 0 exactly, leaving ion b's loop open where b couples and a sits at a node. The residual is now driven from whichever gate ion couples more strongly and a row is skipped only when NEITHER couples
conv.fm_closure_guard.symbol: alpha_{a,m}(tau) = 0 for the gate ions, plural

conv.fock_sum_branches.corrected_form: a joint-space mesolve at dimension 400 would need a Liouvillian of 1.6e5 x 1.6e5 with about 6e7 non-zeros per drive operator; the trajectory path for Lindblad channels is M7/M9b
conv.fock_sum_branches.equation: the prepared state is diagonal in the computational and Fock bases (pumped populations per ion, thermal weights per carried mode, the frozen modes' Fock states included), so its branches are evolved as pure states with sesolve and recombined with their weights, exact up to the branches below SolverOptions.branch_weight_min (1e-6) whose total weight is reported and renormalized; Diagnostics.trajectories counts the branches
conv.fock_sum_branches.source: qutip_trap/run/job.py; PLAN.md Section 5.3 (mesolve is a reference path below dimension ~100)

conv.four_ion_gate_local_fixture.corrected_form: M9a shipped the three-ion case only and README.md claimed both. The four-ion case is the GHZ4 circuit (h + three cnots, four gates) on check_circuits.py's four-ion chain, at freeze_chi_max_rad = 0.3 so that BOTH levels resolve the same single mode: measured |chi| per Moelmer-Soerensen step on that circuit is mode 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 = 0.038 / 0.1078 / 0.1255 / 0.8056 rad for the (0,1) and (2,3) gates and 0.1251 / 0.1123 / 0.0414 / 0.8395 for the (1,2) gate, so 0.3 rad separates the gate mode (mode 7) from the other three at every step. JOINT_EXACT then runs at dimension 192 (4 ions x d_m = 12) and each gate-local space is 48. check_circuits.py's hand-built space (modes 6 and 7 at d_m = 12, dimension 2304), which the audit and the fix brief both suggested, is NOT usable for the comparison: it is not what the criterion selects for either level, GATE_LOCAL's per-step step_space would resolve modes it freezes at |chi| = 0.11 to 0.13 rad (a 14 to 16 % error on a pi/4 angle, which discrepancy_bound does not cover), and no threshold selects exactly {6, 7} at both levels because mode 6 falls to 0.0414 on the (1,2) gate while mode 4 rises to 0.1251 there. At the default 0.05 rad all four x modes are resolved and the joint space is 139968, far above the Section 11.5 guard, so JOINT_EXACT cannot run at all - which is itself the reason Section 5.4 puts four-ion chains in GATE_LOCAL
conv.four_ion_gate_local_fixture.equation: Section 9.8 row 1: three- AND four-ion circuits of 3 to 5 gates at the resolved-mode sets of Section 9.6 agree in their final probabilities within the residual-displacement bound GATE_LOCAL reports

conv.frequencies.corrected_form: papers quote gamma = 2 pi x 19.6 MHz, gamma/2pi = 60 MHz and 19.7 MHz for gamma/2pi interchangeably; the two are distinct types at the public boundary (qutip_trap.units.Hz and RadPerS with rad_s_from_hz / hz_from_rad_s), while the package's internal signatures and dataclass fields carry the unit in the NAME (_hz, _rad_s, _hz_per_g, _per_s) as plain floats rather than as NewTypes - the M0 audit of 2026-09-07 asked for the NewTypes at every frequency boundary with a census test, and the deviation is recorded instead: an AST census on that date found 149 frequency-like parameter and field names in qutip_trap without a unit suffix over 56 distinct names (gamma, omega, mu, rates, omega_f, detuning, ...), every one a closed-form or internal argument whose docstring states its unit, so a suffix census would need an allow-list of that size and the NewType retyping would touch every module; the run-time rule that holds is the boundary conversion with an explicit 2 pi, checked by the constants and closed-form tests
conv.frequencies.equation: internal frequencies angular in rad/s; public API in Hz, converted at the boundary with an explicit 2 pi

conv.frozen_spectator_fallback_draw_is_p.corrected_form: run() does not sample: it enumerates the frozen modes' Fock states as weighted branches, a deterministic quadrature over the same thermal distribution and strictly better than sampling, and passes each branch's tuple to run_pulses. The draw inside run_pulses is the fallback for a direct caller, which has no shot index at all - one call is one evolution - so it is keyed per SAMPLE, not per shot as Section 3.4's (sample, trajectory, shot, ion, channel) key would suggest, and it now says so in an engine note whenever it fires
conv.frozen_spectator_fallback_draw_is_p.equation: Section 5.2: spectators='frozen' samples n_m once per shot from the mode's thermal distribution and multiplies Omega by the exact Debye-Waller factor of that Fock state
conv.frozen_spectator_fallback_draw_is_p.symbol: the frozen-spectator Fock draw in run_pulses

conv.frozen_spectator_shot_sample.corrected_form: never the ensemble-mean factor exp[-eta^2(nbar + 1/2)] inside one shot (Section 13, Debye-Waller statistics)
conv.frozen_spectator_shot_sample.equation: a frozen mode's Fock state comes from the sample key frozen_n[m] or, absent that, from a thermal draw at the state's nbar with the keyed stream (sample, 0, 0, 0, 'frozen_n[m]'); it multiplies every drive on the shot by e^{-eta^2/2} L_n(eta^2) and is recorded in the engine report

conv.gate_fidelity_measure.corrected_form: Low, Yoder and Chuang's F = ||U V^dag|| is identically 1 for a qubit under its own Eq. 2 norm and Brown, Harrow and Chuang's 1 - ||V^dag U|| identically 0 for unitaries; both are replaced by F_K. The row had no ledger record of its own although the M10 modules cite it by name, which Section 14.5's one-record-per-quantity rule asks for
conv.gate_fidelity_measure.equation: for a single-qubit UNITARY error the internal measure is F_K = (1/4)|Tr(U_id^dag U)|^2, the normalization the composite-pulse library and the Section 6.9 filter functions are built to and the one that floors at 1/2 for a fully wrong qubit gate; F_C = |Tr(U_id^dag U)|/2 = sqrt(F_K) and F_avg = (2 F_C^2 + 1)/3 = (2 F_K + 1)/3 are exposed as conversions, so 1 - F_K = 2(1 - F_C) and 1 - F_avg = (4/3)(1 - F_C) at leading order, and every ingested c-coefficient is tagged with the measure it was quoted in (control/composite.py fidelity_k and the measure argument of the error models); at small spectral-norm distance E between unitaries 1 - F_C ~ E^2/2 while 1 - F_K ~ E^2, so the plan's 'converted as E^2/2' is the F_C form. The plan's row says to keep this separate from the RB row and the depolarizing row, and it is separate: conv.rb_error_rate converts a decay BASE p, conv.depolarizing_normalization a channel RATE eps, this row a unitary OVERLAP
conv.gate_fidelity_measure.source: Kabytayev et al. 2014 Sec. II B; Cummins et al. 2003 Eq. 7; Merrill and Brown Eqs. 10-11; control/composite.py

conv.gate_local_discrepancy_has_no_fudge.corrected_form: the Bell comparison asserted < discrepancy_bound + dropped_branch_weight + 1e-6 and the three-ion one < discrepancy_bound + 1e-5. The dropped_branch_weight term is the weight of the initial-mixture branches JOINT_EXACT did not evolve while GATE_LOCAL carried the whole register, and is licensed; the bare 1e-6 and 1e-5 were unrecorded slack and are removed, so both comparisons now hold to discrepancy_bound + dropped_branch_weight exactly as the row states
conv.gate_local_discrepancy_has_no_fudge.equation: Section 9.8 row 1: final probabilities agree within the residual-displacement bound GATE_LOCAL reports; disagreement above it fails

conv.gate_local_residual_bound_pre_step.corrected_form: M9a evaluated 2 nbar_m + 1 at the occupation the step's own output left, so the reported bound depended on the gate's heating: conservative for a heating gate, an under-estimate for a cooling one, and in neither case reproducible from the step's inputs. It now reads the occupation the tracked motional model had when the step started
conv.gate_local_residual_bound_pre_step.equation: Section 9.8: the residual-displacement bound sum_m |alpha_m|^2 (2 nbar_m + 1) that GATE_LOCAL reports and the JOINT_EXACT comparison is held to

conv.gate_local_workers_are_the_ones_use.corrected_form: M9a reported worker_count(options) for every GATE_LOCAL run whether or not anything ran in parallel: the tomography runs its inputs in-process whenever the local space has no resolved mode (every carrier step), a cache hit runs nothing at all, and the walk iterates its quasi-static samples serially. The number reported is now the largest count any step actually used (the tomography's map, or the trajectories inside one engine run). conv.ghz_parity_bound.corrected_form: this record, benchmarks/ghz.py and docs/physics_notes.md said 'an equality for the ideal state, a lower bound in general' and the test asserted the bound BELOW the fixed-phase register fidelity within three sigma; the inequality runs the other way. The committed three-ion run already violated the claim -- bound 0.9935 against the exact fixed-phase 0.98520, the bound 0.008 ABOVE the number it was printed beside -- and the test passed only because its 3-sigma slack, 0.0185, was twice the discrepancy, so it could not detect a systematic phase error, which is the error the exact fidelity was added to catch. For the ideal three-ion |GHZ_theta> at theta = 0.7 the contrast is 1 and the bound 1 while the fixed-phase fidelity is cos^2(theta/2) = 0.882421, a gap of 0.117579. Section 7.9's own 'is a lower bound (Wright 2019)' is about an imperfect analysis pulse degrading the MEASURED contrast, not about the direction of the inequality, so this is a deliberate deviation from the plan's phrasing. Unchanged: phi_0 carries N pi/2 from the rotation axis of GPi2 and the compiled circuit's residual virtual-Z frames, so the parity at phi = 0 is not the maximum (it vanishes for the real GHZ state) and only the contrast enters the bound
conv.ghz_parity_bound.equation: P_0 = P(0...0) and P_1 = P(1...1) from the GHZ circuit H, CNOT chain; on fresh shots the parity <prod_q Z_q> after GPi2(phi) on every qubit oscillates as C cos(N phi + phi_0) with C = 2 |rho_{0...0, 1...1}| (only the sigma_+^{ox N} term carries e^{i N phi}; every other coherence lands in the phase-independent offset), fitted from at least four phases over one period 2 pi/N. Since P_0 = rho_{0...0,0...0} and P_1 = rho_{1...1,1...1}, (P_0 + P_1 + C)/2 = (rho_{0...0,0...0} + rho_{1...1,1...1})/2 + |rho_{0...0,1...1}| = max_theta <GHZ_theta| rho |GHZ_theta> with |GHZ_theta> = (|0...0> + e^{i theta}|1...1>)/sqrt 2: an EQUALITY with the phase-optimised GHZ-class fidelity and therefore an UPPER bound on the fidelity against any FIXED-phase GHZ state. The simulator reports both exact numbers beside the measured bound, GHZResult.register_fidelity_max_phase (what the bound estimates) and GHZResult.register_fidelity (against the compiled circuit's own fixed-phase target), with the shot-noise uncertainties of P_0, P_1 and C combined in quadrature (benchmarks/ghz.py ghz_coherence; tests/test_m10_benchmarks.py)
conv.ghz_parity_bound.source: Sackett et al. 2000; Leibfried et al. 2005; Wright et al. 2019 (the two-qubit form, Section 7.9 [verified])

conv.gradient_drive.corrected_form: Section 13's r_0 with the TOTAL two-ion mass is confirmed by the derivation, not assumed: on a spatially antisymmetric mode w_{i,m} = +-2 Omega_g EXACTLY with Omega_g = (r_0/4) grad(B)(d omega_0/dB) and r_0 = sqrt(hbar/(2 M_total omega_m)), which is what makes the plan's (sigma_z1 - sigma_z2) normalization the right one (measured ratio -1.000000000/+1.000000000). Two things the audit's recommendation supposed do NOT hold: a gradient gate needs a FIELD-SENSITIVE qubit (d omega_0/dB vanishes at a clock point, so Srinivas's |F=3,mF=3> <-> |F=2,mF=2> of 25Mg+ and not the 212.78 G clock line of the 9.13 row), and solve_amplitude_modulation(kind='gradient') does NOT work unchanged, because the force is a Bessel FUNCTION of the tone amplitude (Omega_g J_2(4 Omega_mu/delta)) and not linear in it, so Choi's, Leung's and Blumel's linear closure algebra does not apply and Srinivas's Walsh sign modulation (eight segments over 740 us, the sign carried by the tones' half-difference phase) is the applicable family. WaveformKind gains 'gradient' (two legs, the microwave tones at -/+ delta) and the scheduler plays it through the same sigma_z spin-echo path as a light-shift waveform; the closure SOLVERS do not cover it
conv.gradient_drive.equation: the near-field microwave-gradient drive is now device-level: GradientField carries the electrodes' oscillating gradient amplitude d(B_g . B_hat)/dr (T/m), its frequency omega_g, its axis, the two microwave tones' field amplitude B_1 and the gradient's phase; derive_gradient_drive returns Omega_mu = (B_x/2 hbar)<dn|mu_x|up> from the existing magnetic-dipole coupling, d omega_0/dB from the hyperfine-Zeeman diagonalization, and the per-(ion, mode) laboratory force w_{i,m} = (1/2)(d omega_0/dB) grad(B)(r_hat . e_hat_m) c_{i,m} sqrt(hbar/(2 m_i omega_m)) built from the mode's mass-weighted pattern exactly as a Lamb-Dicke parameter is; the builder's 'gradient' branch adds sum_{i,m} w_{i,m} sigma_z^i (a_m + a_m^dag) cos(omega_g t + phi_g) beside the drive's two microwave tones (BuilderOptions.gradient_form = 'bare', the default, so that J_2(4 Omega_mu/delta) and the J_0 = 0 decoupling emerge from the exact dynamics) or the eliminated (w_{i,m}/2) J_2 sigma_z^i (a_m e^{i(omega_g + 2 delta) t} + h.c.) alone ('dressed', recorded in approximations)
conv.gradient_drive.source: Srinivas et al., Nature 597, 209 (2021) Eq. 1; light/microwave.py; dynamics/hamiltonian.py

conv.heavy_output_criterion.equation: square circuits of width n and depth d = n, every layer a uniform random permutation and a Haar-random SU(4) (Mezzadri's QR construction) on each of the floor(n/2) pairs, adjacent local unitaries merged per qubit; the heavy outputs of a circuit are the strings whose IDEAL probability exceeds the median of the ideal distribution (half the strings); h_U is the measured fraction of shots on them; the width passes when the mean over circuits of h_U clears 2/3 by two sigma AND the run has at least the protocol's 100 circuits ('we set n_c >= 100 circuits'), the confidence being Appendix C Eq. (32), [n_h - z sqrt(n_h (n_s - n_h/n_c))]/(n_c n_s) > 2/3 with z = 2, n_h the total heavy count and n_s the shots per circuit, which with h = n_h/(n_c n_s) reduces IDENTICALLY to mean - 2 sigma > 2/3 with the per-CIRCUIT binomial sigma = sqrt(h(1 - h)/n_c) (volume.py cross_confidence_sigma, heavy_output_pass; the same sigma the Qiskit Experiments reference implementation computes); the standard error of the mean of h_U over the circuits is reported beside it as QVResult.standard_error_of_the_mean and is never the criterion, and QVResult.threshold_cleared carries the confidence half of the criterion on its own, so a run below 100 circuits says so and clears no quantum volume; under a depolarizing composition h_pred = h_ideal (1 - eps) + eps/2 (benchmarks/volume.py)
conv.heavy_output_criterion.section: 10 M10; 4.6 (the four-qubit quantum-volume circuit of Pino et al. 2021)
conv.heavy_output_criterion.source: Cross, Bishop, Sheldon, Nation and Gambetta, PRA 100, 032328 (2019), Appendix C Eq. (32); benchmarks/volume.py; tests/test_m10_benchmarks.py
conv.heavy_output_criterion.symbol: mean(h_U) - 2 sqrt(h(1 - h)/n_c) > 2/3 over n_c >= 100 circuits

conv.hughes_smooth_gate_untested.corrected_form: two independent blockers, both recorded rather than worked around. (1) The detuning ramp is not reconstructible: the plan itself records that Eq. 19 prints delta_max^{j} for delta_max^{-j} and that its constant b is dimensionally inconsistent as printed, so any ramp the simulator plays would be one of its own invention and 'flat to nbar = 9.4' would pin that invention and not the paper's schedule. (2) The temperature the claim names is out of reach of the exact displacement operators on the M4 fixture: nbar = 9.4 needs a Fock cap of about 68 levels, at which the Section 5.1.1 displacement oracle already reports expm against the analytic elements differing by 3e-9 at eta = 0.0786, ten thousand times the 1e-12 tolerance, so the run is refused before it starts. The FM machinery the section says the ramp would use IS in place and is now verified by exact integration (anchor.m4.solvers_verified_by_exact_integration): a callable detuning through waveform_from_callables plays through the engine, so what is missing is the source's ramp, not the capability

conv.improved_sampling_single_segment.corrected_form: two names in the plan do not exist in QuTiP 5.3.1: the plan's `deterministic_weight_info` is `McResult.deterministic_weights` (a list, one entry per initial state, in initial-state order) beside `runs_weights` (per stochastic trajectory, in completion order and matched to the keyed seeds through res.seeds). The single-segment restriction is a real limit of this engine, not of QuTiP: the no-jump/jump split is a decomposition of the WHOLE evolution, so applied to each of the n segments a schedule is cut into it yields a jump expansion of 2^n weighted PURE members that cannot be merged into a density matrix on the trajectory path, and pruning it at branch_weight_min would discard exactly the jump weight the Lindblad channels exist to produce (on the M7 two-ion fixture the per-segment jump probability is 1e-5, so every jump branch sits below the 1e-6 floor after two segments). The bounded fix is a per-segment keyed resampling of the weighted mixture down to ntraj members, which changes every M7 and M9b trajectory number and was left to the coordinator
conv.improved_sampling_single_segment.equation: with improved_sampling=True QuTiP evolves the no-jump trajectory once as a deterministic member of weight p_no-jump and gives the ntraj stochastic trajectories the residual weight, so the engine's per-member weights are res.deterministic_weights for res.deterministic_trajectories and res.runs_weights for res.trajectories; drawing uniformly from the stored trajectories instead biases every per-shot observable by p_no-jump. The engine uses it when the trajectory path is entered exactly ONCE in a schedule (SolverOptions.improved_sampling, default True); a multi-segment schedule keeps uniform-weight trajectories and says so in the run's notes
conv.improved_sampling_single_segment.source: PLAN.md Section 5.3 line 827 and Section 3.4; QuTiP 5.3.1 McResult introspected

conv.kak_weyl_chamber.equation: Q = M^dag U M = O_1 D O_2^T with O_1, O_2 real special orthogonal and D diagonal unitary (O_2 and D^2 from the complex-symmetric unitary Q^T Q, whose real and imaginary parts one real orthogonal matrix diagonalizes); (a, b, c) and phi from the four phases of D through the +-1 table of XX, YY, ZZ on the Bell states; the coefficients moved into the Weyl chamber pi/4 >= a >= b >= |c| >= 0 by pi/2 shifts absorbed as Paulis into A, B, by the axis permutations (S (x) S), (H (x) H), (R_x(pi/2) (x) R_x(pi/2)) and by the pair negations (Z, Y, X (x) 1); emitted as rxx(2a), (S (x) S) rxx(2b) (S^dag (x) S^dag), rzz(2c) with the local factors through decompose_single_qubit, so every Moelmer-Soerensen gate is played at an angle in [0, pi/2] and a generic SU(4) costs three; verified against the target up to a global phase (control/two_qubit.py)
conv.kak_weyl_chamber.section: 7.2 (an arbitrary SU(4) as the standard set's U3 is an arbitrary SU(2)); 7.1; M10
conv.kak_weyl_chamber.source: Kraus and Cirac 2001; Zhang, Vala, Sastry and Whaley 2003; the magic-basis bidiagonalization of Makhlin 2002 as Cirq implements it
conv.kak_weyl_chamber.symbol: U = e^{i phi} (A (x) B) exp[-i (a XX + b YY + c ZZ)] (C (x) D)

The 9.17 escalation-ladder cases d_m = 121, 151 and 201 are now run (as a slow test): all three integrate on the first rung with no retry at the keyed 1e-8, and the plan's 'probably stiff' abort at d_m = 121 with atol 1e-10 does NOT reproduce on a one-mode detuned spin-dependent force, so it is specific to the Section 11.1 two-ion pulse and no failure is manufactured to exercise the ladder (M2 audit E9/B9, E10, E18)

conv.laser_linewidth_phase_diffusion.corrected_form: the operators are excluded from the Section 4.2.8 decay sum rule through MultiLevelBuild.dephasing_slice (they carry no photon and no recoil), and Section 12's grant covers only the laser linewidth AS A SPECTRUM, which is weaker than this constant Lorentzian rate
conv.laser_linewidth_phase_diffusion.equation: Section 8.1 requires -(gamma/2 + delta omega_L/2) on the optical coherences; the Lindblad form supplies -gamma/2 by itself and delta omega_L was absent entirely (the M3a finding). MultiLevelOptions.laser_linewidth_rad_s (one entry per beam, default empty = an ideal laser) adds one phase-diffusion collapse operator per beam, the projector difference on the manifolds that beam connects times sqrt(delta omega_L/4), which damps that transition's coherence at exactly delta omega_L/2 and leaves every population and every within-manifold coherence untouched. Measured: the weak-drive excitation profile keeps its Lorentzian shape and broadens from full width Gamma to Gamma + delta omega_L at constant area (peak x Gamma/(Gamma + delta omega_L)) for delta omega_L/Gamma = 0.5, 1 and 2; rho_eg decays at gamma/2 + delta omega_L/2 and rho_ee still at gamma, both to 1e-9; R_o at delta omega_L = 0 is unchanged bit for bit

conv.level_a_participation_guard.corrected_form: participation_threshold=0.0 reports the steady state anyway, which is how the 30-second relaxation time is exhibited in the test
conv.level_a_participation_guard.equation: level A refused a mode only on the beam-direction projection (k_hat . e_m)^2 < 1e-2; it now also refuses one whose ILLUMINATED ions barely participate, sum_i c_{i,m}^2 < PARTICIPATION_THRESHOLD = 1e-4, and (when the caller states a stage duration through min_rate_per_s) one whose W_m = cooling - heating falls below it. A 40Ca+-like coolant next to a 171Yb+-like qubit under strong radial confinement leaves the two qubit-dominated radial modes at a coolant participation of 6.6e-6 and 5.8e-6 and a relaxation rate below 1 s^-1 (tens of seconds), while returning a mathematically consistent nbar because the participation cancels between eta~ and eta: that is exactly Section 4.2's 'such a mode is not cooled at all' and it was reported as a prepared occupation before (the M3 finding)
conv.level_a_participation_guard.symbol: sum_{i illuminated} c_{i,m}^2 >= 1e-4; optional W_m >= min_rate_per_s

conv.level_a_rates_participation.corrected_form: the W(Delta -+ nu) closed form with each beam shifted in turn is the weak-drive alternative, refused above Omega/Gamma = 0.1 (Section 4.2.8 vii); a mode whose projection on every cooling beam is below (k_hat . e_m)^2 = 1e-2 raises UncooledModeError instead of returning a steady state (Section 4.2)
conv.level_a_rates_participation.equation: per illuminated ion and mode the phonon rates come from the dipole-force spectrum of the ion's internal steady state under all its beams (exact in the saturation) plus the per-channel emission diffusion, with the mass-weighted participation folded into the zero-point length x0_eff = |c| sqrt(hbar/(2 m_i omega)); the mode rate carries W_k = sum_i c_{i,k}^2 and nbar = sum heating/(sum cooling - sum heating) is participation independent when the ions see one intensity (a two-ion COM mode: nbar equal to the single ion's to 1e-6, the rate halved when one ion is illuminated)

conv.level_b_c_handoff_state.corrected_form: nbar stays mandatory (the frozen modes and the provenance read it, and it is the fallback for a mode with no explicit state), and the explicit state's dimension is checked against the space's own truncation
conv.level_b_c_handoff_state.equation: Section 4.2 says the output of every stage is a per-mode thermal density matrix OR THE FOCK DISTRIBUTION FROM LEVEL B, and 4.2.7 adds OR THE LEVEL-C REDUCED MOTIONAL STATE; PreparationStage carried only Mapping[int, float] and prepare_state passed only thermal=nbar, so a non-thermal distribution was silently collapsed to its mean (the M3 finding). A stage now carries an optional per-mode motional density matrix that reaches initial_state(states=...) unchanged, with fock_distribution_state building the diagonal matrix of a level-B population vector; a later cooling stage on the same mode drops the explicit state again

conv.light_shift_force.corrected_form: for a force on one level only (weights (-2, 0), the 40Ca+ S1/2-D5/2 qubit under 398 nm light, or Baldwin's |up>) the single-qubit sigma_z phase is four times the two-body angle, which the spin echo of Section 4.4.4 cancels; the sign of a sigma_z force follows the detuning side alone (no phase flip)
conv.light_shift_force.equation: Omega_gg = sum_e conj(Omega^(2)_eg) Omega^(1)_eg/(2 Delta_e) for each qubit level g under the beam pair; the light-shift drive is (1/2) sum_tones Omega_LS e^{-i(mu t - phi)} [w_dn P_0 + w_up P_1] (x) D + h.c. with Omega_LS = (Omega_upup - Omega_dndn)/2 and weights (Omega_dndn, Omega_upup)/Omega_LS (differing by exactly 2): Zhu's hbar Omega_j cos(Delta k . q_j + mu t) sigma_z^j plus the spin-independent force; the same beams' Raman coupling Omega_R rotates at mu - omega_0 and is kept unless its excitation is below 1e-12
conv.light_shift_force.source: Wineland 2003 (two-photon coupling with g' = g); Zhu-Monroe-Duan 2006 Eq. 2; Ballance 2016; Baldwin 2021
