conv.manifold_rates_mode_selection.corrected_form: two further refusals replace silently negative rates: the two manifolds plus the decaying levels must carry the stationary population (closure_tol, naming the states that hold the rest), and neither manifold may be absorbing (weight_floor on the stationary weight). The 171Yb+ repump configuration hits both, because 3D[3/2]1/2 -> S1/2 at 297 nm is declared as untabulated branching and not as a Transition, so nothing returns from the D branch to S1/2 - the recorded gap of anchor.m3a.yb171_repump_level_gap, now a stated refusal instead of a number
conv.manifold_rates_mode_selection.equation: the two-manifold coarse graining took the second-slowest Liouvillian mode (order[1]) and required it to connect the manifolds; with the D3/2 branch and its 935 nm repump in a 171Yb+ detection model that mode is a D-manifold relaxation and the call failed with 'the slow mode does not connect the two manifolds' (the M5 finding). The mode is now chosen by projecting every eigenvector onto the two manifolds' populations and taking the slowest one that moves population between them; the skipped intra-manifold rates are reported on ManifoldRates.intra_manifold_rates_per_s rather than hidden
conv.manifold_rates_mode_selection.symbol: the slowest Liouvillian mode with weight on BOTH manifolds

conv.mass_ion.corrected_form: eta(N = 17) rounds to 0.0267 at 171 u and 0.0268 at the ion mass
conv.mass_ion.equation: Species.mass_u is the ION mass, the cited atomic mass minus one electron mass (171Yb+: 170.93578 u from 170.9363302 u); the Lamb-Dicke anchor must state its mass

conv.mass_weighted_eigenvectors_parity.corrected_form: renormalizing in raw displacements is a 20 to 160% error invisible at mu = 1 (b1^2 = 0.40641 instead of 0.31608 at mu = 40/27); 'even' read as 'in-phase' inverts the rule
conv.mass_weighted_eigenvectors_parity.equation: eigenvectors orthonormal in u_i = sqrt(m_i) z_i only; physical amplitudes carry 1/sqrt(m_i); inversion parity p = +1 means an ANTISYMMETRIC displacement pattern (centre ion at rest), exempt from uniform-field noise and uncoolable by a centre ion

conv.mathieu_sign.corrected_form: Wineland 1998 and Berkeland 1998 use +2q cos (a half-period shift); factor-4 q definitions elsewhere; House 2008 has Q = -q and prints its first-order matrix with the wrong sign
conv.mathieu_sign.equation: d^2x/dxi^2 + [a - 2q cos 2xi] x = 0, xi = omega_rf t/2, a = 4Z|e|U alpha/(m omega_rf^2), q = 2Z|e|U~ alpha'/(m omega_rf^2)

conv.mathieu_sign_house.corrected_form: copied as printed, a stable trap (a_z = 0.005, q = 0.20) is reported unstable; trap/mathieu.py companion_matrix(lower_left_sign=+1) is the negative control (tests/test_mathieu.py)
conv.mathieu_sign_house.equation: the standard form u'' + (a - 2q cos 2tau) u = 0; House's x'' + [A + 2Q cos 2tau] x = 0 has Q = -q, and his Eq. 7 prints the first-order matrix's lower-left block with the wrong sign

conv.mcsolve_weight_attributes.corrected_form: the plan names the weight record deterministic_weight_info; no such attribute exists in 5.3.1
conv.mcsolve_weight_attributes.equation: with improved_sampling=True mcsolve evolves one deterministic no-jump member (McResult.deterministic_trajectories, weight McResult.deterministic_weights[0]) and gives the stochastic trajectories the residual weights McResult.runs_weights; shots are drawn from that weighted mixture

conv.mean_count_curve.corrected_form: the fit is degenerate at bin-time windows (tens of us: R_b unconstrained, the least-squares returned 1e4 Hz); it needs windows long against 1/R_d and 1/R_b, as Noek's 60 ms, so calibrate_detection draws a separate long record set for the fit
conv.mean_count_curve.equation: the calibration fit for (εR_o, R_d, R_b) from bright-prepared records; equals the exact chain's mean when only R_d and R_b act
conv.mean_count_curve.source: Noek 2013 Eq. 4 with ṗ_1 = R_b p_0 - R_d p_1

conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.corrected_form: mg25.S12.g_J carried 2.00226 sourced PLAN_9_13, which is 9Be+'s measured value transplanted, and the Section 9.13 212.78 G clock-point anchor depends on it at the 0.25 G level (g_J = 2.000 moves it to 213.025 G). g_J must NOT be back-solved from the ratio plus a tabulated mu_I: the corrected and uncorrected shielding conventions give 2.0045 or fail the 9Be+ cross-check at 4e-4. 25Mg+ therefore still raises IncompleteSpeciesTable, now for a DERIVED reason (audit item E21)
conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.equation: no measured absolute g_J of the 25Mg+ ground state exists: both measurements servo the field to the electronic transition and determine only the RATIO g_I/g_J = 9.299484(75)e-5 (Itano and Wineland 1981) or 9.299308313(60)e-5 (Brewer et al. 2019), which is what the table now stores
conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.section: 4.5.1; 9.13; 13 Sign of A_hfs and the g-factors
conv.mg25_no_measured_g_j.source: Itano and Wineland, Phys. Rev. A 24, 1364 (1981); Brewer et al., Phys. Rev. A 100, 013409 (2019); qutip_trap/species/mg25.py

conv.micromotion_amplitude_convention.corrected_form: Blakestad's zone-E numbers are inconsistent in one convention (68 nm peak against 47 nm rms); the M1 code shipped +(1/2) q u_0 with abs() on both the amplitude and the index, i.e. the OTHER rf phase origin, which inverted every micromotion-sideband phase and the sign of the rf-photon correlation servo step while leaving the fitted null (a zero crossing) and J_0 (even) untouched [corrected: M1 audit, fix batch]
conv.micromotion_amplitude_convention.equation: declared explicitly: SIGNED peak amplitude u_1 = -(1/2) q u_0 for the stray-field term, the minus sign forced by conv.floquet_phase_origin (the adopted a - 2q cos 2xi origin makes the in-phase micromotion a contraction, x_mu = -(q_x/2) x_sec cos omega_rf t); beta = delta_k . u_1 is signed too, so sign(beta_ip) = -sign(q_x E_x) and it steps by pi across the compensated shim; the in-phase (nullable) and out-of-phase ((1/4) q R alpha phi_ac, not nullable) indices never collapse into one number; total adds in quadrature, and the builder consumes the pair as (hypot(ip, op), rf phase + -atan2(op, ip))
conv.micromotion_amplitude_convention.section: 13 Micromotion amplitude convention; 4.1.1; Appendix E MicromotionIndex

conv.micromotion_compensation_loop.corrected_form: nothing in run/, dynamics/ or control/ read table.micromotion: the shims and the residual beta were inert bookkeeping, the run always used the device's own Trap.shim_voltages_v / stray_field_v_per_m, and a stale compensation against a drifted stray field was not a reproducible failure mode at all (the entries WERE wired into UPSTREAM['sideband_spectroscopy'] as a gate, which is the other half of the requirement)
conv.micromotion_compensation_loop.equation: run() programs the table's CALIBRATED shim entries onto the device it evolves; the crystal is re-solved at that setting, so the ions' displacement, the beams' intensity at the ions and the Lamb-Dicke parameters move together. A seed shim is not programmed (it is the device's own setting) and an uncalibrated one is reported in the run notes and leaves the device as it is. The reported device hash stays the UNCOMPENSATED device's, because no device parameter changed - only a programmed voltage. This closes the loop PLAN 7.5 asks for by name ('stores shims and beta in the table, so that compensation is calibrated, drifts with the stray field between calibrations and is re-nulled like a laboratory re-nulls it')

conv.micromotion_correction.corrected_form: the RMP's (1 + q/2)^-1 is the u(0) = 1 normalization at one rf phase, an rf-clock artifact [corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]
conv.micromotion_correction.equation: eta_eff = eta C0, C0 the e^{i nu t} Fourier coefficient of the exact Floquet function normalized by Im(u* u_dot) = nu: C0 = 1 + 3q^2/16 + O(q^4) (1.007741 at q = 0.2)

conv.micromotion_jn_weights_dropped.corrected_form: no Section 9.2 row is blocked (that row asks only for the J_0 reduction, 1.018161 at q = 0.3 and 2(C0 - 1) = 3.4 percent, both tested) but a micromotion-sideband-spectroscopy row would be; anchor.m2.micromotion_carrier_factor records that the default is the J_0 average without recording the omission, which this entry does (M2 audit E17, D)
conv.micromotion_jn_weights_dropped.equation: the default unlocked micromotion mode multiplies every drive coefficient by J_0(beta) and drops the incoherent J_n^2 micromotion-SIDEBAND weights entirely, although PLAN.md:502 says the unlocked average keeps 'only J_0 AND the J_n^2 weights' and Section 13's row asks for J_n(beta) on every drive. The machinery exists (micromotion='modulated' with a per-shot rf_phase_rad sample reproduces the full modulation) but nothing in qutip_trap/ produces KEY_RF_PHASE, so the weights are unreachable from a run
conv.micromotion_jn_weights_dropped.symbol: J_0(beta) only, the J_n^2 sideband weights dropped

conv.micromotion_static_spring.corrected_form: the two springs differ by 0.39 q^2, 3.2 % at q = 0.28, so Trap.micromotion_beta gives |beta| = 0.034934 where the 9.12 row prints 0.034 (2 digits); that is why tests/test_trap_model.py bands the trap-level assertion at rel = 0.1 and pins the tight one against the standalone displacement_m helper [M1 audit, fix batch]
conv.micromotion_static_spring.equation: Trap.micromotion_beta balances the residual static force against the PSEUDOPOTENTIAL spring m (Omega/2)^2 (a + q^2/2), the period average of the driven Mathieu equation's particular solution, not against the exact exponent m nu^2 = m (Omega/2)^2 beta^2; the DC Fourier row gives x_0 = f/(a + q^2/2) exactly to O(q^4) and Berkeland's own omega is the pseudopotential secular frequency
conv.micromotion_static_spring.section: 4.1.1; 9.12 Excess micromotion from a stray field
conv.micromotion_static_spring.source: driven Mathieu equation, DC Fourier row; Berkeland 1998 Eq. 16; qutip_trap/trap/model.py

conv.mode_classes_and_tolerances.corrected_form: the plan names 'the residual-displacement tolerance' for freezing without a value; 1e-4 is the M6 default, an approximation of the truncation kind reported per run [background]
conv.mode_classes_and_tolerances.equation: per mode, from the Section 4.4.3 integrals of every played waveform with the prepared occupations: dropped when |alpha|^2 (2 nbar + 1) < 1e-6 and |chi| < 1e-4; frozen when |alpha|^2 (2 nbar + 1) < SolverOptions.freeze_alpha_max (1e-4) and |chi| < freeze_chi_max_rad (0.05); resolved otherwise, with the cap from the loop radius eta Omega/epsilon, the occupation and the Section 5.1.1 margin; a frozen mode's chi is absorbed by the exact spot check on the reduced space (the frozen run is calibrated to the same angle) and reported; modes only carrier pulses touch are frozen

conv.mode_dimension_max.corrected_form: M9a fixed d_max = 64 in select_space and step_space with no way through run(), and when the rule wanted more it silently narrowed the DECLARED expected occupation range with it, so the Section 5.1.1 oracle check and the Section 5.5 margin check ran over less than the physics. Section 5.3 states that a Doppler-cooled nbar ~ 20 mode needs d_m >~ 150 for a boundary population below 1e-4 (measured here: the rule asks for d = 156 at nbar = 20, eta = 0.1, tail 1e-4) and Section 5.2 that long-chain transverse spectators within tens of kHz of the tones cannot be frozen and must be resolved: exactly the combination the clamp could not carry. The ceiling is now SolverOptions.mode_dimension_max, still 64 by default, and a clamp emits a SpaceSelection.notes entry naming the mode, the d the rule asked for, the expected range it asked for and the clamped range
conv.mode_dimension_max.equation: the cap rule takes the populated range of the thermal mode displaced by the loop radius at the boundary threshold, plus the Section 5.1.1 margin for the mode's eta, clamped to mode_dimension_max (default 64)
conv.mode_dimension_max.source: dynamics/engine.py SolverOptions; run/space.py cap_requirement, cap_for, select_space; run/gate_local.py step_space; tests/test_m9_scaling.py

conv.mode_drift_differential_independenc.corrected_form: Section 6.2 warns against exactly this: 'each has a correlation time and is sampled as a trajectory or a quasi-static value by the rule of Section 6.1, NEVER as M independent offsets, because independent sampling makes closure errors average as 1/sqrt(M) instead of adding and lets robustness tests pass for the wrong reason.' The physical fix is one draw per dc electrode projected through d omega_m/d V, and the MISSING DEVICE PARAMETER is that Jacobian: Trap carries omega_hz, shim_voltages_v and an optional geometry, but no d omega_m/d V per electrode, so the projection cannot be built from the present record. Recorded as a known deviation rather than silently left: a multi-mode FM/AM-FM robustness result obtained under it is optimistic by up to sqrt(M)
conv.mode_drift_differential_independenc.equation: the COMMON-mode part is correct and is one draw (KEY_RF_FRACTION, applied as frac x omega_m to every rf-derived family, conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise); the DIFFERENTIAL dc part is drawn as n_modes independent normals of the Drift's rms
conv.mode_drift_differential_independenc.source: M7 audit E-21 / B-10 (noise/model.py:271-283, the size = n_modes draw)
conv.mode_drift_differential_independenc.symbol: mode_drift_differential drawn as M independent per-mode offsets

conv.mode_eigenvector_gauge.corrected_form: James's Table 2 eigenvectors ARE sign-consistent with the closed forms (an extracted item claimed otherwise)
conv.mode_eigenvector_gauge.equation: orthonormal, axial eigenvalues increasing, last component positive; transverse families numbered ascending in frequency (Appendix E), so the COM is the last transverse mode

conv.mode_index.corrected_form: eigensolver output order, frequency order across families or (family, index) pairs, none declared in the second revision [corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]
conv.mode_index.equation: every mode index is a position in Crystal.modes, ordered axial, transverse_1, transverse_2, ascending frequency within a family; eigenvectors unit norm, last component positive

conv.motion_phase_default.corrected_form: Section 4.4.3's sine beat-note convention (phi_b - phi_r = pi, force zero at t = 0) is a convention for the closed forms only: played literally on the check_ms_closure.py fixture (Omega/mu = 0.1) it tilts the axis by 0.202 rad and leaks sin^2 psi = 3.8% into |du>, |ud> (concurrence 0.9597 against 0.9999 with equal phases); the kernels carry phi_m explicitly and Choi's sin(mu t) e^{i omega t} is their phi_m = pi/2 case
conv.motion_phase_default.equation: the played waveforms default to equal tone phases (phi_b = phi_r, the force Omega cos(mu t)); the carrier Omega cos(mu t - phi_m) rotates the spin at F(t) = (2 Omega/mu)[sin(mu t - phi_m) + sin phi_m], whose mean tilts the force axis by psi = (2 Omega/mu) sin phi_m

conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise.corrected_form: the tabulated band of the same spectrum is a common-mode fractional trajectory of the transverse modes, never M independent offsets (Section 6.2)
conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise.equation: a white fractional rf-amplitude density S_V gives a white mode-frequency density omega_m^2 S_V and the coherence of |n> + |n'> decays at (n - n')^2/tau; the axial (dc) family does not follow the rf amplitude
conv.motional_dephasing_from_rf_noise.source: Section 13 row L = a^dag a sqrt(2/tau) with omega_m proportional to V_rf for the transverse families

conv.ms_closure.corrected_form: the second revision halved the closure to 1/(4 sqrt K), a factor-2 force error caught by the derivation audit; Roos's Omega_c = |eps|/(4 eta) reads |eps|/(2 eta) in the plan's Omega
conv.ms_closure.equation: the force on S_y is -(hbar eta Omega/2)(a^dagger e^{i eps t} + h.c.) for the plan's per-tone Omega; closure eta Omega/eps = 1/(2 sqrt K) in every spin normalization; targets -pi/2 on J_y^2, -pi/8 on S_y^2, pi/4 on sigma_y sigma_y

conv.ms_gates_serialized_under_parallel_.corrected_form: the M6 scheduler started an entangling gate at max(clock[a], clock[b]) under parallel=True and never advanced the crystal clock, so two MS gates on disjoint pairs of a four-ion chain were both scheduled on [0, 50] us on the SAME global Raman pair (measured); Schedule.__post_init__ accepted it because it only forbids overlap on a shared ion. The flag was also a caller argument with no device field behind it, against 7.3's 'if the device model allows'
conv.ms_gates_serialized_under_parallel_.equation: under parallel addressing the per-ion clocks carry the single-qubit gates and an entangling gate advances BOTH its ions' clocks and the crystal-wide clock, so carrier pulses on distinct ions overlap and entangling gates never do; HardwareChain.parallel_addressing (additive field, default False) is the device model's permission and schedule(parallel=None)/run(parallel=None) read it, an explicit parallel=True against a chain that declares False being refused
conv.ms_gates_serialized_under_parallel_.source: PLAN.md Section 7.3 ('MS gates are serialized, one at a time per crystal in the first release'; single-qubit gates 'in parallel if the device model allows parallel addressing'); qutip_trap/control/schedule.py

conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.corrected_form: PLAN.md 4.5.6 called the 43Ca+ value 'a thesis value 0.17% from the handbook number that fits f0 nine times better, effectively a fitted constant'. It is not fitted: it is the free-ion moment, which is the moment a trapped-ion Breit-Rabi Hamiltonian takes, and Hanley et al. print it to 9e-6. Mixing the conventions between species is a 0.2-0.25% error in g_I
conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.equation: the tables carry mu_I in THREE different conventions, each now declared per table: 9Be+ -1.177432 mu_N DIAMAGNETICALLY CORRECTED (Dickopf 2024's g_I gives -1.1774316344; the uncorrected NMR value is -1.17449(2), 0.25% away), 25Mg+ -0.85545 mu_N UNCORRECTED (Alder and Yu 1951 via Stone, which carries no correction flag for that row; no corrected 25Mg value exists, and Stone's corrected recommendation is -0.85533(3)), 43Ca+ -1.315350(9) mu_N FREE-ION (Hanley et al. 2021, explicitly uncorrected for the ion's bound electrons; Stone's bare-nucleus value is -1.31733(6))
conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.section: 13 Sign of A_hfs and the g-factors; 4.5.6
conv.mu_i_shielding_convention.source: Stone INDC(NDS)-0794; Dickopf et al., Nature 632, 757 (2024); Hanley et al., arXiv:2105.10352

conv.multi_pair_waveform_angles.corrected_form: measured on a three-ion chain, pair (0, 2): chi(0,2) = pi/4 while the same envelope carries chi(0,1) = chi(1,2) = 0.449272, so the stored angle was 1.75x wrong and the amplitude rescale a factor sqrt(pi/4 / 0.449272) = 1.32 off. The solver's ``pair`` is now threaded into waveform_from_segmented/waveform_from_callables and a multi-pair GateModes with no pair named is REFUSED rather than defaulted
conv.multi_pair_waveform_angles.equation: a GateModes built on more than two ions carries an entangling angle per pair, and the Waveform stores ONE pair's per-mode angles; the builders took the first pair's regardless of the pair the solver targeted, and the scheduler reads Waveform.chi_total_rad for both the s^2 amplitude rescale and the kernel sign
conv.multi_pair_waveform_angles.section: 9.17 'Waveform per (ion, leg)'; Section 10 M4 bullet '3 to 5 ions' (M4 audit 2026-09-07)

conv.multilevel_frame_assignment.corrected_form: the plan's own construction, tagged background; validated against the secular static model (5e-4 in populations, 2e-3 in rate at a 14.7 GHz beat) rather than against a source
conv.multilevel_frame_assignment.equation: frame frequencies assigned manifold by manifold along the beams from the lowest included level at f = 0 so that every detuning sits on the diagonal; levels reached only by decay take the transition frequency as frame (the dissipator is invariant); a beam inconsistent with two assigned manifolds (two tones on one transition, a closed loop) leaves a residual beat, the Hamiltonian is time periodic, and the steady state is the fixed point of the one-period propagator (vern9, nsteps 1e7) period-averaged, the same machinery serving a polarization modulation; incommensurate beats fall back to propagating 1000/Gamma and averaging

conv.native_ms_matrix.equation: MS(phi0, phi1, theta) = exp[-i pi theta GPi(phi0) (x) GPi(phi1)] with theta in turns in [0, 0.25]; GPi(phi) = [[0, e^{-2 pi i phi}], [e^{2 pi i phi}, 0]]; GPi2(phi) = (1/sqrt 2)[[1, -i e^{-2 pi i phi}], [-i e^{2 pi i phi}, 1]]; ZZ(theta) = diag(e^{-i pi theta}, e^{i pi theta}, e^{i pi theta}, e^{-i pi theta}); XX(chi) = MS(0, 0, theta) with chi = pi theta
conv.native_ms_matrix.source: IonQ documentation; qiskit-ionq, ionq-core-python, PennyLane-IonQ client code read 2026-09-04

conv.no_stark_imbalance.corrected_form: control/table.py's Segment docstring claimed 'per-ion imbalance is a CalibrationTable entry', which does not exist and is not what the leg split is: the imbalance is carried by the two legs' own amplitudes, which the solvers set, and the docstring now says so. The closed forms also IGNORE a non-zero imbalance (integrals_segmented reads one amplitude per (ion, segment)), so a waveform built with imbalance != 0 carries the BALANCED pulse's chi_m and alpha_m
conv.no_stark_imbalance.equation: waveform_from_segmented and the solvers accept an ``imbalance`` that splits the two legs' amplitudes, and nothing in the repository ever passes a non-zero value: the compensation LAW xi = (delta eta^2/|eps|)(phi/pi), the differential shift delta_ac^(C) = 2(Omega_r^2 - Omega_b^2)/delta = -8 Omega^2 xi/delta and the delta^(SB) = (eps/2) xi n term that breaks thermal-state operation are unimplemented, and so is the third-tone alternative
conv.no_stark_imbalance.source: Kirchmair 2009 (Omega_b = Omega(1 + xi), Omega_r = Omega(1 - xi)); Innsbruck third-tone alternative (Section 4.4.1, last line)

conv.noise_provenance.corrected_form: before this neither record had a provenance field and NoiseModel.extra was numbers only, so Section 6.1's reporting deliverable could not be produced at all
conv.noise_provenance.equation: one tag per apparatus per rate ('author year, species, N ions'); NoiseModel.apparatus() unions the tags of every NON-QUIET rate (a zero rate contributes nothing to a budget and so no apparatus), undeclared_rate_count() counts the non-zero rates with no tag, and provenance_sentence() is emitted into Diagnostics.approximations whenever either is non-empty
conv.noise_provenance.section: 6.1 'An N-ion error budget assembled from them is stitched from at least three apparatus, and the report says so'
conv.noise_provenance.source: M7 audit E-12 (noise/spectra.py, noise/model.py, run/job.py Diagnostics)

conv.noise_routing.corrected_form: no heuristic on a spectrum's shape decides its route: the two fields declare the split; a grid that cannot resolve the band refuses with the remedy (declare the band above it as white_level)
conv.noise_routing.equation: a NoiseSpectrum's tabulated band is synthesized per dynamical sample on a fixed grid (x(t) = sum_k sqrt(S(omega_k) d omega_k/pi)[a_k cos + b_k sin], <x^2> = (1/pi) int S d omega); its white_level is a Lindblad rate; Drift records are OU chains over the shot clock; collisions are Poisson events per shot

conv.nuclear_g_sign.corrected_form: Harty's g_I^(N) = mu_I/(I mu_N) with a minus sign and Langer's g_I = -mu_I/(I mu_B) with a plus are self-consistent alternatives that must not be mixed: 83.76 kHz and 0.207 G off for 43Ca+
conv.nuclear_g_sign.equation: g_I = -(mu_I/(I mu_N))(m_e/m_p), so H_Z = mu_B (g_J J_z + g_I I_z) B/hbar with one sign for both; 43Ca+ g_I = +2.0467e-4 from mu_I = -1.31535 mu_N

conv.observation_model.corrected_form: the first M8 build keyed the draws by (sample, point index, ion, outcome) only, so a calibration running the same experiment twice, or an experiment repeating a scan, replayed identical noise: the Stark scan read -12.67 Hz for BOTH beams of the fixture drive, exactly, and summed their uncertainties as if independent (3.3 sigma from the truth for a single 2.3 sigma draw counted twice); every experiment of a calibration and every sub-run now carries a stream label appended to the outcome key (Observation.stream, sub_stream)
conv.observation_model.equation: every experiment reads its populations as shots declared through the readout's (eps_B, eps_D), keyed by (sample, trajectory, shot, ion, channel); the fits are weighted least squares whose covariance is scaled by max(1, chi^2/dof), so an under-fitting model widens its own error bars; shots=None returns the exact populations (the M2 to M7 behaviour)
conv.observation_model.symbol: P_declared = P_bright (1 - eps_B) + (1 - P_bright) eps_D; k ~ Binomial(shots, P_declared)

conv.one_rate_per_upper_level.corrected_form: total_decay_rate_rad_s used set.pop() on the distinct rates, so two disagreeing gamma_hz returned an arbitrary one; a level with lifetime_s = None and two inconsistent transitions passed validation (audit item E8)
conv.one_rate_per_upper_level.equation: every E1 transition out of one upper level carries the same gamma_hz, enforced in Species.__post_init__ and re-checked in AtomicStructure.total_decay_rate_rad_s
conv.one_rate_per_upper_level.symbol: Transition.gamma_hz is the UPPER level's TOTAL rate

conv.openqasm2_subset.corrected_form: u1(lambda) = e^{i lambda/2} RZ(lambda): imported as rz, the global phase dropped
conv.openqasm2_subset.equation: header, include (ignored, qelib1.inc gates built in), qreg/creg (flattened in declaration order), gate declarations expanded by inlining (the client SDKs' gpi/gpi2/ms/zz declarations import through their own u, rz, rxx, rzz bodies), register broadcasting, barrier ignored, trailing measure -> Circuit.measure, mid-circuit measure/reset kept as operations, expressions over pi with + - * / ^ and sin cos tan exp ln sqrt; undeclared gpi/gpi2/ms/zz take radians (the IR convention); if and opaque refused
conv.openqasm2_subset.source: OpenQASM 2.0 specification (Cross et al. 2017); qelib1.inc; PLAN.md Section 7.6

conv.operator_order_templates.corrected_form: Maslov's '.' reverses circuit order; IonQ's virtual-Z rule sign depends on this
conv.operator_order_templates.equation: matrix product written right-to-left, circuit time left-to-right; every template checked numerically

conv.optical_phase_beam_path_sign.corrected_form: M2 shipped beam_phase = phi_1 - phi_2 inside e^{-i beam_phase}, i.e. e^{+i Delta phi_i}: a sampled +0.4 rad on beam 1 played GPi2(-0.4) where the plan's convention gives GPi2(+0.4). The relative sign of Delta k . X_i and the optical phase is physical (PLAN.md:808), and it is the sign Section 4.3.7's phi_G = phi_{B,b} - phi_{B,r} cancellation and Section 4.4.2's spin/motion split refer to (M2 audit E2)
conv.optical_phase_beam_path_sign.equation: Delta phi_i is the phase of the BEAT NOTE written E ~ cos(omega_L t - Delta k . r + Delta phi_i), so for a Raman pair with Delta k = k_1 - k_2 and E_j ~ cos(k_j . r - omega_j t + phi_j) it is phi_2 - phi_1, and for a single-beam optical drive (Delta k = k_1) it is -phi_1; the factor on sigma_+ is e^{+i(Delta k . X_i - Delta phi_i)}, so beam 1's sampled path phase enters as e^{+i phi_1} and beam 2's as e^{-i phi_2}
conv.optical_phase_beam_path_sign.source: Monroe et al., RMP 2020 Eqs. 16, 18; tests/test_m2_optical_phase.py

conv.optical_phase_drift.corrected_form: M2 shipped the drift in the beams' INTENSITY only (_pointing_factor), keeping a 2.6e-7 amplitude effect and dropping a 0.51 rad phase for 171Yb+ at 355 nm counter-propagating with u_0 = 14.3 nm at 1 V/m; Section 13's row says 'beam-path AND ion-position drift stored as one scalar per ion per pulse' (M2 audit E1)
conv.optical_phase_drift.equation: the builder's geometric phase is Delta k . (X_j - X_i) with BOTH equilibrium positions carrying the shot's sampled stray-field displacement u_0 = Q E_dc/(m omega^2) (noise/sampling.py key_position_offset_m), so the surviving term is Delta k . (u_0(j) - u_0(i)); the addressed ion's own drift is a per-ion constant that the frame alignment of Section 7.5 step 3 absorbs and cancels out of the difference
conv.optical_phase_drift.section: 13 row 'Optical phase factor on sigma_+' (PLAN.md:1927); 4.1.1 u_0 = Q E_dc/(m omega^2); 5.2 (PLAN.md:808)
conv.optical_phase_drift.source: Berkeland et al., J. Appl. Phys. 83, 5025 (1998) Eq. 16; tests/test_m2_optical_phase.py
conv.optical_phase_drift.symbol: e^{+i(Delta k . X_i - Delta phi_i)} with X_i = X_i^(0) + u_0(i)

conv.oracle_margin_rule.corrected_form: a fatal oracle at small caps would defeat the cap-raising retries of Section 5.5, which start from a deliberately small cap (M2 rule)
conv.oracle_margin_rule.equation: HilbertSpace.displacement_factor asserts the interior elements against the analytic oracle to interior_tolerance(margin, eta) (the table row d = 2 margin, log-interpolated, floored at 1e-12) whenever the margin above the declared range is at least 4 levels; below the table's smallest row the difference is reported by oracle_status and the boundary monitor governs; required margins 6/10/20 at eta 0.1/0.5/1.0 are stored as an interpolated fixture

conv.per_ion_structures_and_selectivity.equation: one stage call now holds a coolant and a qubit species: stage_rates and doppler_cooling take either one AtomicStructure for every illuminated ion or a per-ion mapping, and an illuminated ion with no structure is refused rather than given a guessed one. Section 9.12 row 1360 is pinned as the operator statement it is: the coolant's Hamiltonian and collapse operators act as X (x) 1 on a two-ion joint space, so the qubit ion's reduced density matrix - populations AND coherences of a general state with |rho_01| = 0.36 - is invariant under the whole cooling Liouvillian to below 1e-12 over 40 lifetimes while the coolant's own state moves by more than 1e-3

conv.pgc_two_models.corrected_form: the 171Yb+ F = 1 -> F' = 0 scheme shares no coefficient with either model; only its beam projections and the bridge s_Joshi = (3/2) s0 (Gamma/2)^2/((Gamma/2)^2 + Delta^2) [background] are computed
conv.pgc_two_models.equation: the analytic j_g = 1/2 <-> j_e = 1/2 model with the isotropic alpha = 1/3, the static-gradient per-ion average that raises at |cos 2phi|^2 < 1e-2, and the moving-gradient window W < delta < omega; the Lindblad layer is the M3a builder on two counter-propagating linear beams along B with recoil = minimal (the three-class kernel) and beam phases (2 phi, 0), so the sigma+- standing waves are offset by pi/2 automatically; xi is read from the D1 sigma Rabi frequency as Omega_1^2 Delta/(4 omega (Delta^2 + Gamma^2/4)) = (1/3) Delta s with s referenced to the D2 stretched line (Omega_1 = sqrt(2/3) Omega_stretched)
conv.pgc_two_models.section: 4.2.4; 13 Polarization-gradient depth parameter, Position dependence in the PGC model, Two saturation parameters
conv.pgc_two_models.symbol: xi = Delta s/(3 omega); W = (16/9) eta^2 Gamma s xi cos^2 2phi; H = (2/9) eta^2 Gamma s (8 xi^2 cos^4 2phi + 2 + sin^2 2phi)

conv.played_chain.corrected_form: M2 to M7 played the table's Rabi frequency, Stark shift and crosstalk as the physics, which made a miscalibrated entry error-free by construction
conv.played_chain.equation: every pulse the scheduler emits carries the table's beliefs (Drive.programmed); the engine converts a requested Rabi frequency through the device's derived map divided by the calibrated one, the light shift to the derived shift at the played intensity (delta_derived sum_tones (Omega_phys/Omega_derived)^p), the crosstalk to the derived ratios of the listed neighbours; the identity for a surrogate table (seeds = derived values), so M2 to M7 are unchanged. SCOPE: the conversion applies to the kinds whose rf-power-to-Omega map the light layer derives from the beams and the atomic structure - raman, optical_E1, optical_E2. A microwave, state-dependent-light-shift (sigma_z sigma_z, Section 4.4.4) or microwave-gradient drive is played exactly as requested (control/played.py returns early), so a miscalibrated table produces NO over-rotation, detuning or crosstalk error for it: Section 7.10 exempts nothing and a light-shift drive's Omega is derivable from the beams (Section 4.4.4), so this is a narrowing of M8's central claim to two of four drive kinds, recorded here rather than left in an inline comment (M8 audit D1, open)
conv.played_chain.source: PLAN.md Section 7.10 ('the rf-power-to-Omega map is calibrated by the Rabi scan of Section 7.5 exactly as in the laboratory'); control/played.py

conv.played_zero_truth.corrected_form: Omega_true == 0 with a usable belief now RAISES and names the geometry; the 40Ca+ light-shift fixture's 729 nm E2 beam, whose Delta m = 0 quadrupole factor was exactly zero for k_hat = y_lab with pol = x_lab, was rotated instead of supplied (anchor.m4.light_shift_gate_ca40)
conv.played_zero_truth.equation: the played chain converted a REQUESTED Rabi frequency into the physical one through the ratio Omega_true/Omega_believed, and fell back to ratio = 1 with the note 'no usable Rabi entry' whenever either was zero. That conflated a calibration gap with a beam geometry the device derives ZERO coupling for, in which case it played a pulse the beams cannot deliver under a note that was factually wrong

conv.pm_solver.corrected_form: the data model was widened rather than the Segment type: SegmentedEnvelope gains an optional per-segment phase offset and every integral sees the complex weight z_k = Omega_k e^{i phi_k}, the offsets live in the two legs' HALF-DIFFERENCE (so the ion's spin phase, the half-sum, never moves and the force axis stays put) and envelope_of recovers them instead of collapsing them to a sign. Milne's N + 1 phase segments for N modes needs their time-symmetric phase profile, which this general solver does not impose: at N + 1 = 3 segments it leaves |alpha| ~ 1e-2 on the two-ion fixture while Choi's 2N + 1 = 5 close both modes to 3e-17. The family also cannot use conv.motion_phase_default's tilt-free phi_m = 0, because the motion phase IS its modulation parameter, so Roos's spin-axis tilt psi = (2 Omega/mu) sin phi_m is intrinsic to it: the exact check measures 1.8e-2 leakage against 4.7e-4 (FM) and 4.7e-7 (Fourier AM) on the same fixture
conv.pm_solver.equation: Section 4.4.3 supplies equations for AM (Zhu, Choi), FM (Leung) and AMFM (Blumel) and NAMES NO PM SOURCE, while 3.2's module comment, 7.4 and the M4 bullet all list PM as a deliverable: the plan is internally inconsistent. The solver implemented is the piecewise-constant per-segment MOTION phase at fixed amplitude and beat note, alpha_{i,m} = i eta_{i,m} Omega sum_k e^{i phi_k} F_k^{(m)} with the same symmetrized double integral and the phases inside, solved by least squares like the FM family's vertices, then scaled to |chi| = chi_target; the three sources above are the family's provenance and are [background], not equations the plan supplies
conv.pm_solver.source: Milne et al., PRApplied 13, 024022 (2020); Green and Biercuk, PRL 114, 120502 (2015); Lu et al., Nature 572, 363 (2019)

conv.polarization_components.corrected_form: Steck's tables list sigma+ under q = -1; extracted items interchanged the two labels
conv.polarization_components.equation: eps = sum_q eps_q e_q about B, e_{+-1} = -+(x +- i y)/sqrt 2, e_0 = z; helicity q_gamma = +1 (sigma+), 0 (pi), -1 (sigma-) for absorption |F mF> -> |F' mF + q_gamma>; operator index q_op = m_lower - m_upper = -q_gamma

conv.preparation_recipe.corrected_form: Appendix E's Device has no such field; it is an additive field with default None (the API-freeze test allows additions), needed because the plan's prepare() stage has no other source for the laboratory's procedure
conv.preparation_recipe.equation: the cooling beams at their detunings, the pulsed sideband schedule (beams, modes, pulses per order) and the pump beams are procedural device parameters carried on the Device; standard_recipe builds the 171Yb+ laboratory's recipe from the device's detection and global Raman beams (detection light shifted by -Gamma/2 then optimized over the gate modes' participation weights, pulsed Raman sideband cooling of the coupled modes with 10 second-order then 30 first-order pulses, the pump on F = I + 1/2 -> F' = I + 1/2 at 0.5 I_sat) and records every choice; run_preparation evaluates it with the M3 stages, the pumps' recoil heating added to the cooled occupations

conv.preparation_single_species_f0.corrected_form: the plan grants no species restriction (Section 3.2 lists 171Yb+, 40Ca+ optical, 43Ca+ clock and 137Ba+ presets, and Section 3.4's prepare stage carries no caveat), and until M6's fix the restriction was unrecorded and unescapable in practice: the refusal message named the escape hatch but no non-171Yb+ recipe existed anywhere in the repository, so run() was exercised on one species. The mixed-species half of the restriction stands: prep/ refuses a crystal of two species outright, while the crystal, mode and recoil layers all support one
conv.preparation_single_species_f0.equation: standard_recipe builds a recipe only for a SINGLE-SPECIES crystal (prep/recipe.py _structure) whose qubit's lower level is an F = 0 hyperfine state (its pump is the F = I + 1/2 -> F' = I + 1/2 line of the cycling transition); every other qubit - optical, Zeeman, and any mixed-species crystal - needs an explicit Device.preparation, which run() honours. device/presets.ca40_optical_recipe is the worked example for a 40Ca+ optical qubit: 397 nm Doppler cooling at -Gamma/2 along the oblique path with the 866 nm D3/2 repump, no sideband stage, and a pump into S1/2 mJ = -1/2 by 397 nm sigma- light along B with the same repump (the I = 0 analogue of the 171Yb+ F = 1 -> F' = 1 pump)

conv.preparation_stage_order.corrected_form: the second revision printed the reverse order (pump first); run.prepare (Appendix E) waits for M6, where the Device carries the recipe
conv.preparation_stage_order.equation: PreparationSequence refuses a sequence that does not start with Doppler cooling, a sub-Doppler stage with no Doppler precooling before it, and a pump followed by a cooling stage with no later pump; the hand-off State takes each mode's nbar from the LAST stage that addressed it and each ion's internal state from its last pump (or an explicit state for an unpumped coolant/qubit)

conv.pseudopotential_error_estimate.corrected_form: PLAN 4.1.7 writes 'in units of the mode spacing'; the only length in the clause is the ION spacing and that is the reading taken, since the quantity is the small parameter of Kaufmann's mechanism. A single ion has no Coulomb coupling to modulate and gets a note instead of a number. Nothing reported any of these before [M1 audit, fix batch]
conv.pseudopotential_error_estimate.equation: Device.derived() reports pseudopotential_error = max_i |u_1,i| / min_ij |r_i - r_j|, with u_1 = -(q/2) u_0 the signed excess-micromotion amplitude and the denominator the smallest inter-ion distance: the fractional rf modulation of the Coulomb curvature (~1/r^3, so delta K/K ~ 3 |u_1|/s) that makes the pseudopotential modes of 4.1.3 inexact off the rf null. It is exactly 0 for a chain on the null with no stray field. Also reported: ion_height_m and trap_depth_ev on the surface path (4.1.6 'the module reports h and the trap depth with every device that uses it') and second_order_doppler[i] (4.1.1 'reports the implied second-order Doppler shift for completeness')

conv.pulsed_transfer_matrix.corrected_form: three schedule optimizations (shared duration, independent durations, one duration per order with higher orders first) with a coarse grid before the bounded scalar search, because the occupation is oscillatory in the pulse time (a bounded minimizer alone returned 6.7 against the global 3.1 on Rasmusson's fixed-pulse schedule)
conv.pulsed_transfer_matrix.equation: column-stochastic transfer matrices on the Fock populations with the exact Laguerre elements, coherences discarded between pulses, N pulses composed as an ordered product; the plan's Rabi convention traps population at Omega_{n-1,n} t = 2 m pi (the sources' half-Rabi m pi); the stranded state of order k is round(n'_zero + k) with the first Laguerre zero as a continuous degree; a repump between pulses is a column-stochastic recoil kernel sum_k Poisson(k) K^k
conv.pulsed_transfer_matrix.section: 4.2.8 Pulsed sideband cooling; 13 Sideband-cooling trapping condition
conv.pulsed_transfer_matrix.source: qutip_trap/prep/sideband.py; Che et al. 2017 Eq. 2; Rasmusson et al. 2021 Eqs. 6-7
conv.pulsed_transfer_matrix.symbol: W_k(t): a_n = cos^2(Omega_{n,n-k} t/2), b_n = sin^2(Omega_{n,n-k} t/2), Omega_{n,n-k} = Omega_0 |<n-k|D(i eta)|n>|

conv.quadrupole_coupling.corrected_form: q = Delta m elsewhere; unit-normalized rank-2 tensors (sqrt(3/2) too large); r^2 Y_2m (sqrt(4 pi/5) too large); the lower-level 2j + 1 (sqrt 3 too small); air wavelengths in James's calcium panel and Roos's table; the Boulder Omega is half
conv.quadrupole_coupling.equation: Omega_{mm'} = (e E_0 k/(2 hbar)) |<S||r^2 C^(2)||D>| |Lambda(m, m')| |g^(q)| with q = m - m', k = 2 pi/lambda_vac the single beam's wavenumber, C^(2)_q = sqrt(4 pi/5) Y_2q (Racah), rank-2 tensors normalized to 2/3, A = c alpha k^5 |<||>|^2/(15 (2 j' + 1)) with the upper j'; carrier pi pulse at t = pi/Omega

conv.quadrupole_element_normalization.corrected_form: the (1/75)(omega/c)^5 convention gives exactly one fifth, so its elements are sqrt 5 larger; air wavelengths shift tau by 0.15%
conv.quadrupole_element_normalization.equation: A = (1/15)(omega/c)^5 |<v||Q||w>|^2/(2 j_v + 1) with the UPPER-state degeneracy, prefactor 1.11995e18/lambda[A]^5 s^-1 on vacuum wavelengths (Transition.quadrupole_convention = johnson_1_15)
conv.quadrupole_element_normalization.section: 13 Reduced quadrupole element for D-state lifetimes; 4.5.7
conv.quadrupole_element_normalization.source: Kreuter et al. 2005 Eqs. 7-8; W. R. Johnson's lecture notes

conv.qubit_dephasing_from_field_noise.corrected_form: the white field level is a device declaration (NoiseSpectrum.white_level), never inferred from the band
conv.qubit_dephasing_from_field_noise.equation: S_delta = (2 pi d1)^2 S_B (d1 in Hz/G, S_B in G^2/(rad/s)); gamma_phi = S_delta/2; the Ramsey coherence decays as e^{-gamma_phi t} (tests/test_noise_model.py)
conv.qubit_dephasing_from_field_noise.source: Section 13 chain: H_deph = b sigma_z, b = pi delta nu, S_b = S_delta/4, L = sqrt(gamma/2) sigma_z decays the coherence at gamma = 2 S_b(0)

conv.qubit_dephasing_operator.corrected_form: conventions giving 2/T2 elsewhere [row added after the 2026-09-04 critique]
conv.qubit_dephasing_operator.equation: coherence decays at gamma_phi, so gamma_phi = 1/T2 for the white component; a measured T2 is split into quasi-static (Gaussian) and white (exponential) parts before use

conv.qutip_spectrum_sign.corrected_form: the W(Delta -+ nu) closed form fed the SATURATED W is off by exactly 1 + s (nbar 9.7493e-5 against 6.4998e-5 at s = 0.5): Section 4.2.8 (vii)'s Omega << Gamma is enforced by rate_coefficients_from_model (M3a finding)
conv.qutip_spectrum_sign.equation: for a weak two-level drive QuTiP's spectrum at omega equals the scattering rate at the detuning Delta - omega, so the heating coefficient is A_+ = S_qutip(+nu) + 2D and the cooling one A_- = S_qutip(-nu) + 2D, with 2D = sum_channels alpha_q eta_em^2 Gamma rho_ee (one alpha per polarization channel and one eta_em per line from its own wavenumber); at Omega = Gamma/2, Gamma/nu = 0.02: S(+nu) = 6.71368e-3 against eta^2 W(Delta - nu) = 6.71410e-3 s^-1, 2D = 1.074137e-2 against alpha eta_em^2 W(Delta) = 1.074135e-2
conv.qutip_spectrum_sign.symbol: S_qutip(omega) = int exp(-i omega tau) <dF(tau) dF(0)> dtau = W(Delta - omega)

conv.rabi_frequency.corrected_form: Wineland 1998, Monroe 1995 and Blumel 2021 use P = sin^2(Omega t), half the usual Rabi frequency
conv.rabi_frequency.equation: H = (hbar Omega/2) sigma_+ e^{...} + h.c., carrier pi pulse at Omega t = pi

conv.rabi_from_intensity.corrected_form: Noek's s in the (Gamma/6, 2/3) detection form is I/(3 I_sat), the exact four-level result with one polarization share per sublevel (Sections 8.1, 8.8; derivation audit 2026-09-04)
conv.rabi_from_intensity.equation: E_0 = sqrt(2 I/(eps_0 c)); on the cycling transition this reduces to Omega = Gamma sqrt(I/(2 I_sat)) and s = I/I_sat = 2 Omega^2/Gamma^2 there only

conv.raman_beam_labels.corrected_form: Section 13's row wording 'beam 1 coupling to the upper level' is ambiguous (the intermediate level is 'upper' to both beams); the M0 pulses.py docstring repeated it and now states the frequency-ordering reading (M2)
conv.raman_beam_labels.equation: beam 1 is the higher-frequency beam ABSORBED from the lower qubit level and beam 2 the beam emitted into from the intermediate state, Omega_R = sum_e conj(Omega^(2)_{e up}) Omega^(1)_{e down}/(2 Delta_e); the tone at beat note omega_1 - omega_2 = omega_0 + mu drives |down> -> |up> with momentum k_1 - k_2
conv.raman_beam_labels.source: Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.3; AtomicStructure.raman_coupling_rad_s(g1 = lower, g2 = upper, beam1, beam2)
conv.raman_beam_labels.symbol: Delta k = k_1 - k_2, mu = (omega_1 - omega_2) - omega_0

conv.rayleigh_dissipator.equation: dissipator prefactor Gamma_el/4 while the coherence decays at Gamma_el/2, both consistent; Raman operators sqrt(Gamma_du)|u><d| carry the plain rate

conv.rb_error_rate.corrected_form: the first version of the plan labelled the entanglement infidelity the RB error rate, 1.5x (n = 1) and 1.25x (n = 2) too large, which would have offset every RB comparison of M10; Wright's 'p is the gate fidelity'; Chen's Eq. 3 conflates decay bases with rates and prints a singular matrix
conv.rb_error_rate.equation: an RB decay F(m) = A p^m + B reports r = (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n, the average error per Clifford ((1 - p)/2 for one qubit, (3/4)(1 - p) for two); (4^n - 1)(1 - p)/4^n is the entanglement infidelity of the depolarizing channel with the same p and is reported under that name (noise/summary.py rb_error_per_clifford and depolarizing_entanglement_infidelity; benchmarks/rb.py RBResult.error_per_clifford and depolarizing_entanglement_infidelity)
conv.rb_error_rate.source: Magesan, Gambetta and Emerson 2011; Wright et al. 2019; Chen et al. 2023

conv.rb_sequence_inverse.corrected_form: the inverse of each Clifford, the extraction error Section 7.9 corrects
conv.rb_sequence_inverse.equation: m uniform Cliffords are closed by the inverse of THEIR PRODUCT, computed from the ideal matrices, recognized as a Clifford of its own class (two qubits) and compiled as one more Clifford; the survival is P(every benchmarked qubit reads 0); B is fixed at 1/2^n when fewer than three lengths are scanned or fix_offset is set, since a tiny decay leaves A and B degenerate (benchmarks/rb.py)
conv.rb_sequence_inverse.source: Egan et al. 2021; Mount et al. 2015; Magesan 2011

conv.readout_chain_exact.corrected_form: the single-jump forms are the small-k-tau oracles: with one transition rate the exponential equals them to 1e-13; with both rates it differs by the second jump (1e-3 relative at Crain's 22 us). mcsolve needs the problem in units of the window (its collapse-time search has an absolute time tolerance)
conv.readout_chain_exact.equation: the count distribution over a window is one matrix exponential of the augmented generator (blocks Q - diag(lambda) with diag(lambda) one block up, an absorbing overflow block); the fast path samples the chain exactly (Gillespie) with Poisson counts at the piecewise rates, the trajectory path runs mcsolve on the class space with a photon-counting collapse operator
conv.readout_chain_exact.source: Markov-modulated Poisson process on the bright/dark/shelf chain (derived here); Crain Eq. 1 and Acton Eqs. 5-6 as its single-jump limits

conv.readout_crosstalk_added_counts.corrected_form: the product POVM is exact only at zero crosstalk: at 4 % leakage a dark 171Yb+ ion beside a bright one under the zero-threshold SNSPD protocol reads bright 34 % of the time (0.42 leaked counts in 22 us), the bounded, reported discrepancy of Section 9.5
conv.readout_crosstalk_added_counts.equation: a bright neighbour's leaked light is ADDED COUNTS on its neighbours at the configured PSF fraction AND extra off-resonant pumping on their chains (the 'depumping-reduced N' half, anchor.m5.crosstalk_depumping); the register confusion at configured crosstalk is factored by neighbour range (per-ion conditional tables over the ion's own LEVEL and its neighbours' start classes, exact for per-ion decisions on additive light with the neighbours' pumping frozen at their start class), dense to N = 12
conv.readout_crosstalk_added_counts.source: Wineland 1998 (degraded discrimination, not a changed eta_d); Burrell 2010 (PSF overlap); Acton 2006 Eq. 22 with the corrected I_sat

conv.readout_detected_line.corrected_form: the first M5 implementation summed every non-sink decay line, so a 40Ca+ 397 + 866 nm detection model counted the repump's 866 nm photons: R_o was high by exactly 1 + Gamma(D3/2<-P1/2)/Gamma(S1/2<-P1/2) = 1.0638, i.e. 6.4 %, and eps_B, eps_D and the whole budget with it. Exact for 171Yb+ only because its detection build carries one line. A repump's manifold also enters the model only when the DEVICE has a beam on that line: without the beam the metastable level is a dead end whose own lifetime is the slowest Liouvillian mode and the bright/dark coarse graining has no two-manifold slow mode at all
conv.readout_detected_line.equation: epsilon_sys carries exactly one epsilon_filter and an interference filter passes one wavelength, so R_o counts photons on the species' CYCLING line only: detection_rates_for_ion passes line = '<lower><-<upper>' of species.cycling, rates_from_bloch derives the single non-sink line when the build has one and REFUSES to guess when it has several, and line=ALL_LINES is an explicit all-line diagnostic (the total scattering rate W(Delta) of Section 4.2.2), never a detected rate
conv.readout_detected_line.symbol: R_det = eps_sys R_o on ONE line

conv.readout_likelihood_first_order.corrected_form: the exact forward likelihood on the chain's sub-bin kernel agrees with the first-order form to 1e-5 for the hypothesis matching the record and differs at the percent level for the hypothesis that must invoke a decay (its position inside the sub-bin), with the same decision; the linear brute force underflows near 227 sub-bins
conv.readout_likelihood_first_order.equation: the O(N) recursion in the log domain with log-sum-exp; the decay rate 1/tau is the dark class's rate of becoming bright (the shelf lifetime, or R_b); ties go to bright; the posterior error uses equal priors
conv.readout_likelihood_first_order.source: Myerson 2008 Eqs. 1-2; the exact hidden-Markov forward likelihood derived here (Section 8.7 gap)

conv.readout_micromotion_detection.corrected_form: micromotion_detection_rate existed but had no caller: neither light/bloch.py nor dynamics/multilevel.py carries a modulation index, so the R_o the readout ran on was unmodulated. R_d and R_b carry the same weighting; being linear in intensity with no saturation denominator they barely move (sum_n J_n^2 = 1) while R_o loses the sideband share, so micromotion RAISES the leakage ratio R_d/R_o - an M5 finding, not in any source
conv.readout_micromotion_detection.equation: the detection drive as a whole is phase modulated at the trap's rf frequency, so every rate the Bloch solve returns is the J-weighted sum of the carrier solve and the two first-sideband solves (three solves, the beams shifted by -/+ Omega_rf); readout_stage takes beta = k . u_1 for the SINGLE-photon wavevector of the shortest detection beam and Omega_rf from the trap's rf record, and reports the factor in the diagnostics
conv.readout_micromotion_detection.section: 8.8 'Micromotion on the detection beam'; 13 'J_n(beta) on every drive'
conv.readout_micromotion_detection.symbol: R_o(beta) = J_0(beta)^2 R(Delta) + J_1(beta)^2 [R(Delta - Omega_rf) + R(Delta + Omega_rf)]

conv.readout_polarity_scheme.corrected_form: the qubit label carries no polarity; the code refuses a scheme in which no level fluoresces
conv.readout_polarity_scheme.equation: bright/dark is a property of the readout SCHEME stored as an enum: 171Yb+ direct fluorescence has |1> = F = 1 bright; the 40Ca+ optical qubit has |0> = S1/2 bright and |1> = D5/2 the shelf; shelving transfer is a START distribution per level, so Pi_dark = sum_l p_l |l><l| is not rank one
conv.readout_polarity_scheme.source: Myerson 2008; Christensen 2020; Harty 2014 (direct fluorescence and shelving invert the polarity within one paper)

conv.readout_povm_indexed_by_level.corrected_form: the first M5 implementation sampled each ion's start class and then indexed the POVM by that class, applying the transfer channel TWICE: on a 40Ca+ shelving scheme with a 10 % transfer failure P(declared bright | shelved level) came out 0.1925 instead of 0.1002 (a factor 1.92), and on Harty-like transfer eps_D was 6.04e-4 instead of 3.04e-4. Invisible to the existing test because YB_DIRECT has an ideal transfer, where class and level coincide. A d > 2 leakage level now gets its own row instead of borrowing a qubit level's start distribution
conv.readout_povm_indexed_by_level.equation: the per-ion confusion is an (n_levels, 2) table P(declared | internal LEVEL) with the scheme's shelving/mapping transfer channel folded into the rows, so the fast path indexes it by the projectively sampled level and samples no start class of its own; the register-wide form runs its OWN axis over levels and a neighbour's axis over the neighbour's start class (all the leaked light depends on), marginalizing the neighbours with P(bright | level)

conv.readout_povm_monte_carlo.corrected_form: before this fix readout_stage built the product POVM unconditionally with n_samples = 0, and per_ion_confusion raises for anything but a threshold discriminator, so run(..., discriminator=TimeResolvedML(...)) raised in both readout modes: Section 8.3's strategy interface was advertised through run() and api.py but only the threshold strategy ran end to end
conv.readout_povm_monte_carlo.equation: a threshold discriminator's confusion is exact through the count distributions; every other strategy of Section 8.3 (time-resolved ML, adaptive, first-photon, camera) has no closed form, so readout_stage estimates it from povm_samples sampled records per level per ion (default 2e4, seeded from the run's root seed) and the POVM declares the binomial error bar it earned. readout='full' builds no POVM at all - the record path REPLACES it (Section 5.7) - and the (eps_B, eps_D) report then comes from the run's own records, with nan for a qubit level the circuit never populated

conv.repump_kernel_per_channel_alpha.corrected_form: the q = 9 vector-form sentinel of EmissionChannel.operator_qs no longer falls back to the isotropic 1/3 either: operator_angular_factor reads the channel's own tabulated alpha when the channel has a single polarization index and REFUSES a genuinely q-mixing one, whose alpha is the derived second moment of recoil.derived_angular_factors
conv.repump_kernel_per_channel_alpha.equation: the pulsed-cooling repump kernel of run_preparation computed cos_chi and then called angular_factor(None, cos_chi), which returns 1/3 for ANY cos_chi: a hard-coded isotropic alpha with a dead argument, against light/recoil.py's own 'no scalar alpha is ever hard-coded' and Section 4.2.8 (ii)'s 'one angular factor per channel and mode axis' (the M3 finding). The scalar a one-dimensional Fock kernel needs is now the photon-rate-weighted mean of alpha_q(chi) over the repump beams' own emitted polarization channels in their steady state, read off the BlochModel the recipe already builds for the pump; a polarization-pure repumper on a mode along B returns 2/5 or 1/5 and an unpolarized cycle 1/3
conv.repump_kernel_per_channel_alpha.symbol: alpha_eff = sum_k p_k alpha_{q(k)}(chi) / sum_k p_k

conv.response_phase_reference.corrected_form: the tone phases of every entangling pulse (scheduler and exact spot check alike) carry the arctan reference; the residual is what the exact check reports; a laboratory absorbs it in its phase calibration (M8's scans)
conv.response_phase_reference.equation: the first-order response delays the envelope, so the bichromatic beat note advances arctan(2 pi mu tau_r) = 0.766 rad (the phase of H(mu) = 1/(1 - i 2 pi mu tau_r)) before the field arrives and Roos's spin-axis tilt returns after the per-gate reset: fidelity 0.99700 with 2.9e-3 leakage uncompensated, 0.99974 / 2.2e-4 with the linear mu tau_r reference, 0.99992 / 3.3e-5 with the arctan reference against 0.99987 / 4.5e-5 for an ideal modulator
conv.response_phase_reference.source: check_noise.py 7 on the two-ion 171Yb+ fixture (mu/2pi = 3.06 MHz, tau_r = 50 ns: 2 pi mu tau_r = 0.96 rad)
conv.response_phase_reference.symbol: phi_leg -> phi_leg + sgn(mu) arctan(2 pi |mu| tau_r)

conv.rf_phase_and_parametric_heating.corrected_form: the MISSING DEVICE PARAMETER for the sideband channel is named: trap/heating.micromotion_sideband_heating_rate exists but needs the uncompensated stray field's rf GRADIENT at the ion, which the explicit-frequency Trap record does not carry (it has stray_field_v_per_m, a uniform field, not its rf-frequency gradient), so the channel is unreachable from a NoiseModel. The 2 omega_sec parametric term needs the fractional rf-amplitude density at 2 omega_sec, which S_V does supply - it is simply not implemented, and was previously recorded NOWHERE, which is the defect this record closes
conv.rf_phase_and_parametric_heating.equation: Section 6.2 requires both: 'rf amplitude and phase noise spectra S_V(omega) and S_phi(omega) are device parameters that drive the Omega_rf +- omega_t sideband heating of Section 4.1.5 and a parametric-heating term at 2 omega_sec'. conv.rf_phase_and_parametric_heating.source: M7 audit E-25 / A.1 (noise/model.py's rf_phase_noise field and its docstring; grep -rni parametric finds only surface-electrode geometry)

conv.rotation_generators.corrected_form: reading Maslov's R gates and Trout's XX through one generator convention is a factor 2 in the entangling angle; the plan's row exists to forbid the shared helper, and the code has none
conv.rotation_generators.equation: a single-qubit rotation carries theta/2 in the exponent, R(theta, phi) = exp[-i (theta/2)(cos phi sigma_x + sin phi sigma_y)], so GPi2(phi) = R(pi/2, phi) exactly and GPi(phi) = i R(pi, phi) (equal up to the global phase every fidelity measure quotients), with RZ(theta) = diag(e^{-i theta/2}, e^{i theta/2}); the two-qubit generator carries chi with NO 1/2, XX(chi) = exp(-i chi sigma_x (x) sigma_x), chi = pi/4 maximally entangling and the native MS angle theta = 2 chi in [0, pi/2]. No shared generator helper computes both: each is written where it is used (control/native.py gpi, gpi2, r_phi, rz, xx, ms, zz), because one factor 1/2 shared between the two conventions would halve every entangling angle. The consequence for the twirl is that Trout 2018's over-rotation probability p_xx = sin^2 alpha for exp(-i alpha XX) is the TWO-qubit case only, and it is exposed under that name (noise/summary.py over_rotation_twirl_probability)
conv.rotation_generators.source: Maslov 2017; Trout et al. 2018; control/native.py; control/two_qubit.py; noise/summary.py
conv.rotation_generators.symbol: R(theta, phi) carries theta/2; XX(chi) carries chi with no 1/2

conv.saturation_ceiling.corrected_form: the two-level Lorentzian's Gamma/2 applied to a degenerate manifold; a 'naive four-level' 1/2 for the 171Yb+ detection line
conv.saturation_ceiling.equation: P_f^max = (2J_f + 1)/((2J_i + 1) + (2J_f + 1)): Gamma/4 for 3 ground + 1 excited, Gamma/3 for a Lambda system, Gamma/2 for a two-level atom

conv.scattering_channels.corrected_form: the absorption factor in an eliminated jump operator is the plan's own construction (Section 13's 'never both in a collapse operator' rule is stated for the explicit multi-level builder); the recoil quanta per photon eta_abs^2 + alpha eta_em^2 are the test
conv.scattering_channels.equation: one operator per (emitted polarization, direction node): Rayleigh diagonal over the resolved levels (Gamma_el/4 dissipator prefactor automatically), one Raman operator per (a, b), the out-of-manifold rates summed into the SINK at d > 2 and reported at d = 2; the absorbed beam's e^{+i k_b x} multiplies the emission kick; six axis directions about B with weights alpha_par/2 and alpha_perp/2 are exact in the first and second moments for every dipole pattern and every mode axis; rates scale with the played intensity as (Omega/Omega_nom)^p, p the Stark scaling power
conv.scattering_channels.source: Uys 2010 Eqs. 6-8 (the diagonal Rayleigh operator), Ozeri 2007 (the recoil operator e^{i(k_L - k_s) x}), Joshi 2020 (the moment-exact direction quadrature); assembled in noise/scattering.py
conv.scattering_channels.symbol: L_{q', k_hat} = sqrt(w_k) sum_{a,b} r_{a->b q'} |b><a| (x) D(i(eta_abs - eta_em))

conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.corrected_form: SolverOptions.scattering_channels defaults to False, and run(..., internal_levels=3) used to leave it off, so a d = 3 register carried a SINK level that nothing could populate and reported no leakage estimate for it either: the plan's automatic behaviour was opt-in. An explicit scattering_channels=False is overridden rather than refused, because the plan offers no d > 2 mode without leakage simulation
conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.equation: run(..., internal_levels = d > 2) turns the flag on and records it in the run's notes; internal_levels = 2 keeps the d = 2 per-pulse estimate path of Section 4.3.2. The automatic switch turns on the register operators (leakage into the SINK, spin flips, the differential Rayleigh operator) WITHOUT the recoil displacements: Section 4.5.5's d > 2 requirement is about leakage, and the recoil-dressed operators (one per emission direction, per pulse, per branch) cost 30 to 50x more on the two-ion fixture, so they remain an explicit choice (scattering_channels=True with scattering_recoil='minimal' or 'vector'); a caller who set scattering_recoil='vector' keeps it
conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.section: 4.5.5 'Leakage is therefore simulated, not estimated, whenever d > 2'
conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.source: M7 audit E-10 (run/job.py; tests/test_run_noise.py leakage test); 2026-09-08 consolidation
conv.scattering_channels_at_d_gt_2.symbol: internal_levels > 2 => SolverOptions.scattering_channels = True, scattering_recoil = 'off' unless 'vector' was asked for

conv.scattering_rate_object.corrected_form: the two-level Lorentzian saturates at Gamma/2 where the four-level manifold saturates at Gamma/4; the second revision's Gamma/6 prefactor with (2/3) s_o folded one polarization share too few
conv.scattering_rate_object.equation: one multi-level optical-Bloch steady state supplies the cooling rate W(Delta) in s^-1, the readout rates R_o, R_d, R_b and the dark-state physics; every photon rate is asserted against the equal-population ceiling n_e/(n_e + n_g) of the resonant closed manifold (Gamma/4 for the 171Yb+ F = 1 -> F' = 0 cycle); R_o is the rate of the CONDITIONAL bright state from the slow-manifold coarse graining, because the full steady state of a detected ion sits in F = 0 with weight R_d/(R_d + R_b) ~ 0.95
conv.scattering_rate_object.symbol: W(Delta) = sum_lines sum_k Tr(C_k^dag C_k rho_ss)

conv.section_9_9_convergence_regime.corrected_form: none of the three comparisons was ever run: halving_test was called only from one synthetic unit test, evolve.tightened was exported and never called, and the 'convergence' pytest marker declared in pyproject.toml was used by zero tests. The run level now carries the first arm (SolverOptions.convergence_check repeats the evolution at atol/10, rtol/10 and reports the change in the register populations as Diagnostics.convergence, an addition to Appendix E's Diagnostics; off by default because it triples a run's cost, and the register populations are compared rather than the sampled histogram because they are deterministic), and hilbert.truncation.convergence_report runs all three arms of one validation case as three dynamics.evolve.ConvergenceReport values: tolerances/10, tolerances x10 started from options x10 so the pair is (loose, options), and every resolved cap and the ENR excitation cap + 2 at unchanged tolerances (grown_caps respects Section 9.9's dimension ceiling by leaving a mode whose growth would cross it). The cap arm's report has tolerances == tightened_tolerances, which is how it says the tolerances did not move

conv.servo_residual.corrected_form: the first version sampled raw quasi-static drift against a once-computed table, double-counting the slow band a laboratory servos away
conv.servo_residual.equation: a Drift with a servo bandwidth is high-passed into its residual band over the shot clock: the residual variance of an OU drift of correlation time tau is sigma^2/(1 + 2 pi f_s tau) in the continuous limit and the drift's increment sigma^2 (2 dt/tau) for a lock re-armed every sample; the first sample carries no offset (the calibration measured it)

conv.shim_field_response.corrected_form: the rod/blade path accepted shims, dropped them from residual_field_v_per_m, and folded them into dc_voltages() where one named like the endcap silently changed a_z instead of producing a field [corrected: M1 audit, fix batch]

conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.corrected_form: the plan says round-robin; blocks are the better physics and the deviation is deliberate. One quasi-static draw per contiguous block of the shot clock is what the hardware does, and it is the only allocation consistent with sample_times: round-robin would give every sample the same mean shot time, so an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Drift over the sample times would produce no between-sample spread at all, and the effective sample size would then be the shot count by construction. The M6 code already allocated blocks; its own module docstring and README claimed round-robin
conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.equation: shots are allocated in CONTIGUOUS BLOCKS, M_k = shots // S + 1 for the first shots % S samples, and sample k is drawn at the shot clock t0 + (sum_{j<k} M_j) T_rep; Diagnostics.shots_per_sample_realized reports the realized block sizes and Result.sample_of_shot the shot -> sample map Section 8.6 asks for
conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.source: qutip_trap/run/job.py; PLAN.md Section 3.4 ('distributes shots round-robin over samples')
conv.shot_blocks_per_sample.symbol: sample k owns shots [sum_{j<k} M_j, sum_{j<=k} M_j)

conv.sideband_lineshape.corrected_form: Wineland's and Bluemel's Omega^2/(Omega^2 + delta^2/4) sin^2(t sqrt(Omega^2 + delta^2/4)) is the same curve at half the Omega: fitting it returns Omega/2 (the negative control the test suite keeps), never the fit function
conv.sideband_lineshape.equation: the calibration fit function: a carrier pi pulse at Omega t = pi, half depth (the Lorentzian weight 1/2) at delta = Omega; fitted with weighted least squares to the fine scan of every line

conv.sign_A_hfs_and_g_factors.corrected_form: A > 0 removes the clock points (no 43Ca+ point in 1 to 4000 G, no 9Be+ root in 8 to 16 mT), the ingest test of the sign
conv.sign_A_hfs_and_g_factors.equation: A_hfs is a signed input inferred from mu_I when not printed (9Be+, 43Ca+, 171Yb+ 3D[3/2]1/2 inverted); measured g_J replaces Lande; Steck's g_S = +2.0023193 (CODATA g_e is negative); nuclear Zeeman in Steck's form with a plus sign in H_B
conv.sign_A_hfs_and_g_factors.section: 13 Sign of A_hfs and the g-factors; 4.5.6

conv.simultaneous_rb_units.corrected_form: the first version reported the JOINT decay's (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n as 'the error per Clifford' beside a budget whose unit was one single Clifford, a factor n apart, and the check script divided r_channel by 2 to compare them; anchor.m10.simultaneous_rb_crosstalk then read that factor 2 as a physical finding. Two independent qubits at r_q = r_channel = 3.426e-4 reproduce the committed joint fit p = 0.999080 to 3.5 % in (1 - p), so the composition already predicts the simultaneous decay. Separately, 'two_qubit = len(qs) == 2 and bool(run_kwargs.pop("pair", True))' short-circuited past its own pop on any qubit count but two, leaving pair= in the kwargs splatted into run() and raising TypeError: simultaneous RB on three ions, the natural use of a variant whose point is chain crosstalk, could not run at all
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.equation: simultaneous RB draws INDEPENDENT single-qubit Clifford sequences on several ions and plays them interleaved, so the group is the product C1 x ... x C1 and Section 13's n-qubit Clifford formula does not describe the joint decay. Every benchmarked qubit's own MARGINAL survival P(qubit q reads its target bit) is therefore fitted to A p_q^m + B and reported as r_q = (1 - p_q)/2 (RBResult.marginal_error_per_clifford), one Clifford on ONE qubit the unit -- the unit of the r that qubit measures alone and of the per-qubit composition budget.predicted['r_channel.q{i}'] = (Cliffords per sequence) x sum_kinds (pieces per Clifford) x (the kind's GATE_LOCAL channel reduced to THAT ONE qubit) -- and RBResult.error_per_clifford is their mean. The JOINT survival is fitted too and its (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n kept as RBResult.joint_error_per_layer, the error per LAYER of n Cliffords, which equals sum_q r_q to first order (0.2 % at r_q = 2e-5, 3 % at 3.4e-4 over m up to 512) and is compared with r_channel_joint_layer, the same composition over one layer with the channels reduced to ALL benchmarked qubits
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.section: 7.9 Randomized benchmarking variants; 6.6; 13 RB error rate; M10
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.source: Gambetta et al., PRL 109, 240504 (2012); Magesan 2011; benchmarks/rb.py; tests/test_m10_benchmarks.py
conv.simultaneous_rb_units.symbol: r_q = (1 - p_q)/2 per qubit; (1 - p)(2^n - 1)/2^n per layer

conv.solver_integrators.equation: the escalation ladder is dop853 then vern9; never a multistep method; atol 1e-10, rtol 1e-8

conv.solvers_read_the_device_modes.corrected_form: recorded rather than wired: threading the table's beliefs into the surrogate and the resolved-mode selection changes what M8's calibration converges to and what M9a's mode classes select, which is a change to those milestones' contracts and not to M4's pulse algebra. The shaping docstring no longer claims the override is in force
conv.solvers_read_the_device_modes.equation: Section 7.3's contract is that the solvers work at what the calibration table says and never at the device's hidden truth. In fact every production caller builds GateModes from the device's crystal: gate_modes has a mode_frequencies_hz override that no caller passes, CalibrationTable.lamb_dicke is written by the sideband experiment and read by no solver, and gate_modes has no eta override at all

conv.space_declaration_before_allocation.corrected_form: M9a evaluated the guard AFTER the allocation: HilbertSpace.__post_init__ -> check() -> qt.tensor(*factor_identities()) formed an O(D)-non-zero CSR identity, and only then did run() call within_budget. Measured: 2 ions x 5 modes at d = 16 (dimension 4194304) cost +64 MB inside check(), and the eight-ion eight-mode case Section 5.4 cites would have needed about 86 GB there and died before the guard could reroute it. A Kronecker product's shape is the product of its factors' shapes, so check() now asserts shape == prod(dims) arithmetically and forms the joint identity only below IDENTITY_CHECK_MAX_DIMENSION = 65536; a HilbertSpace is therefore a DECLARATION that allocates nothing (every operator on it is lazy and cached), select_space evaluates within_budget on it and returns the verdict as SpaceSelection.budget, and run() reads that verdict. Deviation from the audit's recommendation: no separate SpaceDeclaration type and no HilbertSpace.declare classmethod were added, because after this fix the space object and the declaration are the same value and a parallel dataclass duplicating its six fields would drift An explicit level='JOINT_EXACT' above the guards used to proceed with a note ('JOINT_EXACT forced above the Section 11.5 guards'); on 2026-09-08 the ENR end-to-end test built a 37752-dimensional space that way ([2, 2, 11, 13, 66], the two resolved x modes beside a 66-dimensional ENR factor), took 20 GB of memory and an hour before QobjEvo rejected its term, so run() now REFUSES the explicit level above the guards with the dimension, the non-zeros and the two knobs named (raise joint_dimension_max / nnz_max to build it deliberately); the test runs at N_exc = 2 (dimension 3432) and pins the refusal at N_exc = 10
conv.space_declaration_before_allocation.equation: Section 11.5: the monitor refuses to build joint spaces above a configurable dimension (default 4096) or non-zero estimate (default 2e7) and directs the run to GATE_LOCAL
conv.space_declaration_before_allocation.source: hilbert/space.py check, IDENTITY_CHECK_MAX_DIMENSION; run/space.py select_space, SpaceSelection.budget; run/job.py; tests/test_m9_scaling.py

conv.spectator_dephasing_gaussian.corrected_form: a constant-rate sigma_z Lindblad term would give an exponential lineshape; the distance dependence between the two anchors is interpolated as a power law of exponent 3.5 (apparatus data, not physics)
conv.spectator_dephasing_gaussian.equation: a spectator's coherence during a neighbour's detection decays as a Gaussian; implemented as a quasi-static frequency offset drawn per shot from N(0, sqrt(2)/alpha), whose ensemble average reproduces the Gaussian exactly
conv.spectator_dephasing_gaussian.source: Crain 2019 Fig. 3 (alpha = 94(5) ms at 200 um, 814(77) ms at 370 um, 1716(80) ms baseline)

conv.spin_motion_phases.corrected_form: Lee writes phi_S = -(half-sum); the second revision's '+phi' axis would have certified a quarter-turn error
conv.spin_motion_phases.equation: phi_s = (phi_b + phi_r)/2, phi_m = (phi_b - phi_r)/2 of the two tone phases; the bichromatic force acts about phi_s + pi/2 in the same-Delta-k geometry (i eta(a + a^dag) carries an i), so MS(phi_0, phi_1, theta) sets phi_s,i = phi_i - pi/2 (control/schedule.py)
conv.spin_motion_phases.source: Haljan 2005; Lee 2005 (opposite sign, converted at ingest); derivation audit 2026-09-04 (row 4.3-5)

conv.stark_compensation.corrected_form: an uncompensated -38 Hz light shift over the 100 us fixture gate costs about 1e-3 of fidelity (an uncompensated 0.024 rad sigma_z rotation per ion); the M6 surrogate carried no Rabi or Stark entry for the entangling drive's beams, so its gate had no light-shift physics at all; M8 seeds them. Without the phase reference the compensated axis rotates by 2 pi delta_s t_start: a compensated GPi2 one millisecond into a schedule lost 1.5e-2 = (2 pi 38 Hz 1 ms)^2/4 on the two-ion fixture while the same pulse at t = 0 was exact, and the Bell circuit through run() read 4.2e-3 against M6's 2.35e-3 (anchor.m8.compensation_phase_reference)
conv.stark_compensation.equation: every tone of a scheduled pulse is detuned by the table's differential light shift for the played amplitude; both legs of a bichromatic segment move together (the motion phase is untouched); a correct belief keeps the pulse resonant with the shifted qubit, a wrong one leaves a reproducible detuning. The tones are phase-continuous in absolute time (the builder plays e^{-i(2 pi mu t - phi)}), so every compensated tone also carries the phase 2 pi delta_s(0) t_start (compensation_phase_rad) that references the compensation detuning to the qubit frame at the pulse start, minus, inside a multi-segment gate, the frame 2 pi int delta_s dt the earlier segments accumulated; the frame update after the pulse is 2 pi int delta_s dt (stark_phase_rad, frame_after)

conv.stark_scaling_with_amplitude.corrected_form: the M4 scheduler scaled every Stark entry as (Omega/Omega_cal)^2; on a Raman waveform played at 550 times the derived carrier Rabi frequency of a weak beam pair that turned a -0.1 Hz shift into -70 kHz and tripped the boundary monitor (M6 finding, never exercised by the M4 tests, whose tables had no Stark entries)
conv.stark_scaling_with_amplitude.equation: p = 1 for a two-photon (Raman or light-shift) drive, whose Rabi frequency and differential Stark shift are both proportional to the intensity; p = 2 for a single-photon optical drive (Omega proportional to the field) and a microwave drive (the ac Zeeman shift proportional to B_1^2)
conv.stark_scaling_with_amplitude.source: Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.10 (shift proportional to intensity); PLAN.md Section 4.3.2

conv.static_error_primitive.corrected_form: Mount's R = exp[-(i/2) theta (1 + eps)(sigma_phi + delta Z)] and Cummins' quaternion pulse (axis (cos phi, sin phi, eps_d)/sqrt(1 + eps_d^2), angle theta sqrt(1 + eps_d^2)) identify eps_a = g and eps_d = f = delta/nu_1 with no rescaling on ingest
conv.static_error_primitive.equation: M = exp[-i theta {(1 + eps_a) rho(phi).sigma + eps_d sigma_z}/2], rho(phi) = (cos phi, sin phi, 0), exact for a square segment under time-independent errors; leading coefficients at theta = pi in 1 - F_K: primitive (pi^2/4) eps_a^2 and eps_d^2 exactly
conv.static_error_primitive.section: 4.3.5 The static error primitive; 13 Detuning symbols

conv.surface_electrode_geometry.corrected_form: y0/h/d for one height; the rf Hessian angle used as a mode axis; a maximum finder for a saddle; the first plan version's sqrt(a(a + b)) with a as an unstated half-width

conv.trajectory_count_two_phases.corrected_form: trajectory_target_tol defaults to None (the fixed ntraj with its keyed seed list, the M6 behaviour), because QuTiP 5.3.1's target_tol accepts a zero-variance first batch: on a damped two-level system it returned 26 trajectories at tol 0.1 and 604 at 0.02, but 2 at 0.005, 0.001 and (0.005, 0.0), where the first two trajectories had both jumped and the estimated error was exactly 0. conv.trajectory_grid_tau_c.corrected_form: the previous default of 4 gave dt = 0.785/omega_max, 7.9x coarser than the plan's rule, and the constant tau_c/10 appeared nowhere in the repository. The generator remains the spectral method rather than the exact OU update, which is the more general choice for an arbitrary tabulated S and is what the periodogram test validates; the plan's 'exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck update' sentence is a deviation recorded here
conv.trajectory_grid_tau_c.equation: the shortest correlation time a tabulated band carries is that of its fastest component, tau_c,min = 1/omega_max, so the rule reads dt <= 1/(10 omega_max); time_grid sets dt = pi/(omega_max x oversample), which meets it at oversample >= 10 pi = 31.4159
conv.trajectory_grid_tau_c.section: 5.5 'an independent fixed grid with Delta t <= tau_c/10'

conv.two_photon_rabi.corrected_form: one symbol meaning Omega/2 in two subsections and Omega in a third inside two-photon formulas that differ by exactly the factor 2 the plan hunts
