The module treats a multiplicative spectrum as additive with β_a = (Ω_l/Ω_max)β and reports that it has done so.
- **No second-order filter function**, hence no quantitative error bar on the first-order path beyond |n-point term| ≤ O(ξ^n); F_zz^{(2)} is used by Green Eq. 34 but defined only in Green, Uys and Biercuk, PRL 109, 020501 (2012). Relatedly there is no closed second Magnus term for an arbitrary sequence (only SK1's), so every ĉ_{m+1} and the cross-term ĉ_{1,1} is fitted numerically.
- **Two published dc floors do not reproduce.** With the corrected Ω^{−2(m+1)} normalization, only SK1's floor matches the figure it is read from (5.8736 × 10⁻⁶ against 5.86 × 10⁻⁶). BB1 recomputes to 3.5368 × 10⁻⁹ against a quoted 3.9 × 10⁻⁹ (10% low) and CORPSE to 1.6725 × 10⁻⁹ against a quoted 3.0 × 10⁻⁹ (a factor 1.8), and a back-solve from the figure would need ĉ₂ ≈ 0.012 against two independent high-precision computations agreeing on 0.006500751892 to nine digits. The simulator carries the computed coefficients and records the discrepancy rather than tuning to the figure.
- **No infrared regulator is supplied by any source**, yet on the ω⁻⁴ spectra a real trap shows, χ genuinely diverges for free induction, the Hahn echo and every odd-n sequence. ω_min is therefore the implementer's choice, materially changing absolute numbers; the plan ties it to the total experiment duration, records it as a tagged assumption and prints it beside every χ. Biercuk's own unexplained odd-n excess error (≈10% against ≈1% at even n, persisting to n = 10) is a known mismatch between this model class and that data set: a faithful finite-τ_π implementation **does** contain a large odd-n penalty, but whether it explains the data is open and the simulator is not tuned to its magnitude.
- **No trapped-ion parameters or measured spectra anywhere in this topic.** Green's Gaussian test spectrum, Kabytayev's hand-normalized 1/f benchmark at Ω = 1.5 × 10⁶ rad/s and Biercuk's un-normalized ambient spectrum are all synthetic or uncalibrated, and Biercuk's ambient case additionally drifts in real time including spur positions. Every absolute infidelity from this layer is therefore conditional on the device's own S_B, S_Ω and (ε_A, ε_D, ε_N), which are user inputs with provenance.
- **No scheduler objective.** Nothing converts a sequence's total rotation angle into a spontaneous-scattering probability, motional heating or laser-power cost, and nothing gives a rule for choosing a composite family from a measured error triple against a target infidelity. The closest published aids are Low-Yoder-Chuang's κ (valid only for same-order, same-γ comparisons, and its Table III values were not transcribed) and the saturation condition |δ| ∼ |ε|^n. Every dc coefficient, filter function and crossover in the sources is quoted at θ = π while the sequences are defined for arbitrary θ, so the θ dependence of the prefactors is unmapped.
- **Nothing beyond square pulses, and nothing about a DD train of composite pulses.** Every derivation in the topic is piecewise-constant; Green states explicitly that continuous modulation can be evaluated only approximately. There is no filter function for a decoupling sequence whose π pulses are themselves composite (a BB1 or a DCG inside a CPMG or UDD train), which is precisely the construction the finite-pulse degradation result points to as the fix, and the plan's own chip-trap practice (Section 7.8) uses Gaussian-enveloped SK1.
- **Nothing non-Gaussian, non-stationary or quantum-bath, and no phase-noise quadrature.** Every usable result needs zero-mean Gaussian wide-sense-stationary classical noise, which is also what licenses W = e^{−χ} and the moment closure. Telegraph noise, two-level fluctuators, spin baths, slow drift and laser phase noise as a spectrum are outside the model, and the cross-spectrum S_ad is assumed exactly zero.
- **No errata search was performed and only arXiv preprints were read.** Roughly twenty printed defects were repaired across five papers in this topic, which is itself a reason to check the journal versions (PRA 70 052318; PRA 67 042308; Adv. Chem. Phys. 154 241; PRA 89 022341; PRA 90 012316; NJP 15 095004; PRA 79 062324) before shipping any of them. Until then every **[corrected]** tag here is brief-derived, not a published erratum.
- **One brief-level check did not reproduce and one is a typo in the Run 5S brief.** The Run 5S brief's assertion that Wimperis's W1 = R(π, φ)R(2π, 3φ)R(π, φ) equals −I is wrong in the plan's own generator convention: it is **+I** (two π pulses give −I, the 2π filler gives −I). And the Run 5S brief's "2.9 × 10²⁰" for the SK1 dc floor with Ω⁻⁴ omitted recomputes as 2.97 × 10¹⁹; the physics of the trap it illustrates is unaffected. Both are recorded so that a future reader does not "fix" the tests back to the Run 5S brief.
- **No hyperfine (F-basis) version of the coherent-population-trapping Liouvillian.** The excited-to-ground coherence-transfer structure is given in J and m_J only. For 171Yb+ the branching among F′ levels and the corresponding 6j coherence-transfer weights are needed and absent, and the dark-state coefficient vectors are transcribed only for the 1 ↔ 0 and 1 ↔ 1 entries of the source's table (each needing the σ-index repair), so the general J_i ↔ J_i and J_i ↔ J_i − 1 vectors that a large-J or D₅/₂-P₃/₂ case would need are unavailable. Section 8.1's ceiling assertion is therefore the only guard the detection module has against a wrong dark-state basis.
- **The species-specific dark-resonance map exists for one species.** The S-P-D Raman-resonance zeros and the optimum destabilizing field are transcribed only for 88Sr+ (P_f vanishing at δ_B = (5/22)γ and (5/6)γ with the optimum at δ_B ≈ 0.05γ). The Ca+ and Ba+ values, and the general recipe for locating those zeros from g-factors and detunings, are missing, so a per-species destabilization optimizer cannot be guarded away from them; and the ac Stark shift of the cooling line by a strong repumper is only remarked on qualitatively, so line-centre pulling by the destabilizing beam cannot be predicted.
- **The corrected Λ-arm repumper window is a Run 5 repair with no published erratum.** What follows from the rate-equation steady state is (1 − α)R_d > αR_i, i.e. √α Ω_SP < Ω_DP < γ/2; the printed condition is too strong by 1/α² (about 200× for Ca+ and Sr+) and leaves no valid operating point. The repair is cross-checked only against the source's own figure, and it consumes the 40Ca+ P₁/₂ branching fraction, which is itself uncertain at the 30% level (1:12 in one source, 1:16 in another for the same quantity, with later work nearer 1:17.6 and no dedicated measurement verified in any run). Section 4.2's repumper design therefore carries a 30% uncertainty that no test can remove.
- **The collision bound is not reproducible from its own coefficients.** Recomputing R = Σ_s Γ_s p_s/(k_BT) at 300 K with 10⁻¹¹ mbar of each partner gives 4.36 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ against the printed "< 3 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹"; the source states no temperature and no conversion rule, and its 50/50 N₂/H₂ composition is imported from a different apparatus. The neglect conclusion survives either way, but 3 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ must not be presented as derived, and the coefficients themselves are quoted rather than measured by the reporting paper, so error bars and level assignments need the 1995 primary source. Because collisional decay is indistinguishable in shape from natural decay, any higher-pressure comparison must be measured at several pressures and extrapolated.
- **Blackbody physics for the Ca+ D levels stops at the D-D M1 channel.** There is no BBR-driven D → P depopulation estimate for Ca+, no temperature-dependent correction to the measured 1168 and 1176 ms, and no ambient-temperature formula, so "what is the 40Ca+ D₅/₂ lifetime at 4 K or 350 K" cannot be answered from the source set - unlike 88Sr+, whose D₅/₂ → P₃/₂ channel Section 4.5.7 now quantifies. Also absent: the 729 and 854 nm laser-induced deshelving rates that dominate real experiments, which the reshelving rate equation parameterizes as a single R without predicting it.
- **The Raman and Rayleigh dissipators still carry no recoil operator.** They are internal-state only, with no photon-recoil kick, no scattering-induced heating rate and no Lamb-Dicke dressing - only the source's remark that the per-π-pulse probability rises by 1/η for sidebands, with no operator form. The twelve-operator polarization-gradient kernel of Section 4.2.4 is the only recoil model any Run 5 source supplies, and its transfer to the scattering channels is untested. Related and still open: no criterion for the detuning at which Rayleigh suppression sets in, and no unified formula spanning the clock-state 1/Δ⁴ and the general 1/Δ² regimes, which would need the Ozeri 2005 and 2007 papers transcribed properly rather than through the rejected rate-difference form.
- **Wineland 2003 Eqs. 2.5-2.9 and 2.11-2.12 remain untranscribed.** The most consequential is the net 9Be+ Stark shift, which pairs all eight coefficient sets of the general scattering rate with the same detunings at first power and is what a simulator needs in order to null a differential shift - and is the counter-example that makes the clock-qubit shift's non-nullability meaningful. Also missing: the Rabi-flopping equations that define the half-angle π-pulse convention, the displacement operator and sideband Rabi frequencies, and the Debye-Waller factors the paper names as necessary outside the Lamb-Dicke limit but never gives.
- **The two polarization-gradient layers have no transfer path between them.** The analytic model's 1/3, 1/9, 16/9, 2/9 and 8ξ² prefactors are specific to j_g = ½ ↔ j_e = ½; the sources explicitly warn they fail for j_e = 3/2, and whether they carry to the 171Yb+ F = 1 → F′ = 0 scheme is asserted by nobody, that source printing no display equations at all. The only bridge is the derived, unverified s_Joshi = (3/2)s₀(Γ/2)²/((Γ/2)² + Δ²), so no closed-form light-shift depth, pumping rate, cooling rate prefactor or steady state exists for the 171Yb+ scheme - only the measured s₀² exponent - and the criterion "light-shift depth ≈ ħω/2 gives one quantum" cannot be turned into a numeric test. There is also no j_g = ½ ↔ j_e = 3/2 model at all, which is the relevant case for D2-line cooling.
- **Polarization-gradient cooling has no B-field dependence, no D branch, no 3D form and no model outside the Lamb-Dicke regime.** The analytic model omits Zeeman shifts entirely, so it cannot predict how cooling degrades as the Zeeman splitting approaches the detuning or as the quantization axis tilts off the beams; it omits the P₁/₂ → D₃/₂ branch the experiment handles with an 866 nm repumper, so the three-manifold Liouvillian and the repumper rate needed to keep the four-level reduction valid are both absent; everything analytic is 1D along one axis, with no multi-beam geometry, no planar-crystal theory and no 3D Doppler closed form; and outside η√(⟨n⟩ + ½) ≪ 1 there is only the observation that the limit rises and the optimum shifts to larger ξ. Multi-ion use additionally needs per-mode Lamb-Dicke parameters that neither source supplies, and one source's trap-frequency triple is unlabelled by axis in a way a normal-mode recomputation contradicts.
- **Two published corrections behind the Run 5 numbers are unobtainable.** The intensity-dependent analytic correction for ²P₁/₂ F = 1 scattering that the 171Yb+ theory curves carry comes from an unpublished companion reference, so a from-scratch simulation cannot overlay those panels; and the derivation of the three-point recoil weights is credited to a 1993 paper that does not show it, so generalizing them to a different quantization-axis geometry is not possible from the source set.
- **Provenance ceiling.** Every Run 5 source was verified against an arXiv e-print, all published versions being paywalled or bot-walled, and the errata check of 2026-09-04 found no published erratum for any of them. So the repairs this topic makes on its own authority - the reversed dark-state pairing, the "≈ 63°" misprint, the reciprocal θ_BE mapping, the 2π/Φ harmonic count, the repumper inequality, the omitted −i/ħ, the Γ-versus-√Γ jump scaling and the coherent recoil sum - stand on this plan's recomputation and are tagged brief-derived rather than published errata. One preprint's title differs from the published title under the same DOI, and the 171Yb+ Letter appeared about 17 months after its only preprint version, so its numbers could have been revised in proof.
- **No merge model exists in any source.** Every splitting formula in the Run 5 set is one-directional. Nothing states whether the time reverse of a split waveform is optimal, how the relative motional phase of the two wells at the moment of merging enters, how merge excitation scales with duration, or what a merge costs; one source recombines ions only for state detection and reports no merge budget, and the other reports a single combined split-and-combine duration without saying whether it covers one operation or the pair. There is also no data on repeated split-merge cycling or cumulative excitation over a circuit. Section 4.6 therefore specifies merging as the plan's own construction - the time reverse of the split with an explicit relative-phase parameter - tagged **[background]**, and milestone M12's exit criteria cannot test it against anything.
- **Diabatic transport with zero final excitation is a criterion, not a protocol.** The Fourier condition on the well acceleration says when the excitation vanishes but no source supplies a solved family: no bang-bang or two-well-hop construction, no integer-secular-period timing condition beyond the idealized impulsive case, and no invariant-based inverse-engineered trajectory. The only anchor is the published Sterk statement that one shortcut-to-adiabaticity trajectory is the lowest-order member of its Bézier family, near the boundary of the feasible space. Closing this needs Torrontegui et al. 2011, Fürst et al. NJP 16, 075007 (2014) and Kaushal et al. (2020), none of which was read.
- **Quantum dynamics through the splitting critical point are absent.** Every splitting treatment in the set is classical, with phonon numbers obtained post hoc as ΔE/(ħω_f) - an explicit ceiling, not a state. Missing: the second-quantized two-ion Hamiltonian through the critical point, the mode structure where the external well is purely quartic (the harmonic normal-mode picture fails there), the squeezing generated by the frequency collapse to ω_CP, and any wavefunction-level criterion for when the classical treatment fails, beyond the empirical remark that the Lamb-Dicke regime is regained above roughly 40 µs. Section 4.6's two-ion Hessian at the critical point (COM = ω_CP exactly, stretch stiffer by √(5/3)) is the plan's own derivation, corroborated only by another trap's simulated 880/700 kHz ratio of 1.257, and is tagged **[background]** pending an independent re-check.
- **The splitting adiabatic-suppression constant is undefined in its source.** The exponent constant of δE′ = δE exp[c²(1 − 1/χ)] occurs exactly once in the whole e-print, inside that formula, and cannot be evaluated from the paper; it is an O(1) fit parameter, with c ≈ 0.93 the value that reproduces the source's own statement that single-phonon splitting needs several hundred microseconds. Relatedly, the printed impulsive chain and the printed closed form differ by exactly 4, so the printed π²/8 must be used as a pair with the fitted ξ² = 0.1 and never re-derived.
- **The published error-function transport quanta figures do not reproduce.** The factor 2 in the erf suppression amplitude was independently re-derived and is correct as printed, yet with it the source's own sub-quantum claims fail (γ = 3.259 at y = 12 for 400 µm, γ = 4.322 at y = 13 for 2.2 mm). Both come out right only if the 2 is dropped, so the paper's numerics almost certainly lost it. The equations are the regression targets and the two quanta figures are recorded as disagreements; the design conclusion (a smooth ramp beats a sine ramp by roughly an order of magnitude in duration) survives, since the defect is only about 3% in the control parameter.
- **No electrode basis potentials exist in any Run 5 source.** No published basis set, no objective function or regularization for the constrained voltage solve, no derivation of the residual acceleration from geometry, and no coefficient rows for the alternative trap geometries a regression suite would need. One source's boundary-element model is unpublished and accurate only to 10% in axial frequency; another simulated exactly one trap. The dominant real-world excitation channel - residual force and curvature from finite electrode structure - therefore has no quantitative model, and the practically dominant failure mode, a 3 mV offset near the critical point driving n̄ above 15, cannot be predicted. Section 4.1.6's gapless-plane layer is the plan's own substitute and carries its own **[background]** tag.
- **No bridge from residual quanta to a circuit-level error model.** Nothing maps a residual n̄ or a residual coherent displacement onto Mølmer-Sørensen or light-shift gate infidelity, onto spin dephasing accumulated during a shuttle, or onto a Kraus channel; one source cites the claim that single quanta of coherent excitation cost fidelity and gives no formula. There is no composition rule for the hundreds of transports in a schedule, and the inter-segment motional-phase bookkeeping (which needs the unimodular phases the closed forms drop) is unspecified. The one published two-qubit budget carries no transport row and does not close against its own measurement (an upper bound of <7.2 × 10⁻³ against a measured zone average of 7.9(4) × 10⁻³, with rows summing to 7.3 × 10⁻³), so the absence of a transport row is not evidence that transport heating is negligible; the plan carries the residue as a per-gate modelling uncertainty of order 10⁻³ rather than resolving it.
- **Mixed-species transport and splitting have no model.** The only statement in the set is that a different sympathetic-cooling species "will require special consideration since all modes will be excited during both diabatic transport and separation". There are no mass-ratio mode-participation expressions, no mixed-species normal-mode spectra for the crystals actually used (needed both to turn one fitted temperature into per-mode occupations and to model sympathetic cooling rates, which scale with the coolant eigenvector amplitude), no species-dependent well positions, and no differential pseudopotential barrier at a junction. Palmero et al. PRA 90, 053408 (2014) is cited but was not read.
- **Micromotion is absent from both splitting frameworks and unquantified at a junction apex.** Both splitting treatments assume the ions sit on the rf node with tight radial confinement persisting throughout, so neither contains a pseudopotential term or any micromotion at all: no Mathieu treatment, no radial-axial coupling during transport or splitting, no tilt-induced mode rotation and no radial-mode excitation, even though scaling the axial frequency necessarily moves the radials. At a junction apex, where the axial rf field and hence the micromotion are maximal, the only quoted amplitude is a model estimate at a deliberately low-gradient zone 880 µm away, and that number is not self-consistent in one peak-or-rms convention.
- **The inter-segment state hand-off is unspecified.** The closed-form amplitude solution holds only at constant frequency and the squeezing parameters depend on the past evolution, but no source prescribes how to propagate the Ermakov state (ρ, ρ̇, μ), the accumulated squeezing (δ, θ) and the coherent phase across a transport, a split, a junction and a merge - which is exactly what accumulating squeezing over a multi-segment schedule requires. Section 4.6 specifies that carry-across as the plan's own construction.
- **Junction coverage is single-apparatus and dated.** One source family supplies the rf pseudopotential barriers, the apex axial anti-confinement, the frequency schedule and two technical noise channels, and its junction is a two-wafer three-dimensional design with rf bridges rather than a modern surface-electrode junction. Missing: surface-trap junction barrier structure, an explicit-Ω_rf or Floquet treatment of micromotion at the apex, the excitation cost of crossing a large-micromotion region, and two-dimensional transport with rotating principal axes. The DAC-comb artefact that dominated the measured excitation is 2011 hardware and is specified as an optional term.
- **The splitting voltage recipe is not geometry-general, and its counterexample is a surface trap.** Its source assumes that "any reasonable segmented trap geometry will exhibit similar characteristics", yet its own tabulated surface trap with a segmented ground plane has the centre and splitting quartic coefficients sign-flipped relative to every three-dimensional design, and the authors warn that the quartic Taylor truncation itself breaks down there. This bears directly on Section 4.1.6, which is the plan's surface-electrode layer. Relatedly, the quartic expansion is used at or past its own stated validity edge: it holds while the well separation is small against the segment width, but the critical-point separation is already a sizeable fraction of the segment spacing and the final separation exceeds it, with no error estimate supplied.
- **Splitting excitation has no external validation and N > 2 is unquantified.** The measured budgets present are 1.4 to 2.1 quanta per two-ion split with partial de-excitability and a simulated floor near one phonon at tens of microseconds; a nine-ion partitioning result reports reliability across all combinations but no excitation numbers, and one two-ion transport result is qualitative only. Ruster et al. 2014, Kaufmann et al. 2017, Kaushal et al. 2020 and the Quantinuum QCCD reports would be the external checks and were not read.
- **Transport-induced decoherence and recooling are unmodelled.** Every Run 5 transport entry is unitary apart from an ambient-heating rate: no dephasing rate during transport, no spin-motion entanglement from the waveform, no magnetic-field-gradient phase along the path, and no coherence budget per shuttle beyond one spin-echo 1/e time and one qualitative Ramsey verification. No cooling-time budget as a function of the excitation to be removed is given, and no source reports a post-cooling occupation for any cooling stage, so the residual n̄ entering a gate is a free parameter.
- **Transport failure and reordering rates are unquantified, with a known undetected path.** The sources describe such events only as "rare" and "automatically detected and scrubbed", and the crystal-mode-structure probe used to catch them is explicitly blind to events that swap the qubit ions and to multiple reorderings that restore the correct order before the probe. The heralded-erasure channel of Section 4.6 therefore has no rate and a known undetected-error path with no bound.
- **None of the Run 5 transport corrections could be checked against a version of record.** Every verification was against arXiv preprints, publisher pages having been unreachable during the run, and the splitting source exists as arXiv v1 only. About ten printed defects are corrected across Section 4.6; each should be re-checked against the journal text before it enters a code comment, and each is brief-derived rather than a published erratum.

**What the derivation audit does not establish (2026-09-04).** The audit re-derived equations from the plan's stated conventions and confirmed or corrected them numerically; it did not check citations against the source PDFs, so the provenance claims about printed errors (Wineland's Eq. 62, Brownnutt's Eq. 14, Turchette's Eq. 2) rest on the errata check and on internal consistency; it left every empirical species input unverified (ε_sys presets, background rates, measured branching ratios, reduced-element values are ingest data, not derivable quantities, and both derivers of the readout rows said so); it audited equations, not the code that will implement them; four rows rest on one blind derivation and one on one adjudicator, and about fifteen setups were judged insufficient, so a handful of confirmations rest on a guessed convention that happened to match. Five items it left open are recorded here so that they are not mistaken for settled: which triangle of the displacement matrix ⟨n′|D|n⟩ a plan sentence calls 'above' the diagonal (now stated explicitly in Section 5.1.1, but the modulus is transpose-symmetric and nothing computable depends on it); the 171Yb+ P₁/₂ → D₃/₂ reduced element, whose value hinges on using the 2.438 µm channel wavelength rather than the 935 nm repump (Section 4.5.6 now pins it); the number of digits at which the 87Rb reference elements are quoted, which follow the stored lifetime (Section 4.5.6); the sign branch of the entangling angle, which Section 4.4.3 now states as |χ| = π/4 modulo π/2 with the compiler's sign; and the apparatus quantities of Section 8 (detection efficiencies, background rates, the D₃/₂ branching), which no derivation can supply. The two equations that lost their comparer to the output caps, the transverse Hessian of Section 4.1.3 and the emission angular factors of Section 4.2.8, keep their earlier tags and the committed check scripts behind them (`check_recoil.py`, `check_surface_mixed.py`), and are the first candidates for a second audit pass.

**What the 2026-09-04 four-lens critique changed and what it left open.** The critique of Appendix D (four lenses, 64 findings) was folded on 2026-09-04 as edit batches 19a to 19e; every fix is marked **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]** where it lands and Section 9.17 carries its regression targets. What it did not settle is recorded here so that none of it is mistaken for done: the theorist's overall paragraph names a q-for-Q and a b-for-β slip in displayed equations of Section 4.1 without a line, and neither was located; three of the numerics critic's measurements are quoted from the critique and not yet reproduced by a committed script (the `mesolve`/`sesolve` wall-time ratio 69.5 at dimension 64, the `PicklingError` under `map="parallel"`, and the ENR displacement's ⟨n₀⟩ = 2.2412 against 2.25), so they carry no **[recomputed here]** tag; the Monroe 1995 beam geometry behind the Lamb-Dicke anchor is inferred from the quoted numbers (a 90° crossing reproduces them, a counter-propagating pair does not) and is to be confirmed against the paper's figure; the Doppler acceptance test of Section 4.2.1 (three n̄ from one Δ) is stated as the design and not yet computed; the 171Yb+ g_J the plan now adopts is a theoretical determination (Han et al. 2025) with no modern measurement behind it; and the cost model of Section 11 was rebuilt on the v4 benchmark, whose findings Section 11.2 and Appendix D record, including that the v3 table had timed a dense operator through four unmerged coefficient terms.
12.title: Risks, open physics and how the plan handles them

13.text:
Every quantity below has at least two conventions in the primary literature, and the research runs found published factor errors that trace to mixing them. The simulator adopts one convention per quantity, records the source it follows, restates it in the docstring of every module that touches the quantity, and pins the conversions with tests.

| Quantity | Simulator convention | Follows | Alternatives seen in sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frequencies | Internal: angular, rad/s. Public API: Hz, converted at the boundary with an explicit 2π | RMP 2003 | RMP writes ν for an angular frequency; papers quote "γ = 2π × 19.6 MHz", "γ/2π = 60 MHz" and "19.7 MHz" for γ/2π interchangeably [corrected]; Leung quotes 3.045 MHz as an ordinary frequency and Zhu's ω_{ξ,k} refers to ω_z, not ω_ξ [corrected] |
| Mathieu equation | d²x/dξ² + [a − 2q cos 2ξ]x = 0, ξ = ω_rf t/2, a = 4Z∣e∣Uα/(mω_rf²), q = 2Z∣e∣Ũα′/(mω_rf²) | Leibfried et al. 2003 | Wineland 1998 and Berkeland 1998 use +2q cos (a half-period shift); factor-4 q definitions elsewhere [verified] |
| Characteristic exponent | Monodromy matrix; β ≈ √(a + q²/2) as a check | Floquet theory | RMP Eqs. 10-11 carry a printed index-shift error [corrected] |
| Ladder operators | x̂ = x₀(a + a†), x₀ = √(ħ/2mω) | RMP Eq. 26 | James uses the Kittel convention with an explicit i [verified]; Brownnutt arXiv v1 prints â with √(ħmω) [corrected]; Ozeri 2007 and Baldwin 2021 put a factor 4 under the root of z₀ or η [verified flag] |
| Lamb-Dicke parameter | η_{j,k} = b_j^{(k)}(Δk·ê_k)√(ħ/2mω_k) per ion and mode for the drive's effective Δk | Wineland 1998 Eq. 33; Monroe 2020 | James's s_m^{(p)} = √N b_m^{(p)}μ_p^{−1/4} against the single-ion frequency [verified]; single-beam k in some papers |
| Rabi frequency | H = (ħΩ/2)σ₊e^{…} + h.c., carrier π pulse at Ωt = π | RMP 2003; Monroe 2020; Lee 2005 | Wineland 1998 (ħΩ = −μB₁/4), Monroe 1995 and Blümel 2021 Eq. S28 use P = sin²(Ωt), half the usual Rabi frequency [verified flag] |
| Two-photon Rabi frequency | Ω_R = Σ_e Ω₂*Ω₁/(2Δ_e) with Ω_j = E_j⟨e∣d·ε̂_j∣g⟩/ħ the single-photon Rabi frequencies in the ħΩ/2 convention and Δ_e = ω_L − ω_eg; light shift δ_g = Σ∣Ω∣²/(4Δ_e) (Section 4.5.4) | Wineland 2003 Eqs. 2.3, 2.10 read as the matrix-element normalization they are; second-order perturbation theory | Wineland's overall minus sign is his Ω ≡ −E₀⟨d⟩/(2ħ) definition, a phase convention; RMP A13 and Wineland 2003 read as Ω₁Ω₂/Δ_R are 2× too large; Monroe 1995's Ω = g₁g₂/Δ goes with P = sin²(Ωτ) [corrected] |
| Detuning symbols | δ = ω_L − ω₀ from the carrier; μ = beat-note detuning from the carrier; δ_{i,m} = μ_i − ω_m always two-indexed; δ̂ = dimensionless composite-pulse detuning error | Run 2B consolidation | Landsman's δ measured from a mode; Mount's dimensionless δ [corrected] |
| Effective wavevector | Δk = k₁ − k₂ with beam 1 coupling to the upper level; the magnitude 2k sin(θ_cross/2) from the configured geometry; beam labels fixed at ingest | RMP; Wineland 1998; Lee 2005 | Landsman's k = k₂ − k₁; Lee's arXiv v1 Eq. 2 inverts its own beam-to-level assignment, the journal version being correct [corrected: preprint only] |
| Optical phase factor on σ₊ | e^{+i(Δk·X̄_i − Δφ_i)} globally; beam-path and ion-position drift stored as one scalar per ion per pulse | Monroe 2020 Eqs. 16, 18 | e^{−i(…)} in Monroe Eqs. 3, 5 and Lee Eqs. 3, 5 [corrected] |
| Participation factor | counted once, in b_j^{(k)}, with ξ_m = √(ħ/2Mω_m) | Monroe 2020 | Lee's 1/√2 inside η for two ions; Ozeri's z₀ = √(ħ/4Mω) [corrected] |
| Rotation generators | R(θ, φ) carries θ/2 in the exponent, XX(χ) carries χ with no ½; no shared generator helper; p_xx = sin²α is the two-qubit case only | Maslov 2017; Trout 2018 | [corrected] |
| Displacement integral | Choi's form with sin(μt) inside the integrand and bare e^{iω_m t}, or δ_m = ω_m − μ with a slow envelope, never mixed; FM uses θ_m(t) = ∫δ_m dt′ | Choi 2014 | Landsman's printed bare-ω_m form with a slow envelope integrates to nearly zero [corrected] |
| Micromotion correction | η_eff = ηC₀ with C₀ the e^{iνt} Fourier coefficient of the exact Floquet function normalized by its Wronskian, Im(u* u̇) = ν, from the monodromy module: C₀ = 1 + 3q²/16 + O(q⁴) (1.007741 at q = 0.2), no first-order term; excess micromotion as phase modulation with index φ_Ω | derivation audit of 2026-09-04 (`check_c0_floquet.py`); Wineland Eqs. 71-72; Berkeland Eq. 21 (misprint corrected) | the RMP's (1 + q/2)⁻¹, whether attached to Ω₀ or to η, is the u(0) = 1 normalization at one rf phase, an rf-clock artifact [corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]; "Debye-Waller" is a different factor [corrected]; pdftotext renders φ_Ω as φ_V [corrected] |
| Lamb-Dicke base | single-ion mass, unit-norm b, participation never pre-folded: η_{i,m} = (Δk·ê_m) b_{i,m} √(ħ/2m_ion ω_m); for mixed species the same form with the mass-weighted orthonormal eigenvector component c_{i,m} and the ion's own mass (Home 2013 Eq. 19; Morigi-Walther Eq. 12) | Monroe 2020; trap and Hamiltonian briefs; Section 4.1.7 | Sørensen-Mølmer's and Leung's per-ion COM η already contains 1/√N (0.1103 single-ion against 0.0493 at N = 5 and 0.0268 at N = 17 for 171Yb+ at 355 nm, 3.045 MHz); Srinivas puts the total two-ion mass inside r₀ [corrected] |
| Scattering-rate object | one multi-level optical-Bloch steady state supplies the cooling rate W(Δ), the readout rate R_∘ and ρ_ee | Run 3 consolidation | the two-level Lorentzian saturates at Γ/2 where 171Yb+ detection saturates at Γ/4 with ρ_ee → s_∘/18 at low intensity for s_∘ = I/I_sat (s_∘/6 in the second revision, one polarization factor of 1/3 short; derivation audit 2026-09-04) [corrected] |
| Cooling coefficients A_± | bare coefficients with units of rate, A_± = W(Δ ∓ ν) + (η̃²/η²)W(Δ) with η̃² = α(k_em x₀)² the emitted photon's Lamb-Dicke parameter, the Fock rate equation carrying the drive's η²; the carrier weight reduces to α for one resonant beam along the mode axis (Stenholm's case) and vanishes only for EIT at the dark resonance [corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04] | Stenholm 1986 Eqs. 5.49-5.54; Cirac 1992 Eq. 30; Marzoli 1994 Eq. 2; Eschner 2003 Eq. 6; Morigi 2000; Lechner 2016 | RMP Eqs. 117-119 put η² inside; Cirac's printed Eqs. 50 and 52 correlate the sideband sign with the rate index and lack 2η²; the first version of this plan excluded the carrier term, which changes the steady state [corrected] |
| Mode addressing | every mode is a (family, index) pair; axial ascending in μ, transverse descending in γ; eigh output reversed for transverse | Marquet 2003; James 1998 | 'N modes' written for a 3N-mode chain [corrected] |
| Heating-rate meaning | a quoted rate is d⟨n⟩/dt at n = 0, that is ΓN̄; thermal diffusion is Γ(2N̄ + 1); rates of one bath object add; ṅ ∝ ω^{−(α+1)} when S_E ∝ ω^{−α} | Brownnutt 2015 | Trout's symmetric infinite-temperature pair {√ṅ a, √ṅ a†} [verified] |
| Micromotion factors on drives | C₀ on η and J_n(β) on every drive: gates, cooling and detection | Run 3 consolidation | applied to gates only in the cooling, two-qubit and readout sources [corrected] |
| Debye-Waller statistics | shot-to-shot: Ω constant within a shot and distributed across shots; never a within-shot damping | Wineland 1998; Cetina 2022 | [corrected] |
| Doppler limit | computed from the force model; the closed forms ħΓ/2 (ξ = 1) and 0.35ħΓ (RMP's ξ = 2/5) differ by 1.43 | RMP Eq. 106; Berkeland Eq. 13 | [corrected] |
| Sideband-cooling trapping condition | Ω_{n−1,n}t = 2mπ in this plan's Rabi convention | Section 4.2 | Ωt = mπ in Wineland 1998 and Monroe 1995 [corrected] |
| Zero-point energy | dropped, H = Σħω_k a†a | Wineland 1998; Marquet 2003 | James keeps +ħω_k/2 per mode; a convention, not an error [verified] |
| Mode eigenvectors | Orthonormal, axial eigenvalues increasing, last component positive | Marquet 2003; James 1998 | Transverse modes numbered by decreasing frequency [verified] |
| Electric-field noise density | Single-sided S_E; Γ_h = e²S_E/(4mħω) | Brownnutt Eqs. 11-12 | Two-sided gives e²S_E/(2mħω); the arXiv preprint of Turchette prints Eq. 3 inconsistent by 2, the published PRA version is consistent [corrected: preprint only] |
| Heating master equation | rates Γ(N̄+1) on a, ΓN̄ on a†; Γ_h = ΓN̄ | Wineland Eq. 62 (typo fixed); Brownnutt Eqs. 15-17 | the journal prints 2aρ†a†, a typesetting artifact absent from both arXiv versions of the paper [corrected] |
| Motional dephasing operator | L = a†a√(2/τ), coherence of ∣n⟩ + ∣n′⟩ decays at (n − n′)²/τ | Ballance 2016 | other normalizations of γ_φ |
| Qubit dephasing operator | L = √(γ_φ/2) σ_z, coherence decays at γ_φ, so γ_φ = 1/T₂ for the white component; a measured T₂ is split into its quasi-static (Gaussian) and white (exponential) parts before use | Section 5.7; Ramsey test in Section 9.7 | conventions giving 2/T₂ elsewhere [corrected: row added after the 2026-09-04 critique] |
| Spin operator in MS formulas | S_α = Σ_i σ_α^i (eigenvalues 0, ±2 for two ions) for the displayed propagator, the P₀, P_{±2} decomposition and Kirchmair's envelopes; the force on S_y is −(ħηΩ/2)(a†e^{iεt} + h.c.) for the plan's per-tone Ω; closure ηΩ/ε = 1/(2√K) in every spin normalization, with the phase target −π/2 on J_y², −π/8 on S_y², π/4 on σ_yσ_y | Sørensen-Mølmer 2000; Kirchmair 2009; Roos 2008; derivation audit 2026-09-04 (`check_ms_closure.py`) | Sørensen-Mølmer's J_α = ½Σσ_α with closure 1/(2√K) is ingested unchanged (the second revision halved it to 1/(4√K), a factor-2 force error caught by the derivation audit); Roos's Ω_c = ∣ε∣/(4η) reads ∣ε∣/(2η) in the plan's Ω [corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04] |
| Detuning | δ = ω_drive − ω_transition; red negative | RMP 2003 | Sørensen-Mølmer's δ is the tone detuning from the carrier with ε = ν − δ from the sideband [verified]; some define positive magnitudes |
| Beat-note phase of the force | sine convention, Ω(t) sin(μt), force zero at t = 0 | Choi 2014 | cosine conventions elsewhere; the sine choice sets the sign of α [verified] |
| Spin and motion phases | half-sum φ_s = (φ_b + φ_r)/2 and half-difference φ_m = (φ_b − φ_r)/2 of the tone phases, with σ_φ = e^{−iφ_s}σ₊ + e^{iφ_s}σ₋; the force axis carries a further π/2 from the i of the sideband coupling (plus Δk·X̄_i in the same-Δk geometry), a constant the frame alignment absorbs (Section 4.3.4) | Haljan 2005; derivation audit 2026-09-04 | Lee 2005 writes φ_S with the opposite sign [corrected]; the second revision's Section 9.4 pin omitted the π/2 [corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04] |
| Entangling angle | χ_ij = Σ_m η_imη_jm∫∫[Ω_i(t)Ω_j(t′) + Ω_j(t)Ω_i(t′)]… with the pair sum over i < j (Choi's printed factor 2 holds only for proportional envelopes; derivation audit 2026-09-04), maximally entangling at χ = π/4; XX(χ) = exp(−iχσ_xσ_x) | Choi 2014; Maslov 2017; Debnath 2016 | Blümel's factor-2-free kernel with target π/8 (double the kernel to convert) [corrected]; Roos's ∣λt*∣ = π/8 for two ions; Bermudez's exp(−iθS_φ²/4) [verified]; Roos's and Kirchmair's π/8 comes from S without the ½ and must not be rescaled, whereas Blümel's kernel must be doubled [corrected] |
| Observable rotation | O_V = V†OV | Kirchmair Eq. 11 | Kirchmair's and Roos's abbreviation VOV† is a typo [corrected] |
| Bright/dark polarity | Property of the readout scheme, stored as an enum | verified across sources | Direct fluorescence and shelving invert it within the same papers [verified] |
| Linewidth Γ | Angular population decay rate, assertion Γ/2π equals quoted MHz | Noek 2013; Crain 2019 | see frequencies row |
| Detection efficiency | ε_sys applied once, at scattered → detected rate; R_bg separate | Crain 2019 (Eq. 3 corrected) | Acton's α/η [verified] |
| Saturation intensity | I_sat = πhcΓ/(3λ³), the two-level value for a transition of unit relative strength (cycling transition) | Steck; standard | Acton prints ħ for h [corrected] |
| Rabi frequency from intensity | Ω = E₀ ∣ε_q ⟨F′ m_F + q∣d_q∣F m_F⟩∣/ħ with E₀ = √(2I/(ε₀c)); for the cycling transition this reduces to Ω = Γ√(I/(2I_sat)), and s = I/I_sat = 2Ω²/Γ² there only | Steck | Noek's s in the (Γ/6, 2/3) detection form is I/(3I_sat), the exact four-level result with one polarization share per sublevel (Sections 8.1, 8.8; derivation audit 2026-09-04) [corrected] |
| Hyperfine dipole matrix elements | ⟨F m_F∣d_q∣F′ m_F′⟩ = ⟨J‖d‖J′⟩ (−1)^{F′+J+1+I} √((2F′+1)(2J+1)) {J J′ 1; F′ F I} (−1)^{F′−1+m_F} √(2F+1) (F′ 1 F; m_F′ q −m_F), with Γ = ω³(2J+1)∣⟨J‖d‖J′⟩∣²/(3πε₀ħc³(2J′+1)) for the lower level J and upper level J′; the 3j selection rule m_F = m_F′ + q makes q = m_lower − m_upper (see the polarization row) | Steck (Rb87 data, Eqs. 35-38) | reduced elements normalized with or without √(2J+1); the simulator reproduces the 171Yb+ 1/3 : 2/3 branching and the 50.8 mW/cm² I_sat as its ingest test (Section 9.13) [recomputed here]; Steck's factorization and normalization [verified] |
| Nuclear g-factor sign | g_I = −(μ_I/(I μ_N))(m_e/m_p), so that H_Z = μ_B(g_J J_z + g_I I_z)B/ħ with one sign convention for both; 43Ca+ g_I = +2.0467 × 10⁻⁴ from μ_I = −1.31535 μ_N | Steck; Harty 2014 | Harty writes μ_I directly; some sources define g_I with the opposite sign [recomputed here] |

- **Curvature naming** (row already present): add 171Yb+ as a second anchor - the quoted +310.8 Hz/G² is `taylor_c2`, recomputed as 310.76 Hz/G² from (g_J − g_I)²μ_B²/(2h²ν₀), and three printed hyperfine splittings differ from the zero-field value by exactly that shift at 3.0 to 5.3 G **[recomputed here]**.
- **Sign of A_hfs and the g-factors** (row already present): add that the ubiquitous "1.39-1.40 MHz/G" is the product g_Fμ_B/h and not the dimensionless g_F (171Yb+ ²S₁/₂ F = 1: g_F = g_J/2 = 1.001128, g_Fμ_B/h = 1.4012 MHz/G), that δ_B as printed by the polarization-gradient sources is the adjacent-m_F splitting rather than the full span, and that 9Be+'s negative nuclear moment puts F = I − ½ = 1 above F = 2, which is what assigns the (Δ + ω₀) and (Δ − ω₀) denominators of Wineland's eight-channel scattering rate to their bracket groups **[recomputed here]**, **[corrected]**.
- **Saturation intensity** (row already present): add that Ejtemaee and Haljan's 51 mW/cm² for 171Yb+ at 369.5 nm is this same convention to 0.4% (recomputed 50.78 mW/cm² at Γ_e/2π = 19.6 MHz) **[recomputed here]**.
- **Rabi frequency** and **Two-photon Rabi frequency** (rows already present): extend the Alternatives column with the two Run 5 half-conventions, Uys's Ω_R = μE₀/(2ħ) and Wineland's g = E∣⟨stretched⟩∣/(2ħ) with Ωτ_π = π/2, both exactly half the plan's Ω, plus Joshi's Ω referenced to the S₁/₂-P₃/₂ stretched transition (a code normalizing on the actual D1 σ transition is off by √(3/2) in Ω and 3/2 in s); the π **time** is convention-independent, so what breaks is any formula written in the symbol **[corrected]**.
- **Symbol collisions** (closing paragraph of Section 13): add W (polarization-gradient cooling rate versus blackbody-stimulated transition rate), H (heating rate in s⁻¹ versus Hamiltonian), Γ (natural linewidth versus Sisyphus cooling rate Γ_c versus reshelving-broadened Γ′ = Γ + R versus a collisional specific coefficient in cm³ s⁻¹), n̄ (mean phonon number versus mean thermal photon occupation), α (dark-state branching fraction versus the isotropy average versus a π-pulse degradation slope) and q (3j polarization index versus recoil momentum class versus the Mathieu parameter).
- **"Electric-field noise density"** and **"Heating master equation"**: add that the same single-sided Γ_h = e²S_E/(4mħω) drives the splitting, transport and junction channels of Section 4.6, made time-dependent through ω(t) along a trajectory, and that the equal-rate pair {√Γ a, √Γ a†} used by the transport sources is the N̄ ≫ 1 limit of these rows rather than a competing convention - it must not be imported with a finite N̄, which adds unphysical damping on microsecond timescales.

- **"Surface-electrode geometry"**: add that a segmented ground plane can sign-flip the centre and splitting quartic Taylor coefficients relative to every three-dimensional segmented trap, so that the Section 4.6 splitting voltage recipe is not geometry-general and the quartic truncation itself can fail there.

Symbol collisions renamed in code: nuclear spin versus laser intensity (I), pulse area versus polarization (π), laser detuning versus Zeeman splitting (Δ, δ), Ramsey arm versus shelf lifetime versus acquisition window (τ), mode index versus ion mass (m, M in Landsman and Monroe) [verified], "even modes" meaning spatially symmetric (odd index) in Egan [verified], the Mathieu parameter versus the ion charge (q in Sections 4.1.1 and 4.1.2, 4.1.5; `q_mathieu` and `Q_charge` in code) and the mode eigenvector component versus the characteristic exponent (b in Sections 4.1.3 and 4.1.5; `b_mode` and `beta_mathieu`) [corrected: added after the 2026-09-04 critique], and n_max (highest Fock index) versus d_m (mode dimension, n_max + 1); across the Run 4 sources also α (recoil geometric factor, Laguerre order, dc radial asymmetry, mode index, Madsen's aspect ratio, the double-thermal weight), β (Floquet exponent, mass-weighted eigenvector, Chiaverini's depth prefactor, the quartic axial coefficient, Wübbena's amplitude ratio), κ (Nizamani's rf depth factor, Madsen's dc efficiency), d (ion height, layer separation, compensating ground width, half separation), U₀ (Wesenberg's energy scale, Madsen's dc voltage), ω₀ (optical transition frequency in Steck, qubit frequency in Ozeri, Wineland and Uys) and γ (five distinct decay rates: population, optical coherence, dressed-state width, radiative Raman width, phenomenological contrast decay), each namespaced by source at import.
13.title: Conventions the simulator fixes

14.1.text:
The application presents one simulated trapped-ion quantum computer at five levels of abstraction. The user starts where a cloud customer stands, with a circuit and a histogram, and zooms in step by step until the screen shows the Hamiltonian terms, matrix elements and collapse operators that the simulator is actually integrating. Every level is runnable: the user can execute the machine while looking at it from any height. The application is a separate package, `qutip_trap_app`, that depends on the released `qutip_trap` and uses only its public API. Nothing in the core library is written, scheduled or changed for the GUI: milestones M0 to M10 do not depend on M11, the core's CI does not run the app's tests, and when the app needs something the core lacks, that need is filed as a core feature request and judged on the core's own merits while the app works around it on its own side. Two axes are kept separate in the design. The **abstraction of the view** is what the screen shows. The **fidelity of execution** is which engine of Section 5.4 computed it. The zoom ladder pairs a default engine with each level, but any level can display a run made by a deeper engine, and shallower engines are always labelled as derived.

Four rules make the ladder honest rather than decorative.

1. **One record, many views.** Every level is a view over the same run record (Section 14.3). Nothing on any screen comes from a separate illustrative model. A histogram bar is the count of recorded shots; a Bloch vector is the reduced state of the recorded joint state; an ion's drawn position is the equilibrium solver's output at scale.
2. **Coarse-graining commutes with simulation, within a stated bound.** Running at a shallower fidelity must reproduce the deeper engine within the bound the shallower engine reports (the residual displacement of GATE_LOCAL, the channel-derivation residual of the app-side channel replay). The app can check this on demand, and Section 9.11 tests it.
3. **Every displayed formula and number carries its provenance.** The four tags of Section 1 appear as chips on the screen, linked to the Part II item and its source. A quantity without a tag is a bug.
4. **Every result carries its convergence report.** The truncation-boundary population and the tolerance-halving check of Section 5.5 are shown with every trace, and a failing check colours the result rather than hiding it.
14.1.title: The idea and the contract

14.2.text:
| Level | What the user sees | What the user can change | Default engine | Zoom-in targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0, Machine | The device card (species, ion count, native gate set, calibrated gate errors, SPAM), a circuit editor with OpenQASM 2 and IonQ JSON import, shot count, the results histogram with counts and probabilities, and the compiler's target distribution shown beside the simulated one and never in its place | Circuit, shots, qubit-to-ion mapping | Channel replay (app-side, built from the core's Section 6.8 channel summaries), labelled as derived | A histogram bar opens the shots behind it; a shot opens its photon-count records; a gate opens Level 1; the device card opens the Level 4 pages; the SPAM figure opens the readout page |
| 1, Circuit | The compiled native-gate timeline on ions (GPi, GPi2, MS or XX, ZZ, virtual-Z frame updates), each gate with its target unitary, calibrated parameters (χ, phases, duration) and the error channel derived for it; the register state after each gate as reduced density matrices, Bloch vectors and Pauli expectations; the phase register per ion | Gate parameters, compiler template choices, idle intervals | Channel replay or deeper | A gate opens its pulses at Level 2; a channel opens its derivation (process tomography of the simulated pulse); the phase register opens the virtual-Z rule with its pinning test (Section 7.6) |
| 2, Schedule | Pulses on a time axis: which ions each beam illuminates and from which direction, the tones with their detunings drawn against the mode spectrum beneath, phases, amplitude and frequency waveforms with their segment tables, durations and dead times, the crosstalk light on neighbours, and loop-closure indicators per mode | Waveforms, detunings, amplitudes, durations, crosstalk parameters | GATE_LOCAL | A pulse opens Level 3; a tone opens the Hamiltonian term it produces; a mode opens the crystal page at Level 4 |
| 3, Dynamics | Inside one pulse for one dynamical sample: qubit populations and coherences against time, Fock distributions per mode as heatmaps, the spin-dependent phase-space trajectories α_m(t) closing or failing to close, the accumulated entangling angle χ(t), the Debye-Waller factor, quantum jumps (heating, scattering) marked where they occurred, the process matrix of the finished pulse, and the quasi-static noise values drawn for this sample | Initial motional state per mode, noise rates, truncation caps and solver tolerances (with the convergence check re-run) | JOINT_EXACT, re-simulated on demand for the zoomed pulse | A Hamiltonian term opens its matrix elements and the Ω_{n′,n} table at Level 4; a jump opens the collapse operator and the derivation of its rate |
| 4, Physics | The first-principles pages: species (level diagram with the driven transitions, branching ratios, hyperfine structure, the qubit pair), trap (electrode potentials to Mathieu a and q to β and ν, pseudopotential, the stability diagram with the operating point, micromotion), crystal (equilibrium positions to scale, normal modes with animated eigenvectors, η per ion, mode and Δk), light (beams as fields with k-vectors and polarizations, the Raman configuration, Ω from intensity, Stark shifts, scattering rates against detuning), noise (the S_E model and heating rates, dephasing spectra, the crosstalk matrix), cooling (stages and n̄(t) per mode from the rate or master equations), readout (R_∘, R_d and R_b against saturation, count histograms, the discriminator and its threshold, the error budget), and the Hamiltonian builder page showing the H(t) terms and collapse operators assembled for a chosen pulse | Any device parameter: voltages and rf amplitude, laser powers, detunings and geometry, temperatures, noise densities, detection window | JOINT_EXACT with the preparation and readout layers, so a run is the whole process from cooling to photon records | Zooming out re-derives every level above through the calibration emulation |

A **numerics panel** accompanies every level: Hilbert-space dimensions and truncation caps in use, boundary population, the tolerance-halving result, trajectory count, wall time, and the engine that produced what is on screen.
14.2.title: The zoom ladder

14.3.text: The run record is the single data structure the levels read. Job (device-model hash, seed, package version, convergence policy) → compiled circuit → schedule → per-sample dynamics traces → readout records → results. A dynamics trace stores, at configurable sample times, expectation values, reduced internal-state density matrices, per-mode occupation distributions, the α_m(t) trajectories and the jump list; full joint kets are stored only while the joint dimension is below a configurable cap. Anything not stored is recomputed on demand: zooming into a pulse re-simulates that pulse alone from its recorded initial state and its recorded noise sample, which by the measured timings of Section 11.1 takes about half a second for a 100 µs entangling pulse at joint dimension 48, two seconds at 256 and minutes at 2048; the record therefore stores the traces of the run itself, re-simulation is immediate only for small joint spaces, larger ones are filled in by a background job, and every result is cached in the record. Readout records hold photon counts per ion per sub-bin and the discriminator's posterior, so a shot can be opened down to its count trace. Records export to a JSON document with binary arrays (HDF5 optional) and re-import bitwise, which is what makes a published screenshot reproducible.
14.3.title: One run record, many views

14.4.text: The device model at Level 4 is the single source of truth. A change there, a trap voltage, a beam power, a detection window, re-derives the analytic layer immediately (mode structure, η, pulse-solver solutions, the closed-form estimates of the gate channels, the device card's estimated columns) and invalidates the calibration table, whose regeneration by simulated experiment (Section 7.5) takes hours at the measured rates of Section 11.1 and runs only as a user-initiated background job; dependent views show a stale badge until that job completes, and the device card states which of its numbers are analytic estimates and which are calibrated. A change at a shallower level is a request rather than an edit: asking for XX(0.3) at Level 1 invokes the pulse solver; setting a detuning by hand at Level 2 is applied as written, and the gate at Level 1 then displays its actual unitary, not the requested one. Requests the device cannot satisfy are shown with the reason, for example loop closure impossible within the power limit or a requested angle outside the calibrated range. At no point does the app let a level float free of the device model.
14.4.title: Knobs propagate downward

14.5.text:
- **Provenance chips** on every formula and number, generated from a provenance ledger: a YAML file kept beside the plan with one record per quantity (`id`, `symbol`, `tag`, `section`, `source`, `equation`, `corrected_form`), which the core's `Device.derived()` provenance and the app's chips both consume, so the Section 9.11 static test is a set difference over ids rather than a hand-maintained index; hovering a chip shows the tag, the source and the corrected form where the plan corrects the source.
- **Convergence badges** on every result and trace, red when the halving test of Section 5.5 fails.
- **Verify deeper.** At Levels 0 to 2 one action runs the same job at the next-deeper engine, on a subset of shots when the full run would be slow, and shows the discrepancy against the bound of Section 9.8 or the channel-derivation residual.
- **Target beside simulated.** Levels 0 and 1 show the compiler's target semantics next to the simulated result, never as the result.
- **Units and conventions.** Frequencies are displayed in Hz with the 2π conversion visible; the convention row of Section 13 that governs a displayed quantity is one hover away.
- **No cartoons.** Every drawn element is computed: ion positions from the equilibrium solver, beams from the configured geometry, mode vectors from the Hessian, spectra from the built Hamiltonian. The few illustrative elements, such as a level diagram's vertical spacing, are labelled "not to scale".
- **Reproducibility.** Seed, device hash, package version and convergence report travel with every exported record.
- **Presets from the validation suite.** Any entry of Section 9 can be loaded as a device configuration plus experiment, for example Harty's microwave randomized benchmarking, Kirchmair's thermal Mølmer-Sørensen scan or Myerson's readout optimum; the app runs it and places the published number beside the simulated one with the provenance chip.
- **Explain panel.** At every level, the Part II subsection that governs what is on screen is shown beside it.
14.5.title: Correctness affordances

14.6.text:
- **Routes mirror the ladder** with the declarative `ft.Router` of Flet 0.85: `/job/{id}` for Level 0, `/job/{id}/circuit/{gate}` for Level 1, `/job/{id}/schedule/{pulse}` for Level 2, `/job/{id}/dynamics/{pulse}/{sample}` for Level 3, and `/device/{page}` for the Level 4 pages, with a breadcrumb zoom bar and keyboard zoom in and out. Browser history works in the served web mode because routes are real.
- **Core contract.** The app calls only public core API that exists for the core's own reasons: the device model and its hash, `run(circuit, shots, level)` and the `Result` with its diagnostics and convergence report, the experiment API, the per-pulse evolution and process-tomography entry points that the core's validation suite and Section 6.8 reporting already use, and the compiler's target unitaries. The channel-replay engine (`replay.py`) is built app-side from the Section 6.8 summaries. If a zoom view needs data the core does not expose, the app records the gap and shows the view as unavailable rather than patching the core.
- **Layering.** `viewmodel/` is pure Python with no Flet import: it turns run records into view data, performs the coarse-graining, and resolves provenance; it is where the correctness tests run. `views/` holds the Flet controls per level. `workers.py` runs core calls in a `ProcessPoolExecutor`, streaming progress and partial results through `page.pubsub`; view updates are scheduled with `page.run_task`, so the UI never blocks on a solver.
- **Charts.** `flet-charts` LineChart and ScatterChart for time series, calibration scans and phase-space loops; BarChart for histograms; MatplotlibChart for level diagrams, mode eigenvectors and the stability diagram; `ft.RawImage` (Flet 0.86) for streamed heatmaps such as Fock distributions and Wigner functions; DataTable for matrix elements, segment tables and parameter tables.
- **Testing.** pytest on the view-models (coarse-graining identities, provenance coverage, record round trips); `flet test` integration tests for navigation and run flows; the physics itself is never tested through the UI.
- **Packaging.** `flet run` for the desktop window during development, `flet run --web` for the served browser mode, `flet build macos`, `windows` or `linux` for distributable bundles with the physics dependencies installed as binary wheels. The static Pyodide web build is not a target (Section 1.5).
14.6.title: Flet implementation

14.7.text:
| Action | Budget | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Zoom into a pulse: one trajectory of a 100 µs entangling pulse with the recorded noise sample and jump record | ≤ 1 s at joint dimension ≤ 256 (two modes, d_m = 8); ≤ 10 s at ≤ 864 (three modes, d_m = 6) | Section 11.1 (v4) measured 0.6 s and 6 s per 100 µs gate |
| Zoom into a pulse: jump ensemble and process matrix | background job with progress (tens to hundreds of trajectories; 16 tomography inputs) | Section 5.4 |
| Level 4 parameter change: recalibration by simulated experiment | hours; user-initiated background job with a stale badge until it completes | Section 7.5 at the rates of Section 11.1 |
| Zoom into a pulse at larger dimension | recorded traces shown at once; re-simulation as a background job with progress | Section 11.1 (v4) measured 6 s at dimension 864 and 2.1 min at 2048; Section 11.2 cost model |
| Level 0 or 1 run by channel replay, 20 qubits, 100 gates | seconds | density matrix to 12 qubits, sampling beyond |
| Level 4 parameter change, re-derivation of modes and η | immediate | closed-form and small eigenproblems |
| Level 4 parameter change, pulse re-solve per pair | ≤ 10 s in background with stale badges | AM and FM solvers of Section 4.4.3 |
14.7.title: Interactive budgets

14.8.text: Live hardware submission, multi-user server deployment, and mobile bundles (possible with `flet build`, but wheel availability of the physics stack on Android and iOS is not part of this plan).

15.title: Sources

2.text:
This section is the narrative version of the pipeline; Part II gives the equations. Read it as the sequence of physical states the simulated device passes through for one shot of one circuit.

**Before the circuit.** N ions of one species sit in a linear Paul trap. Their equilibrium positions are set by the balance of the axial confining potential and mutual Coulomb repulsion; their small oscillations about those positions decompose into 3N normal modes, N along each axis, each a harmonic oscillator with its own frequency and pattern of ion participation. The modes are the bus every entangling gate uses, so the simulator computes them from the trap parameters rather than taking them as free inputs, and it records how far each ion participates in each mode (that participation, times the photon-recoil scale of the drive, is the ion's Lamb-Dicke parameter for that mode).

**Cooling.** Doppler cooling on the cycling transition brings every mode to a thermal state whose mean phonon number is set by the transition linewidth and the mode frequency. Resolved-sideband or EIT cooling then brings the modes used by gates close to the ground state; the simulator produces per-mode thermal states with mean occupations derived from the cooling model and parameters, and, where requested, simulates the cooling dynamics themselves as a check. Optical pumping puts every ion in the qubit's |0⟩ with a small, species-specific residual population elsewhere. This is the initial state of the run: internal states nearly pure, motional modes thermal, no correlations.

**Compilation and calibration.** The user's circuit is rewritten into the native gate set: single-qubit rotations about equatorial axes (GPi, GPi2 with a phase), the two-qubit entangling gate (MS with two phases and an angle, or ZZ), and Z rotations that cost nothing because they are absorbed into the phases of later pulses. Each native gate becomes a pulse whose parameters (Rabi frequency envelope, detuning, phase, duration, which modes it closes loops on) are not typed in by the user but come from calibration tables the simulator built by running the same experiments a laboratory runs on the simulated device: Rabi flopping to find the π time, sideband spectroscopy to find mode frequencies, gate scans to find the amplitude and detuning that produce maximal entanglement, and phase scans to align the entangling axis with the single-qubit frame.

**Gates.** Each pulse illuminates chosen ions (with a small, unavoidable fraction of light on their neighbours) and adds a drive term to the Hamiltonian: the ion's internal transition coupled to the motion through the exact displacement operator. A single-qubit pulse on resonance with the carrier rotates the spin while the motion, because the beams are chosen co-propagating or the drive is a microwave, barely notices. A Mølmer-Sørensen pulse drives both sidebands slightly off resonance; the resulting spin-dependent force pushes the driven mode around a closed loop in phase space so that, when the loop closes, the motion is back where it started and the two spins have acquired a joint geometric phase. Throughout, the mode heats at a rate set by electric-field noise, spins dephase from magnetic-field and laser noise, and the drive scatters photons off resonance at a rate set by the detuning and power. The simulator evolves the joint state under all of it, pulse by pulse, including the idle intervals between pulses.

**Readout.** A detection beam on the cycling transition makes an ion in the bright state scatter photons at a rate set by saturation and detuning, and an ion in the dark state scatter almost none, except that off-resonant excitation slowly pumps dark to bright and bright to dark. A fraction of the photons reach a detector; some background arrives too; some of one ion's light lands on its neighbour's detector. The simulator samples the count record for each ion from this model, applies the same discriminator the device would, and returns bits. For optical qubits and shelved hyperfine qubits the dark state is a metastable level whose decay during the window is another error channel.

**Results.** One shot is one sample of the whole chain. Shots aggregate into counts and probabilities. The results object also carries the diagnostics that make the run auditable: truncation-boundary populations, which modes were included, the fidelity level, the calibration values used, and, when asked, the final density matrix or trajectory states.
2.title: The physical process the simulator reproduces

3.1.text:
- **Physics objects, not gate matrices.** The only place a unitary matrix appears is in the compiler's definition of what a native gate is supposed to do and in the validation suite that compares simulated pulses to it. The simulator never applies that matrix to the state.
- **One Hamiltonian builder.** Every pulse, whether a calibration scan, a single-qubit gate, a Mølmer-Sørensen gate or a cooling pulse, is expressed as a set of drive terms on a shared Hilbert space and assembled by the same builder. Approximations are options of the builder, defaulting to none.
- **Device parameters in, everything else derived.** The user specifies physical parameters (species, trap frequencies or voltages, beam wavelengths, geometry and powers, magnetic field, noise spectral densities, detector efficiency). Lamb-Dicke parameters, Rabi frequencies, Stark shifts, scattering rates, heating rates, mode structure and gate pulse parameters are derived, the last of these by the simulator's own calibration routines.
- **Every run reports its own approximation status.** Truncation-boundary population, mode drop decisions, frame choices, and which fidelity level (Section 5) was used are attached to every result.
- **Deterministic by seed.** All stochastic elements (quantum-jump trajectories, quasi-static noise sampling, photon-count sampling) draw from keyed substreams of one root seed, spawned by (sample, trajectory, ion, channel) so that reproducibility survives parallel execution and truncation retries (Section 3.4).

3.2.title: Package layout

3.3.text:
- `Species`: immutable atomic data for one isotope: mass; nuclear spin I and magnetic moment; level list (n, L, S, J) with energies, lifetimes, hyperfine constants A and B and Landé g_J; transitions with wavelength, natural linewidth Γ and the branching ratios that the angular algebra does not fix (fine-structure branching to D levels); the designated qubit pair; the cycling transition, repump transitions, shelving transition where applicable. Everything hyperfine-resolved (Zeeman energies at the operating field, dipole matrix elements, polarization-resolved Rabi frequencies, Raman and Rayleigh amplitudes, leakage branching) is derived by `species/atomic.py` (Section 4.5), never typed in. Species modules ship with citations for every number.
- `Field`: the static magnetic field vector at the ions; it defines the quantization axis in which beam polarizations are decomposed into σ⁺, π and σ⁻ components, and its magnitude and noise spectrum feed the Zeeman shifts of every level.
- `Trap`: either explicit secular frequencies (ω_x, ω_y, ω_z) with a radial principal-axis rotation angle, or (V_rf, Ω_rf, U_dc, geometry factors) converted through the Mathieu module with the convention documented in Section 13, plus the stray field and the shim voltages that compensate it, from which the residual excess-micromotion β per beam direction follows (Section 4.1.1). Provides the potential's harmonic coefficients, the mode directions and optional anharmonic terms; milestone M12 (Section 4.6) adds an optional dc voltage schedule V_n(t) and a zone list, from which the well trajectory and the instantaneous curvature are derived after the Section 7.10 hardware chain rather than from the commanded staircase. The axis angle exists because the explicit-frequency path would otherwise pin the modes to the laboratory frame, and a mode with no projection on any cooling beam is uncoolable; the stray field and shims exist because compensation is something a laboratory measures and re-nulls, not an assumption (both added after the 2026-09-04 experimentalist critique).
- `Crystal`: derived from `Trap` and `Species` and N: equilibrium positions, the 3N normal modes as (frequency, eigenvector) pairs grouped by axis, per-ion per-mode Lamb-Dicke parameters for a given Δk.
- `Beam`, `BeamPair`: wavelength(s), k-vectors, polarization, waist, power, pointing; per-ion intensity via the beam profile (this is where addressing crosstalk originates).
- `Drive`: a physical drive on a set of ions: type (Raman, single-photon optical, microwave), effective Rabi frequency envelope Ω(t), detuning schedule δ(t) (per tone), phase schedule φ(t), effective Δk, Stark shift; derived from beams by `light/`.
- `Pulse`: a `Drive` with start and end times and metadata linking it to the gate it implements.
- `HilbertSpace`: the composite space with ion qudit dimension d (2 by default, 3 or more when leakage is modelled), mode list with truncation policy, and cached operators.
- `NoiseModel`: spectral densities and stochastic-process parameters with the derived rates.
- `Device`: the aggregate; exposes `derived()` with all computed quantities and their provenance.
- `Circuit`: a list of operations on qubit indices in a small IR (native gates plus standard gates before compilation), with classical measurement targets.
- `Schedule`: ordered pulses with timings, plus the per-qubit phase frame at each point.
- `Result`: per-shot records and aggregates, plus a `diagnostics` block.
3.3.title: Core data model

3.4.text:
```
Device + Circuit
  -> compile: Circuit -> native gates (phase-tracked)                    [control.compiler]
  -> calibrate (cached per Device): CalibrationTable                    [calibration/, through dynamics.engine]
  -> schedule: native gates -> Pulses with absolute times               [control.schedule]
  -> prepare: motional state per mode + internal state per ion          [prep.*]
  -> evolve: for each pulse, build H(t), c_ops; advance state           [dynamics.*]
       (between pulses: free evolution with heating/dephasing for idle time)
  -> readout: fluorescence model -> photon counts -> bits; measure, reset and recool are IR
       operations, so the loop is prep -> [gates | measure | reset | recool]* -> results (7.2) [readout.*, prep.*]
  -> Result
```

Shots are produced by the ensemble structure of the physics, with one vocabulary throughout the plan: a **sample** is one draw of every quasi-static parameter (Section 6.1); a **trajectory** is one quantum-jump unravelling within a sample, or the single deterministic density-matrix evolution when `mesolve` is used; a **shot** is one measurement record. `run(circuit, shots, samples=None, level=...)` distributes shots round-robin over samples (default samples = min(shots, 64)), chooses the trajectory count per sample in two phases, an estimate from `mcsolve`'s `target_tol` on the final populations (which needs `e_ops`, Section 5.4) followed by a replay of a fixed seed list of that length, draws shots from the weighted trajectory mixture (Section 5.3), and reports the realized (samples, trajectories, shots per sample) triple in the diagnostics together with the effective sample size from which the histogram's error bars are derived, since shots drawn from one sample are not independent draws from the ensemble. Estimators are chosen per quantity: deterministic `mesolve` where the joint dimension allows it, first-order perturbative channel evaluation for error rates at the 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁶ level that no trajectory count could resolve, trajectories with `target_tol` otherwise, and Gauss-Hermite quadrature rather than Monte Carlo over quasi-static parameters when a closed form is being reproduced. Randomness comes from one root `SeedSequence` per run, spawned deterministically by (sample, trajectory, shot, ion, channel), the shot slot added because photon-count sampling is per shot per ion and two shots on one (sample, trajectory) would otherwise share a record and the error bars would lose the within-trajectory detection variance, so that every variate's key is independent of execution order and of truncation retries; the per-trajectory children are passed to `mcsolve` as an explicit seed list, and the reproducibility test is a tolerance test (agreement to 10⁻¹² over 1 and 18 workers plus per-trajectory identity under the same seed) rather than a bitwise one, because `MultiTrajResult` accumulates running sums in completion order and floating-point addition is not associative (4.4 × 10⁻¹⁶ measured on 5.3.1 with identical seeds), and because `target_tol` stops on a check whose firing point depends on scheduling (200 trajectories serial against 5 parallel in one measured call; 2026-09-04 numerics critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**.


# Part II. Physics specification

Every numbered subsection below is the specification of one module. Equations are given in the convention the simulator adopts (Section 13 lists the conventions and the source each follows). Provenance tags: **[verified]** checked against the primary source by independent verifier agents; **[corrected]** the verifiers found an error in the extracted or printed form and the corrected form is given; **[extracted]** taken from a primary source with a quote, not independently checked; **[background]** standard physics the author supplies without a source check in these runs.
3.4.title: Control flow of `run`

4.1.title: Trap potential, ion crystal, motional modes, micromotion and heating

4.1.1.text:
Near the trap centre the potential is quadrupolar in both its static and its rf part **[verified]** (Leibfried, Blatt, Monroe, Wineland, RMP 75, 281 (2003), Eqs. 1-2):

Φ(x, y, z, t) = ½ U (α x² + β y² + γ z²) + Ũ cos(ω_rf t) · ½ (α′ x² + β′ y² + γ′ z²),

with Laplace's equation forcing α + β + γ = 0 and α′ + β′ + γ′ = 0, which is why no static minimum exists. Each Cartesian coordinate obeys a Mathieu equation. The simulator adopts the RMP 2003 convention **[verified]**:

d²x/dξ² + [a_x − 2 q_x cos(2ξ)] x = 0,  ξ = ω_rf t / 2,  a_x = 4 Z|e| U α / (m ω_rf²),  q_x = 2 Z|e| Ũ α′ / (m ω_rf²),

i.e. a factor 4 in the static parameter and 2 in the rf parameter, with q_y = −q_x for a linear trap. Two convention facts the code must encode explicitly: (i) Wineland et al. 1998 and Berkeland et al. 1998 write the driven term with the opposite sign, +2 q cos, and Landa et al. 2012 with the minus sign; the sign of q is a half-rf-period time shift, so β and all frequencies are unchanged, but the phase of micromotion relative to the rf drive flips **[verified]**; (ii) β is even in q, so q_y = −q_x does not split the two radial secular frequencies; they differ only if a_x ≠ a_y **[corrected]** (a verifier caught the opposite inference in an extracted item; it is not in the source). Brownnutt et al. 2015 use the same factors (a_x = 4|e|Φ″_dc/(m Ω²), q_x = 2|e|Φ″_rf/(m Ω²)) **[verified]**, and Berkeland et al. give the linear-trap geometry explicitly, a_x = a_y = −a_z/2 = −4 Q κ U₀/(m Z₀² Ω²), q_x = −q_y = 2 Q V₀/(m R′² Ω²), q_z = 0 **[verified]**, where R′ is the effective radial scale with R′ ≅ R, equal to R for infinitely long hyperbolic electrodes; the extraction's R′ ≥ R was wrong, and the paper's own example uses R′ ≅ R = 1.0 mm with q_x ≈ 2√2 ω_x/Ω = 0.28 **[corrected]**. No source gives the geometry factors κ, R′, Z₀ or Φ″ for any electrode design, and none treats surface-electrode geometry at all; for such traps the simulator takes Φ″_dc and Φ″_rf from a user-supplied field solution (FEM or the gapless-plane approximation) through the geometry-free map above and locates the rf null from the Dehmelt pseudopotential Ψ = q²|E_rf(r)|²/(4mΩ²) **[background]**.

**Characteristic exponent and stability.** To lowest order β_x ≈ (a_x + q_x²/2)^{1/2} and the secular frequency is ν = β_x ω_rf/2 **[verified]**; the preprint form β = [(a + q²/2)/(1 − 3q²/8)]^{1/2}, dropped from the published Wineland 1998, is far more accurate, 0.12% from the exact exponent at q = 0.3 against 1.8% for the bare lowest-order form **[corrected]**. Stability in three dimensions requires 0 ≤ β_i ≤ 1 for every axis, and the Floquet root search must be restricted to that branch because the determinant also vanishes on the lattice ±β_j + 2n **[verified]**; traps run in the lowest stability region with a ≈ 0 and q < 0.5 **[background]**. For the exact β the printed continued fractions of RMP 2003, Eqs. (10)-(11), carry an off-by-one index error and cannot be used as an algorithm **[corrected]**; a verifier derived the correct recursion from Eq. (9), D_{2n} = [a_x − (2n + β_x)²]/q_x. The simulator will instead compute β by the monodromy method **[background]**: integrate the Mathieu equation over one period in ξ (π) for the two fundamental solutions, form the 2×2 monodromy matrix M, declare stability when |tr M| < 2, and obtain cos(πβ) = tr M / 2. This is convention-independent and is tested against the lowest-order formula at small (a, q) and against the stability boundary q ≈ 0.908 at a = 0.

**Pseudopotential.** Averaging over the rf period gives a harmonic pseudopotential; with a ≈ 0 the radial secular frequency is ω_r = Q V₀/(√2 Ω_T m R²) with Q the ion charge (Wineland 1998 Eq. 6, whose symbol q is the charge) **[verified]**, equivalently ω_r = q Ω_T/(2√2) with q the Mathieu parameter; the two symbols collide throughout the sources and are separated in code as Q and q (Section 13) **[corrected]**. This formula is bound to the q definition it comes with **[verified]**; the module therefore exposes secular frequencies computed from (a, q) rather than a stand-alone voltage formula, and provides voltage-to-(a, q) converters for the documented geometries.

**Trajectory and intrinsic micromotion.** To first order in a and second order in q (Wineland 1998, Eq. 4) **[verified]**:

u_i(t) = A_i { cos(ω_i t + φ_i) [1 + (q_i/2) cos(Ω_T t) + (q_i²/32) cos(2Ω_T t)] + β_i (q_i/2) sin(ω_i t + φ_i) sin(Ω_T t) }.

The secular motion is multiplied, not added to, by a micromotion modulation of fractional amplitude q_i/2 at Ω_T **[verified]** (Wineland's rf phase origin, a_i + 2q_i cos Ω_T t; under the plan's adopted Mathieu sign, Section 13, every Ω_T t in that trajectory reads Ω_T t + π, the only change); axial motion in a linear trap (q_z = 0) has no intrinsic micromotion **[verified]** (Berkeland's Eqs. 7-13 were checked against page renders because that PDF's text layer mangles its mathematics font). In the quantum treatment (RMP 2003, Eqs. 16-29, 37) **[verified]** the motional Hamiltonian H = p²/2m + (m/2) W(t) x² with W(t) = (ω_rf²/4)[a_x + 2 q_x cos(ω_rf t)] in the RMP's rf phase origin (the plan's adopted Mathieu sign has −2q_x cos(ω_rf t); see below) is solved by a c-number Floquet function u(t) with u(0) = 1, u̇(0) = iν, whose Wronskian is fixed at 2iν; the ladder operators of a static reference oscillator of frequency ν are constants of motion, and x̂(t) = x₀[â u*(t) + â† u(t)].
