The two saturation parameters are different objects, stored separately: Joshi's s is per beam, already detuning-suppressed and referenced to the P₃/₂ stretched transition, while Ejtemaee's s₀ = I/(51 mW/cm²) is per beam **on resonance** in the two-level I_sat = πhcΓ/(3λ³) convention, which recomputes to 50.78 mW/cm² at 369.5 nm, so the printed 51 is that same convention to 0.4% **[recomputed here]**; the bridge s_Joshi = (3/2)s₀(Γ/2)²/((Γ/2)² + Δ²) is derived in the Run 5 consolidation and printed by neither paper, so it is tagged derived, **[background]**, and used only to check that s₀ = 11-15 at Δ/2π = 310 MHz lands inside Joshi's bound s < 0.07. And the analytic prefactors do **not** transfer: 1/3, 1/9, 16/9, 2/9 and the 8ξ² are specific to j_g = ½ ↔ j_e = ½, the sources warn they fail for j_e = 3/2, and whether they carry to the 171Yb+ F = 1 → F′ = 0 scheme is asserted by nobody, that source printing no display equations at all. The two layers are therefore separate models with no shared coefficients until a source for the second is transcribed, and a simulator must not validate one against the other's steady-state number: 0.87 quanta analytic phase-averaged, about 1 as the 171Yb+ expectation, 1.5-2 measured there, 7.7(1.1) outside the Lamb-Dicke regime in the analytic model's own experiment **[contested]**. The analytic model also drops the Zeeman term on which the 171Yb+ CPT-free window depends (g_F μ_B B/ħ at 5.9 G is an adjacent-m_F splitting of 2π × 8.27 MHz against a scattering rate of order 10⁶ s⁻¹), so merging them means adding it - and the trade-off is real, CPT-negligibility pushing to high field and low intensity while the s₀² rate law pushes to high intensity **[verified]**.
4.2.4.title: Polarization-gradient (Sisyphus) cooling

4.2.5.text: A second species (or, in the omg scheme, a metastable manifold) is cooled with light the qubit species does not see; Coulomb coupling shares the energy through the normal modes. Home et al. 2009 fix the archetype: a 9Be+-24Mg+-24Mg+-9Be+ crystal whose order is preserved through separation and recombination, Doppler cooling on Mg+ to n̄ ≈ 15, then second- and first-sideband cooling on Mg+ only, reaching ⟨n⟩ ≈ 0.06 per axial mode in 5.1 ms per composite operation against 3.6 ms of transport **[verified]**. The mode structure of the mixed crystal (two highest axial modes 251 kHz apart, gate detuning 83.6 kHz, force duration 2π/δ, phase-contribution ratio 2.72) **[verified]** is the reason the crystal module works from a per-ion mass list from the start. In the first release the sympathetic stage is modelled at level A: the coolant's Doppler or sideband cooling sets each shared mode's n̄ through its participation eigenvector, and the qubit ions' internal states are untouched; the dual-species mode solver is the extension that makes level C possible.
4.2.5.title: Sympathetic cooling

4.2.6.text: Optical pumping drives every level except the target out of the manifold until population lands in the one dark state; it takes a few microseconds and leaves the ion in a definite internal state with a residual error set by off-resonant excitation of the target **[extracted]**. The laboratory order is Doppler cooling first, then sideband or EIT cooling with its own repump, then a final optical pump immediately before the circuit, with a re-pump after any interleaved recooling: Doppler cooling runs on a repumped cycling transition and scrambles the internal state (171Yb+ over S₁/₂ F = 1 through the 14.7 GHz sideband, 40Ca+ over both S₁/₂ Zeeman states), so a pump done first is erased, which is the order Section 2 and the 9Be+ anchor of Section 4.2.2 (50 µs Doppler precooling, then 7 µs of optical pumping, then Raman sideband cycles) already state; the second revision printed the reverse order here (pump to |↓⟩, cool to about 1 mK leaving ⟨n⟩ ≥ 1, sideband cool), which an implementer following it would have turned into a scrambled initial state and a preparation error orders of magnitude too large, so the stage order is a scheduler constraint (Section 7.3) and not prose (2026-09-04 experimentalist critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]** (Wineland 1998 prints ⟨n⟩ ≥ 1 after Doppler cooling, not ≳). The simulator models preparation at level C by the multi-level master equation of Section 4.2.8 on the internal manifold, with the pumping beam's polarization-resolved Rabi frequencies and the branching ratios of Section 4.5.2 and the recoil operators for the emitted photons, from which the residual population in non-target states (the SPAM preparation error of Section 8), the pumping time and the motional heating during pumping follow. Species anchors: 171Yb+ pumps to |0⟩ = |F=0, m=0⟩ with a 2.1 GHz sideband on S₁/₂|F=1⟩ → P₁/₂|F=1⟩ (1/3 branching into |0⟩ per excitation), with a 3.07 GHz sideband on the 935 nm repump essential **[extracted]**; 9Be+ pumps into |2,2⟩ in about 7 µs **[verified]**; 43Ca+ prepares the stretch state with error below 10⁻⁴ **[extracted]**.
4.2.6.title: Optical pumping and internal-state preparation

4.2.7.text:
After every stage the simulator can run the same diagnostics the laboratory runs and compare them with the state it actually prepared: (i) sideband-asymmetry thermometry, P_e^{rsb}/P_e^{bsb} = [n̄/(n̄ + 1)]^k for k-th-order sidebands, exact in η, in pulse duration and for any coupling matrix element because the same Ω_{m+k,m} appears on both sides (Turchette 2000 Eqs. 8-11; verified to 6 × 10⁻¹⁵ at η = 1.5, n̄ = 8), inverted as n̄ = R_k^{1/k}/(1 − R_k^{1/k}); the constancy of the ratio under varying pulse time is itself the test of thermality, since constancy forces a geometric distribution **[verified]**; (ii) blue-sideband Rabi flopping, P_↓(τ) = ½(1 + Σ_n P_n e^{−γ_n τ} cos(2Ω_{n+1,n}τ)), inverted by cosine transform for the Fock distribution P_n **[verified]** (Wineland 1998 Eq. 42, with Ω defined by ħΩ = −μB₁/4 so that the flopping frequency is 2Ω); and (iii) the thermal Debye-Waller reduction of a carrier Rabi frequency by spectator modes, Ω̄ = Ω^{(0)} Π_p Σ_{n_p} P_{n_p} e^{−η_p²/2} L_{n_p}(η_p²) ≈ Ω^{(0)} Π_p exp[−η_p²(n̄_p + 1/2)] with P_n = n̄^n/(1 + n̄)^{n+1} **[verified]** (Wineland 1998 Eqs. 122-124), which is what the carrier-Rabi calibration of Section 7.5 fits.

The hand-off state is a product of per-mode thermal states (level A or B) or the level-C reduced motional state, with the internal state from Section 4.2.6; Section 9.3 requires that the diagnostics recover the prepared n̄ within the statistical error a laboratory would quote, and that the level-A closed forms agree with level C where both apply.
4.2.7.title: Thermometry and hand-off

4.2.8.text:
Run 3 named the spontaneous-emission recoil kernel as unsupplied by any source (Section 12): the emitted-photon Lamb-Dicke factor η̃ in the sideband-cooling floor of Section 4.2.2, the angular factor ξ = 2/5 in the Doppler limit of Section 4.2.1, the Δn ≈ 0 claim for repump photons and the recoil of Rayleigh scattering during gates (Section 6.5) all depend on it. This subsection specifies it and the multi-level master equation it belongs to. Run 4 checks the forms against Stenholm 1986, Morigi 2003 and Wineland and Itano 1979, and the recoil follow-up run (Run 4R, Appendix D) reconciled them across Cirac, Blatt, Zoller and Phillips 1992, Marzoli et al. 1994, Itano and Wineland 1982, Eschner et al. 2003, Steck's Quantum and Atom Optics and the cooling chapter of Roos's 2000 thesis, read from the papers themselves after the first attempt found them paywalled; Javanainen and Stenholm 1981 was not obtained and its content is covered through Cirac 1992 and Stenholm 1986. The physics is textbook **[background]**, the angular integrals below were recomputed on 2026-09-04 **[recomputed here]**, and the cross-source paragraph below carries the follow-up's verdicts.

**The recoil term.** A photon of wavevector k_eg emitted in direction k̂ carries momentum ħk_eg k̂ away from the ion, so the decay |e⟩ → |g⟩ displaces the motional state by the operator e^{−ik_eg k̂·x̂}. Averaged over the emission pattern N_q(k̂) of the decay's polarization type q, the spontaneous-emission part of the master equation for an ion of internal levels plus motion is

𝓛_se ρ = Σ_{e→g, q} Γ_{e→g,q} [ ∫ dΩ_k N_q(k̂) e^{−ik_eg k̂·x̂} |g⟩⟨e| ρ |e⟩⟨g| e^{+ik_eg k̂·x̂} − ½{|e⟩⟨e|, ρ} ],

with Γ_{e→g,q} the channel rates of Section 4.5.2 and, for a quantization axis along B̂, N₀(k̂) = (3/8π) sin²θ for π decays and N_{±1}(k̂) = (3/16π)(1 + cos²θ) for σ decays, θ the angle between k̂ and B̂. Writing the emitting ion's position as k̂·x̂_i = Σ_m b_{i,m}(k̂·ê_m) x₀,m (a_m + a_m†) over the modes, with b_{i,m} the ion's participation of Section 4.1.3 (c_{i,m} for mixed species), the operator inside the integral is a product of displacements Π_m D_m(−i k_eg b_{i,m} x₀,m k̂·ê_m), built exactly as in Section 5.1.1, one operator set per emitting ion and decay channel (the first version of this plan dropped b_{i,m}, which over-weights recoil into a centre-of-mass mode by N; caught by the 2026-09-04 critique); the recoil kernel over Δn is the distribution of |⟨n + Δn|D|n⟩|² averaged over N_q, exact in η through the Laguerre elements of Section 4.3.1.

**Angular factors.** To second order in the recoil the average enters only through α_m ≡ ∫ dΩ N_q(k̂)(k̂·ê_m)², the mean squared projection of the emission direction on the mode axis, and the recoil heating per photon scattered by ion i into mode m is α_m b_{i,m}²(k_eg x₀,m)² quanta, so that the effective emission Lamb-Dicke parameter of Section 4.2.2 is η̃_{i,m}² = α_m b_{i,m}²(k_eg x₀,m)²; summed over the modes of one axis the recoil energy per photon equals the free-ion recoil energy (ħk_eg)²/2m times that axis's α, which is the module's unit test. For a π decay α = 1/5 along B̂ and 2/5 perpendicular to it; for a σ decay 2/5 along B̂ and 3/10 perpendicular; for an isotropic average 1/3 (all recomputed by quadrature, `check_recoil.py`). This is Stenholm's factor: with the one-dimensional emission kernel (Γ/2)∫₋₁¹ dx W(x) ρ(k + qx), the pattern normalized as ½∫W dx = 1 and α ≡ ½∫x²W dx, the pattern W = (3/4)(1 + x²) gives α = 2/5 along the beam and the isotropic W = 1 gives 1/3 (Stenholm 1986 Eqs. 4.16-4.24) **[verified]**; Stenholm's α weights the emission recoil alone, the induced recoil supplying the 1 in his free-particle diffusion coefficient ∝ (1 + α) (Eqs. 4.40-4.42) and his trapped-ion coefficients carrying α as the additive carrier term of Eq. 5.41, and his Eqs. 4.31b-c carry two misprints (a plus for an equals sign, and ρ₂₂ at P + ħq/2 for P + ħq) that Eqs. 4.34-4.38 of the same paper fix **[corrected]**. Stenholm's Lamb-Dicke sideband-cooling rate equation then has A_± = P(Δ ∓ ν) + αP(Δ), the carrier scattering entering both rates through the recoil factor, with the steady state ⟨n⟩ = (γ/ν)²(α + 1/4) for γ ≪ ν (γ the half-width; 7/12 and 13/20 in units of (γ/ν)² for α = 1/3 and 2/5, Eqs. 5.49-5.54): this is the RMP's ⟨n⟩_min ≈ (Γ̃/2ν)²[(η̃/η)² + 1/4] of Section 4.2.2 with (η̃/η)² = α, which reconciles the two sections. Wineland and Itano 1979 give the same kernel exactly (their Eq. 31 is the Laguerre matrix element of Section 4.3.1 with the three-dimensional factorization over modes, checked by Run 4 against the matrix exponential to 10⁻¹⁵ for η up to 2.5; the factor they name Debye-Waller is the cross-section-level exp(−k²⟨x²⟩), the square of the amplitude prefactor), the general bound-atom rate equation as a Lorentzian-weighted sum over the initial and the intermediate, absorbed, motional states with the mean emission recoil R added per event (Eq. 48, one beam, low saturation), the free-atom Doppler limit ⟨E_K⟩_min = ħγ/4 per degree of freedom, k_B T_min = ħγ/2 (Eq. 11; 0.24 mK at γ = 2π × 10 MHz), the weak-binding bound-atom treatment that shares the emission recoil isotropically (1/3 per axis) and needs three orthogonal beams, one beam along (1, 1, 1) when the three frequencies differ, or collisional thermalization, the resolved-sideband floor ⟨n⟩ = (5/16)(γ/Ω_x)² for a carrier-plus-two-sideband emission spectrum, and the exact first and second moments of the emission recoil for isotropic emission, ⟨ΔE⟩ = R and ⟨(ΔE)²⟩ − R² = (2/3)R⟨H_t⟩ (Eqs. 36-37, from a commutator identity valid for bound and free atoms; the invariant form (ħ²k²/M²)Σ_iα_i⟨P_i²⟩ generalizes it to an anisotropic pattern and the printed ⟨H_t⟩ form under-predicts the free-atom Doppler variance by exactly 2) **[verified]**; their per-axis bookkeeping silently charges the full 2R per event to the driven axis, that is α = 1, which is why their ħγ/2 Doppler total is the (1 + α)/4 form at α = 1 and their 5/16 sideband floor is (α + 1/4)/4 at α = 1, and their isotropic partition (4R/3 along the beam, R/3 transverse) is replaced by the trace-one emission tensor diag(α_x, α_y, α_z), R(1 + α_∥) on the driven axis and Rα_⊥ on each transverse one **[corrected]**; the RMP's ξ = 2/5 is thus the σ pattern along the beam, and Rasmusson et al. 2021's n̄_D ≈ Γ/(2ω) is the bare form without it, so a test that compares Doppler limits must state which α it carries. The RMP's ξ = 2/5 in the Doppler limit of Section 4.2.1 is therefore the σ pattern along the field or the π pattern perpendicular to it, and the 1.43 fork between k_B T_min = 0.35ħΓ and ħΓ/2 recorded there is the difference between including this factor and not; n̄_D comes from the Section 4.2.2 rate coefficients evaluated with the configured α and cos²θ_L, as Section 4.2.1 requires, and the force-model value is reported only as the ν/Γ < 0.1 cross-check (the second revision's sentence here still named the force model as the producer, against 4.2.1; 2026-09-04 critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**. Sizes: for 171Yb+ at 369.5 nm on a 3 MHz mode, k x₀ = 0.053, so a scattered photon deposits about 1.1 × 10⁻³ quanta with α = 2/5; the few photons of optical pumping (Section 4.2.6) or a repump step therefore leave Δn ≈ 3 × 10⁻³, which is the quantitative content of the sources' "Δn ≈ 0", while the 10⁴ photons of Doppler cooling deposit tens of quanta, which is the Doppler limit itself; a Rayleigh event during a gate (probability of order 10⁻⁴, Section 6.5) heats by about 10⁻⁷ quanta, present but negligible.

**Cross-source reconciliation (Run 4R) [verified], [corrected].** The follow-up run established the following, each by reading the equation on the page and recomputing it. (i) The exact recoil term above is what Cirac et al. 1992 Eqs. 1-3, Steck Eqs. 5.416-5.417 and the one-dimensional reduction Γ∫₋₁¹ du f̃(u) 𝓓[e^{−ik_em u ẑ}]ρ all write, with three normalizations in the literature that must not be mixed: Itano's and Steck's three-dimensional density integrates to one over the sphere, Steck's azimuthally reduced f̃(u) integrates to one on [−1, 1], and Cirac's W(x) carries the explicit measure dx/2, so that f̃(u) = 2πf(θ, φ) = W(u)/2, and dropping Cirac's ½ doubles the recycling rate and breaks trace preservation. Cirac's W = (3/4)(1 + x²) is not a generic dipole pattern despite the paper's wording: it is the σ pattern with the mode axis along the quantization axis, and the two published values of 2/5 are different geometries (Itano Eq. 22 is the π pattern with the mode perpendicular to the dipole axis; Cirac's and Itano's 24Mg+ f_sz are the σ pattern along it) that coincide numerically **[corrected]**. (ii) The emission diffusion coefficient in the adiabatically eliminated motional master equation is D = ½ Σ_{i→j} ρ_ii^SS Γ_{i→j} α_{ij,m} η_ij², one Lamb-Dicke parameter per decay channel built from that channel's own wavenumber and one angular factor per channel and mode axis, and it multiplies Cirac's half-rate dissipator L_em μ = D(2XμX − X²μ − μX²) = 2D·𝒟[X] with X = a + a†, so its contribution to the phonon heating rate is 2D = Σ ρ_ii Γ_ij α_ij η_ij², which collapses to α η_em² R_sc only when every channel shares one pattern and one wavenumber (an implementer who feeds D to the plan's global 𝒟[L] convention halves the heating, and one mean α is up to 37% wrong for mixed π and σ channels; derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**; Cirac's γ_ji is a half rate and Marzoli's printed Eq. 4 reads as full rates and is twice this, while Marzoli's Eq. B4, an independent Lamb-Dicke expansion of the exact V-system equations, confirms the half-rate form **[corrected]**. α multiplies only the spontaneously emitted photon's recoil; the absorption recoil enters through e^{ik_L·x̂} in the Hamiltonian and never through a collapse operator, and the V-system form D = (s₁₀/4)ρ₀₀[Γ₁₂(η₁₀² + αη₁₂²) + Γ₁₀η₁₀²(1 + α)] is the test that catches both an α on the absorbed photon and a missing 1 on the closed cycle. (iii) The rate coefficients are A_± = 2Re[S(∓ν) + D] in general, with η² inside S and D, and, below saturation, W(Δ) → Ω²Γ/(4Δ² + Γ²) = (Ω²/Γ)L(Δ) with the dimensionless Lorentzian L(Δ) = Γ²/(4Δ² + Γ²), so that A_± = (Ω²/Γ)[L(Δ ∓ ν) + (η̃²/η²)L(Δ)], which is Eschner et al. 2003 Eq. 6 once their unprojected η² and explicit cos²θ_L are folded into the plan's η_{i,m} (Δk·ê_m inside η, Section 4.1.3) and their α into (η̃/η)²; the code stores the bare A_± in s⁻¹ with W(Δ) = Γρ_ee from `light/bloch.py`, which returns a rate for both of its consumers, and η² stays outside A_± in the rate equation Ṗ(n) of Section 4.2.3 (the second revision printed (Ω²/Γ)η²[cos²θ_L W(Δ ∓ ν) + αW(Δ)] here, η² inside and the projection twice, which fed into 4.2.3 would have multiplied every cooling rate by a second η² while leaving every n̄ test unchanged; the test is that η²(A₋ − A₊) reproduces Lechner's 19 × 10³ s⁻¹; 2026-09-04 critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**: this is Section 4.2.2's form, and Cirac's printed Eqs. 50 and 52 have the sideband sign correlated with the rate index (heating at red detuning) and lack a factor 2η², both corrected by three independent routes **[corrected]**. (iv) The steady state is not a recoil floor: η² = ω_R/ν cancels identically from A₊/(A₋ − A₊), so the recoil frequency sets the cooling rate and not n̄; at Δ = −ν with Γ ≪ ν, n̄_SB = (Γ/2ν)²[α(k_em/k_L)²/cos²θ_L + 1/4] = (Γ/2ν)²[(η̃/η)² + 1/4], which is Roos's Eq. 3.20 with (η̃/η)² = α(k_em/k_L)²/cos²θ_L, and α → 0 leaves (Γ/4ν)² from off-resonant blue-sideband excitation, not zero; at α = 2/5 with k_em = k_L and one on-axis beam the recoil term is 62% of n̄ and the blue sideband 38%, the closed-cycle special case, while the quenched 40Ca+ scheme of Section 4.2.2 (729 nm drive, 393 nm recoil photon, (k_em/k_L)² = 3.44, (η̃/η)² = 1.37) has bracket 1.62, the regression (the second revision's bracket here dropped the (k_em/k_L)² its own sentence names and returned 0.65 for that case, the very number 4.2.2 marks as the uncorrected value; 2026-09-04 theorist critique) **[verified]**, **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**. In the Doppler regime at Δ = −Γ/2 the same coefficients give n̄_D = (Γ/4ν)(1 + α/cos²θ_L), Itano and Wineland's E_K = (1 + f_s)ħΓ/8 (ħΓ/6 for α = 1/3, 7ħΓ/40 for 2/5), their three-beam optimum γ_si/γ_tot = √f_si/Σ_j√f_sj, and a single beam along one axis leaves the other two heating linearly with no three-dimensional steady state **[verified]**. (v) For a quenched or repumped upper level the effective two-level parameters are Γ′ = ΠΓ₁₀ and γ′ = Π(Γ₁₀ + Γ₁₂)/2 with Π = (Ω_aux/2)²/[δ_aux² + ((Γ₁₀ + Γ₁₂)/2)²] = s_aux/2 (Marzoli Eqs. 12, 15; Roos Eq. 3.21, whose (Γ_aux + Γ) is the total fast-level linewidth), so γ′/Γ′ is (Γ₁₀ + Γ₁₂)/(2Γ₁₀) and not ½, the resolved-sideband criterion is ν ≫ Γ′ and ν ≫ γ′ separately, and in the V configuration the effective roles swap so that cooling needs blue detuning δ₂₀ = +ν **[verified]**; Cirac's Λ-plus-repumper system gives ⟨n⟩_min = 1/√β − ½ at Ω_φ² = 4Δν/√β inside the window R ≪ ν ≪ Γ ≪ Δ (0.554 at β = 0.9, 2.66 at β = 0.1 for Γ = 1, ν = 0.1, Δ = 10), which reproduces the paper's Fig. 8 **[verified]**. (vi) Printed errors the implementer must override, not copy: Cirac Eq. 7 (operator ordering, which would weight diffusion by the lower level), Eq. 28 (index order), Eqs. 50 and 52 (above), Eq. 54 (ρ_g omitted); Itano and Wineland Eq. 14 (a plus for an equals); Steck Eq. 5.522 (the pattern weight omitted, so it evaluates to 4π/3), Eq. 19.214 (a spurious tilde) and Eq. 19.212 (the integral-sign subscript on Ω); Roos Eq. 3.11 (Laguerre index n rather than n_< for m < 0, a factor 2 at (n, m) = (1, −1) and 2.9 at (8, −3)), the exponent of Section 4.3.1's form being already correct **[corrected]**. (vii) Validity conditions the module asserts at run time rather than documents: η_ij²(2n + 1) ≪ 1 per transition including the emitted photon, Ω ≪ Γ for every closed form, cooling rate W ≪ ν and ≪ every internal rate for the adiabatic elimination, Γ′, γ′ ≪ ν for resolved sidebands and Γ > ω_R for Doppler cooling, s_aux ≪ 1 and |δ| ≪ Γ₁₀ + Γ₁₂ for the three-level reduction, and the reduction's neglect of the ion's motion during its stay in the fast level, whose error no source quantifies and which the level-C solve measures. Two gaps the sources leave and the simulator fills by construction: no source works out the joint multi-mode recoil dissipator, which the product of displacements over modes with one sampled direction k̂ is, tested by the Cartesian sum rule Σ_axes α = 1, the single-kick expectation and Itano's per-event invariant Σ_i⟨ΔE_i⟩ = 2R + ħk·v; and no source treats a mode axis oblique to the quantization axis or a decay that is a coherent superposition of q components, for which the scalar patterns are insufficient and the jump operator per direction and polarization must be the vector form Σ_q(ε̂*_{k̂λ}·ê_q) d_q e^{−ik_em k̂·x̂}, which sums over the two polarizations to the scalar patterns when one q decays and carries Steck's tensor f_qq′ otherwise **[background]**; the module builds that form and derives α from it, so no scalar α is ever hard-coded.

**Implementation as collapse operators.** QuTiP needs a finite set of collapse operators, not an integral over directions. The module discretizes each decay channel's emission pattern on a quadrature of K directions with weights w_k (a product Gauss-Legendre grid in cos θ and trapezoid in φ, or Lebedev), giving K operators √(Γ w_k) |g⟩⟨e| ⊗ Π_m D_m(−i k_eg b_{i,m} x₀,m k̂_k·ê_m) per channel and emitting ion, exact to the order of the quadrature in η̃; for a mode along a principal axis the reduction to one dimension uses 16 Gauss-Legendre nodes on [−1, 1] with p_j = w_j f̃(u_j), which is exact to 10⁻¹⁰ for η_em < 0.3 because the integrand is a low-order polynomial times a smooth exponential; the one-dimensional marginals for the principal orientations are (3/4)(1 − u²) for a π pattern along the axis (α = 1/5), (3/8)(1 + u²) for a σ pattern along it or a π pattern perpendicular to it (α = 2/5; the same marginal, not merely the same α), (9 − 3u²)/16 for a σ pattern perpendicular (3/10) and ½ for isotropic emission (1/3), and two Gauss-Legendre nodes return α = 1/3 for every quadratic marginal, so three nodes are the minimum for the second moment and six to eight for the full Δn kernel at η_em ≤ 0.9 (a Run 4 brief's claim that two nodes suffice was refuted by its own consolidation) **[verified]**, **[corrected]**. Morigi's EIT figure is the closed form's test in the other direction: at her Fig. 3 parameters (ν = 2.0068, γ = 20, Ω₁ = Ω₂ = 17 MHz, Δ_Morigi = −70 MHz, which is Δ = +70 MHz in the plan's sign, Section 13, because her optimum reads Ω² = 4ν(ν − Δ_Morigi) where Section 4.2.3's reads Ω_r² = 4ν(ν + Δ), so Δ = −Δ_Morigi) the rate coefficients give n̄ = 0.005102 against (γ/4|Δ|)² = 0.0051020 and her caption's 0.005, while the caption's printed Δ_Morigi = +70 MHz (Δ = −70 in the plan's sign) returns −1.005 from the Section 4.2.3 closed form, a negative occupation that trips its own A₋ − A₊ ≤ 0 guard, so the module is parameterized from her body text; the two Rabi frequencies enter that closed form as the quadrature sum Ω_r = √(Ω₁² + Ω₂²) = 24.04 MHz, the value that satisfies Ω_r² = 4ν(ν + Δ) = 578 at Δ = +70 (a single 17 in its place returns 0.147, 29 times the target; `check_critique_v3.py`), and since Ω₁ = Ω₂ sits outside the weak-probe regime Ω_g ≪ Ω_r of Section 4.2.3, level C rather than the closed form validates the figure (the second revision quoted the fixture in Morigi's sign with neither the sign map nor the composition rule; 2026-09-04 experimentalist critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**, **[recomputed here]**; her optimum Ω² = 4ν(ν − Δ_Morigi) is leading order in γ/|Δ| (the exact stationary point is 0.5% below) **[verified]**, **[corrected]**. Three assertions run before any solve: Σ_j p_j = 1 and Σ_j p_j u_j² = α to 10⁻¹², so that a failure is a quadrature bug and never a physics one; Σ_k C_k†C_k = Γ|e⟩⟨e| ⊗ 𝟙 to machine precision, because the kicks are unitary and the internal decay rate must not depend on the motion; and the single-kick expectation, the Kraus map applied once to |e, 0⟩ giving ⟨n_m⟩ = α_m b_{i,m}² η_em,m² exactly with ⟨p⟩ = 0. The minimal quadrature that reproduces the first and second moments exactly (for each emission axis a ±k̂ pair with weights α/2 each, plus the complementary weight on a no-recoil operator, each axis resolved over its modes through b_{i,m}) is the default for Lamb-Dicke-regime cooling and the sideband floor, which need nothing beyond second order; the full quadrature is the option for hot ions, where the Δn distribution's tails matter. Trajectories (`mcsolve`) then produce discrete recoil jumps whose direction-by-direction cross term −2R k̂_i k̂_si averages to zero but contributes shot-to-shot variance that `mesolve` cannot see, and `mesolve` the averaged kernel; the semi-analytic path solves the internal-only steady state with `steadystate`, obtains S(±ν) from `spectrum` or `correlation_2op_1t` of the dipole-force operator on the internal Liouvillian, forms D from the populations, and raises rather than returning a negative n̄ when A₋ − A₊ ≤ 0. With recoil switched off the operators reduce to the internal-state collapse operators of Section 4.5.5, which is the d > 2 scattering model of Section 6.5.

**The multi-level optical Bloch equations.** With the levels and matrix elements of Section 4.5 the cooling, pumping and detection stages share one Hamiltonian builder: H = Σ_p E_p|p⟩⟨p| + Σ_beams Σ_{(p,q)} (ħ/2) Ω^{(beam)}_{pq}(t) e^{−iω_beam t} |q⟩⟨p| + h.c., with E_p the field-dependent energies of Section 4.5.1 and Ω_{pq} the polarization-resolved Rabi frequencies of Section 4.5.2, plus the motional Hamiltonian and the drive's displacement operators when a mode is included (level C). A rotating frame that removes the optical frequencies exists when each fine-structure manifold can be assigned one frame frequency such that every beam's detuning from every transition it drives is small: the builder assigns frame frequencies manifold by manifold, checks each beam against the manifolds it connects, moves the residual detunings onto the diagonal, and flags any beam whose residual is inconsistent with an already assigned manifold (two beams on one transition at different frequencies, or a closed loop of beams whose frequencies do not sum consistently), in which case the Hamiltonian is explicitly time periodic and is integrated as such or handled with `FloquetBasis`. The steady state of this system (`steadystate`) is the single scattering-rate object of Section 13 that supplies W(Δ) for cooling (Section 4.2.2), R_∘, R_d and R_b for readout (Section 8.1) and the dark-state physics of coherent population trapping; its time evolution from a given initial state gives the optical-pumping fidelity and duration of Section 4.2.6 from first principles, which fills the gap Run 3 named from both ends of the stack; and with one motional mode and the recoil operators above it is the level-C cooling simulation of Sections 4.2.1 to 4.2.4. The effective two-level descriptions of those sections (repumper-broadened linewidth Γ̃, the three-level EIT Fano profile, the two-level Doppler force) are recovered from it by adiabatic elimination under the conditions Marzoli et al. 1994 state, which Run 4 supplies; the simulator tests each closed form against the level-C solve in its stated regime.

**Pulsed sideband cooling with exact matrix elements** (Che et al. 2017; Rasmusson et al. 2021) **[verified]**, **[corrected]**. The rate picture of Section 4.2.2 is completed for pulsed schemes with the exact Ω_{n,n−k} of Section 4.3.1: one cycle, a k-th-order red-sideband pulse of duration t (a free parameter, not a π time; Rasmusson's worked example is t = 1.016 × 2π/Ω) followed by fast optical pumping, is a column-stochastic transfer matrix W_k(t) on the Fock populations, one matrix per sideband order with diagonal a_n = cos²(Ω_{n,n−k}t/2) and k-th upper diagonal b_n = sin²(Ω_{n,n−k}t/2), coherences being discarded between pulses because the pumping erases them; N pulses compose as an ordered matrix product, and the mean occupation after a schedule is Σ_n n[W(t_{N−1})⋯W(t₀) p_th]_n. Three optimizations are supported: a single shared pulse time, independent pulse times by gradient descent, and one pulse time per sideband order with higher orders applied first, which the sources find optimal (Che's 75-pulse schedule for 25Mg+ from n̄ = 17 at η = 0.3: fifteen second-order pulses, fifteen first-order, fifteen second-order, thirty first-order, 9 µs each at Ω₀/2π = 150 kHz). The exact matrix elements are what make higher orders necessary: because Ω_{n,n−k} ∝ L^{(k)}_{n−k}(η²) has zeros, single-order cooling strands population at the Rabi node. At η = 0.3 the first zero of L^{(1)}_{n′}(0.09) lies at n′ = 39.8 and that of L^{(2)}_{n′}(0.09) at n′ = 71.8 **[recomputed here]**, so with the index n′ = n − k of Che's Eq. 2 the stranded states are n = 41 and n = 74, whereas Che's Fig. 2 and simulations report 40 and 72, the roots indexed by the initial n rather than by n − k, an off-by-k inconsistency internal to the paper; the simulator uses the exact element, reproduces Che's accumulation centres (43, 41, 40 after 40, 150, 500 first-order cycles and 75, 73, 72 for the second order) only with the shifted index, and treats that comparison as a test of the index convention rather than of the physics **[corrected]**. Two more of Che's printed forms are not copied: his Eq. 4 prints the thermal distribution without the exponent n (the Fig. 2 inset is the geometric n̄ⁿ/(n̄ + 1)^{n+1}), and his carrier Ω₀e^{−η²/2} is the n = 0 value only, the general carrier Ω₀e^{−η²/2}L_n(η²) having a zero between n = 15 and 16 at η = 0.3, next to his n̄ = 17 **[corrected]**. Repumping heats by off-resonant Raman scattering during the pumping interval, Δn̄ = t_re s_re Γ_re³η²/(4Δ_HF²) (0.03 quanta per 10 µs repump for 25Mg+), which caps the cooling at about 0.97 quanta per cycle and is the recoil term of this subsection in its Λ-system form. Thermometry after such cooling must not assume a thermal distribution: Rasmusson's time-averaged red-sideband signal P̄^{RSB}_{↑,m} converges to half the tail sum Σ_{n≥m} p(n) independently of the decoherence rate, and stepping the sideband order m extracts individual populations, while the ratio method r = n̄/(n̄ + 1) of Section 4.2.7 holds for thermal states only, so the simulator's thermometry experiments offer both and the double-thermal model p = αp_th(n̄_l) + (1 − α)p_th(n̄_h) as the fit for post-cooling distributions. Anchors: Rasmusson's 171Yb+ at ω_z = 2π × 0.670 MHz and η = 0.18, where 50 multiorder pulses (first, second and third order, W_m built from Ω_{n,n−m} for each) from n̄ = 15.36 reach n̄ = 0.06 while single-order cooling leaves about 0.3 quanta stranded above the first-order zero near n = 112, and where 25 first-order fixed pulses from n̄ = 14.6 predict n̄_sim = 3.57(58) against measured thermometry of 0.58(56) (ratio), 8.0(1.3) (SVD) and 4.1(7) (time-averaged), so that only n̄_sim is a target and the three measurements are anchors of the estimator bias; Che's 25Mg+ at 2π × 1.5 MHz with η = 0.3 and a 500 Hz decoherence rate on 151 Fock levels. This also supplies the second-sideband cooling rate that Run 3 listed as missing: it is the same expression with k = 2 and the exact matrix element, not a Lamb-Dicke expansion. Morigi 2003 completes the EIT picture of Section 4.2.3 at the master-equation level: with the Λ system's recoil kernel included, the second-order recoil-diffusion term vanishes identically at two-photon resonance, so EIT cooling has no recoil floor and its optimum ⟨n⟩ = (γ/4|Δ|)² stands unchanged, while the effective Lamb-Dicke parameter of the scheme is the projected difference η₁cos φ₁ − η₂cos φ₂ of the two legs (each η_j = k_j x₀ from the full wavevector, the projection applied separately, and the Lamb-Dicke expansion parameter being the thermally inflated η_j√(2⟨n⟩ + 1)), zero in a Doppler-free geometry **[verified]**; two of Morigi's printed forms are not copied: her Eq. 22 with her own α = ∫N cos²φ overstates the recoil diffusion by a factor 2 (the Liouvillian prefactor is α/2, the half-rate form of the diffusion coefficient above), and the arXiv v1 Eq. 29 has a plus for a minus that breaks probability conservation; the recoil-free property itself, P̃₀L̃₂P̃₀ = 0 because the dark steady state has no excited population, stands **[corrected]**.
4.2.8.title: Spontaneous emission with recoil, and the multi-level master equation

4.3.text: This is the core of the simulator: one Hamiltonian builder that every pulse goes through. The conventions below are the simulator's; Section 13 lists the alternatives the sources use.
4.3.title: Spin-motion interaction Hamiltonian and single-qubit control

4.3.1.text:
For N ions with internal transition frequency ω₀, modes m with frequencies ω_m and ladder operators a_m, and a running-wave drive on ion i with Rabi frequency Ω_i, effective wavevector projection δk along the motional axis, frequency ω_L and phase φ_i, the lab-frame Hamiltonian is (Monroe 2020 Eqs. 6-7; RMP 2003 Eqs. 60-63; Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.1) **[verified]**

H_lab = (ω₀/2) Σ_i σ_z^i + Σ_m ω_m a_m†a_m − Σ_i d̂_i · E(X̂_i),  E_i = E_{i0} cos(k X̂_i − ω_L t − φ_i),

with ħ = 1 and X̂_i = X̄_i + Σ_m b_{im} ξ_m^{(0)}(a_m + a_m†), ξ_m^{(0)} = √(ħ/2Mω_m). Moving to the frame of the qubit and applying the optical rotating-wave approximation (dropping e^{±i(ω_L+ω₀)t}, valid for ω_L, ω₀ ≫ Ω) leaves the exact spin-motion interaction (Monroe Eq. 8, in the interaction picture for the motion) **[verified]**

H = Σ_i (Ω_i/2) σ₊^i e^{i(δk X̄_i − μ_i t − δφ_i)} Π_m exp[iη_{im}(a_m† e^{iω_m t} + a_m e^{−iω_m t})] + h.c.,

where μ_i = ω_L − ω₀ is the detuning from the carrier and η_{im} = b_{im} δk ξ_m^{(0)} the Lamb-Dicke parameter of ion i on mode m (Section 4.1.3). The simulator keeps the motion in the Schrödinger picture instead (Section 5.2), so the operator Π_m exp[iη_{im}(a_m + a_m†)] = Π_m D_m(iη_{im}) is time independent and the time dependence sits in the scalar coefficient (Ω_i(t)/2) e^{−i(μ_i t − φ_i(t))}. Resonances occur when μ_i = Σ_m ℓ_m ω_m for integers ℓ_m, the sideband of total order p = Σ|ℓ_m| carrying a prefactor of order η^p/√(p!), since ⟨p|D(iη)|0⟩ = e^{−η²/2}(iη)^p/√(p!) **[corrected; the earlier η^p/p! understates the third and fourth sidebands by 2.4 and 4.9 times at η = 0.1, and the truncation and mode-dropping heuristics use the exact element rather than the scaling]**. The RMP 2003 form of the same expansion carries the micromotion sidebands through the Floquet function u(t); as printed, its Eqs. 67-68 and the sentence "β_x ω_rf ≈ ν" drop a factor 1/2 relative to the paper's own Eq. 37 (ν = β_x ω_rf/2), which would double the secular sideband spacing in the micromotion comb **[corrected]**.

**Exact matrix elements.** For a single mode the coupling between |↓, n⟩ and |↑, n′⟩ is (Wineland 1998 Eq. 18; RMP 2003 Eq. 70) **[verified]**

⟨n′| e^{iη(a+a†)} |n⟩ = ⟨n′|D(iη)|n⟩ = e^{−η²/2} (iη)^{|n′−n|} (n_<!/n_>!)^{1/2} L^{|n′−n|}_{n_<}(η²),  Ω_{n′,n} = Ω |⟨n′|D(iη)|n⟩| = Ω e^{−η²/2} (n_<!/n_>!)^{1/2} |η|^{|n′−n|} |L^{|n′−n|}_{n_<}(η²)|,

exact in η for one running-wave drive and one mode, the signed element being what the builder uses and the modulus what a Rabi frequency means (the first two revisions equated the modulus to the signed Laguerre expression, which is negative for odd |n′ − n| at negative η and beyond the polynomial's first zero, already at n = 6 to 8 for η = 0.5; caught by the derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. In the Lamb-Dicke regime, η√⟨(a+a†)²⟩ ≪ 1 (a state-dependent condition), this reduces to Ω for the carrier, ηΩ√n for the first red and ηΩ√(n+1) for the first blue sideband **[verified]**, and the first-order Hamiltonian is (RMP Eq. 72) H_LD = (ħ/2)Ω₀σ₊{1 + iη(a e^{−iνt} + a†e^{iνt})}e^{i(φ−δt)} + h.c., with the red sideband a Jaynes-Cummings and the blue an anti-Jaynes-Cummings coupling **[verified]**. Because the builder uses D(iη) exactly, the Debye-Waller factors are included automatically: the carrier operator on each spectator mode is D̂_{im} = e^{−η_{im}²/2} L_{n_m}(η_{im}²) ≈ 1 − η_{im}²(n_m + 1/2) + … (Monroe Eq. 11) **[verified]**, its thermal average is exp[−η_p²(n̄_p + 1/2)] per mode, and Wineland 1998 Eqs. 122-127 give both the mean and the rms shot-to-shot fluctuation of the Rabi frequency when spectator modes are thermal and frozen during a run (their worked example: 100 modes at n̄ = 0.1, η = 0.01) **[verified]**. The sideband Hamiltonians with driven-mode and spectator-mode Debye-Waller operators are Monroe Eqs. 16-19 **[verified]**.

**Two-level propagators for tests.** Within the subspace {|↓,n⟩, |↑,n′⟩} at detuning Δ from the (n′−n)-th sideband the exact propagator has generalized Rabi frequency (Δ² + 4Ω²_{n′,n})^{1/2} in Wineland's convention and f_n^l = √(δ′² + Ω²_{n+l,n}) in the RMP's, with the drive phase entering as φ + (π/2)|n′−n| (Wineland Eq. 21; RMP Eq. 84) **[verified]**; these closed forms are the unit tests for the builder. The resonant map is |↓⟩|n⟩ → cos(Ω_{n,n′}t)|↓⟩|n⟩ − i e^{iφ} sin(Ω_{n,n′}t)|↑⟩|n′⟩ in Wineland's half-Rabi convention (Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.4), which reads cos(Ω_{n,n′}t/2) and sin(Ω_{n,n′}t/2) in the plan's convention of the next paragraph, the conversion made once at ingest (2026-09-04 critique); the companion Eq. 2.5 is misprinted in the source (its left side should read |↑⟩|n′⟩) and must not be implemented as printed **[corrected]**.

**Rabi-frequency conventions.** Wineland 1998 defines ħΩ = −μ_M B₁/4, half the usual Rabi frequency, so its carrier π pulse is at Ωt = π/2 and its blue-sideband flopping appears at 2Ω_{n+1,n} (Eq. 42) **[verified]**; Monroe 1995 uses P = sin²(Ωτ) likewise **[verified]**; the RMP, Monroe 2020, Lee 2005 and Mount 2015 write H = (ħΩ/2)σ₊ + h.c. so that a π pulse is Ωt = π. The simulator uses the latter, Ω defined so that the resonant carrier flops as sin²(Ωt/2), and converts imported numbers.
4.3.1.title: The Hamiltonian the builder implements

4.3.2.text:
Two beams (fields E_j cos(k_j·x − ω_{Lj}t + φ_j), j = 1, 2) coupling |↓⟩ and |↑⟩ through far-detuned excited states |i⟩ produce, after adiabatic elimination (Δ_i ≫ γ_i and Δ_i ≫ the two-photon coupling), an effective Hamiltonian of the single-photon form with the substitutions (Wineland 2003 Eqs. 2.2-2.3; RMP Eq. A12; Wineland 1998 Eqs. 37-41) **[verified]**

k → Δk = k₁ − k₂,  ω_L → ω₁ − ω₂,  φ → φ₁ − φ₂,  Ω e^{iφ} → e^{i(φ₁−φ₂)}/(2ħ²) Σ_i ⟨↑|d·E₂ε̂₂|i⟩⟨i|d·E₁ε̂₁|↓⟩/Δ_i,

which is twice the coupling matrix element that Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.3 prints with 1/(4ħ²), because Ω here is defined by H = (ħΩ/2)σ₊ + h.c. while that paper's Ω is defined by ħΩσ₊ (Section 4.3.1); for a single intermediate state it is Ω₁Ω₂/(2Δ) in single-photon Rabi frequencies of the same convention (Section 4.5.4), and the same 1/(4ħ²) prefactor is correct for the ac Stark shift below, because a level shift and a half-Rabi-frequency share it (the first version of this plan substituted the 1/(4ħ²) form into the (ħΩ/2) slot; caught by the 2026-09-04 critique) **[corrected]**.

The Lamb-Dicke parameter becomes η = Δk z₀ (counter-propagating beams: |Δk| ≈ 2k; co-propagating: Δk ≈ 0, no motional coupling **[verified]**). Factor-of-2 traps: with single-photon Rabi frequencies defined through (ħΩ/2)-type couplings, the RMP's Eq. A13 reads Ω = −2|Ω_{g3}Ω_{e3}|/Δ_R, which is twice "the product divided by Δ_R" and four times a coupling-strength reading **[corrected]**; the arXiv v1 preprint of Lee et al. 2005 (quant-ph/0505203v1) prints the ac Stark shift χ_{m,i} with denominator 2 where 2Δ is required, dimensionally a frequency squared, and swaps the beam-to-level assignment in its Eq. 2, whereas the published J. Opt. B version prints both correctly; the errata check of 2026-09-04 traced the first revision's reading to the preprint (pdftotext also drops the Δ glyph from the journal PDF, which is the likely route in) **[corrected: preprint only]**. The simulator computes the two-photon Rabi frequency and the light shifts from the dipole matrix elements, detunings and intensities in one function, with tests against the 9Be+ closed forms below.

**ac Stark shifts.** Each beam j shifts each qubit level m_S by δ(m_S, j) = (1/4ħ²) Σ_i |⟨m_S|d·E_jε̂_j|i⟩|²/Δ_i (Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.10) **[verified]**; for the 9Be+ |2,2⟩ ↔ |1,1⟩ qubit the eight-term differential shift (Eq. 2.11) collapses for ω₀ ≪ Δ, ω_F to Eq. 2.12 and has a polarization null **[verified]**. For clock qubits the differential shift is the difference of four detuning-weighted diagonal amplitudes, Δ_St = g²[a^{(1/2)}_{↑↑}/(Δ+Δ_hf) + a^{(3/2)}_{↑↑}/(Δ+Δ_hf−Δ_f) − a^{(1/2)}_{↓↓}/Δ − a^{(3/2)}_{↓↓}/(Δ−Δ_f)] (Ozeri 2005 Eq. 3) **[verified]**; for far-detuned clock-qubit Raman drives the ratio of total scattering to Stark phase saturates at 0.9579 γ/Δ_hf ≈ 0.0154 photons per radian for 9Be+ **[verified]**. In a bichromatic drive with asymmetric detunings μ_{i+}, μ_{i−} the Stark term is s_i = μ_{i+} − μ_{i−} (Monroe Eq. 20) **[verified]**. Stark shifts enter the builder as time-dependent σ_z terms proportional to the instantaneous intensity envelope, so amplitude-shaped pulses shift the qubit frequency during the pulse exactly as in the laboratory; the third-tone cancellation used by Innsbruck (Section 4.4) is a scheduled drive like any other.

**Clock-qubit Raman coupling and scattering** (Ozeri et al. 2007) **[verified]**. For the |F = I−1/2, m_F = 0⟩ ↔ |F = I+1/2, m_F = 0⟩ transition driven by a blue/red beam pair detuned Δ from P₁/₂ (Δ − ω_f from P₃/₂):

Ω_R = (g_b g_r/3)(b₋r₋ − b₊r₊) ω_f/[Δ(Δ − ω_f)],

so the coupling interferes destructively between the two fine-structure paths and falls as 1/Δ² for |Δ| ≫ ω_f, exactly like the Raman scattering amplitude **[verified]** (Ozeri 2005: the P₁/₂ and P₃/₂ Raman amplitudes are equal in magnitude and opposite in sign, while the Rayleigh amplitudes share a sign but not a magnitude **[corrected]**). The probability of any scattering event during a π rotation depends only on γ, ω_f and Δ, with all power and waist dependence cancelling:

P_total = (πγ/ω_f)(2Δ² + (Δ − ω_f)²)/|Δ(Δ − ω_f)|,  minimum at Δ = (√2 − 1)ω_f,  P_∞ = 3πγ/ω_f **[verified]**;

the single-qubit gate error is the Raman-scattering probability, ε_S = P_Raman (Eq. 11), whose minimum inside the fine-structure interval is 8πγ/(3ω_f) **[corrected]** (the extracted item called it a maximum), and which in laboratory quantities reads ε_S = 2π|Ω_R| ħ ω_{3/2}³ w₀²/(3c²P) with P the power per beam and w₀ the waist (Eq. 17), the paper's "λ_{3/2} = c/ω_{3/2}" being a typo for 2πc/ω **[verified flag]**. Scattering into low-lying D levels is not protected by the interference: ε_D = f P_total with branching ratio f, giving an irreducible floor ε_D∞ = 3πγf/ω_f (Eqs. 19-21); Table I of that paper gives f⁻¹ = 17 (43Ca+), 14 (87Sr+), 3 (137Ba+), 290 (171Yb+), 700 (199Hg+), and no D level for 9Be+, 25Mg+, 67Zn+, 111Cd+ **[verified]**. Rayleigh scattering at large detuning does not decohere a hyperfine qubit but imparts recoil, which matters for gates through motion (Section 4.4) **[verified]**. The species module stores Ozeri's Table I constants (for 9Be+: I = 3/2, γ/2π = 19.6 MHz, ω₀/2π = 1.25 GHz, ω_f/2π = 0.198 THz, λ = 313.1/313.0 nm; 43Ca+: I = 7/2, 22.5 MHz, 3.23 GHz, 6.68 THz, 396.8/393.4 nm) and the η convention warning that Ozeri's z₀ carries a factor 4 under the root **[verified flag]**. The scattering channels are implemented as Lindblad operators on the extended internal space (d > 2) with rates Γ_{i,f} = g²γ|a^{(1/2)}_{i→f}/Δ + a^{(3/2)}_{i→f}/(Δ − Δ_f)|² summed over final states **[verified]**, and as an estimated per-pulse error when d = 2.

**Frequency-comb Raman drives** (Mount et al. 2015) **[verified]**. A mode-locked comb drives the qubit through the resonant tooth pair and, with weights 1 : 2 : 1, through off-resonant pairs at δ′ and 2δ′; a second-order Magnus average turns these into a static detuning tilt, so the imperfect pulse propagator is R = exp[−(i/2)θ(1 + ε)(σ_φ + δZ)] with a multiplicative area error ε and a dimensionless detuning δ **[verified]**. This is the error model the simulator uses for composite-pulse tests, and it is all that Section 4.3.5 needs; Section 4.3.7 builds the comb drive itself from first principles, as a set of tones over tooth pairs of which Mount's three-term model is the truncation, together with the comb's own resonance conditions, ac Stark shifts and noise channels.
4.3.2.title: Stimulated-Raman drives

4.3.3.text: A microwave field drives the hyperfine transition directly with η ≈ 0 (no motional coupling without a field gradient). Harty et al. 2014 fix the archetype **[verified]**: 43Ca+ clock qubit S₁/₂^{4,0} ↔ S₁/₂^{3,+1} at B₀ = 146.094 G, f₀ = 3,199,941,077 Hz (after removing a −5 Hz differential ac Zeeman shift from trap rf currents), curvature d²f/dB² = 2.4 mHz/mG², μ_I = −1.31535 μ_N with inverted ordering (F = 3 above F = 4); drive from a frequency-octupled 400 MHz DDS with Ω/2π = 21 kHz, t_{π/2} = 12.1 µs, 14 µs dead time for DDS phase switching, deliberate detuning +4.5 Hz and amplitude stability |ΔΩ/Ω| ≲ 5 × 10⁻⁴. The imperfectly polarized field couples off-resonantly to spectator Zeeman transitions Δ_Z/2π ≈ 50 MHz away, giving spectator flopping of order (Ω/Δ_Z)² ≈ 10⁻⁷ and an ac Zeeman shift of the qubit transition of −1.0 Hz; with the convention δ = ω_drive − ω₀ a negative transition shift increases the detuning, δ_eff = δ − δ_ac = +5.5 Hz **[corrected]** (the extracted item had the sign wrong). The paper's own error model, a product of imperfect π/2 propagators and 14 µs dead-time propagators over the longest randomized-benchmarking sequences, predicts 0.81(14) × 10⁻⁶ per gate against the measured 1.0(3) × 10⁻⁶ **[verified]**; the simulator reproduces this as a test (Section 9.2). Memory: Ramsey contrast exp(−t_R/T₂*) with T₂* = 50(10) s at the clock point, without shielding or decoupling **[verified]**.
4.3.3.title: Microwave drives

4.3.4.text: The drive phase φ = φ₁ − φ₂ (plus the geometric term δk X̄_i for the ion's equilibrium position) may be set to zero once per ion, after which every operation on that ion must be referenced to that phase **[verified]** (Wineland 2003). The carrier, red-sideband and blue-sideband Hamiltonians all carry the same optical phase factor e^{i(ΔkX_{0,i} − Δφ)} (Lee 2005 Eqs. 6-8) **[verified]**, so a carrier rotation axis at angle β_i in the xy plane is set by the beat-note phase (Monroe Eq. 10) **[verified]**. In a bichromatic drive the two optical phases recombine into a spin phase, the half-sum of the tone phases, that sets the axis σ_{φ_s} of the spin-dependent force, and a motion phase, the half-difference, that sets the phase of the force on the mode (Lee Eqs. 28-30; Monroe Eqs. 20-22) **[verified]**. The simulator's convention is Haljan's, φ_s = +(φ_b + φ_r)/2 for the half-sum (Sections 4.4.2 and 13); Lee writes φ_S = −(half-sum), whose minus sign the extracted prose had dropped **[corrected]**, and it is converted at ingest (the first version of this plan adopted Lee's sign here and Haljan's in Section 4.4.2, a contradiction caught by the 2026-09-04 critique). The axis of the force is not the half-sum itself: expanding the plan's own drive factor e^{i(Δk·x̂ − μt + φ)} to first order gives the sideband coupling an explicit i (iη(a + a†)), and i[σ₊e^{iψ} − h.c.] = σ_{ψ+π/2}, so in the same-Δk (phase-sensitive) geometry the force axis sits at π/2 + Δk·X̄_i + (φ_b + φ_r)/2, a quarter turn from the carrier axis at the same beat-note phase, while in the crossed-Δk (phase-insensitive) geometry η_r = −η_b adds a further π and Δk·X̄_i cancels; the constant offset is what the phase-frame alignment of Section 7.5 step 3 measures and the native MS(φ₀, φ₁) definition absorbs, so it changes no gate, but the Section 9.4 pin must carry it: an MS pulse with φ_b = φ_r = φ on ions at the frame origin entangles about the azimuth φ + π/2 in the same-Δk geometry (the second revision's '+φ' would have certified a quarter-turn error; derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. Whether the gate is phase sensitive or insensitive is decided by beam geometry: with two beat notes on the same beam pair both above (or below) the third beam's frequency, Δk_r = Δk_b and the optical phase enters the spin phase (sensitive); with one above and one below, Δk_r = −Δk_b and the optical phase enters only the motion phase, which cancels when the loop closes (insensitive) **[verified]**. Virtual Z rotations are frame updates: RZ(θ) on qubit i shifts the phase reference of every later pulse on i by −θ in time order (Section 7.6), costing no error beyond bookkeeping and no time beyond the hardware's phase-switching dead time **[corrected]**, and identity gates in benchmarking are implemented as delays of one pulse duration so that idle errors are counted **[verified]** (Harty 2014).
4.3.4.title: Phases, frames and virtual Z

4.3.5.text:
A native GPi(φ) or GPi2(φ) is a resonant carrier pulse of area π or π/2 with phase φ relative to the ion's frame; the target unitary is R(θ, φ) = exp(−iθσ_φ/2), σ_φ = X cos φ + Y sin φ **[verified]** (Mount 2015 Eq. 1). The half-Pauli generator is load-bearing for everything below: a 2π segment is exactly −I, and R(π, φ)R(α, β)R(π, φ)† = R(α, 2φ − β) is the in-plane reflection every corrector phase descends from, so halving the tabulated angles to "pulse areas" θ/2 breaks the 2π quantization and with it every sequence **[verified]**, **[recomputed here]**. Products run right to left, so a scheduler emitting (θ_l, φ_l) in time order folds them in reverse (Section 13), and a negative nominal area is played as a positive area at phase φ + π - exact under amplitude error and **not** under detuning error, the σ_z term not reversing with the drive phase.

**The static error primitive and the four channels.** Run 5 reconciled five composite-pulse sources onto one object **[verified]**: M(θ, φ; ε_a, ε_d) = exp[−iθ{(1 + ε_a)ρ̂(φ)·σ + ε_d σ_z}/2], ρ̂(φ) = (cos φ, sin φ, 0), exact for a square segment under time-independent errors. It is Section 6.4's R = exp[−(i/2)θ(1 + ε)(σ_φ + δZ)] (Mount 2015) and also Cummins' quaternion pulse, whose axis (cos φ, sin φ, ε_d)/√(1 + ε_d²) and angle θ√(1 + ε_d²) identify ε_a = g and ε_d = f = δ/ν₁ with no rescaling on ingest **[verified]**. Four systematic channels map onto it (Merrill and Brown Sec. 2.2.1) **[verified]**: **amplitude** ε_A = Ω′/Ω at fixed duration, M = R(θ(1 + ε_A), φ); **pulse length** ε_T = δt/Δt, the same propagator for a square pulse but kept separate so the coupled model v_{x,y} = u_{x,y}(1 + ε_T), v_z = (u_z + ε_D)(1 + ε_T) is reproducible; **addressing** ε_N = Ω′/Ω on a spectator, whose zero is **inverted** (ε_N = 0 is ideal, U_T = I, M = R(θε_N, φ)), so R(θ(1 + ε_N), φ) by analogy with ε_A is wrong; and **detuning** ε_D = Δ/Ω, whose error generator +ε_D θ H_z scales with pulse area and keeps its plus sign even where the drive phase is π and the in-plane term is negative - flipping it along with the middle CORPSE pulse makes all three generators commute and returns the bare-pulse infidelity to six digits **[verified]**. Amplitude and addressing errors have δu ∝ u, so the leading error is a vector sum; detuning does not commute with the ideal generator, which is why CORPSE needs a Magnus expansion and BB1 does not.

**Order bookkeeping and the fidelity measure.** Order n means residual O(ε^{n+1}), hence distance slope n + 1 and **infidelity slope 2(n + 1)**, never 2n; two source abstracts write O(ε^n) loosely against their own equations **[corrected]**. Three measures appear and differ by 2 and 4/3 in infidelity: F_C = |Tr(U_id†U)|/2 (Cummins' quaternion fidelity and Merrill-Brown's minimized-state form are the same number), F_K = ¼|Tr(U_id†U)|² = F_C², and F_avg = (2F_C² + 1)/3, so 1 − F_K = 2(1 − F_C) and 1 − F_avg = (4/3)(1 − F_C) to leading order **[verified]**, **[recomputed here]**. The simulator adopts F_K internally, the normalization Section 6.9's filter functions are built to, and converts on ingest; every published c-coefficient carries the same factor 2. Two printed "fidelities" must be replaced rather than implemented: Low-Yoder-Chuang's F = ‖UV†‖ is identically 1 for a qubit under its own normalized trace norm and Brown-Harrow-Chuang's 1 − ‖V†U‖ identically 0 for unitaries **[corrected]**, **[recomputed here]**. Below E ≈ 10⁻⁸ a subtracted 1 − F hits the float64 floor, so sequences are scored by the operator distance and converted as E²/2, or run in mpmath as the check script does.

**The verified library.** Each family is a list of (θ_l, φ_l) in time order, folded right to left, with the target phase φ_t added rigidly to every entry **including** the zeroth pulse; adding it reproduces Z(φ_t)U_T^{(0)}Z(φ_t)† exactly, where subtracting it (the direction one source's prose suggests) leaves O(ε) **[corrected]**, **[recomputed here]**. The table gives the sequence, the quadrature it corrects, its order, and the printed defect the module repairs; k = arcsin(sin(θ/2)/2) and φ₁ = arccos(−θ/4π) throughout.

| Family | Sequence, time order (θ_t at phase 0 first) | Corrects | Order | Printed defect repaired |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SK1 (BHC Eqs. 9-10; MB Eq. 30) | (θ, 0), (2π, +φ₁), (2π, −φ₁) | amplitude, addressing | 1 | Eq. 10 prints U_1X(+θ): **first** order, exactly twice the bare-pulse error. Use U_1X(−θ); keep Eq. 9's own U_1X(a) = R₀(+aε) and take the ceiling on ∣a∣ **[corrected]** |
| SKn (BHC Eqs. 13-14; MB Eqs. 36-38) | M_{A_n}⁻¹ U_nX(‖A_n‖^{1/n}) M_{A_n} SK(n−1) | as SK1 | n | ‖·‖ is the **spectral** norm (trace norm is 2× and breaks cancellation by 2^{1/n}); M_{A_n} is the **imperfect** pulse; the index k of A_k, U_kX, M_{A_k} is never mixed with k + 1; U_nY conjugates with π, not the printed π/2; the SK2 rhombus needs φ_γ = arcsin(−sin 2φ_SK1/2) **[corrected]** |
| BB1 = B2 = W1 (Wimperis; MB Eq. 43) | (θ, 0), (π, φ₁), (2π, 3φ₁), (π, φ₁) | amplitude | 2 | none in Eq. 43; the **minus** in the arccos and the **3φ₁** middle phase are both load-bearing **[verified]** |
| NB1 = N2 (MB Eq. 42) | (θ, 0), (π, φ₁), (2π, −φ₁), (π, φ₁) | addressing | 2 | differs from B2 only in −φ against 3φ, the commonest transcription bug; one code path with a phase-map argument **[verified]** |
| PB1 = P2 = PD2 (MB Sec. 4.2.1) | (θ, 0), (2π, φ_P2), (2π, −φ_P2), (2π, −φ_P2), (2π, φ_P2), φ_P2 = arccos(−θ/8π) | both, reduced efficacy | 2 | **five** pulses, not four: the (1,2,1) three-pulse closure does not apply, and forcing it is 3700× worse than P2 and 16× worse than no correction **[corrected]** |
| P2j, N2j, B2j (MB Eqs. 44-50) | T_{2j}(1, φ_{P2j}) after (θ, 0), φ_{P2j} = arccos(−θ/(2πf_j)) | amplitude (P, B), addressing (N) | 2j | **f_j = (2^{2j−1} − 2)f_{j−1}**, f₁ = 4 (P) or 2 (N, B): 4, 24, 720, 90720 and 2, 12, 360, 45360. The printed −1 destroys first-order compensation and drops the slope from 10 to 2. The odd-k B2j bottom layer needs a fourth pulse, M(kπ,φ)M(kπ,3φ)M(kπ,3φ)M(kπ,φ); as printed it is not palindromic and is 1200× worse than no correction **[corrected]** |
| CORPSE (CLJ Eqs. 13-15; MB Eq. 55) | (2π + θ/2 − k, 0), (2π − 2k, π), (θ/2 − k, 0) | detuning | 1 | none; n = (1,1,0) gives 420°/300°/60° at θ = π and only n₁ − n₂ + n₃ = 0 returns +R(θ,0) **[verified]** |
| short-CORPSE | (θ/2 − k, 0), (2π − 2k, π), (θ/2 − k, 0) | detuning | 1 | as CORPSE, n = (0,1,0) **[verified]** |
| SCROFULOUS (CLJ Eqs. 18-23) | (θ₁, φ_S), (π, φ_S − arccos(−π/2θ₁)), (θ₁, φ_S), θ₁ = arcsinc(2cos(θ/2)/π), φ_S = arccos(−π cos θ₁/(2θ₁ sin(θ/2))) | amplitude | 1 | arcsinc branch (0, π] with arcsinc(0) = π, and the **minus** in φ₂ is load-bearing: the plus branch gives 180° at θ = 180°, against the known 180₆₀ 180₃₀₀ 180₆₀ **[corrected]** |
| reduced CinSK (Kabytayev Table I) | CORPSE block, then (2π, −φ₁), (2π, +φ₁) | **both at once** | 1 in each | none; slope 4 under ε_a = ε_d where SK1, BB1 and CORPSE fall to 2 **[verified]** |
| reduced CinBB (Kabytayev Table I) | CORPSE block, then (π, φ₁), (2π, 3φ₁), (π, φ₁) | **both at once** | 1 in each, 2 in amplitude | none; retains BB1's sixth-order amplitude coefficient 9.388566 while holding slope 4 under simultaneous error **[verified]** |

Leading coefficients at θ = π in 1 − F_K, all **[recomputed here]**: primitive (π²/4)ε_a² and ε_d² exactly; SK1 22.830256 ε_a⁴ = (π² sin 2φ₁)²; BB1 and CinBB 9.388566 ε_a⁶; SCROFULOUS 4.566051 ε_a⁴ but 4.000000 ε_d², four times the primitive detuning sensitivity, where BB1 pays essentially nothing there and is the safe default when both channels are live; CORPSE 6.5008 × 10⁻³ ε_d⁴, degraded 115-fold to 0.75 ε_d⁴ by either concatenation. CORPSE is asymptotically fourth order but has a wide intermediate regime where the ε_D³ term dominates, so a fit at ε_D ≈ 0.05 legitimately returns 4.5 to 6.0 and the exponent must be fitted below 10⁻⁴ **[verified]**. The module root-finds every Trotter-Suzuki phase on the leading ε coefficient rather than hard-coding f_j, asserts the printed anchors φ_P2 = arccos(−θ/8π) and φ_P4 = arccos(−θ/48π), and caches T_{2j−2} as one 2 × 2 matrix raised to integer powers (P4 = 37 pulses, P6 = 1189); palindromic ordering kills every even-order term, so only even orders exist in that ladder.

**The Low-Yoder-Chuang construction** supplies the general-θ closed forms the plan previously had from nowhere. A length-L = 2n sequence 𝒮 = ∏_j M_{φ_j}[θ₀] at θ₀ = 2π multiplies the target M₀[θ_T], with γ = θ_T/θ₀ and x = εθ₀/2. **PD_n** is palindromic (φ_k = φ_{L−k+1}, killing Im Φ for **even** j) and **AP_n** antipalindromic (φ_k = −φ_{L−k+1}, killing it for **odd** j) - a parity easy to invert - and only half the phases are tabulated. Under t_k = tan(φ_k/2) each family is at most quartic in t₁² and so closed-form solvable: AP1 gives cos φ₁ = −γ/2 = −θ_T/4π (**this is SK1**), PD2 gives cos φ₁ = −γ/4 = −θ_T/8π with t₂ = −t₁ (**this is PB1**), AP2 and PD4 have printed coefficient polynomials, and **ToP_n** gives exact seeds at γ = 2b from which arbitrary γ follows by numerical continuation wherever det J ≠ 0, so the standard names are aliases of these forms rather than reimplementations **[verified]**, **[recomputed here]**. The printed reality domain |γ| ≤ 2⌊n/2⌋ + 2 is a necessary outer bound only (PD4 is real only for |γ| ≤ 4), and PD_n exists only for even n **[corrected]**. The **ε-free certificate** is Eq. 11: a sequence is order n if and only if **Φ_L^j(φ) = f_L^j(γ) for 0 < j ≤ n**, where Φ_L^j = Σ_{h₁<…<h_j}exp(−iΣ_k(−1)^kφ_{h_k}) and f_L^j(γ) = Σ_k(−1)^k C(T, k)C(L − T, j − k) with T = (γ + L)/2 a generally non-integer generalized binomial. The alternating sign runs over the **position** k within the chosen subset, not over the pulse index, and the sum is over combinations, not permutations - the most error-prone point in the formalism; fill Φ by its dynamic-programming recursion, never by enumerating subsets. This certifies a candidate with no ε sweep and no propagator solve, and it **fails** at j = n + 1, pinning the order at exactly n **[verified]**, **[recomputed here]**. Broadband BB_n at θ₀ = π comes from the PD_n phases through the toggling map ψ_k = −Σ_{h<k}(−1)^hφ_h + Σ_{h>k}(−1)^hφ_h, which forces L ∈ 4ℤ and hence even n, while narrowband uses the original phases unchanged; the strongest cross-paper check available is that toggled PD2 at γ = 1 gives ψ = (φ₁, 3φ₁, 3φ₁, φ₁) with φ₁ = arccos(−1/4), which is Wimperis's BB1 at θ = π (distance slope 3.000 against 1.000 untoggled) **[verified]**, **[recomputed here]**.

**PDn, the Mount anchors, and the order ladder as a test.** The plan's PDn row stays: the palindromic family with 2n π pulses cancels area error to O(ε^n) and its tabulated PD6 phases are indexed by the target angle θ_t, not the target phase (a source typo) **[corrected]**. Run 5 supplies the general-θ_t construction Section 12 listed as missing, through PD_n above, so PD6 is no longer a background entry, although its phase vector at arbitrary γ still needs the numerical continuation and is not a printed formula. Measured anchors are unchanged: B2-compensated gates stay below 1% error for |ε| < 0.4 and PD6 for |ε| < 0.6; randomized benchmarking F(L) = A₀p^L + B₀ with error (1 − p)/2 gave 3.6(3) × 10⁻⁴ per Clifford on that comb-driven system **[verified]**, and 1.0(3) × 10⁻⁶ for Harty's microwave gates **[verified]**. Duration at constant amplitude is τ_seq = Σ_l θ_l/Ω, so τ_SK1 = τ_BB1 = (4π + θ)/Ω, τ_CORPSE = (4π + θ − 4k)/Ω and τ_CinSK = τ_CinBB = (8π + θ − 4k)/Ω (the CORPSE list sums to 4π + θ − 4k and each concatenation appends 4π of correctors, so at θ = π, k = π/6 the pulse list 420° + 300° + 60° + 360° + 360° = 1500° = 8π + π/3; the second revision printed 8π + 2θ − 4k, 12% long at θ = π, and `check_composite.py` now asserts every family's Σ_l θ_l against these forms; 2026-09-04 experimentalist critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**, **[recomputed here]**, and the scheduler quotes both infidelity and duration because total rotation sets the scattering and heating exposure of Sections 6.5 and 6.2; no source gives a rule for choosing a family from a measured (ε_A, ε_D, ε_N) triple, so that rule is the simulator's own (Section 12). The shipped regression is the measured order ladder in 1 − F_K at θ = π (`check_composite.py`, Section 9.15): primitive 2 in both quadratures, SK1 4 amplitude and 2 detuning, BB1 6 and 2, CORPSE 2 and 4, SCROFULOUS 4 and 2, reduced CinSK and CinBB 4 under simultaneous ε_a = ε_d **[verified]**, **[recomputed here]**. These residuals are the ideal-limit **floor** of the 2 × 2 algebra: none of these papers has a Hamiltonian, an ħ or a time, so off-resonant sideband coupling, the Debye-Waller factor, leakage, spontaneous emission, the correctors' own ac Stark shift and heating over a five- to eightfold longer sequence are all outside them, and are separated from the composite-pulse residual by running the same pulse list through the Section 4.3.1 Hamiltonian and differencing.
4.3.5.title: Single-qubit gates and composite pulses

4.3.6.text: For an ion displaced from the rf null by a stray field, the drive seen by the ion is phase modulated at Ω_T with index φ_Ω = (q_x/2)[k_x Δ_x − k_y Δ_y] (Wineland 1998 Eqs. 71-72; the symbol is φ_Ω, which pdftotext renders as φ_V **[corrected]**), reducing every carrier matrix element by J₀(φ_Ω) and adding micromotion sidebands **[verified]**, consistent with Berkeland's J_n²(β) spectrum in Section 4.1. The builder applies this as an optional multiplicative modulation of the drive coefficient; the intrinsic-micromotion factor C₀ (Section 4.1.1) is already inside the η the builder receives from `Crystal.lamb_dicke` and is never reapplied here (2026-09-04 architect critique). The modulation e^{iβ cos(ω_rf t + δ)} also needs the pulse start time relative to the trap rf: a drive flagged `rf_locked` carries an rf phase reference and keeps the coherent sideband, an unlocked one averages δ per shot so that only J₀ and the J_n² weights survive (`Drive.rf_phase`, Appendix E), and the default without a declared reference is the unlocked average, because a result that depended on the integrator's time origin would be an artifact (Section 12 had listed the rule as absent; 2026-09-04 experimentalist critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**.
4.3.6.title: Micromotion in the drive

4.3.7.text:
Every 355 nm Raman system on 171Yb+ drives the qubit with a mode-locked pulse train, not two continuous-wave tones, so the chain of Sections 4.3.2 and 4.5.4 becomes a sum over comb-tooth pairs. Run 5S (Appendix D) read six clusters for this - Hayes 2010, Islam 2014, Inlek 2014, Mizrahi 2013 with its Appl. Phys. B companion of 2014, Campbell 2010, Lee 2016 - for 63 model entries, a third of them corrected on transcription or on the sources' own printed errors. The set is one species at one wavelength; the module takes (ν_rep, τ, Δ, species, geometry) as inputs, and Section 9.15 holds its numbers.

**The idealized train and its comb.** A train of N identical pulses at a fixed point is E(t) = Σ_{n=1}^{N} f(t − nT) e^{iω_c t} (Hayes Eq. 1) **[verified]**, whose unnormalized forward transform f̃(ω − ω_c) Σ_n e^{−i(ω−ω_c)nT} has teeth at ω_c + 2πmν_R spaced by ν_R = 1/T. The carrier exponential sits **outside** the sum: that is the zero-carrier-envelope-offset idealization, and writing e^{iω_c(t−nT)} instead reintroduces a per-pulse phase e^{−inω_cT}, a nonzero offset frequency **[verified]**. A Λ-configuration Raman process needs no carrier-envelope phase at all - the qubit sees only tooth-frequency *differences*, and f_ceo cancels between two copies of one comb **[verified]** - so the simulator carries only the inter-comb (AOM) phase, which is the spin-dependent-force phase. Tooth width follows the Dirichlet kernel |sin(Nϑ/2)/sin(ϑ/2)|: exact FWHM 1.206716 ν_R/N in amplitude and 0.885899 ν_R/N in power at N = 256 **[recomputed here]**; the widely quoted 0.886 is the intensity value, so code holding amplitudes uses 1.2067. The sources state only the scaling and never a linewidth (Section 12).

**Tooth amplitudes and the intensity sum rule.** Tooth k from the comb centre has g_k = g₀ √(πν_rep τ) sech(2πk ν_rep τ) with g₀² = Σ_k g_k² = γ²Ī/(2I_sat) (Lee Eq. 1, identical to Mizrahi Eq. 20 under ω_rep = 2πν_rep) **[verified]**, γ **angular** and Ī the **peak on-axis time-averaged** intensity 2P̄/(πw₀²) with w₀ the 1/e² intensity radius - unstated but forced by reproducing that source's own second-order shift, since P̄/(πw₀²) halves g₀² **[corrected]**. τ is the sech **field**-envelope parameter, never a width, and its envelope is sech(πt/(2τ)): the tooth formula sech(2πk ν_rep τ) is the Fourier transform of a field sech(πt/(2τ)) (FT[sech(at)] ∝ sech(πω/2a), and a = π/2τ gives sech(ωτ) = sech(2πkν_repτ) at ω = 2πkν_rep), so the field FWHM is (4/π) arccosh(2) τ = 1.6768 τ and the intensity (sech²) FWHM is (4/π) arccosh(√2) τ = 1.1222 τ; the second revision printed 0.8384 τ and 0.5611 τ, the widths of sech(πt/τ), whose teeth would read sech(πkν_repτ), so a τ inferred from a measured pulse width was off by 2 and with it every sech(ω_qτ/2) suppression and the 27% pair-versus-single test (`check_critique_v3.py`, which also checks the transform pair numerically; 2026-09-04 theorist critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**, **[recomputed here]**. The sum rule is asymptotic in ν_rep τ, not algebraic (1.000000000000 at ν_rep τ = 1.68 × 10⁻³, 3.14 at 1) **[recomputed here]**, so the module builds the sech profile to |k| ~ several hundred and renormalizes to it rather than trusting the √(πν_rep τ) prefactor. Hayes' equivalent E₀ is **fluence**-normalized, ∫|f|²dt = E₀²τ against a peak f(0) = √(π/2)E₀ = 1.25331414 E₀, so a measured peak passed as E₀ overstates Ω₀ and Ī by π/2 = 1.5708 **[corrected]**.

**The tooth-pair sum and the two-photon Rabi frequency.** All pairs of separation l add coherently at the beat note l(2πν_rep): Ω^{(l)} = Σ_k g_k g_{k+l}/(2Δ) ≈ Ω₀ sech(πl ν_rep τ), Ω₀ = g₀²/(2Δ) **[verified]**. The *pair* argument is half the *single-tooth* one - at l = 105, ν_rep = 120 MHz, τ = 14 ps, sech(πlν_repτ) = 0.863911 against sech(2πlν_repτ) = 0.595332, a 27% error and the cheapest flag for a factor-2 bug **[recomputed here; corrected]** - and is itself 5% high against the exact convolution, so the module records the ratio as a unit test rather than asserting equality **[corrected]**. Three closed forms circulate and must not be harmonized: sech(ω_qτ/2) = 1 − x²/8 (Mizrahi Eq. 22, from the exact time-domain Rosen-Zener solution), (ω_qτ)/sinh(ω_qτ) = 1 − x²/6 (the exact convolution of two sech spectra), and (ω_qτ/2)/sinh(ω_qτ/2) = 1 − x²/24 (Hayes, whose field-sech τ is twice the Lee-family τ for one pulse) **[contested]**; the first two give 0.925994 and 0.902128 at 80 MHz and 10 ps, a 2.65% gap **[recomputed here]**, and the plan implements sech(ω_qτ/2) and reports the gap. **Chain I against Chain II.** One source prints the intensity-to-Rabi calibration two ways, Ω = g²/(2Δ) with g = γ√(I/(2I_sat)) and Ω = g²/Δ; both are internally self-consistent, differ by exactly 2 in every Rabi rate, and no source resolves it **[contested]**. The plan's Section 13 row Ω_R = Σ_e Ω₂*Ω₁/(2Δ_e) selects **Chain I**, a choice derived from the plan's own convention and endorsed by no paper (**[background]**; Section 12 keeps it contested), so the printed π-pulse energy is a factor 2 too small: E_π = π²I_sat w²Δ/γ² is 13.561 nJ on Chain II, matching the printed ~12 nJ, against 27.122 nJ on Chain I at I_sat = 1500 W/m², w = 10 µm, γ = 2π × 19.6 MHz, Δ = 2π × 22.11 THz **[recomputed here]**, and Hayes' Ω₀ = sγ²/(2Δ) is halved at ingest. The fine-structure detunings are **signed**, Δ_{1/2} = +33 THz and Δ_{3/2} = −67 THz at 355 nm, so 1/Δ = 1/Δ_{1/2} − 1/Δ_{3/2} **adds** to Δ/2π = 22.1100 THz where magnitudes give 65.029 THz, a factor 2.941 in Ω **[recomputed here]**.

**Resonance conditions.** For a single comb, ω_q = n ω_rep with n integer, equivalently q ≡ ω₀/(2πν_R) ∈ ℤ **[verified]**, and the integer/half-integer dichotomy under a pulse picker is the test: q = 156.5090, 313.0181 and 469.5213 at Hayes' 80.78 MHz and its 1-in-2 and 1-in-3 picked rates, with qubit evolution only at the integer **[recomputed here]**. Integer q is necessary, not sufficient; the rate is suppressed unless the pulse bandwidth exceeds ω_q. Two comb copies offset by an acousto-optic difference frequency give ω_q = n ω_rep ± ω_A (Mizrahi Eq. 29) and, with a sideband, |2πjν_R + Δω| = ω₀ ± ω_t, j a signed integer and Δω = 2π(ν₁ − ν₂) signed **[verified]**; the sign of Δω selects red from blue and is the primary control input, so the module root-finds this rather than hard-coding a tooth index. In ordinary-frequency (AOM/PLL) form the same statement is |jν_rep + Δν_M| = ν_ab ± ν_t, Islam's branch being ν_sb = nν_rep − |Δν_M| = ν_LO + ν_M2, time independent because ν_LO and ν_M2 are synthesizer frequencies, subject to nν_rep > ν_LO (stated) and ν_M1 > ν_M2 (implicit, and what lets the outer absolute value be dropped) **[corrected]**. The lock arithmetic is the test: 157 × 80.6 MHz = 12.65420 GHz, ν_ab/ν_rep = 156.8588 so n = 157, ν_M1 = 216.200 MHz (printed ~217) and ν_M2 = 204.819 MHz (printed ~205) **[recomputed here]**. Inlek's two-tooth Mølmer-Sørensen conditions close with n = 160 on the **red** leg and m = 154 on the **blue**, swapped in extraction with a 483.42 MHz miss **[corrected]**, and the feed-forward chain ν_PLL = n[ν_rep + δ_r(t)] − ν_MO gives 285.20, 198.22 and 43.49 MHz for the red, blue and copropagating-carrier loops at ν_MO = 12.606 GHz, with loop-closing AWG frequencies 111.83 and 38.19 MHz **[recomputed here]**.

**How the drive enters the builder, and when the mapping is legal.** A comb drive is a **set of tones** in the sense of Section 5.2: H = Σ_j (Ω_j/2)[e^{i((jω_rep + ω_A − ω_q)t + φ₀)} σ₊^{(i)} ⊗ Π_m D_m(iη_{im}) + h.c.] with Ω_j = Ω₀ sech(jω_rep τ/2) - one drive term per beat note, all sharing the same time-independent operator σ₊ ⊗ Π_m D_m(iη), each with its own scalar coefficient **[verified]**. The resonant tooth pair is the tone at j = n; the off-resonant pairs at multiples of the repetition rate are the remaining tones with sech² weights. Near-resonant tones stay explicit as `QobjEvo` coefficients while only far-detuned ones fold into the static fourth-order shift below, never both **[verified]**; the cut is explicit: a tone pair stays explicit when |μ_j − ω_res| ≲ 10/t_g (about 100 kHz for a 100 µs gate) and everything beyond folds into the l-sum shift, with a convergence test that moves the cut by 2× and reports the change in the gate phase, because the off-resonant beat notes sit at multiples of ω_rep = 2π × 120 MHz and retaining even the nearest one raises the highest frequency in the frame from about 3 MHz to 120 MHz, a 40× step-count multiplier that turns the Section 11.1 cost of a 100 µs gate at dimension 2048 into hours (2026-09-04 numerics critique) **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**. Mount 2015's three-term model (Section 4.3.5), the resonant pair plus off-resonant pairs at δ′ and 2δ′ with weights 1 : 2 : 1, is that tone set truncated to three beat notes with the sech² envelope flattened, which its 0.53% variation per tooth index licenses **[recomputed here]**; Mount 2015 is outside the Run 5S source set, so the identification is derived (**[background]**) and the Mount propagator stays the composite-pulse error model of Section 4.3.5. The **validity hierarchy** of the pulse-train-to-continuous-wave mapping is a runtime guard logged before every solve **[verified]**: N ≫ 1 (teeth resolved); ω_q τ ≪ 1 (the pulse bandwidth must straddle the qubit splitting or no pair drives the transition); ω_q ≪ 1/τ ≪ |Δ| ≲ ω_FS (adiabatic elimination legitimate, and Δ not far above the fine structure or the D1/D2 amplitudes cancel); θ ≪ 1 per pulse; ω_rep τ ≪ 1 (the sum rule); and ω_t t_N ≫ 1 with η√(n̄+1) ≪ 1 for the resolved-sideband picture against ω_t t_N ≪ 1 for the ultrafast kick. The selector between the two pictures is **train duration against the trap period plus the Lamb-Dicke condition**, not the Bessel-order ratio J₂ ≪ J₁, which holds throughout the ultrafast source **[corrected]**; no source bounds the crossover, so the guard routes to the exact pulse-by-pulse propagator instead of interpolating (Section 12). The single-pulse ceiling is the exact Rosen-Zener result P_{0→1} = sin²(πu) sech²(πν_HF T_pulse) (Campbell Eq. 6; Mizrahi Eq. 18), reproducing the measured 72% and 91% as 0.720860 at 14.8 ps and 0.914142 at 7.6 ps, where reading ν_HF as angular gives 0.002474 - the discriminator that pins that source's H/h ordinary-frequency convention **[recomputed here]**. There is **one** sech(ω_qτ/2) factor, not three: the Rosen-Zener contrast, the finite-duration reduction of the kick area and the tooth-pair suppression are one amplitude factor seen in the time and frequency domains, all 0.925994 at τ = 10 ps, and applying it twice or three times multiplies the suppression spuriously **[corrected]**. The pulse-count map is N = f_rep t and Ω₀ = f_rep θ, the printed 2π-prefactored forms being wrong by (2π)² = 39.478 under that paper's own angular convention **[recomputed here; corrected]**.

**Spin-motion coupling in the two regimes.** In the slow regime the exact one-period propagator is V = e^{−iH₀T} exp[−i(θ_p/2)(σ₊e^{iΔk x̂} + h.c.)] with H₀ = ω_t a†a + ½(ω₀ + Δω)σ_z, the beat-note offset absorbed into the qubit term and the kick left Δω-free (Hayes Eqs. 4-6) **[verified]**; at first order in θ_p and inside the Lamb-Dicke regime the pulse sum becomes a grating, Σ_n Q_n ≈ iη [sin(Nϑ_r/2)/sin(ϑ_r/2)] e^{iϑ_r(N−1)/2} σ₊a + h.c. with ϑ_r = (ω₀ + Δω − ω_t)T = 2πj - an N-slit selection rule of peak value N **[verified]**. The θ_p/2 belongs to the V^N expansion, not the Dirichlet factor, so the sideband coupling over the train is Ω_sb = θ_p η N/2, not ηN **[corrected]**. In the fast regime a simultaneous counterpropagating pulse pair is an impulsive Kapitza-Dirac kick, H = −Θ_B δ(t − t₀) sin[Δk x̂ + φ(t₀)] σ_x, whose propagator is exact in η by Jacobi-Anger, U_{t₀} = exp{iΘ_B sin(Δk x̂ + φ)σ_x} = Σ_n e^{inφ} J_n(Θ_B) D(inη) σ_x^n, needing no Lamb-Dicke assumption because D(ia)D(ib) = D(i(a+b)) exactly **[verified]**. The printed pairing of an Ω/2 Hamiltonian prefactor with Bessel argument θ = ∫Ω dt cannot hold: the identity closes to 10⁻¹⁴ only when the Bessel argument equals the exponent coefficient **[recomputed here; corrected]**, so the plan carries **one** symbol Θ_B *defined* as the Bessel argument, with a perfect kick at total train area Σ_k Θ_{B,k} = π - read literally the printed Hamiltonian moves that to 2π and saturates near 50% at π. The ideal kick U_SDK = e^{iφ′}D(iη)σ_∓ − e^{−iφ′}D(−iη)σ_± is unitary for *either* relative sign (σ_±² = 0 kills the cross terms); the minus makes it anti-Hermitian with U² = −𝟙, the algebraic reason the area must be π **[recomputed here; corrected]**. No source gives η numerically except Hayes' 0.1, and Hayes writes e^{ikx̂} with a bare k, yet 0.1 closes only with Δk = √2 k (0.1063 against 0.0751 for bare k at 1.64 MHz), so that paper's "k" *is* the two-photon Δk **[recomputed here; corrected]**; with Δk = 2k, η = 0.2233 at 743 kHz, and η√(n̄+1) = 1.74 at the assumed n̄ = 40 makes the Lamb-Dicke branch illegal and the full cos(Δk x̂) drive mandatory **[recomputed here]**. The blue-sideband generator M̂ = ie^{iφ₀}a†σ₊ − ie^{−iφ₀}aσ₋ is Hermitian with M̂² = n̂ + 1 on one spin block and n̂ on the other, so its printed cos/sin closed form is exact only on the n = 0 → 1 manifold and the rate is Θη√(n+1) per {|n,↓⟩, |n+1,↑⟩} block, never Θη **[recomputed here; corrected]**.

**Mølmer-Sørensen gates and the phase structure.** With two tones symmetrically detuned by δ from the red and blue sidebands, single-loop closure is δ = 2ηΩ with t_g = 2π/δ, that is ηΩ/δ = ½ **[verified]**, Ω being the per-tone resonant *carrier* Rabi frequency; this is the plan's own closure ηΩ/ε = 1/(2√K) of Section 4.4.1 at K = 1, which the spin-operator normalization does not change (Section 13; the second revision's 'halved on ingest' rule was the factor-2 error the derivation audit of 2026-09-04 removed). In the phase-insensitive geometry the two legs carry separate wavevector differences, Δk_r = k_A − k_{B,r} and Δk_b = k_{B,b} − k_A, with φ_G = φ_{S,i} + φ_{S,j}, φ_{S,i} = −½(Δk_r·X_i − Δφ_r + Δk_b·X_i − Δφ_b) and φ_{M,i} = +½(Δk_r·X_i − Δφ_r − Δk_b·X_i + Δφ_b) (Inlek Eqs. 4-5, whose two printed lines of Eq. 4 disagree by a factor 2; both self-consistent readings give identical φ_S and φ_M, so the second line and Eq. 5 are implemented) **[contested]**. Because Δk_r + Δk_b = k_{B,b} − k_{B,r} contains no k_A, the k_A rf phase and any k_A path drift cancel identically and φ_G ≈ φ_{B,b} − φ_{B,r}, whereas the sensitive geometry gives φ_G ≈ φ_{B,r} + φ_{B,b} − 2φ_A and keeps the drifting position term **[verified]** - the geometric criterion of Section 4.3.4 and the spin/motion split of Section 4.4.2, with the plan's Haljan sign φ_s = +(φ_b + φ_r)/2 applied after conversion. The path dependence is *transferred* to φ_{M,i}, not destroyed, so each ion carries its own φ_{M,i} from its own equilibrium position and the displacement is driven with e^{iφ_{M,i}}; the regression test is that a global path drift leaves fidelity unchanged, which bites only if φ_M is per-ion and is not folded into the spin phase. Wave-front alignment enters through λ′ = 2π/Δk ≈ λ/√2 = 251.0 nm at a 90° crossing with Δφ_M = 2πl sin θ/λ′, and the source's own triple does not close - 30 µm at θ = 0.02° gives 15.0° end-to-end against a stated "< 10°", and θ < 0.0133° is what is needed **[recomputed here; corrected]** - so the module implements the formula with an explicit end-to-end convention rather than an angle.
