**ac Stark shifts, second and fourth order.** At second order E^{(2)}_{00} = (g₀²/12)(1/Δ − 2/(ω_F − Δ)) and E^{(2)}_{10} is the same with Δ → Δ + ω_HF, so the differential enters the comb only through g₀² by the sum rule and is comb-shape independent **[verified]**. The 1/12 is a second-order 1/4 times a 1/3 scalar polarization average, and the −2 is the (2J′+1) line-strength ratio *times* a sign from writing the P_{3/2} detuning as the positive ω_F − Δ; in signed form both weights are positive, (g₀²/12)(1/Δ_{1/2} + 2/Δ_{3/2}), and pairing −2 with one's own signed Δ_{3/2} double-counts it, inflating E^{(2)}_{00} by a factor 133 at the near-total D1/D2 cancellation of 355 nm (1/33 + 2/(−67) = 0.00045 THz⁻¹ against 1/33 + 2/67 = 0.0602 THz⁻¹, both positive; the second revision printed this as a sign flip from about +0.1 to −2 MHz, which neither reading gives; `check_critique_v3.py`) **[corrected]**, **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**, **[recomputed here]**. The printed −7.3 kHz is an **ordinary** frequency δω^{(2)}/2π, recomputed as −7.63 kHz **[recomputed here; corrected]**. At fourth order (second order in intensity) E^{(4)}_n = −Σ_{a≠n} Ω_{n,a}²/(4δ_{n,a}) with δ_{n,a} = ω_a − j(2πν_rep) the residual detuning of the *nearest* beat note, j = argmin_j|ω_a − 2πjν_rep|, and δ_{a,n} = −δ_{n,a}; the printed plus sign paired with the printed δ is self-contradictory, disagreeing with that paper's own three-level result, so exactly one of (minus, δ = splitting − beat note) or (plus, δ = beat note − splitting) is implemented **[corrected]**. The comb generalization multiplies each term by C_{n,a} = Σ_k sech²((j+k)πν_repτ)/(1 − k(2πν_rep)/δ_{n,a}), with Ω_{n,a} the polarization-weighted Ω₀ carrying **no** sech factor - the sech² weights live inside the k sum, so applying sech twice is a silent factor-0.75 error **[corrected]** - and C is neither normalized to one nor small, its k = 0 term alone being 0.746343 at j = 105. Its convergence is the trap: at ν_rep = 120 MHz, τ = 14 ps and ω_HF/2π = 12.642821 GHz (j = 105, δ_{00,10}/2π = +42.8210 MHz) the partial sums run 0.746343, 0.453162, 0.450920, 0.669087, 0.940671, 0.943780, 0.943789 for |k| ≤ 0, 5, 10, 100, 500, 1000, 5000 **[recomputed here]**, because the sech² weight is centred at k = −j with half-width 1/(πν_repτ) ≈ 189: the |k| ~ 5 to 10 plateau is a factor 2.093 **low** and a successive-partial-sum test converges falsely there, so the module sums to |k| ≳ 1000 and validates by doubling. The guard is δ_{n,a} ≠ 0, **never** j ≠ 0: j = 0 is the operative case for the Zeeman partners (ω_Zee/2π ≈ 7 MHz < ν_rep/2), where C_{10,11} = C_{10,1−1} = 0.988841 exactly, and that equality makes the elliptical-polarization cancellation E^{(4)}_{10} = 0 survive the comb generalization; a j ≠ 0 guard deletes exactly those terms **[recomputed here; corrected]**. The module implements the algebraically identical single sum over the separation l = j + k, E^{(4)}_n = Σ_{a≠n} (Ω_{n,a}²/4) Σ_l sech²(πlν_repτ)/(ω_a − l(2πν_rep)), which removes j and δ_{n,a} entirely so the guard error cannot be made (**[background]**, derived by reindexing). For a **single comb** with the resonant beat note excluded, the conditionally convergent bilateral sum δ₄ = −Σ_{j≠n} Ω_j²/(2(jω_rep − ω_q)) must be symmetrized in ±j pairs, and that symmetrization produces the closed form δ₄ ≈ 0.853 Ω₀²ω_qτ/ω_rep with 0.853 = ∫₀^∞ sech²v tanh v/v dv = 7ζ(3)/π² = 0.852556797635 **[recomputed here]**; the signed sum already contains the counter-rotating Bloch-Siegert term as its j = −n member and must not double-count it **[verified]**, and the closed form is leading order only (effective coefficient 0.756 at τ = 10 ps) **[recomputed here]**. For **two offset combs** the fractional offset σ = ω̃_A/ω_rep, ω̃_A = ω_A mod ω_rep, can null the shift; the printed counter-rotating sum needs a plus, not the printed minus, and the closed form's smooth term is exactly twice the single-comb coefficient, 3.410227 = 4 × 7ζ(3)/π². Its nulls are roots of a three-pole truncation, not of the exact sum - 0.353353 at τ = 5 ps, 0.399342 at 10 ps, 1/√12 = 0.288675 as τ → 0, against the exact 0.315397, 0.366248 and 1/4 - so the Stark-nulling AOM offset is root-found on the exact sum, subject to the excluded offsets ω_A ≠ kω_rep and ≠ (k+½)ω_rep that keep a spin-dependent force available **[recomputed here; corrected]**. The series is **marginal at full power**: the source never states |Ω_{n,a}| ≪ |δ_{n,a}|, and at its own operating point Ω₀/2π = 45.7 MHz *exceeds* δ_{00,10}/2π = 42.8 MHz, so the expansion parameter is order unity and nothing bounds the error; the module offers a non-perturbative check by direct diagonalization of the tooth-pair-coupled ground manifold and does not claim the closed form at full power (Section 12) **[contested]**.

**Comb noise channels and where they enter.** Three channels are comb-specific, each mapping onto one entry point of Section 6.1.

- **Harmonic-amplified repetition-rate drift.** The beat note is a tooth-index *difference*, so ν_sb = nν_rep − |Δν_M| has ∂ν_sb/∂ν_rep = n and δν_sb = n δν_rep: at n = 157 a free-running 1 Hz/min becomes 157 Hz/min = 2.617 Hz/s at the qubit **[verified]**, and a 10⁻⁷ fractional drift at 80 MHz becomes 1.26 kHz **[recomputed here]**. It is driven from a ν_rep(t) process, not an ad-hoc qubit-frequency noise term, so the gain emerges rather than being asserted: the slow part is option (c), a quasi-static per-shot sample, the 1 Hz to 10 kHz band option (d), a sampled trajectory. Drift alone is insufficient - it accumulates 0.008 Hz over the measured 3 ms unlocked Ramsey time - so a fast jitter is fitted to that 3 ms, ~53 Hz rms on the beat note (derived, not sourced) **[corrected]**.
- **Feed-forward per-tooth residuals.** The lock cancels drift algebraically to all orders, but only for the selected tooth's lower sideband: on tooth m the residual is (m − n) δν_rep for the lower sideband, (m + n) δν_rep for the upper (worse than unlocked) and m δν_rep for a bare tooth **[corrected]**. A tooth-pair sum for a Stark shift or a spin-dependent force applies these coefficients pair by pair, not as a global lock - no source does this - and for the off-resonant Stark drive the sensitivity exceeds the bare tooth-index lever, 360× fractional on δω^{(4)}, of which jν_rep/δ_{00,10} = 294× is the detuning **[recomputed here]**.
- **Intensity noise.** Ω(t) = Ω₀(1 + ξ(t)) with one-sided white S_ξ = α_lin is option (d), with error ε ≈ (π²/2) α Ω₀² T and **Ω₀ in Hz, never rad/s**: at α = −115 dB/Hz, Ω₀ = 600 kHz, T = 1 ms the Hz reading gives 5.6179 × 10⁻³, consistent with the source's own ε < 1%, while rad/s gives 0.2218, wrong by (2π)² = 39.478 **[recomputed here; corrected]**. The relation is dimensionally consistent either way, so only this test settles it; structurally π²/2 = (2π)²/8 = 4.9348022005, the conversion already absorbed. The PLL-achieved −120 dB/Hz is the default, and the prefactor is order-unity-loose, strict power-to-field propagation giving π²/8 **[contested]**.

The static fourth-order shift and any retained off-resonant tones are option (a); the shot-constant beat-note phase φ₀ is option (c), sampled once per shot and never averaged inside a trajectory. Option (b), a Lindblad rate, gets nothing new from this layer, which is the first gap.

**What the comb sources do not supply.** **No spontaneous-emission rate exists in the comb layer at all**: every Hamiltonian in all six sources is post-adiabatic-elimination and carries no Lindblad term (γ is not even defined in one of them except inside Ω₀ = sγ²/(2Δ)), so per-gate Raman and Rayleigh probabilities, branching ratios and P-manifold decay during the pulse are absent. The plan does not take them from these sources: the scattering channels of Section 4.5.5 are computed from the *same* tooth sums, the residual excited population being Σ_k |g_k|²/(4Δ²) over teeth exactly as Section 4.5.4's adiabatic-elimination residual, so drive and dissipator cannot drift apart; until that is validated the simulator bounds rather than computes the fidelity ceiling of a 355 nm comb drive. **No multi-ion comb Mølmer-Sørensen construction exists**: every comb equation in the set is single-ion and single-mode, so modes, participation factors, per-mode η_{im} and phase-space closure come from Sections 4.1.3 and 4.4.3, and the reported two-ion fidelities are consistency checks, not targets. **No wave-front phase-gradient tolerance closes**: only ΔL ≪ cτ ≈ 3.0 mm (printed as c/τ, dimensionally an acceleration **[corrected]**) and the λ′ formula above, whose own numbers do not close. Section 12 carries these, plus the missing noise spectra, the missing numerical η, the missing fourth-order shift for a *resonant* carrier drive, and the (τ, bandwidth) inconsistency that moves C_{00,10} from 0.9438 to 0.7174 **[recomputed here]**.

**Printed source errors corrected here**, for the errata record: the pulse-count-to-Rabi map N = 2πω_rep t and Ω₀ = 2πω_rep θ, wrong by (2π)² = 39.478 under its own angular convention; the multi-level fourth-order Stark sign, needing an overall minus with the antisymmetry δ_{a,n} = −δ_{n,a}, its guard being δ_{n,a} ≠ 0 and never j ≠ 0; the two-comb sum's counter-rotating term, which must carry a plus, and its null offsets, roots of a truncation (0.353, 0.399, 1/√12) rather than of the exact sum (0.315, 0.366, 1/4); the Kapitza-Dirac Hamiltonian and its Bessel expansion, printed inconsistently by a factor 2 in three places; Inlek's red and blue tooth orders, swapped in extraction with a 483.42 MHz miss, and its printed AWG frequencies, each high by exactly 2ν_α = 5.00 MHz; Hayes' E₀, fluence- and not peak-normalized, a factor π/2 = 1.5708; the blue-sideband closed form, which assumes its generator squares to the identity and so omits the √(n+1); and two ordinary-frequency values quoted inside otherwise-angular papers, δω^{(2)}/2π = −7.3 kHz and δω^{(4)}/2π = 23 and 12 MHz, the latter needing an explicit 2π before entering any angular equation, which turns a comfortable 435 ns addressing-raster margin into a marginal 69 ns at ten ions. Smaller ones are listed per source in Section 15, including the path-matching condition printed as c/τ and the three printed clock splittings that are second-order-Zeeman-shifted values rather than the zero-field 12.642812118466 GHz (Section 13).
4.3.7.title: Frequency-comb (mode-locked) Raman drives

4.4.text: All entangling gates in the simulator are geometric-phase gates on shared motional modes. The builder of Section 4.3 produces them from ordinary drive terms (two tones, or two beams with a difference frequency near a mode); nothing below is a separate gate implementation. The equations here are what the calibration layer fits and what the validation suite checks, and they fix the conventions.
4.4.title: Two-qubit entangling gates

4.4.1.text:
**Microscopic Hamiltonian.** Bichromatic light at ω₀ ± δ on N ions coupled to one mode (Sørensen and Mølmer 1999, 2000; Mølmer and Sørensen 1999) **[verified]**:

H₀ = ħν(a†a + ½) + (ħω_eg/2)Σ_i σ_z^i,  H_int = Σ_i Σ_{t=1,2} (ħΩ/2)(σ₊^i e^{i(η_i(a+a†) − ω_t t)} + h.c.),  ω₁ = ω_eg − δ, ω₂ = ω_eg + δ (the ion index on η, the tone index on ω; the papers' single index j covers both),

exact in η (the simulator integrates exactly this, as the original papers did in their numerics **[verified]**). In the Lamb-Dicke regime, dropping the carrier and the far-off-resonant (ν + δ) terms, the interaction is a spin-dependent force f(t)J_y x + g(t)J_y p whose propagator is exact for any f, g because [x, p] is a c-number (Sørensen-Mølmer 2000 Eqs. 6-9) **[verified]**:

U(t) = e^{−iA(t)J_y²} e^{−iF(t)J_y x} e^{−iG(t)J_y p},  F = ∫f, G = ∫g, A = −∫F g.

The same structure in the notation the simulator adopts (Kirchmair et al. 2009 Eqs. 3-4; Haljan et al. 2005 Eq. 1) **[verified]**: with the tones detuned ε = ν − δ from the sideband,

H(t) = −(ħηΩ/2)(a† e^{iεt} + a e^{−iεt}) S_y,  U(t) = D̂(α(t) S_y) exp[i(λt − χ sin(εt)) S_y²],  α(t) = (ηΩ/2ε)(e^{iεt} − 1),  λ = η²Ω²/(4ε),  χ = η²Ω²/(4ε²),

with Ω the per-tone Rabi frequency of the plan's convention (H_tone = (ħΩ/2)σ₊e^{i(...)} + h.c.; to first order in η the blue tone alone feeds a†e^{iεt} and the red tone alone a e^{−iεt}, each with amplitude ηΩ/2), so each eigenstate m of S_y is displaced along a circle of radius |m|ηΩ/(2ε) that closes at εt = 2πm (Haljan's α₀ = Ω_sb/(2ε) with Ω_sb = ηΩ the sideband Rabi frequency) **[verified]**. The first two revisions of this plan displayed −ħηΩ(...)S_y with α(t) = (ηΩ/ε)(e^{iεt} − 1), a form that is correct only for a Rabi frequency defined without the ½ (Ω′ = Ω/2, the reading under which Roos's Ω_c = |ε|/(4η) becomes |ε|/(2η) in the plan's Ω; whether Kirchmair's and Roos's own Ω is that one was not re-verified here, and the ingest converter carries the factor), a doubled force that the derivation audit of 2026-09-04 caught and direct integration confirmed (`check_ms_closure.py`) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. The two-ion decomposition D̂(αS_y) = P₀ + P₂D̂(2α) + P₋₂D̂(−2α) with P₀ = 1 − S_y²/4, P_{±2} = (S_y² ± 2S_y)/8 **[verified]** is how the simulator's tests evaluate thermal averages analytically; note that the observable rotation is O_V = V†OV, not VOV† as printed in both Kirchmair 2009 and Roos 2008 **[corrected]**.

**Effective coupling and thermal insensitivity.** Second-order perturbation theory gives Ω̃ = −(Ωη)²/(ν − δ) for the bichromatic |ggn⟩ ↔ |een⟩ coupling (twice the monochromatic value −(Ωη)²/(2(ν−δ)) of the 1999 PRL's Eq. 3; the papers reuse the symbol **[verified]**), independent of n because the (n+1) path through |n+1⟩ and the n path through |n−1⟩ enter with opposite-sign denominators and interfere destructively **[verified]**. The multiparticle form is H = 4(χ/ħ)J_x² with χ = η²Ω²ν/(2(ν² − δ²)) in a convention where J carries ħ, producing the GHZ state at t = π/(8χ) **[verified]**; the normalization must travel with χ. Loop closure and maximal entanglement: G(τ) = F(τ) = 0 with (ν − δ)τ = 2πK and A(τ) = −π/2, giving ηΩ/(ν − δ) = 1/(2√K) and τ = √K π/(ηΩ) in Sørensen-Mølmer's spin normalization J_y = ½Σσ_y **[verified]**; and the ratio ηΩ/ε is a ratio of physical quantities that cannot depend on whether the spin operator is written J_y or S_y = 2J_y: in the plan's per-tone convention the maximally entangling closure is ηΩ/ε = 1/(2√K) with τ = 2πK/ε = π√K/(ηΩ) whichever generator is written, and only the two-body phase target rescales as the square of the spin normalization, A(τ) = −π/2 on J_y², −π/8 on S_y² and χ = π/4 on σ_yσ_y, so that |λt*| = π/8 on S_y² gives Ω = ε/(2η√K) and Roos's Ω_c = |ε|/(4η) is the same condition for a Rabi frequency defined without the ½ **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. The second revision of this plan stated the S_y form as ηΩ/ε = 1/(4√K), τ = π√K/(2ηΩ) and Ω_c = |ε|/(4η) in the plan's own Ω and reported that integrating 'the displayed Hamiltonian' gives a Bell state at 1/4 and a product state at 1/2; both statements were true of the doubled Hamiltonian −ħηΩ(...)S_y and false of the plan's drive. Integrating the exact bichromatic Hamiltonian with (ħΩ/2)σ₊ per tone for one loop from |↓↓⟩ (η = 0.05, ν = 2π × 1 MHz, ε = 2π × 10 kHz, d_m = 16) gives concurrence 0.9999 with populations (0.493, 0, 0, 0.507) at ηΩ/ε = 1/2 and concurrence 0.38 with populations (0.038, 0, 0, 0.962), a χ = π/16 pulse, at 1/4, and the effective Hamiltonian −(ħηΩ/2)(...)S_y reproduces both (`check_ms_closure.py`) **[recomputed here]**; the same error had reached the timing-benchmark fixture of Section 11.1, whose 'v2' closure was a χ = π/16 pulse while the withdrawn 'v1' closure at 1/2 was the maximally entangling one. Section 13 carries the row, and the simulator's S_α = Σ_i σ_α^i is the convention of every MS formula in this plan. Validity: η√(n+1) ≪ 1, which allows n well above 1 **[verified]**, plus Ω ≪ ν to avoid off-resonant carrier excitation.

**Corrections beyond the leading order** (Roos 2008) **[verified]**. Keeping the carrier exactly through a frame rotating at F(t) = (2Ω/δ)(sin(δt + ζ) − sin ζ), the effective Hamiltonian at δ = ν − ε is

H_eff/ħ = −ηΩ(J₀ + J₂) S_{y,ψ}(a†e^{i(εt−ζ)} + h.c.) − (η²Ω²/2δ) J₀² S_{y,ψ}² + (2η²Ω²/3δ) J₁² S_{z,ψ}²,

with Bessel functions at argument 4Ω/δ: the force is saturated by (J₀ + J₂), the second term is the counter-rotating spin-spin coupling, the third an unwanted S_z² coupling, and the spin axis is rotated by ψ = (4Ω/δ) sin ζ **[verified]**. These are second-order Magnus terms, not ac Stark shifts **[corrected]**. The exact propagator has α(t) = (ηΩ/ε)(J₀ + J₂)e^{−iζ}(e^{iεt} − 1) and phase rates λ, χ; smooth (non-square) envelopes break loop closure unless the pulse is repeated with the sign of the coupling reversed, which closes the loop at the end of the two-pulse sequence (2τ, not τ) **[corrected]**. Because the simulator integrates the exact Hamiltonian, these appear automatically; the closed forms are test targets and calibration models.

**Thermal-state observables.** For |↓↓⟩ with a thermal mode (Kirchmair Eq. 14) **[verified]**: the populations with two, one and zero ions bright are p₂ = (1/8)(3 + e^{−16|α|²(n̄+½)} + 4cos(4γ)e^{−4|α|²(n̄+½)}), p₁ = (1/4)(1 − e^{−16|α|²(n̄+½)}), p₀ by normalization, with γ = λt − χ sin(εt). Haljan's cat signal P_↓ = ½[1 − exp(−½ṅτ|4α₀|² − (n̄ + ½)|2α(τ)|²)] adds the heating term **[verified]**. The 40Ca+ anchors: ν/2π = 1.232 MHz, η = 0.044, F = 0.993(1) at t_g = 50 µs (ε/2π = 20 kHz), 0.971(2) at 25 µs, and with a Doppler-cooled n̄ = 20(2) at the same 50 µs setting, parity contrast 0.964 **[corrected: gate time attached]**; the paper's fidelity formula as printed has a sign slip (+Im ρ_{dd,uu} should be −Im) **[corrected]**.

**Stark-shift compensation** (Kirchmair Sec. 2.2) **[verified]**: imbalancing the tones, Ω_b = Ω(1 + ξ), Ω_r = Ω(1 − ξ), produces a compensating carrier light shift δ_ac^{(C)} = 2(Ω_r² − Ω_b²)/δ = −8Ω²ξ/δ with ξ = (δη²/|ε|)(φ/π), at the price of an S_z a†a term δ^{(SB)} = (ε/2)ξn that breaks thermal-state operation. Innsbruck's third-tone cancellation (Section 4.3) is the alternative.
4.4.1.title: The Mølmer-Sørensen interaction

4.4.2.text: The bichromatic force couples the mode to σ_φ = e^{−iφ_s}σ₊ + e^{iφ_s}σ₋ with spin phase φ_s = (φ_b + φ_r)/2 and motion phase φ_m = (φ_b − φ_r)/2 in Haljan's convention **[verified]** (Lee 2005 writes φ_S = −(half-sum) with the opposite sign convention **[corrected]**). With co-propagating beat waves a shared optical phase fluctuation enters φ_s (phase sensitive); with counter-propagating beat waves it enters only φ_m, and slow, global fluctuations of the motion phase are harmless because they cancel at loop closure **[corrected: the qualifier "slow global" is load-bearing]**. Quantinuum's wrapper-pulse construction and the phase-insensitive geometries of Section 4.3.4 are scheduler options. Asymmetric detunings μ₊ ≠ μ₋ produce a Stark term s_i = μ₊ − μ₋ **[verified]**.
4.4.2.title: Phases and geometry

4.4.3.text:
For a chain, every mode of the driven axis participates. In the Lamb-Dicke limit the propagator is (Choi et al. 2014 Eqs. 1-3; Zhu, Monroe, Duan 2006 Eq. 4) **[verified]**

U(τ) = exp[Σ_i φ̂_i(τ)σ_x^i + iΣ_{i<j} χ_{ij}(τ)σ_x^iσ_x^j],  φ̂_i = Σ_m(α_{i,m}a_m† − α*_{i,m}a_m),

with the pair sum over unordered pairs, so that the coefficient of σ_x^aσ_x^b is χ_ab itself (the source's Σ_{i,j} would double it); the sign relating Choi's +iχ_ab to XX(χ) = exp(−iχσ_xσ_x) of Section 7.6 is set by the detuning side and is the sign s the compiler records,

α_{i,m}(τ) = iη_{i,m}∫₀^τ Ω_i(t) sin(μt) e^{iω_m t} dt,  χ_{ij}(τ) = Σ_m η_{i,m}η_{j,m} ∫₀^τ dt′∫₀^{t′} dt [Ω_i(t)Ω_j(t′) + Ω_j(t)Ω_i(t′)] sin(μt) sin(μt′) sin[ω_m(t′ − t)],

with η_{i,m} = b_{i,m}Δk√(ħ/2Mω_m) and the sine beat-note convention (force zero at t = 0) **[verified]**. The XX gate on ions a, b requires |χ_{ab}(τ_g)| = π/4 modulo π/2, the sign s being recorded by the compiler so that a solver landing on −π/4 is not scored as a failure (derivation audit of 2026-09-04), and α_{a,m}(τ_g) = 0 for all N modes (2N real conditions); with Ω_a = Ω_b and 2N + 1 equal segments this is a linear system **[verified]**. The symmetrized envelope product replaces the factor 2 of Choi's printed form 2Ω_i(t)Ω_j(t′): the second-order Magnus term is Σ_{i,j}σ_x^iσ_x^j K_ij with a time-ordered kernel that is odd under t ↔ t′, so grouping (a, b) with (b, a) gives χ_ab = K_ab + K_ba, which equals 2K_ab only when Ω_a(t) ∝ Ω_b(t); the printed form is exact for the equal-envelope gate solver, wrong by ±18% for independently shaped per-ion envelopes (±30% in a three-ion example), and as printed gives χ_ij ≠ χ_ji although σ_x^iσ_x^j is symmetric (derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. Blümel et al. 2021 use a kernel without the pair sum and therefore a maximally entangling target of π/8, so a simulator using the π/4 convention must double their kernel, not halve it **[corrected]**. The simulator adopts χ = π/4 with the symmetrized kernel and tests both conversions.

**Amplitude modulation** (Zhu-Monroe-Duan 2006; Choi 2014) **[verified]**: segment the pulse into m constant-amplitude pieces χ(t) = Ω_p sin(μt); the residual-displacement infidelity for thermal spectator modes is F_in ≈ Σ_k β̄_k[|α_j^k|² + |α_n^k|²]/4 with β̄_k = coth[√(μ_k/4) ln(1 + 1/n̄₁)]. Zhu et al.'s Eq. 8 for the Lamb-Dicke thermal infidelity is inconsistent by a factor 2 with the fidelity formula printed above it, and their mode-frequency relation should read ω_{ξ,k} = √λ_{ξ,k} ω_z (the printed ω_ξ is a typo that is silent for axial modes and tenfold wrong for transverse modes at β_x = 10) **[corrected]**; their single-mode closed form Eq. 7 omits a factor 1/l_ξ **[corrected]**. Choi's anchors: five 171Yb+ ions, transverse COM 2.5-4.5 MHz, axial 310-550 kHz, 355 nm Raman, τ_g = 104 µs with 5 segments for two ions and 190 µs with 9 segments for five **[verified]**.

**Frequency modulation** (Leung et al. 2018) **[verified]**: H_MS = (Ω/2)Σ_k [S^k_{φ,γ} a_k† e^{iθ_k(t)} + h.c.] with θ_k(t) = ∫₀^t δ_k(t′)dt′ (the printed Eq. 5 lacks the parentheses that make it Hermitian **[corrected]**); the Magnus series terminates and the propagator is D̂({α̂_k})Ê(β_{ij}); the trajectory α_k(t) = (Ω/2)(η_{i,k} + η_{j,k})∫₀^t e^{iθ_k}dt′; the residual-displacement error is ε ≈ Σ_k|α_k(τ)|² (the joint-state overlap gives e^{−|α|²}, the traced-out fidelity ½(1 + e^{−2|α|²}) **[corrected]**); robustness to a common detuning drift δ₁ follows from ∂α_k/∂δ₁ ∝ the time-averaged trajectory, so the cost function Σ_k|∫₀^τ∫₀^t e^{iθ_k}dt′dt|² enforces α_{k,avg} = 0 for time-symmetric pulses **[verified]**; β_{ij} = Ω² cos γ Σ_k η_{i,k}η_{j,k}β_k is a weighted sum of trajectory areas, not the bare sum **[corrected]**. Anchors: five 171Yb+ ions at 3.045 MHz radial (an ordinary frequency; the item had dropped the 2π **[corrected]**), 90 µs pulses applied twice, 13 oscillations; the experiment needed Ω = 2π × 600 kHz against 151 kHz predicted, attributed to overestimated Lamb-Dicke parameters **[verified]**. This discrepancy is exactly the kind the calibration layer must be able to reproduce and then correct.

**Amplitude-and-frequency-modulated, stabilized gates** (Blümel et al. 2021) **[verified]**: expand the control g(t) = Σ_n A_n sin(2πnt/τ) (about 300 basis functions for 100 µs), impose closure and its first K frequency derivatives, (∂^k/∂ω_p^k)α_p^i(τ) = 0 for every mode and ion, as a homogeneous linear system MA = 0; the zero-temperature infidelity from residual displacement is f = (4/5)Σ_p(|α_p^i|² + |α_p^j|²) = (4/5)AᵀFA, the entangling angle χ = AᵀKA, and the power-optimal solution is the eigenvector of the projected kernel with the largest eigenvalue, Ω₀ = (π/(8|λ_max|))^{1/2} in their π/8 convention. The printed (S6), (S8), (S9) drop a complex conjugate and are not usable as written **[corrected]**. Their hardware: seven 171Yb+ ions with the middle five as qubits, 12.6428 GHz, rf at 2π × 23.83 MHz; mode frequencies and Lamb-Dicke parameters calibrated by blue-sideband spectroscopy with P = sin²(Ω_i^p t) on resonance, so Ω_i^p is half the usual Rabi frequency **[verified flag]**.

The `control/shaping` module implements all three (segmented AM, vertex-parameterized FM with cosine interpolation, Fourier-sine AMFM with K-th-order stabilization and the extended-null-space relaxation Γ = MᵀM) against the same α and χ integrals, in the simulator's π/4 convention, and verifies every solution by exact integration of the full Hamiltonian through the injected `PulseEngine` protocol rather than by importing `dynamics` (control/ never imports dynamics/, which consumes its Pulse objects; the cycle the 2026-09-04 architect critique found), which also captures what the Lamb-Dicke solvers omit (carrier, Debye-Waller, off-resonant terms).
4.4.3.title: Multi-mode gates and pulse shaping

4.4.4.text:
**Field-sensitive qubits** (Ballance et al. 2016) **[verified]**: two Raman beams with beat frequency δ = f_z + δ_g, δ_g = 2/t_g, so K = 2 loops close on the axial COM mode; a two-pulse spin-echo sequence; SPAM-corrected Bell infidelity 2.5(7) × 10⁻³ with gate error 1.1(7) × 10⁻³ at t_g = 100 µs and Δ = −3.0 THz. Error formulas from their supplement: thermal ε_n̄ = (1/4)π²η⁴n̄(2n̄ + 1) = (π²/4)η⁴⟨n²⟩ for n̄ < 1, referenced to an entangling angle calibrated at n = 0 (calibrating the power on the thermal ensemble instead leaves the variance form (π²/4)η⁴n̄(n̄ + 1); the two agree to O(n̄), differing by 2% at n̄ = 0.02 and 50% at n̄ = 1, and the Debye-Waller law χ(n) = χ₀[1 − η²(2n + 1)] behind both was confirmed by the derivation audit of 2026-09-04); heating ε_h = ṅt_g/(2K) with ṅ the gate-mode rate (2.2 s⁻¹ for the two-ion COM mode); motional dephasing with Lindblad operator L = a†a√(2/τ) giving ε_d = α_K t_g/τ, α_K = 1/(2K) + 3/(16K²) = (8K + 3)/(16K²) = {11/16, 19/64, 35/256} = {0.6875, 0.2969, 0.1367} for K = {1, 2, 4}, the 1/(2K) being residual spin-motion entanglement and the 3/(16K²) the randomized geometric phase; Ballance prints {0.686, 0.297, 0.137}, the first being the value at finite t_g/τ = 10⁻³ rather than the asymptotic coefficient (derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[verified]**, **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]** (0.297 × 100 µs/200 ms = 0.15 × 10⁻³ reproduces the paper's line; the heating form ε_h = ṅt_g/2K is an empirical fit from their numerical model, stated only for ε_h ≪ 0.1, with ṅ the gate mode's rate taken as twice the single-ion 1.1 s⁻¹). Parameters **[verified]**: f_z = 1.95 MHz, f_r = 4.5 MHz, η_COM = 0.123, η_str = 0.094, n̄ ≈ 0.02, τ ≳ 200 ms, waist 27 µm; the paper's 2 µK is n̄hf_z/k_B = 1.87 µK, not the Bose temperature 23.8 µK, so simulations are seeded from n̄ = 0.02, never from T = 2 µK. Their carrier Rabi frequency is reduced by 0.83 through axial micromotion; that number is J₀(β) with β = |Δk| × 38 nm = 0.851 for |Δk| = 2π√2/397 nm, J₀ = 0.827, and it brings a first micromotion sideband of relative weight J₁²/J₀² = 0.22, a 22% off-resonant channel the paper does not list **[corrected]**. Zhu-Monroe-Duan's Eq. 2, H = Σ_j ħΩ_j cos(Δk·q_j + μt)σ_j^z, is the lab-frame form **[verified]**.

**Clock qubits** (Baldwin et al. 2021) **[corrected]**: the qubit is |↑⟩ = |F=1, m_F=0⟩ and |↓⟩ = |F=0, m_F=0⟩ of the ²S₁/₂ manifold, |↑⟩ being the only ground state the gate light couples (to the Zeeman-split D₃/₂ |F=1, m_F=±1⟩ levels) and |↓⟩ decoupled by the 12.6428 GHz hyperfine splitting; the paper's opening clause prints the assignment inverted and is contradicted by its own next sentence, its detection counts (about 9 photons for F=1 and 0.1 for F=0) and its optical pumping into F=0. Because clock states have no differential vector light shift, the gate uses a polarization gradient from four couplings with phases {0, 0, −π/2, π/2} through the Zeeman-split D₃/₂ levels of 171Yb+, with the single-photon detuning set by the Zeeman splitting itself, Δ/2π ≈ B × 1.4 MHz/G (7.8 MHz at 5.57 G); after adiabatic elimination H ≈ ηΩΣ_j(−1)^j(1 + σ_z^j)(a e^{iδt+iφ_j} + h.c.) with Ω ≈ g²/Δ, only |↑⟩ shifted, on the axial stretch mode. Two loops in a microwave spin echo give R_x(π)U(π/4)R_{−x}(π)U(π/4) = diag(1, i, i, 1). The printed geometric phase Φ = 2π(Ωη/δ)² is the per-loop coefficient of Ŝ² in Φ_loop Ŝ², with Ŝ = σ_z² − σ_z¹ the force operator of the H two clauses above and Ŝ² = 2 − 2σ_z¹σ_z²: one closed loop of duration 2π/δ gives 2π(ηΩ/δ)² on Ŝ², hence 4π(ηΩ/δ)² on σ_z¹σ_z², and the 8π(Ωη/δ)² of the paper's Eq. 1 is the σ_zσ_z coefficient over the K = 2 loops of the spin echo; the two are consistent once the operator normalization and the loop count are named, which the second revision's bare 'inconsistent, gives 8π' did not do, leaving the calibrated Ω for the two U(π/4) segments ambiguous by 2 or 4, so the fixture integrates the printed H through the echo numerically and asserts diag(1, i, i, 1) (Section 9.17; 2026-09-04 theorist critique) **[corrected]**, **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**; their η carries a factor 4 under the root **[verified flag]**. The paper's simulation kept both D-state levels and all six modes with no Lamb-Dicke expansion, dimension 4² × Π(n_max+1), although the printed total of 5600 does not follow from the stated cutoffs **[corrected]**; in its scattering estimate ε_γ^D the condition Δ ≪ Δ_hf refers to the ground-state hyperfine splitting of 12.6428 GHz, left undefined in the paper, under which |↓⟩ does not scatter at all and every Raman or Rayleigh event off the D state is a which-path measurement of the qubit, the opposite regime from P-state Raman gates **[corrected]**, which is precisely the simulator's JOINT_EXACT construction.
4.4.4.title: Light-shift (σzσz) gates

4.4.5.text:
With an oscillating magnetic-field gradient at ω_g and two microwave tones symmetrically detuned by δ from the ac-Zeeman-shifted qubit frequency (Srinivas et al. 2021 Eq. 1) **[verified]**:

H_I(t) = ħΩ_g J₂(4Ω_μ/δ)(σ_z1 − σ_z2)(a e^{iΔt} + a†e^{−iΔt}),  Ω_g = (r₀/4)[∇(B_g·r̂_q)·r̂](∂ω₀/∂B),  Ω_μ = (B_x/2ħ)⟨↓|μ̂_x|↑⟩,

with intrinsic dynamical decoupling when J₀(4Ω_μ/δ) = 0, i.e. Ω_μ/δ ≈ 0.601, which suppresses dephasing at frequencies well below δ **[verified]**; realized as eight Walsh-modulated pulses over 740 µs on 25Mg+ with error budget dominated by motional dephasing (5.8 × 10⁻⁴ at a 64 ms motional coherence time) **[corrected minor]**. The simulator's "electronic drive" type builds this Hamiltonian from the configured gradient and field sensitivity.
4.4.5.title: Microwave-gradient gates

4.4.6.text: Hughes et al. 2025 write any geometric-phase gate in the frame ħ(ω_m − δ)a†a as H_g = ħδ(t)a†a + (ħΩ_g(t)/2)Ŝ_α(a† + a) **[verified]**, which splits into forced and null oscillators; the maximally entangling angle in their Eq. 4 is θ_g = π/4 (Ŝ_α² has eigenvalues 0 and 4), not π/2 **[corrected]**. Adiabatically eliminating spin-motion entanglement by ramping δ(t) with β̇/δ ≪ 1 gives θ_g ≃ ∫(Ω_g² + α̇²)/δ dt and a temperature-insensitive gate; the printed Eqs. 9-10 contain an anti-Hermitian residual term (±iħβ̇p̂ should be ±ħβ̇x̂), Eq. 16 mislabels β̇/δ as β̇, and Eq. 19's constant b is dimensionally inconsistent as printed **[corrected]**. Their appendix gives the infidelity from mode-frequency fluctuations as exactly two terms, a thermal spin-motion term ∝ (2n̄ + 1)|α_t|²λ² and a temperature-insensitive gate-angle term **[verified]**, and the SLERB metric ε_2q = (6/5 ε_RB + 4/5 ε_leak) × 6/13 **[verified]**. The simulator implements the detuning ramp as an ordinary FM schedule; these formulas are its tests.
4.4.6.title: Smooth gates without ground-state cooling

4.4.7.text:
Bermudez et al. 2017 give the closed forms that the second revision of this plan took as the noise module's targets for an N-ion MS gate **[verified as transcribed]**, with the caveat that their Γ_d and Γ_I are never assigned values in the paper but fitted to reproduce reported fidelities, and the N² global-noise branch was chosen the same way **[corrected]**: motional error ε_m ≈ [πN(δ − ω_z)/(2ω_z²t_g)]·0.8(n̄ + 1) + [π²N(N − 1)η⁴/(8N²)](1.2n̄² + 1.4n̄) (spectator loops plus Debye-Waller); dephasing error ε_d ≈ 2Γ_d t_g Σ_{ij} e^{−|z_i − z_j|/ξ_c}, which is 2t_gN/T₂ for uncorrelated and 2t_gN²/T₂ for globally correlated field noise; intensity-noise error ε_I ≈ Γ_I t_g η²(n̄ + ½) + Γ_I t_g η²(N − 1)/4; and the recalibration rule t_g(n̄_f) = t_g(0)(1 + η²(2n̄ + 1)/N) after heating **[verified as transcribed]**, together with the mapping of the total ε onto Pauli depolarizing channels for circuit-level simulation **[verified]**. The derivation audit of 2026-09-04 re-derived these budgets from the exact gate dynamics (two blind derivations, a comparer and two adjudicators, one of whom held out for the printed forms) and found them to be scale estimates with fitted coefficients rather than derivable results, so the plan's targets are the derived forms below and Bermudez's are kept as the source's statements: the spectator-loop error is ε_loop = Σ_{m≠g}(2n_m + 1)Σ_i|α_{i,m}(t_g)|² = π²NK Σ_{m≠g}(2n_m + 1)(ω_z/ω_m) sin²(δ_m t_g/2)/(δ_m t_g)² with δ_m = μ − ω_m (Bermudez's πN(δ − ω_z)/(2ω_z²t_g) = π²NK/(ω_z t_g)² is the right scale with the mode sum collapsed into the constant 0.8, and the thermal weight is 2n_m + 1, not 0.8(n̄ + 1)); the Debye-Waller error is (π²/8)N(N − 1)(η⁴/N²)(n̄² + n̄), the bracket being Var(n) rather than 1.2n̄² + 1.4n̄ (28 to 34% high); the dephasing error is ε_d = (Γ_d t_g/2)Σ_ij C_ij Cov_t(σ_z^i, σ_z^j) ≤ (Γ_d t_g/2)Σ_ij C_ij, so Nt_g/(2T₂) for uncorrelated and N²t_g/(4T₂) for global noise with T₂ the single-ion 1/e coherence time, 4 and 8 times below the printed 2t_gN/T₂ and 2t_gN²/T₂ (no single convention for Γ_d rescues both printed forms at once); the intensity-noise spin term is Γ_I t_g η² · 3(N − 1)/(8K), not (N − 1)/4, because the phase accumulates as (1 − cos δt) and ∫(1 − cos δt)² dt = (3/2)t_g, a Γ_I-independent ratio of the two terms (fitted intercept-to-slope ratios 1.003 to 1.010 of the derived form against 1.5/K of the printed one); and the recalibration rule keeps η²(2n̄ + 1) but not the 1/N. Section 9.16 pins the derived forms against exact integration **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. Kirchmair's budget adds laser frequency noise (2 × 10⁻³ per gate from incoherent carrier excitation), heating ΔF = Γ_h t_g/2, and Rabi-frequency variation δΩ/Ω ≈ 1.4 × 10⁻² **[corrected minor]**; Ballance's adds photon scattering as the largest term (Section 4.3.2). Section 6 turns these into collapse operators and sampled parameters, and Sections 9.4 and 9.16 require the simulated gate to reproduce each derived closed form in its regime of validity.

**Reconciliations established by the recovery consolidation (Appendix D, Run 3).** (1) The three published thermal Debye-Waller infidelities are one formula, (π²/4)η⁴⟨(n − n_ref)²⟩ over the thermal distribution, with n_ref = n̄ for Sørensen-Mølmer, who re-optimize the pulse duration to the mean, n_ref = 0 for Ballance, calibrated at n = 0, and n_ref = −½ for Zhu, referenced to η²(2n + 1) = 0; in units of (π²/4)η⁴ they read n̄² + n̄, 2n̄² + n̄ and 2n̄² + 2n̄ + ¼, or 2.000, 3.000 and 4.250 at n̄ = 1, so the apparent factor-2 disagreement is a Rabi-calibration reference that no paper documents, and the simulator records which reference a device's calibration uses **[corrected]**. (2) Multi-mode closure counts must include both transverse families: with 2N radial modes Choi's segment count 2N + 1 becomes 4N + 1 (35 → 69 at N = 17) and Blümel's constraint rows N(K + 1) become 2N(K + 1) (51 → 102 at N = 17, K = 2); a solver built on one family leaves the other family's loops open **[corrected]**. (3) Trout's circuit-level dephasing rate r_d = 15 s⁻¹ and the 0.5 s T₂ it cites were reconciled by the second revision through Bermudez's global-noise branch, T₂ = 2N²/r_d = 0.53 s at N = 2; with the derived global coefficient N²t_g/(4T₂) of Section 4.4.7 the same pair gives T₂ = N²/(4r_d) = 0.067 s, so the reconciliation no longer closes and the pair (15 s⁻¹, 0.5 s) is recorded as unreconciled, the naive 1/(2r_d) = 33 ms being no better **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. (4) Roos's Table 1 entry κ/θ = 8/(3η) for the σzσz gate contradicts his Eq. 15, which gives (8/3)η, a factor 1/η² = 100 at η = 0.1 (the second revision printed 900; 2026-09-04 theorist critique), and his Eq. 22 sign is inverted relative to its parent Eq. 19 **[corrected]**. (5) Kirchmair's F = 0.993(1), the 2 × 10⁻³ carrier-excitation figure and δΩ/Ω = 1.4 × 10⁻² are attributed by that paper to Benhelm et al. 2008 **[corrected]**. (6) Hughes's Eq. 19 prints δ_max^{j} for δ_max^{−j}, which would freeze the ramp, and Eq. 20 omits a†a **[corrected]**. (7) Arbitrary-angle XX(χ) is covered by no source; the simulator obtains it by rescaling the null-space pulse amplitude by s with s²χ_max = χ and re-checking closure, and labels the mapping as derived **[background]**. (8) Three published residual-displacement infidelities are one quantity in three fidelity measures: with ε_ent = Σ_{j,m}|α_{j,m}|²(2n̄_m + 1) the entanglement infidelity of a two-qubit gate whose spin-dependent force leaves displacement α_{j,m} on mode m for ion j, Landsman's (4/5)ε_ent is the average gate infidelity (the two-qubit conversion d/(d + 1) = 4/5), Leung's Σ_k|α_k|² is ε_ent at n̄ = 0, and Zhu's Σ_k β̄_k(|α_j^k|² + |α_n^k|²)/4 with β̄_k = coth[√(μ_k/4) ln(1 + 1/n̄₁)] = 2n̄_k + 1 is a state infidelity for his chosen input, a factor 1/4 below ε_ent for the same displacements; the simulator reports ε_ent, converts the sources, and Section 9.4 pins the conversions by direct integration rather than by citation **[background; the plan's own reconciliation, added after the 2026-09-04 critique]**.
4.4.7.title: Error model of a gate, as the sources quantify it

4.5.text: Every optical quantity in Sections 4.2 to 4.4 and 8 (Rabi frequencies, Stark shifts, scattering rates, branching ratios, repump and detection rates, the qubit frequency and its field sensitivity) is a function of a small set of atomic constants per species and of the beam geometry. The research runs of 2026-09-03 extracted those quantities as the papers quote them, per species and per experiment, and Section 12 recorded that the angular algebra behind them had been worked in the source set for 9Be+ only. This section specifies the layer that derives them for any species, so that a species module holds only measured constants with citations and everything hyperfine-resolved is computed. The conventions are Steck's (Quantum and Atom Optics, and the alkali D-line data notes), chosen because they are stated with every phase and normalization written out and are the ones most of the trapped-ion literature follows. The formulas below are standard atomic physics **[background]** whose transcription against those sources is checked in Run 4 (Appendix D); every number quoted is **[recomputed here]** with the scripts of Appendix D and compared with anchors that earlier runs verified independently.
4.5.title: Atomic structure and the light-atom coupling chain

4.5.1.text:
A species module lists, per fine-structure level (n, L, S = 1/2, J): the energy, the lifetime, the magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine constants A and B, and the Landé factor g_J; per isotope, the nuclear spin I and magnetic moment μ_I. From these the atomic module builds, for every level, the hyperfine-plus-Zeeman Hamiltonian in the |m_I, m_J⟩ basis,

H/h = A I·J + B [3(I·J)² + (3/2) I·J − I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [2I(2I−1)J(2J−1)] + (μ_B/h)(g_J J_z + g_I I_z) B,

with A and B in Hz and μ_B/h = 1.399624 MHz/G, the atomic layer working in Hz throughout and converting to rad/s at its boundary (Section 5.6),

with the quadrupole term present only for I ≥ 1 and J ≥ 1, and the nuclear factor g_I = −(μ_I/(I μ_N))(m_e/m_p) in Steck's sign convention, so that both g factors enter with one sign and g_I is of order 10⁻³ g_J; it diagonalizes H numerically at the configured field. The eigenvectors give the mixing between hyperfine states that the dipole matrix elements of Section 4.5.2 need at intermediate fields; the eigenvalues give every transition frequency, its first and second derivatives with respect to B (the sensitivities that H_int of Section 5.7 and the dephasing model of Section 6.3 consume), and the field-independent points. For J = 1/2 the closed Breit-Rabi form is the unit test of the diagonalization:

E(F = I ± ½, m_F)/h = −ΔE_hfs/(2(2I+1)) + (g_I μ_B/h) m_F B ± (ΔE_hfs/2)[1 + 4m_F x/(2I+1) + x²]^{1/2},  x = (g_J − g_I) μ_B B/(h ΔE_hfs),  ΔE_hfs = A(I + ½) with A in Hz (every term in Hz; the second revision added a joule to two Hz terms; 2026-09-04 theorist critique),

with the stretched states m_F = ±(I + ½) exactly linear in B. Recomputed anchors (Section 9.13): the sixteen 43Ca+ ground levels agree between the two methods to 10⁻¹² MHz at 0, 10, 146.0942 and 500 G; the 43Ca+ |4,0⟩ ↔ |3,+1⟩ transition is stationary at 146.0942 G with f₀ = 3,199,941,076.93 Hz and curvature 2.415 mHz/mG², matching Harty et al. (Section 4.3.3; A = −806.4020716 MHz, g_J = 2.00225664, μ_I = −1.31535 μ_N); 9Be+ |2,0⟩ ↔ |1,+1⟩ is stationary at 119.446 G with f₀ = 1,207,495,853.5 Hz against the 119.45 G and 1,207,495,843 Hz of Langer et al. 2005 (A = −625.008837048 MHz, μ_I = −1.177432 μ_N, g_J = 2.00226; the 10 Hz residual is the precision of the constants used, which fixes the test tolerance and the citation requirement); 25Mg+ |3,+1⟩ ↔ |2,+1⟩ is stationary at 212.78 G with f₀ = 1.686462 GHz against the 212.8 G and 1.686 GHz of Srinivas et al. (Section 4.4.5); and the 171Yb+ clock transition's quadratic shift is 310.9 Hz/G² both numerically and from the closed form (g_J − g_I)²μ_B²/(2h²A) with A = 12.642812118 GHz in Hz (the second revision printed 2hA, one factor of h short; 2026-09-04 theorist critique), against the 310.8 Hz/G² of Section 6.3. The coefficient moves by 0.03% across the three g_J values the second revision carried in different rows (2.00225664, which is 43Ca+'s; 2.00254; 2.00292, giving 310.76, 310.85 and 310.97 Hz/G²), so the plan adopts one cited value for the 171Yb+ ground state, g_J = 2.002615(70) (Han et al., arXiv:2501.09973, 2025, a multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock and multireference configuration-interaction determination whose own second-order coefficient is 31.0869(22) mHz/µT² = 310.869 Hz/G²; the only other value in the literature is a spectroscopic 1.998 of larger uncertainty), which with g_I from μ_I = +0.49367 μ_N gives 310.87 Hz/G² and sets the test tolerance at ±0.02 Hz/G² from the g_J uncertainty, with the quoted 310.8 inside it (`check_critique_v3.py`) **[verified]**, **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]**, **[recomputed here]**. The negative A of 43Ca+ is what places F = 3 above F = 4 (Section 8.4); the module derives that ordering rather than storing it.

Two consequences for the rest of the plan. First, the field-sensitivity numbers of Section 6.3 (1.4 MHz/G per unit g_F m_F at low field, 2.8 MHz/G for a Δm_J = 1 Zeeman qubit; 310.8 Hz/G² as the coefficient of B² for 171Yb+, and for 43Ca+ at 146 G Harty's d²ν/dB² = 2.4 mHz/mG², i.e. 1.21 mHz/mG² as a coefficient of (δB)², the two conventions of the Section 13 curvature row) are now derived: the low-field slope is g_F μ_B m_F/h with g_F = g_J[F(F+1) + J(J+1) − I(I+1)]/(2F(F+1)) + g_I[F(F+1) − J(J+1) + I(I+1)]/(2F(F+1)), and the quadratic coefficients come from the diagonalization. Second, the operating field is a `Field` object with magnitude, direction and noise spectrum: its direction is the quantization axis of Section 4.5.3, and a field offset sampled per shot (Section 6.3) is converted into per-ion, per-level frequency offsets through the computed sensitivities, never through a hand-entered MHz/G.
4.5.1.title: Fine, hyperfine and Zeeman structure at the operating field

4.5.2.text:
The decay rate of an upper fine-structure level J′ to a lower level J fixes the reduced dipole matrix element, in Steck's normalization,

Γ_{J′→J} = ω³/(3πε₀ħc³) · (2J+1)/(2J′+1) · |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩|²,

and when J′ decays to several lower levels (P₁/₂ → S₁/₂ and D₃/₂ in Yb+, Ca+, Ba+ and Sr+) the level's total Γ is the sum of the partial rates and the fine-structure branching ratio is their ratio, a radial-integral quantity that the species module stores with its citation (0.501(15)% for 171Yb+ P₁/₂ → D₃/₂, Section 8.1). Everything below the fine-structure level is angular algebra and is computed. The hyperfine-resolved element factorizes by the Wigner-Eckart theorem (Steck's convention; the Rb87 notes' Eqs. 35-37),

⟨F m_F|d_q|F′ m_F′⟩ = ⟨J‖d‖J′⟩ (−1)^{F′+J+1+I} √((2F′+1)(2J+1)) {J J′ 1; F′ F I} · (−1)^{F′−1+m_F} √(2F+1) (F′ 1 F; m_F′ q −m_F),

with a 6j symbol in braces and a 3j symbol in parentheses, nonzero only for m_F = m_F′ + q. Two sum rules that the ingest test checks numerically, both printed by Steck (Rb87 data Eqs. 39-40) **[verified]**: Σ_{m′,q}|⟨J m|d_q|J′ m′⟩|² = |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩|² (the normalization convention itself) and Σ_{q,F}|⟨F (m_F′+q)|d_q|F′ m_F′⟩|² = (2J+1)/(2J′+1) |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩|², so the total decay rate out of any upper sublevel |F′ m_F′⟩ equals Γ_{J′→J} whatever its hyperfine quantum numbers, the relative strength S = (2F′+1)(2F+1)(2J′+1) (3j)² (6j)² is the branching ratio of that decay channel and sums to one over the lower manifold, and the total absorption strength out of any lower sublevel, summed over upper states and polarizations, equals |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩|². Steck's alternative reduced element (J‖d‖J′) = √(2J+1)⟨J‖d‖J′⟩ is the conversion the ingest test applies to sources that use it. Recomputed (Section 9.13): the 171Yb+ P₁/₂ F′ = 1 level decays 1/3 to S₁/₂ F = 0 and 2/3 to F = 1, and F′ = 0 decays only to F = 1, which is the branching that Section 8.1's leakage rate R_d and Section 4.2.6's optical pumping (1/3 per excitation into |0⟩) assumed; for I = 1/2 the stretched ground state's absorption strength to P₃/₂, summed over polarizations, lies half in the cycling |2,2⟩ component and entirely there for σ⁺ light, which is why that transition is closed.

At intermediate fields the |F m_F⟩ states of Section 4.5.1 are mixtures, and the module evaluates the element between the actual eigenvectors, Σ c^{(a)*}_{F m_F} c^{(b)}_{F′ m_F′} ⟨F m_F|d_q|F′ m_F′⟩, which is what makes the 43Ca+ shelving probabilities of Section 8.1 (ground states other than the stretch state shelving with up to about 30% probability at 146 G) computable rather than tabulated.

**Intensity, saturation and the Rabi frequency.** A beam of intensity I has field amplitude E₀ = √(2I/(ε₀c)) and polarization components ε_q in the spherical basis of Section 4.5.3; the Rabi frequency of the transition |a⟩ → |b⟩ that it drives, in the plan's convention H = (ħΩ/2)σ₊ + h.c. (Section 4.3.1), is

Ω_{ab} = E₀ Σ_q ε_q ⟨b|d_q|a⟩ / ħ.

The saturation intensity I_sat = πhcΓ/(3λ³) (Section 13) is a property of a two-level transition whose dipole element squared is 3πε₀ħc³Γ/ω³; for such a transition, and only for such a transition, Ω = Γ√(I/(2I_sat)) and the saturation parameter s = I/I_sat equals 2Ω²/Γ². Recomputed (Section 9.13): 171Yb+ 369.5 nm has |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩| = 1.751 e a₀ and I_sat = 50.77 mW/cm² (the 50.8 mW/cm² of Section 9.12); 40Ca+ 397 nm 2.045 e a₀ and 45.11 mW/cm²; 40Ca+ 393 nm 2.972 e a₀ and 50.25 mW/cm². Which transitions qualify is decided by the angular algebra, and the two readout schemes of Section 8.1 fall on opposite sides of the line. The stretched-state σ⁺ cycling transition |I+½, I+½⟩ → |I+3/2, I+3/2⟩ through P₃/₂ has relative strength exactly (2J+1)/(2J′+1) = 1/2 of |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩|², the same factor that appears in Γ_{P₃/₂→S₁/₂}, so Ω = Γ√(I/(2I_sat)) holds and Acton's s = I/I_sat is exact. The 171Yb+ S₁/₂ F = 1 → P₁/₂ F′ = 0 detection line has J = J′ and relative strength 1/3 per Zeeman component, so with the full-line Rabi frequency Ω = Γ√(I/(2I_sat)) each ground sublevel |1, m⟩ couples to |0, 0⟩ through one polarization component with |⟨0,0|d_q|1,m⟩|² = |⟨J‖d‖J′⟩|²/3, so its Rabi frequency is Ω_m² = |ε_q|²Ω²/3, and since Σ_q|ε_q|² = 1 for any single beam the three sublevels share Σ_m Ω_m² = Ω²/3 however the beam is polarized, the magic-angle choice |ε_q|² = 1/3 giving each Ω_m² = Ω²/9; in a rate model with the three ground states equally populated the excited fraction is Σ_m (1/3)(Ω_m²/Γ²)[1 + (2Δ/Γ)²]⁻¹ = (Ω²/9Γ²)[1 + (2Δ/Γ)²]⁻¹ = s_∘/18 at low intensity with s_∘ = 2Ω²/Γ² for the full-line Ω, which is the Γ/18 prefactor of Section 8.1 (the second revision wrote Ω/√3 per sublevel and s_∘/6, counting the hyperfine factor but not the polarization share; derivation audit of 2026-09-04), and the saturation ceiling of Γ/4 follows from four equally populated levels. Noek's prefactor is therefore derived, not fitted, his s = 2Ω²/Γ² in the (Γ/6, 2/3) form being s_∘/3, and the factor between Crain's quoted I/I_sat and the saturation inferred from his measured rate (Section 8.8) must be intensity calibration, detuning or polarization, all of which the level-C Bloch solve of Section 8.1 takes as inputs **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. The code never accepts "I/I_sat" for a transition it has not classified as closed two-level.
4.5.2.title: Dipole matrix elements, lifetimes, branching and saturation

4.5.3.text: The quantization axis is the direction B̂ of the static field (Section 4.5.1). A beam with wavevector k̂ and complex unit polarization vector ε̂ in the laboratory frame is decomposed as ε̂ = Σ_q ε_q ê_q with ê_{±1} = ∓(x̂′ ± iŷ′)/√2 and ê₀ = ẑ′ = B̂, where x̂′ and ŷ′ complete a right-handed frame with B̂; ε_q = ê_q*·ε̂, and q = +1, 0, −1 drive σ⁺, π and σ⁻ absorption |F m_F⟩ → |F′ m_F + q⟩; the rotation of the laboratory Jones vector and k̂ into the B̂ frame is the module's own construction (no source in Run 4 supplies it, though every sign in the layer depends on it) and it asserts |ε₋₁|² + |ε₀|² + |ε₊₁|² = 1 at beam construction **[background]**. This q is the photon-helicity label. In Steck's matrix-element formulas (Section 13) the index on the operator component is q_op = m_F − m_F′ = m_lower − m_upper, because the lower state is the bra, so a σ⁺ absorption appears in his Eqs. 34-37, in his sublevel Rabi frequencies Ω(m_e, m_g) = ⟨F_g m_g|F_e m_e; 1 −(m_e − m_g)⟩Ω_{−(m_e−m_g)} and in his tables under q = −1: the two labels are opposite because d·ε̂ = Σ_q (−1)^q d_q ε_{−q}, so the field component ε_{+1} couples through d_{−1}. The code stores the helicity label, converts at the one place the Wigner-Eckart routine is called, and a test asserts that a pure ε_{+1} beam drives only m → m + 1 (the 2026-09-04 verifiers found the extracted Steck items with the two labels interchanged; Steck's Rb87 Eq. 57 for the polarization-resolved scattering branching also omits Γ as printed and returns a population rather than a rate) **[corrected]**. Since ε̂ ⊥ k̂, a beam along B̂ carries no π component, a linearly polarized beam perpendicular to B̂ with ε̂ ⊥ B̂ carries equal σ⁺ and σ⁻ components (|ε_{±1}|² = ½), and one with ε̂ ∥ B̂ is pure π. Every beam in `light/beams.py` stores k̂ and ε̂ in the laboratory frame and the atomic module returns its q components at each ion, so that the polarization purity on which Harty's ac Zeeman shift (Section 4.3.3), the optical-pumping efficiency (Section 4.2.6), the coherent-population-trapping factor of Section 8.1 and the polarization-gradient gate of Section 4.4.4 all depend is a computed number with a documented laboratory-frame origin, not a per-transition fudge factor. Polarization impurity is a device parameter (an ellipticity and a misalignment angle), sampled quasi-statically when a spectrum is given.
4.5.3.title: Polarization in the atomic frame

4.5.4.text:
For two beams j = 1, 2 with frequencies ω_j, field amplitudes E_j and polarizations ε̂_j, and the set of intermediate levels |e⟩ (all hyperfine and Zeeman sublevels of the P₁/₂ and P₃/₂ manifolds at their field-dependent energies), each far detuned, Δ_e^{(j)} = ω_j − ω_{e,g} with |Δ_e| ≫ Ω, Γ_e, adiabatic elimination of the excited manifold gives, in the plan's convention (Section 13: Ω = −Ω₁Ω₂/(2Δ_R)), the effective two-photon Rabi frequency between ground states g₁ and g₂ and the light shift of each ground state:

Ω_{g₁g₂} = Σ_e Ω^{(2)*}_{e g₂} Ω^{(1)}_{e g₁} / (2Δ_e^{(1)}),  δ_g = Σ_j Σ_e |Ω^{(j)}_{e g}|² / (4Δ_e^{(j)}),

with Ω^{(j)}_{eg} = E_j ⟨e|d·ε̂_j|g⟩/ħ the single-photon Rabi frequencies of Section 4.5.2 and Δ_e = ω_L − ω_eg the plan's detuning sign (Section 13), so that red-detuned light lowers a ground level and the Raman coupling is the coherent sum over all intermediate sublevels with their signs; the second-order derivation gives these signs directly (E_g^{(2)} = |ħΩ/2|²/(E_g − E_e) = ħ|Ω|²/(4Δ)), and the minus sign in Wineland 2003's Eq. 2.3 and in the Section 13 row comes from that paper's definition Ω ≡ −E₀⟨↑|d·ε̂|↓⟩/(2ħ), a phase convention that the drive phase φ absorbs. Both are evaluated by explicit summation over the level structure of Section 4.5.1, and the closed forms of Sections 4.3.2 and 4.4.4 are their tests: Ozeri's clock-qubit Ω_R = (g_b g_r/3)(b₋r₋ − b₊r₊) ω_f/[Δ(Δ − ω_f)] is what the sum reduces to when the excited hyperfine splittings are neglected against Δ and the P₁/₂ and P₃/₂ paths are combined with their 6j weights (Ozeri's g_b and g_r are each beam's peak field times the fully m_F-resolved stretched cycling element |⟨P₃/₂, F = I + 3/2, m = F|d·σ̂₊|S₁/₂, F = I + ½, m = F⟩| over 2ħ, not a reduced matrix element, from which they differ by a Clebsch-Gordan factor of order 30% in Ω_R; and his τ_π = π/(2Ω_R) is a half-Rabi convention converted on ingest **[corrected]**) (the two paths enter with opposite signs, which is the origin of the ω_f/[Δ(Δ − ω_f)] structure and of the 1/Δ² fall-off); the 9Be+ eight-term differential shift of Wineland 2003 Eq. 2.11 and its polarization null; the vanishing differential vector shift of clock states that Baldwin's gate exploits. The decomposition into scalar, vector and tensor polarizabilities is an equivalent representation offered for reporting **[background]**, not a separate computation.

Two approximations enter here by default and are the only ones added to the optical rotating-wave approximation of Section 1.2, both reported with their size: the adiabatic elimination itself, whose residual excited-state population Σ_e |Ω^{(j)}_{eg}|²/(4Δ_e²) is exactly the quantity the scattering channels of Section 4.5.5 use, so the two are consistent by construction; and the counter-rotating two-photon pairing (beam 2 exciting g₁ and beam 1 de-exciting to g₂), which oscillates at about twice the qubit splitting and would need picosecond steps to integrate, and is instead replaced by its second-order frequency shift of order |Ω_{g₁g₂}|²/(2ω₀) (about 2π × 40 Hz for a 1 MHz Raman Rabi frequency on 171Yb+), which the calibration layer absorbs like any other static shift. A frequency-comb drive is the same computation over the set of tooth pairs, with the single-photon couplings replaced by the comb amplitudes g_k = g₀√(πν_rep τ) sech(2πk ν_rep τ) obeying Σ_k g_k² = g₀² and the two-photon Rabi frequency becoming the tooth-pair sum Ω^{(l)} = Σ_k g_k g_{k+l}/(2Δ) at beat-note separation l; the residual excited-state population is then the same sum over teeth, so the scattering channels of Section 4.5.5 stay consistent with the comb drive by construction (Section 4.3.7).
4.5.4.title: Raman couplings and light shifts from the level structure

4.5.5.text:
Off-resonant light also scatters, through the same intermediate sum. The amplitude for scattering a photon of beam j from ground state a to ground state b with emitted polarization q′ is the Kramers-Heisenberg sum A^{(j)}_{a→b,q′} ∝ Σ_e ⟨b|d_{q′}|e⟩⟨e|d·ε̂_j|a⟩/Δ_e^{(j)}, and the rate is Γ_e times the far-detuned excited population times the branching, combined coherently over e: Γ^{(j)}_{a→b} = Σ_{q′} |Σ_e √Γ_e c_{e→b,q′} Ω^{(j)}_{ea}/(2Δ_e^{(j)})|², with c_{e→b,q′} the normalized decay amplitude of Section 4.5.2 (Σ_{b,q′}|c_{e→b,q′}|² = 1) and √Γ_e inside the coherent sum, one factor per intermediate path (strictly √(Γ_e(ω_j/ω_e)³), a 10⁻⁴ fine-structure correction), because the emission element ⟨b|d_{q′}|e⟩ = √(3πε₀ħc³Γ_e/ω_e³) c_{e→b,q′} carries it; the second revision placed Γ_e outside the sum, which is exact only when every intermediate level has the same total rate, true for 9Be+ under one radial integral and false for the species whose P₃/₂ branches to D levels, by up to 11× per channel (derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**. This is the general form of Ozeri 2005's Γ_{i,f} = g²γ|a^{(1/2)}_{i→f}/Δ + a^{(3/2)}_{i→f}/(Δ − Δ_f)|² (Section 4.3.2), and the tabulated 9Be+ amplitudes of Section 9.10 (Raman a^{(1/2)} = −√2/3, a^{(3/2)} = +√2/3; Rayleigh 2/3 and 1/3 for σ⁺ on m = −1/2, and so on) together with Ozeri 2007's P_total, ε_S and ε_D are its tests; the module produces the corresponding amplitudes for 43Ca+, 171Yb+, 133Ba+ and 88Sr+ from their level structures, which closes the "worked for 9Be+ only" gap of Section 12. Four things Run 4 fixed in Ozeri's paper as a source: the sentence after his Eq. 18 defines λ_{3/2} = c/ω_{3/2}, contradicting his Eq. 18, Table I and every Table II value, and taken literally inflates the required laser power by (2π)² = 39.5, so λ = 2πc/ω is used (his Table II reproduces to two figures for eight ions with it; the Yb+ row does not: it prints 0.2 × 10⁻⁴ and 2 mW where the paper's own Eq. 17 gives 0.29 × 10⁻⁴ and 2.9 mW, and it is excluded; the first revision of this plan had the printed and recomputed pairs transposed, caught by the errata check of 2026-09-04); his P_total has two equally deep minima, 2√2 πγ/ω_f at Δ = (√2 − 1)ω_f and at −(√2 + 1)ω_f, with P_∞ = 3πγ/ω_f, and P_min is not a gate-error floor because P_Raman falls as 1/Δ²; the Raman scattering rate falls as 1/Δ⁴ and the per-π-pulse probability as 1/Δ², two statements his text leaves implicit; his 5/12 recoil average is isotropic, the dipole-weighted value for fixed polarization being 9/20 (8% more, 27/25; the second revision wrote 16%), his D(β) = exp(βa − β*a†) is the conjugate of QuTiP's convention (harmless only because his β is imaginary), his ε_S is an upper bound (Eq. 11 discards a positive term) and his P_Rayleigh silently includes the D-level Raman channel for Ca+, Sr+, Ba+ and Yb+, overstating the elastic rate by fP_total **[corrected]**.

Three kinds of channel follow, all Lindblad operators on the joint space (Section 5.7):

- **Raman scattering** (b ≠ a): √Γ_{a→b} |b⟩⟨a| ⊗ R, with R the recoil operator of Section 4.2.8. When b is outside the qubit pair this is **leakage**, the channel that Section 12 recorded as absent from every source: for a hyperfine qubit the leaked population sits in the other Zeeman sublevels of the same or the other F manifold, and its fate at readout (bright or dark) follows from the manifold (Section 8.1; for 171Yb+ the F = 1 sublevels are bright and F = 0 is dark); for an optical qubit it sits in other D₅/₂ or S₁/₂ sublevels with their own readout polarity and lifetimes. Leakage is therefore simulated, not estimated, whenever d > 2, and its rate is the sum of the out-of-pair Raman rates otherwise.
- **Rayleigh scattering** (b = a) with **equal** amplitudes for the two qubit states, r_↑ = r_↓ for every emitted mode: the collapse operator is proportional to the identity on the spin and acts only on the motion through R, so it heats but does not decohere; this is the regime of Section 4.3.2's statement that Rayleigh scattering at large detuning leaves a hyperfine (clock) qubit's coherence intact.
- **Differential Rayleigh scattering**, r_↑ ≠ r_↓ (Uys et al. 2010): the operator r_↑|↑⟩⟨↑| + r_↓|↓⟩⟨↓| = ½(r_↑ + r_↓)𝟙 + ½(r_↑ − r_↓)σ_z has a σ_z part that dephases the qubit at a rate proportional to Σ_modes |r_↑ − r_↓|², an error absent from Ozeri 2007's Raman-only estimate. It vanishes for clock states far from the fine-structure levels, where the two amplitudes coincide by symmetry, and does not vanish for Zeeman qubits or at detunings comparable with the fine-structure splitting. The module computes r_↑ and r_↓ from the same amplitude sum, so the channel comes for free once the amplitudes exist. Uys et al. 2010 give the rate **[verified]** (Eqs. 4, 5 and 7 transcribed by Run 4 and re-read from the e-print by a three-verifier panel in Run 5, which confirmed them and sharpened four conventions; see the closing paragraph of this subsection): with Kramers-Heisenberg amplitudes A^{i→j}_{J,λ} = b_λ⟨j|d·ε̂*_{λ+(i−j)}|J, λ+i⟩⟨J, λ+i|d·ε̂_λ|i⟩/(δ_{iJλ} μ²) normalized to the largest dipole element μ of the manifold, so that the scattering rates are Γ_{ij} = Ω_R²γ Σ_λ (Σ_J A^{i→j}_{J,λ})² with Ω_R = μE₀/(2ħ) (a coherent sum over the intermediate fine-structure levels J inside the square, an incoherent sum over the driving polarization components λ outside it), the elastic decoherence rate is

Γ_el = Ω_R² γ Σ_λ (Σ_J A^{d→d}_{J,λ} − Σ_{J′} A^{u→u}_{J′,λ})²,

the square of the difference of the two states' elastic amplitudes, and it enters the master equation as 𝓛_el ρ = −(Γ_el/4)[ρ − σ_z ρ σ_z], so that the qubit coherence decays at (Γ_Ram + Γ_el)/2 while populations relax at the Raman rates alone **[verified]**. Four conventions in Uys's formula that Run 4 fixed: the amplitudes A^{i→j}_{J,λ} carry units of inverse angular frequency and are signed, not dimensionless; μ = ⟨3/2, 3/2|d·ε̂₁|1/2, 1/2⟩ is a fixed normalization tied to Ω_R = μE₀/(2ħ), not a free choice; Uys's δ = ω_transition − ω_laser is positive for red detuning, the opposite of this plan's Δ; and Γ_el is a dephasing rate, not an elastic scattering rate, vanishing for equal amplitudes however large the elastic rates and reaching 2(Γ_dd + Γ_uu) for equal and opposite ones, so the rate-difference estimate (Γ_uu − Γ_dd)²/(Γ_uu + Γ_dd) of Ozeri 2007 under-predicts the measured decoherence at the detuning where the two rates are equal, where the estimator vanishes identically while the measured rate does not (the second revision quantified this as 'a factor of five', a ratio to zero; 2026-09-04 theorist critique) **[corrected]**. Because the detunings in the two amplitudes can have opposite signs the terms can add, and the earlier rate-difference estimate ½Γ_el ≈ (Γ_uu − Γ_dd)²/(Γ_uu + Γ_dd), which is Ozeri 2007's ε_δ = (dΓ/Γ_Rayleigh)² P_Rayleigh, underestimates the measured decoherence fivefold at the detuning where the two elastic rates are equal; Rayleigh decoherence is negligible only when both conditions hold, detuning large compared with the qubit splitting and clock states, in which case Γ_el ∝ 1/Δ⁴ against 1/Δ² in general. Their anchor is a 9Be+ electron-spin qubit at 4.5 T (Ω_z = 2π × 124.1 GHz, 313 nm light, P₃/₂ resonances at −79.4 and −37.7 GHz from the cycling transition, equal elastic rates near −56 GHz). Ozeri 2007's closed forms for linearly polarized beams of equal coupling are the tests of the amplitude sum: Γ_total = (γ/3)[g_b²(b₋² + b₊²) + g_r²(r₋² + r₊²)][1/Δ² + 2/(Δ − ω_f)²], Γ_Raman = (2γ/9)[same bracket][ω_f/(Δ(Δ − ω_f))]², P_Rayleigh = (πγ/ω_f)(3Δ² − 2Δω_f + ω_f²/3)/|Δ(Δ − ω_f)|, with g_{b,r} = E_{b,r}|⟨P₃/₂, F = I+3/2, m_F = F|d·σ̂₊|S₁/₂, F = I+1/2, m_F = F⟩|/(2ħ) the half-convention Rabi frequency of the stretched cycling transition and γ/g² = 4ħω³/(3πε₀c³E²) the atomic-constant ratio that removes the dipole element from the scattering error, g being the stretched-state coupling defined above (Ozeri Eqs. 14-18, verified by derivation from his Eqs. 1, 3 and 12 and numerically against the Rb87 D2 line) **[verified]**; their z₀ = √(ħ/(4Mω)) is the two-ion normal-mode extent, the factor-4 flag of Section 13, and their Rayleigh recoil ⟨|β|²⟩ = (5/12)η² is the isotropic average for their crossed-beam geometry, a special case of the kernel of Section 4.2.8.

**What the Run 5 verifier panel established for the two transcriptions Section 12 flagged** **[verified]**, **[corrected]**. Uys's Eqs. (1)-(8) and Wineland 2003's Eqs. (2.13)-(2.18) were re-read from the cached e-prints by a three-verifier panel in Run 5; the forms above stand, with their conventions sharpened. The Uys amplitudes A^{i→j}_{J,λ} are **signed reals**, because δ_{iJλ} = Ω_{J,λ+i} − Ω_i − ω₀ changes sign across the intermediate levels and per-term moduli destroy Γ_el, a squared difference of amplitude **sums** that is largest precisely where the two elastic rates coincide; λ indexes the **incident** component, carrying b_λ, fixing M_J = λ + i and entering δ_{iJλ}, the scattered index being the derived λ + (i − j), so the two readings coincide only for the elastic terms Eq. (7) uses (refuted 3-0 as a "scattered-photon index", fatal only for a polarization-asymmetric drive) **[corrected]**. The μ² normalization must pair with an Ω_R = μE₀/(2ħ) from the **same** stretched-state μ, half the plan's single-photon Ω, so feeding a plan-convention Ω into Γ_{ij} = Ω_R²γ Σ_λ(Σ_J A)² is a factor 4, and since the source prints no normalization for b_λ the drive builder asserts Σ_λ|b_λ|² = 1. The three collapse operators are ½√Γ_el σ_z, √Γ_du|u⟩⟨d| and √Γ_ud|d⟩⟨u| in the plan's 𝓓[L]ρ convention, and the asymmetry is deliberate: the Raman operators carry the plain rate under the root, the Rayleigh one Γ_el/4, and that prefactor is correct **and must not be "fixed" to Γ_el/2** even though the observable coherence decays at Γ_el/2 - a `mesolve` run with c = ½√Γ_el σ_z alone leaves populations exactly unchanged and returns Γ_el/2, while √(Γ_el/2)σ_z decays twice as fast. The three-operator generator reproduces Eq. (8) elementwise with zero trace derivative, and the spin-echo readout ρ_uu = ½(1 − e^{−(Γ_Ram + Γ_el)τ/2}) has initial slope (Γ_Ram + Γ_el)/4, so twice the fitted short-time slope is the quoted total decoherence rate; it reads the transverse Bloch length, not the population block **[recomputed here]**. On the Wineland side the eight-channel Eq. (2.14) rationals 2/3, 1/3, 1, 1/6, 1/2, 5/6 are relative dipole **line strengths** per polarization component, summed over the excited sublevels of a fine-structure level and normalized to the stretched σ₊ element that defines g_{b,r} - not branching ratios; each bracket sums to 1 for ²P₁/₂ and 2 for ²P₃/₂, which is why one shared γ is exact in LS coupling, and the per-beam polarization amplitudes are unit-normalized, a constraint the paper never prints but every reduction needs **[corrected]**. Wineland's Ω is a half-angle amplitude with a π pulse at Ωτ_π = π/2, so τ_π = π/(2|Ω|) and any formula written in the symbol converts on ingest while the π **time** is convention-independent; Δ is referenced to ²P₁/₂, so the ²P₃/₂ pathway detuning is Δ − ω_F and the two carry opposite signs at the optimum, +82.01 and −115.99 GHz for 9Be+ **[recomputed here]**. The optimization is of the **ratio** R_SE/|Ω| and never of R_SE: minimizing |x(x − 1)|[1/x² + 2/(x − 1)²] with x = Δ/ω_F gives x = √2 − 1 = 0.414214 and minimum 2√2, hence R_SE/|Ω| = 4√2 γ/ω_F and P_SE = 2√2 πγ/ω_F = 8.885766 γ/ω_F = 8.706 × 10⁻⁴ for 9Be+ at γ/2π = 19.4 MHz and ω_F/2π = 198 GHz, whereas the negative test of minimizing the bracket alone returns the different and wrong x = ω_F/(1 + 2^{1/3}) = 0.442493 **[recomputed here]**. The two per-π-pulse figures near 10⁻³ must not be conflated: 2√2 πγ/ω_F is the m_F = 0 clock line with b₋ = r₋ = b₊ = −r₊ = 1/√2, the |2,2⟩ ↔ |1,1⟩ Zeeman-type qubit with b₀ = 1, r₊ = r₋ = 1/√2 giving (8π/√6)γ/ω_F = 10.260399 γ/ω_F = 1.0053 × 10⁻³ **[recomputed here]**. Eqs. (2.17) and (2.18) share one (g_b² + g_r²)/3 prefactor and bracket, so δ_{0↔0} = −(ω₀/γ)R_SE holds exactly for any Δ and polarization: compute the bracket once, reuse it for the dissipator weight and for the shift, added as −(δ_{0↔0}/2)σ_z, and note that unlike the |2,2⟩ ↔ |1,1⟩ shift it is polarization-independent and therefore unnullable **[recomputed here]**. Two caveats travel with R_SE - it over-estimates decoherence when |Δ| ≫ ω_F, where elastic events dominate, and at large fine structure Raman scattering from further levels must be added - but Table 1 sits at Δ = 0.414 ω_F, so neither discounts the tabulated numbers, the far-detuned replacement being the Γ_el above **[contested, reconciled]**. What Run 5 does **not** close is recoil: these dissipators stay internal-state only, so the kernel of Section 4.2.8 is the only operator form available and its transfer here is untested (Section 12).
4.5.5.title: Scattering amplitudes: Raman, Rayleigh and differential Rayleigh decoherence

4.5.6.text:
| Stored per species, with citation | Derived by `species/atomic.py`, tested in Section 9.13 |
|---|---|
| Mass; nuclear spin I; nuclear moment μ_I | g_I; the full ∣m_I, m_J⟩ hyperfine-Zeeman spectrum of every level at any field; state labels by adiabatic connection |
| Per level: energy, lifetime, A, B, g_J | Zeeman energies and mixings; every transition frequency with dB and d²B sensitivities; clock points; the level ordering (sign of A) |
| Per fine-structure transition: wavelength, Γ, fine-structure branching (S versus D) | reduced dipole element; I_sat for closed two-level transitions; every hyperfine and Zeeman-resolved dipole element, decay branching and absorption strength |
| Nothing about polarization | q components of every beam at every ion from the laboratory-frame geometry and B̂ |
| Nothing about Raman couplings | Ω_{g₁g₂}, per-level light shifts, differential shifts, comb sums, adiabatic-elimination residuals |
| Nothing about scattering | Raman, leakage and Rayleigh amplitudes and rates per beam; differential-Rayleigh dephasing; the Lindblad operators of Section 5.7 |
| The designated qubit pair, cycling, repump and shelving transitions | classification of each as closed two-level or not; bright and dark manifolds for the readout POVM |

**Conventions Run 4 settled for the species layer** **[verified]**, **[corrected]**. Three normalizations of the dipole element coexist and stack: Steck's Brink-Satchler reduced element ⟨J‖d‖J′⟩ (no 1/√(2j + 1)), the fully m_F-resolved stretched cycling element that Ozeri, Uys and Wineland use as their anchor, smaller by √(1/2) on a J = 1/2 → 3/2 line (87Rb D2: 2.989311 against 4.227524 e a₀ at τ = 26.2348(77) ns, the elements being derived from the stored lifetime with its uncertainty and never typed in, since the rounded 26.24 ns already gives 4.227104 e a₀; so substituting one element for the other moves every rate by 2), and the Edmonds round-bracket element, larger by √(2j + 1); one level up, Steck's Γ_{J_gJ_e} = ω³(2J_g + 1)|⟨J_g‖d‖J_e⟩|²/(3πε₀ħc³(2J_e + 1)) is the total, m_F-independent decay rate out of any sublevel of J_e into the fine-structure level J_g and equals b(J_e → J_g)/τ, so on a unit-branching alkali D2 line it is 1/τ, Ozeri's, Uys's, Wineland's and Olmschenk's γ exactly, with no second factor 2 (the second revision of this plan claimed one; the degeneracy ratio inside the formula is the same factor already spent in converting the reduced element to the stretched one, and applying it again is a factor 4 on a D2 line; caught by the derivation audit of 2026-09-04) **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]**; every stored element and rate carries a convention tag and is converted once at ingest, and the degeneracy ratio is never applied on top of a 3j-normalized element. The two hyperfine factors are directed quantities built from one 6j symbol with swapped prefactors, S_FF′ = (2F′ + 1)(2J + 1){…}² summing to one over excited F′ and b(F′ → F) = (2F + 1)(2J′ + 1){…}² summing to one over ground F, never one "hyperfine factor". The sign of A_hfs is an independent signed input that sources rarely print (9Be+, 43Ca+ and the 171Yb+ ³D[3/2]₁/₂ level are all inverted multiplets); with A > 0 the 43Ca+ clock point exists nowhere between 1 and 4000 G and the 9Be+ one nowhere between 8 and 16 mT, which is the module's ingest test of the sign, inferred from μ_I when not printed. The measured g_J replaces the Landé formula (5.9 ppm off for 87Rb; g_J = 2.000 exactly moves the 43Ca+ clock point by 160 mG and 47 Hz), Steck's g_S = +2.0023193 is opposite in sign to CODATA's g_e and the module uses Steck's convention throughout, and the three self-consistent nuclear-Zeeman forms (Steck's μ_I = −μ_B g_I I/ħ with a plus sign, Langer's g_I = −μ_I/(Iμ_B) with a plus, Harty's g_I^{(N)} = μ_I/(Iμ_N) with a minus) must not be mixed: Harty's g with Langer's sign is an 83.76 kHz error in f₀ and 0.207 G in B₀ for 43Ca+. The exact 2 × 2 fixed-M diagonalization is primary and the Breit-Rabi closed form a cross-check because the radicand collapses to (1 ± x)² at the stretched states and the closed form returns the wrong branch beyond |x| = 1 (2437.6 G for 87Rb); eigenstates are labelled by adiabatic continuation from B = 0, and drive matrix elements are computed in the field-dressed eigenbasis, since Steck's drive Hamiltonian assumes degenerate sublevels and at 146 G the mixing is what creates the clock point. "Curvature" is stored twice under distinct names, the second derivative d²ν/dB² (Harty prints 2.4 mHz/mG²) and the Taylor coefficient ½d²ν/dB² (Langer prints 0.305 Hz/µT²), and accumulated phase is 2π∫[ν(B) − ν(B₀)]dt with the bracket in Hz (both of Langer's figures fix the 2π: 75.8 µs against his printed 80 µs, 52.2 s against his 50 s). The second-order sums carry a three-index detuning Δ_i(m_S, beam) = ω_beam − (ω_i − ω_{m_S}), and a code with a single Δ_i per intermediate level and beam returns exactly zero for the 0 ↔ 0 clock light shift, the sharpest test of that convention (Section 9.13); the sums have no iγ/2 in their denominators and are used only far from resonance, the multi-level Bloch solve of Section 4.2.8 taking over within a few linewidths. I_sat = πhcΓ/(3λ³) is the cycling value with σ₀ = 3λ²/(2π), exactly one third of the random-orientation ħω³Γ/(4πc²) that is also widely quoted (87Rb D2: 1.669325 against 5.007975 mW/cm²), λ is the vacuum wavelength, and for a degenerate manifold the scalar saturation parameter is abandoned for per-sublevel Rabi frequencies. Apparatus figures must not become species constants: the 9Be+ 1.81(2) Hz trap-rf ac Zeeman shift, the −5 Hz 43Ca+ trap shift already subtracted from f₀, the −1.0 Hz microwave ac Zeeman shift acting only during π/2 pulses, the 14.7 s Ramsey contrast time, the 4.2 kHz differential Stark detuning, the F₇/₂ filling rate, the 5 G quantization field, beam powers and waists and the collection efficiency are all settable device scalars defaulting to zero or none; and two constants carry conditional provenance as a field, not a comment: the 171Yb+ branching 0.00501(15) holds only with τ(P₁/₂) = 8.07 ns, because the fit measures the product γR, and the 43Ca+ μ_I = −1.31535 μ_N is a thesis value 0.17% from the handbook number that fits f₀ nine times better, effectively a fitted constant. Steck's QAO Eq. 7.132 prints the hyperfine operator with half-value ħ exponents, still unfixed in revision 0.16.10 of 27 June 2026 (use the dimensionless S = I·J/ħ² form), his Rb87 Eq. 60 drops a prime, and his uncoupled-basis elements QAO 7.328-7.331 are the A-only J = 1/2 or I = 1/2 case, not a general intermediate-field kit (B needs I, J ≥ 1 and C needs I, J ≥ 3/2), so the general-J diagonalizer of Section 4.5.1 is the plan's own construction built from powers of I·J **[background]**.

The species modules of milestone M0 (171Yb+, 40Ca+, then 43Ca+, 133Ba+, 137Ba+, 9Be+, 25Mg+, 88Sr+) therefore shrink to a table of cited constants each, and the anchors of Section 9.13 are the acceptance test of the shared algebra. The Run 4 extractions fix the first entries **[verified]**, **[corrected]**: for 171Yb+ (Olmschenk et al. 2007) the S₁/₂ **zero-field** splitting 12,642,812,118.5 Hz with quadratic shift 310.8 Hz/G², recomputed from first principles as taylor_c2 = (g_J − g_I)²μ_B²/(2h²ν₀) = 310.76 Hz/G² and therefore confirmed to be the Taylor coefficient and not d²ν/dB² **[recomputed here]** (the splittings 12.642815, 12.642819 and 12.642821 GHz printed elsewhere in the literature are this same second-order shift at 3.0, 4.7 and 5.3 G and must never be stored as zero-field constants), the ground-state g-factor g_F(F = 1) = g_J/2 = 1.001128 with g_Fμ_B/h = 1.4012 MHz/G - the ubiquitous "1.4 MHz/G" being that product and not the dimensionless g_F, whose misuse returns an adjacent-m_F splitting of 11.6 MHz instead of 8.27 MHz at 5.9 G, a 40% error in the quantity that gates the coherent-population-trapping window of Section 4.2.4 **[recomputed here]**, the P₁/₂ splitting 2.105 GHz, D₃/₂ 0.86(2) GHz and ³D[3/2]₁/₂ 2.2095(11) GHz, the P₁/₂ lifetime 8.07(9) ns from Pinnington et al. (γ/2π = 19.7 MHz, an inference from the shared citation rather than a printed symbol) with branching 0.00501(15) to D₃/₂ (measured on 174Yb+, isotope independent), the D₃/₂ lifetime 52.7 ms with its 935.2 nm repump and 3.07 GHz sideband (the P₁/₂ → D₃/₂ decay channel itself lies at 2.438 µm, the 935.2 nm line being D₃/₂ → ³D[3/2]₁/₂, a conflation that changes the inferred P₁/₂ → D₃/₂ reduced element by 4.2 times and that one derivation of the 2026-09-04 audit fell into, so the species table stores the channel wavelength next to its element), and the F₇/₂ trap state cleared at 638.6 nm; two glosses the extractors added and the verifiers removed: the detection error is dominated by off-resonant excitation of the bright state through the 2.1 GHz P₁/₂ splitting, not by the 14.7 GHz dark-state detuning (Section 8.1's R_b), and the insensitivity of detection to 935 nm power above 500 µW follows from the 0.005 branching ratio, not from repump saturation; for 43Ca+ (Harty et al. 2014) μ_I = −1.31535 μ_N with the zero-field splitting from Arbes et al., to which the Breit-Rabi fit needs a third constant g_J that the paper never prints (2.00226; g_J = 2.000 moves the field-independent point by 0.16 G and f₀ by 48 Hz, so Section 9.13 cites it), a 16-state ground manifold spanning 3.6 GHz at 146 G with adjacent Zeeman splittings of about 50 MHz (Zeeman spreads 409 MHz within F = 4 and 306 MHz within F = 3, the paper's "~500 MHz"), lasers at 397 and 866 nm for Doppler cooling plus 393, 850 and 854 nm for readout and reset, the M-resolving 393 nm shelving in which ground states other than the stretch state shelve with at most about 30% probability, and the two-frequency σ⁺ 397 nm pumping with microwave clean-up; for 9Be+ (Langer et al. 2005) the clock point B₀ = 11,944.6 µT and 1,207,495,843 Hz with curvature 0.305 Hz/µT² and a 1.81(2) Hz ac Zeeman correction, the 17.6 kHz/µT slope of the |2,2⟩ ↔ |1,1⟩ magnetometry transition at B₀, the 21 kHz/µT slope of the field-sensitive |2,−2⟩ ↔ |1,−1⟩ qubit, and further field-independent points at 0.01196 T and 0.02231 T, whose state pairs the paper conveys only graphically and the diagonalization resolves as |2,1⟩ ↔ |1,0⟩ at 119.643 G and |2,1⟩ ↔ |1,1⟩ at 223.073 G (recomputed slopes 17.64 and 21.0 kHz/µT, curvature 0.3049 Hz/µT²) **[recomputed here]**.
4.5.6.title: What the species database stores and what it derives

4.5.7.text:
The 40Ca+ S₁/₂ ↔ D₅/₂ transition at 729 nm and the 88Sr+ S₁/₂ ↔ D₅/₂ transition at 674 nm are dipole-forbidden electric-quadrupole (E2) lines, so the dipole algebra of Sections 4.5.2 to 4.5.5 does not give their Rabi frequencies. A dedicated run (Appendix D, Run 4Q) read James 1998 Sec. 4-5 and Appendix, the Roos 2000 thesis and Schindler et al. 2013 for this coupling; 18 items were checked, 11 were refuted on transcription or source errors and corrected, and the forms below carry the verifiers' corrections.
