Two kinds of rows share the tables and have different CI semantics. **Pinned tests** (closed forms, recomputed values, identities, conversions) fail the build; where a row states no tolerance, the default is 10⁻⁹ relative for closed forms and exact identities, the printed number of significant digits for recomputed values, and 10⁻¹² for operator identities. **Consistency anchors** (laboratory numbers quoted from a paper) are tracked metrics with the acceptance band stated in the row or, by default, the published uncertainty, or 20% where none is given; they report but do not fail the build, because Section 12 records that published fidelities cannot be reproduced from first principles without recomputing the mode structure and pulses under stated assumptions. Every row is written in the simulator's own conventions and names the Section 13 row it depends on; a source's convention appears only as a labelled conversion test. Multi-ion rows run with the resolved-mode set their device preset declares and the frozen-spectator contribution of Section 5.2 reported. All tests run in JOINT_EXACT mode unless marked.

9.13.text:
Recomputed on this machine (`check_atomic.py`, `bench_numerics.py`, `bench_ms_timing.py`, Appendix D); each becomes a test. The atomic anchors were computed from the Breit-Rabi formula and from a general hyperfine-plus-Zeeman diagonalization with Steck's conventions (Section 13) and compared with published values that the earlier runs had verified independently.

| Test | Expected | Source, tag |
|---|---|---|
| Breit-Rabi against numerical diagonalization | 43Ca+ (I = 7/2, A = −806.4020716 MHz, g_J = 2.00225664, μ_I = −1.31535 μ_N) at 0, 10, 146.0942 and 500 G: all 16 levels agree to 10⁻¹² MHz | closed form vs `eigh` [recomputed here] |
| 43Ca+ clock point | ∣4,0⟩ ↔ ∣3,+1⟩ stationary at B₀ = 146.0942 G, f₀ = 3,199,941,076.93 Hz, curvature 2.415 mHz/mG² | Harty 2014: 146.094 G, 3,199,941,077 Hz, 2.4 mHz/mG² [verified] |
| 9Be+ clock point | ∣2,0⟩ ↔ ∣1,+1⟩ at 119.446 G, 1,207,495,853.5 Hz with A = −625.008837048 MHz, μ_I = −1.177432 μ_N, g_J = 2.00226; the 10 Hz residual against the published value is the precision of the g-factors used, so the tolerance is 20 Hz and the constants must be cited | Langer 2005: 119.45 G, 1,207,495,843 Hz, +1.81(2) Hz ac Zeeman correction; A and the g-factors are not printed there and must be cited from elsewhere [verified] |
| 25Mg+ clock point | ∣3,+1⟩ ↔ ∣2,+1⟩ at 212.78 G, 1.686462 GHz with A = −596.254376 MHz, μ_I = −0.85545 μ_N | Srinivas 2021: 212.8 G, 1.686 GHz [verified] |
| 171Yb+ clock quadratic shift | 310.87 Hz/G² numerically and from (g_J − g_I)²μ_B²/(2h²A) with A = 12.642812118 GHz in Hz and the adopted g_J = 2.002615(70) (Han et al. 2025), tolerance ±0.02 Hz/G² from the g_J uncertainty; the earlier row's 310.85 used an uncited g_J = 2.00254 and printed 2hA (`check_critique_v3.py`) | Olmschenk 2007 / Fisk: 310.8 Hz/G²; Han et al. 2025: 31.0869(22) mHz/µT² [verified]; [corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]; [recomputed here] |
| Wigner-Eckart branching | 171Yb+ P₁/₂ F′ = 1 decays 1/3 to S₁/₂ F = 0 and 2/3 to F = 1; F′ = 0 decays only to F = 1; for I = 1/2 the ∣1,1⟩ → P₃/₂ absorption strength summed over polarizations is 1/2 in the cycling ∣2,2⟩ component | angular algebra vs Section 8.1's 1/3 branching [recomputed here] |
| Γ to reduced element to I_sat | the rate in both formulas is the partial rate of the fine-structure transition: 171Yb+ 369.5 nm with Γ_S/2π = 19.62 MHz: ∣⟨J‖d‖J′⟩∣ = 1.752 e a₀, I_sat = 50.83 mW/cm² (1.751 and 50.77 at the retired 19.6 MHz reading); 40Ca+ 397 nm with the quoted 21.57 MHz and 393 nm with 23.4 MHz read as partial rates: 2.045 e a₀, 45.11 mW/cm² and 2.972 e a₀, 50.25 mW/cm² (if those quoted linewidths are totals the elements fall by 3%, branching 0.941 and 0.940, and the species table must say which); Ω(I = I_sat) = Γ/√2 | Section 9.12's 50.8 mW/cm² [verified]; Steck's Γ to reduced-element normalization anchor [verified] |
| Displacement operator, exponential vs analytic | interior block agreement 3 × 10⁻¹⁶ (d_m = 10, η = 0.1), 7 × 10⁻⁸ (10, 0.5), 2 × 10⁻⁴ (10, 1.0), ≤ 10⁻¹⁵ at d_m = 40 for all three η; exponential unitary to 10⁻¹⁵; analytic top-column norm loss 9.3% at (10, 0.1); both triangles of the analytic form, with (iη)^{∣n′−n∣}, match the exponential | Section 5.1.1 [recomputed here] |

| Step density | DOP853 evaluations 1.3 × 10³ → 3.2 × 10³ (carrier, 2 µs) and 5.1 × 10³ → 1.6 × 10⁴ (spin-dependent force, 10 µs) from d_m = 6 to 41; 14 to 45 steps per mode period; identical under Python 3.13.14 and 3.14 | Section 5.2 [recomputed here] |

The v3 run (0.09, 0.35, 12.3, 124 s and 0.13, 0.47, 15.1, 137 s) reproduces on the idle machine (113.6 and 131.1 s at 2048, `outputs/bench_ms_timing_v3_idle_rerun.out`) and is the four-term dense case; the v2 run at ηΩ/ε = 1/4 (a χ = π/16 pulse) gave 0.08, 0.43, 13.6, 179 s and the first fixture (η 0.08, 0.06, 0.05) 0.09, 0.37, 10.1, 102 s, both kept as controls (`outputs/bench_ms_timing.out`, `bench_ms_timing_v1.py`) | Section 11.1 [recomputed here]; closure [corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]; construction [corrected: critique, 2026-09-04] |

| QuTiP interface facts | `propagator(H, t, piecewise_t=…)`, `mcsolve` option `improved_sampling`, coefficient signatures `f(t)` and `f(t, **kwargs)`, array coefficients with `tlist` and `order=0`, integrator option `nsteps` all present in 5.3.1 | introspected [recomputed here] |
| 9Be+ further anchors | ∣2,2⟩ ↔ ∣1,1⟩ slope at B₀: −17.64 kHz/µT (Langer 17.6); ∣2,−2⟩ ↔ ∣1,−1⟩ slope 21.0 kHz/µT at low field (Langer ≈ 21); clock curvature 0.3049 Hz/µT² (Langer 0.305); further stationary pairs ∣2,1⟩ ↔ ∣1,0⟩ at 119.643 G and ∣2,1⟩ ↔ ∣1,1⟩ at 223.073 G (Langer 0.01196 T, 0.02231 T) | Langer 2005, which prints both slopes as unsigned magnitudes [verified]; [recomputed here] |
| Mixed-species two-ion table | Be+/Mg+ with single-ion frequencies (12.26, 11.19, 2.69) and (4.82, 3.72, 1.65) MHz: x modes 12.11, 4.67; y modes 11.03, 3.53; z modes 4.04, 1.90 MHz; axial eigenvectors (−0.926, 0.379), (0.379, 0.926); off-species radial amplitudes 0.018 (x) and 0.020 (y) as printed, against 0.017 and 0.022 from the caption's transposed (3.72, 4.82) order, which is the negative control | Home 2013 Table I [verified]; caption [corrected]; [recomputed here] |
| Isolated impurity radial frequency | for an impurity of mass μm in Kielpinski's transverse matrix the normalized frequency is ζ = √(ε²/μ² − 1/(2μ)), not ε/μ, because the static defocusing term picks up one factor of 1/μ and the pseudopotential term two | Kielpinski 2000 Eqs. 17-19 [verified]; gloss [corrected] |

| Mixed two-ion axial modes | ω±²/ω_z1² = 1 + 1/μ ± (1 − 1/μ + 1/μ²)^{1/2}: 0.500847 and 2.250636 at μ = 23.985042/9.0121822 (isotope masses; the natural-abundance 24.305 u would give 0.495185 and 2.246406), with ω₊² + ω₋² = 2(1 + 1/μ) = 2.751484 as the mass-agnostic identity; 1 and 3 at μ = 1; mass-weighted eigenvectors orthonormal | Wübbena 2012 Eqs. 12-14; Morigi-Walther Eq. 8 [verified]; [recomputed here] |
| Laguerre nodes in pulsed cooling | first zeros as a continuous degree: 39.7908 (k = 1) and 71.7720 (k = 2) at η = 0.3, 112.2895 and 202.0112 at η = 0.18; with the degree n′ = n − k the stranded upper states are n = 41 and 74 (η = 0.3) and 113 (η = 0.18); the printed 40, 72 and 112 are degree labels; Lamb-Dicke breakdown Ω_{20,19}/Ω = 0.570893 against η√20 = 0.804984 (41% high) at η = 0.18, carrier e^{−η²/2} = 0.9839305; the closed form matches `expm` to 10⁻¹⁵ up to η = 2.5 | Che 2017 Eq. 2 versus Fig. 2; Rasmusson Eq. 3 [corrected]; [recomputed here] |

| Five-wire null and depth | y₀ = √(2ab + a²)/2 = 0.921954 for a = 1, b = c = 1.2; x₀ = ac/(b + c) in House's coordinates, the null moving toward the narrower rail; Nizamani's κ form equals House's Eq. 28 for c = b; depth maximal at b/a = 1.19149 for fixed a and at b/a = 3.676 (κ = 0.022542) for fixed ion height with c = b; the c = b/2 branch peaks at 4.902 with κ = 0.020038, exactly 8/9, but extrapolates a formula House derived for c = b only, so the module's numerical saddle is the reference there; House's Eq. 7 with the printed sign reports the stable (a_z, q) = (0.005, 0.20) as unstable, the negative control | House 2008; Nizamani 2012 [verified], [corrected]; [recomputed here] |
| Zigzag-mode Floquet shift | three-ion 40Ca+ zigzag at q = 0.206: pseudopotential 730(14), 1041(12) kHz against measured 714(2), 1078(2) and Floquet-Lyapunov 715.1, 1078.5 kHz; the centre-of-mass modes obey the single-ion Mathieu equation and are unshifted by the Coulomb micromotion coupling, while their pseudopotential β ≈ √(a + q²/2) sits 5.4 × 10⁻³ (y) and 9.1 × 10⁻³ (x) below the exact exponent | Kaufmann 2012 Table I [verified]; c.m. statement [corrected] |
| Surface-trap multipole anchors | Wesenberg Eq. 11 parameters (Ω = 2π × 100 MHz, V_rf = 100 V, M = 10 u, d = 100 µm): q₀ = 0.98, maximal secular frequency 5.5 MHz, maximal quadrupole depth 55.8 meV; the symmetric five-wire trap reaches 0.9514 of it; Chiaverini four-wire: null height √3/2 of the rail pitch, curvature 8/3, depth 1/72 and frequency 0.29 of the four-rod quadrupole; Madsen asymptote 2589 K µm²/V² for 111Cd+ at 50 MHz | Wesenberg 2008; Chiaverini 2005; Madsen 2004 [verified], [corrected] |

| Hyperfine sum rules and stretched elements | 87Rb D2: S_FF′ rows {1/20, 1/4, 7/10} (F = 2) and {1/6, 5/12, 5/12} (F = 1), D1 {1/2, 1/2} and {1/6, 5/6}, each summing to 1 to 10⁻¹²; 171Yb+ {½ ½ 1; 1 0 ½}² = 1/6, b(1 → 0) = 1/3, b(1 → 1) = 2/3, b(0 → 0) = 0 (1/2 or 1/4 means the 6j normalization or the sum direction is wrong); ∣⟨J‖er‖J′⟩∣ = 4.227524 e a₀ (D2, τ = 26.2348 ns) and 2.993125 (D1), stretched cycling element √(1/2) × 4.227524 = 2.989311 e a₀ (tabulated 2.98931(44)); inverting the degeneracy ratio is 4× on D2 | Steck Rb87 Eqs. 34-42, Tables 7-8; Olmschenk [verified] |
| Saturation intensity, both normalizations | 87Rb D2 cycling ħω³Γ/(12πc²) = 1.669325 mW/cm² (tabulated 1.66933(49)), random-orientation ħω³Γ/(4πc²) = 5.007975, exactly 3.0000×; D1 1.495851 and 4.487552 (tabulated 4.4876(43)); σ₀ = 3λ_vac²/(2π) = 2.9066929377205 × 10⁻⁹ cm² against 2.906692937721(93) × 10⁻⁹ | Steck Rb87 Eqs. 61-62, Table 7 [verified] |
| Second-order Zeeman from Breit-Rabi | 87Rb 575.146 Hz/G² (g_J = 2.002331070, g_I = −0.0009951414, Δ_hfs = 6.834682610904290 GHz) against Steck's 2π × 575.15; 171Yb+ 310.797 Hz/G² with g_J = 2.00292 (g_I = 0) and 310.85 with 2.00254 against the quoted 310.8, both uncited values now superseded by the adopted g_J = 2.002615(70), which gives 310.87 (Section 4.5.1); g_J's fourth decimal is the tolerance; B in gauss | Steck Rb87 Eq. 29, Table 6; Olmschenk [verified]; [recomputed here] |
| Three-index detuning | the 0 ↔ 0 clock light shift δ = −(g_b² + g_r²)(ω₀/3)[1/Δ² + 2/(Δ − ω_F)²]; at Δ = (√2 − 1)ω_F, ∣δ/Ω∣ = 4√2 ω₀/ω_F = 3.6 × 10⁻² for 9Be+ (Wineland's Table 1); a single Δ_i per intermediate level and beam returns exactly zero; companion P_SE = 2√2 πγ/ω_F = 8.7 × 10⁻⁴ at γ/2π = 19.4 MHz, ω_F/2π = 198 GHz | Wineland 2003 Eqs. 2.10-2.18 [verified] |
| Uys bounds and Lindblad prefactor | 0 ≤ Γ_el ≤ 2(Γ_dd + Γ_uu); amplitudes a = 1.0, b = −0.9 give Γ_el = 3.61 against Γ_dd + Γ_uu = 1.81; `mesolve` with √(Γ_el/4)σ_z gives dρ_ud/dt = −(Γ_el/2)ρ_ud with zero diagonal change; √(Γ_el/2)σ_z gives Γ_el and fails; near −56 GHz in 9Be+ at 4.5 T the amplitude form gives about 5× the rate-difference estimate, which returns about zero | Uys 2010 Eqs. 4-8, Fig. 3 [verified] |

Thermal envelope ordering: ⟨√n⟩/√n̄ → √π/2 = 0.88623 (0.88600 at n̄ = 1000) and ⟨√(n(n−1))⟩/n̄ → 1 (0.99950 at n̄ = 1000), so the two terms grow as √n̄ and n̄² and their ratio as n̄^{3/2} | Sterk et al. 2022 Eq. 1 [corrected], [recomputed here] |
| Convolution against the exact displaced thermal state | At n̄_th = 0.1: p₀ = 0.822579 (convolution) against 0.830092 (Laguerre), max∣Δp∣ = 1.297 × 10⁻² and variance 0.21000 against 0.23000 at n̄_α = 0.1; p₀ = 0.334436 against 0.366264, max∣Δp∣ = 3.183 × 10⁻² and variance 1.11000 against 1.31000 at n̄_α = 1. The variance difference is exactly 2n̄_th n̄_α in both. The printed index range m = n..N sums to e^{−n̄_α} = 0.36788 at n̄_α = 1 | Walther et al. 2012 Eq. 2 [corrected], [recomputed here] |
| End-to-end junction transport (integration target, not a unit test) | A designed adiabatic junction waveform must return essentially **zero** coherent excitation, since the measured 0.053 ± 0.003 quanta per E-C-E round trip (350 µs, 1.76 mm, two barrier crossings) and 0.18 ± 0.02 per E-C-F-C-E and E-C-V-C-E are noise-limited rather than adiabaticity-limited; anomalous heating alone contributes 0.007 to 0.014 quanta | Blakestad Table I, Secs. V C-E [verified] |
| End-to-end splitting (integration target) | The quartic-plus-Coulomb model on Bowler's schedule (2.6 MHz initial, minima near 700 kHz COM and 880 kHz stretch, final 2.85 and 2.77 MHz) over 55 µs with a 17 µs first segment must give about 2 quanta per ion, dominated by the coherent component, with about 0.2 quanta from ambient heating, and must remain partially de-excitable (2.1 → 1.4, 1.9 → 1.6) under a resonant uniform-field displacement | Bowler et al. 2012, two-ion paragraph and Fig. 5 [verified] |
| End-to-end fast transport (integration target) | Sweeping the dwell of an 11.2 µs out-and-back 280 µm sin²-position ramp at 1.41 MHz must give n̄_α(τ_d) periodic with period 1/ν_ax = 709.22 ns, minima ≤ 0.1 quanta and maxima of order 100; sweeping the kick delay of a 4 µs transport plus one 400 ns square kick must give a sinusoidal n̄_α(τ_k) whose two kick polarities are offset by half a motional cycle | Walther et al. 2012 Fig. 3 [verified] |
| Round-trip time reversal (self-consistency) | In a noiseless constant-ω simulation, applying the exact time reversal of a forward waveform after a hold of an integer number of secular periods returns α → 0 and n̄ to its initial value up to integrator error, and the excitation-versus-hold-offset curve is flat for an optimized waveform and sinusoidal for an unoptimized one | Sterk et al. 2022 (phase independence); Pino et al. 2021 (combine as the time reverse of split) [background] |

9.16.text:
The blind re-derivation audit of Appendix D confirmed 37 of 58 load-bearing equations and corrected 16; the rows below are the numerical checks its derivers, comparers and adjudicators ran to discriminate the plan's forms from the corrected ones, written as the test suite must reproduce them. Each row names the equation by its audit id (section-index of the harvest). Two of them are re-derived by committed scripts (`check_c0_floquet.py`, `check_ms_closure.py`); the rest were computed by the audit's agents in the run's own scripts and are recorded here as targets an implementer reproduces, not as **[recomputed here]** numbers, since Appendix D's rule is that the tag requires a committed script.

| Test | Expected | Source, tag |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1-1: Build the plan's written-out thermal RHS with spre/spost/sprepost and compare to qutip.liouvillian(H, [sqrt(G(Nb+1)) a, sqrt(G Nb) a^dag]) at D = 40/60/90; then check d<n>/dt at n = 0, the steady state, and the ladder ratio. | Relative Liouvillian difference <= 2e-16; Tr(rho-dot) <= 1.2e-10; d<n>/dt∣_{n=0} = Gamma*Nbar exactly (150000.000000000 at G = 5e4, Nb = 3); steadystate <n> = Nbar and p1/p0 = p2/p1 = Nb/(Nb+1) = 0.750000000. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.1-2: In the SITE basis only (H = Sum p_j^2/2 + (1/2) x^T A x, drive exp(i K x_j), no normal modes), compute ∣<n'∣e^{i K x_j}∣0>∣ and compare to ∣eta∣ exp(-(1/2) Sum eta^2) with eta from the plan's formula using the SINGLE-ion mass and unit-norm b. | N = 2, K = 0.2/0.6: max relative error 3.3e-15 (0.279443943497 both ways), where the bare ∣eta∣ = 0.3 is 7% off - the Debye-Waller factor is the whole gap. Using N m instead of m fails by sqrt(N). | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.1-3: Integrate a classical ion in Ornstein-Uhlenbeck field noise (sigma^2 = 0.02, tau_c = 0.05, omega = 1) and compare the exact double-integral heating slope to e^2 S_E^(1)/(4 m hbar omega) with S_E single-sided; also run 4000 Monte Carlo trajectories. | Slope ratio 0.99991 (9.97416e-4 vs 9.97506e-4); MC <n>(200) = 0.19743 ± 0.00319 vs 0.19950 (-0.65 sigma). Rival prefactors are excluded: (1/2) S1 gives 2.000, (1/4) S2 gives 0.4997. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.1-6: At mpmath 50 dps for N = 2..10, solve the equilibrium, build the closed-form A_mn, and check row sums, mu_1, mu_2, the b_N > 0 gauge, and mu_3 against the printed table. | Equilibrium residual <= 3.5e-47; max∣row sum - 1∣ <= 8e-50; ∣mu_1 - 1∣ <= 6.2e-50; ∣mu_2 - 3∣ <= 5.9e-50; b^(1) = (1,...,1)/sqrt(N) and b^(2) = +u/∣∣u∣∣ to 1.6e-50; mu_3 = 29/5 at N = 3 and 5.81, 5.818, 5.824, 5.829, 5.834, 5.838, 5.841 for N = 4..10 at rtol 1e-3. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.1-7: Compute the l' = 0 micromotion sideband amplitude quantum-mechanically (Fock 60, exponential midpoint 4096 steps per rf period, Floquet modes of U(T)) at q = 0.1/0.2/0.3 and divide by eta = Delta k x_0; repeat with the rf clock shifted by T_rf/2. | ∣a_0∣/eta = 1.00188921 / 1.00774102 / 1.01816014, equal to 1/sqrt(S_W) to 5e-7 and NOT to 1/Sum c_n (0.95192/0.90670/0.86308) or 1/(1+q/2). Unchanged under t -> t + T_rf/2; the u(0)=1 recipe swings 0.863 -> 1.180. | derivation audit 2026-09-04, re-derived in `check_c0_floquet.py` |
| 4.2-1: In an exact 2-level (x) Fock model with unexpanded drive exp(i eta(a+a^dag)) and jumps sqrt(Gamma w_j) sigma_- exp(-i k_em x_0 u_j(a+a^dag)), scan f = k_em x_0/eta over {0, 0.5, 1, 2} at fixed eta and alpha, and fit the carrier weight in A_pm from the steady-state P1/P0 and the Liouvillian gap. | Fitted carrier weight = alpha f^2, so it equals alpha only at f = 1 and vanishes at f = 0; the plan's alpha-only form fails for every f != 1. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.2-3: Assemble the printed plus-sign sideband coupling i eta(sigma_+ a + sigma_- a^dag) and the plan's minus-sign form; check Hermiticity, then sesolve from ∣g,n> with normalize_output = False. | Printed form: ∣∣H + H^dag∣∣ = 0 exactly, spectrum purely imaginary (max∣Re∣ = 1.4e-17), norm grows in any solver. Minus form: ∣∣H - H^dag∣∣ = 0, max∣P_e - sin^2(eta Omega sqrt(n) t/2)∣ <= 2.6e-8, ∣norm^2 - 1∣ <= 1.5e-8. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.2-6: Symbolically evaluate the exact steady state nbar = A_+/(A_- - A_+) at Delta = -nu and at Delta = -Gamma/2 with f_s = alpha(k_em/k_L)^2/cos^2(theta_L), and check the alpha -> 0 limit and the alpha/Omega/eta dependence. | nbar(-nu) = (G/4nu)^2[1 + f_s(G^2 + 16 nu^2)/(G^2 + 4 nu^2)] -> (G/2nu)^2[f_s + 1/4]; exactly (G/4nu)^2 at alpha = 0 for any G/nu, not zero. nbar(-G/2) = (G/4nu)(1+f_s) - 1/2 + nu/(2G) + f_s nu^3/G^3. d(nbar)/d(eta) = d(nbar)/d(Omega) = 0 identically; A_- - A_+ free of alpha. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.3-2: Over eta in {-0.9, -0.1, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.9, 1, 1.5, 2, 3} x n, n' <= 8, compare Omega_{n',n} from the plan's printed RHS, the modulus-corrected RHS and the signed element against ∣<n'∣expm(i eta(a+a^dag))∣n>∣ at N = 400; assert non-negativity. | Corrected modulus form: max error 2.19e-14; signed form vs complex element: 4.88e-14. Printed RHS: negative at 210/891 points, max discrepancy 1.2006 Omega (eta = -0.9, 0 <-> 1) and already negative at eta = +0.5 for n = n' >= 6. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.3-3: Compute <p∣(a+a^dag)^p∣0> and the ratio of the exact ∣<p∣D(i eta)∣0>∣ to the eta^p/p! heuristic at eta = 0.1, p = 0..6, against e^{-eta^2/2}(i eta)^p/sqrt(p!). | <p∣(a+a^dag)^p∣0> = sqrt(p!) exactly (1, 1, 1.4142136, 2.4494897, 4.8989795, 10.9544512); closed form matches expm to 1.4e-17; exact/heuristic = sqrt(p!) e^{-eta^2/2} = 2.4373 (p=3) and 4.8745 (p=4), i.e. the plan's 2.4 and 4.9. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.3-4: Drive the same physical pulse in both conventions: exp(-i(Omega t/2) sigma_x) and exp(-i Omega_W t sigma_x) with Omega = 2 Omega_W; compare P_up, the pulse areas at the same wall-clock t_pi, and P_up at Omega_W t = pi. | P_plan(Omega -> 2 Omega_W) - P_W simplifies to exactly 0; Omega t_pi = pi and Omega_W t_pi = pi/2 at identical wall-clock time; sin^2(pi) = 0.0 at Omega_W t = pi, so Omega_W t = pi is a full cycle, not a pi pulse. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.3-5: With exp(i eta(a+a^dag)) unexpanded and no sideband RWA, sweep phi_b = phi_r = phi over {0, 0.35, pi/4, 0.9, 1.3, -0.5, 2.0} at kappa = 0, integrate one closed loop and fit the two-ion entangling axis from the Pauli decomposition of <s',0∣U∣s,0>; repeat in the crossed-Delta k geometry. | Same-Delta k: axis = (phi + pi/2) mod pi to <= 8.9e-16 (1.570796, 1.920796, 2.356194, 2.470796, 2.870796, 1.070796, 0.429204). Crossed-Delta k (eta_r = -eta_b): axis = phi mod pi. The carrier axis is exactly c in both. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.4-4: Integrate the plan's displayed MS Hamiltonian (no 1/2) for one loop from ∣dd>∣0> at eta Omega/eps = 1/4 and 1/2 (Fock 60-90, atol 1e-13), then separately integrate the plan's exact drive H = (hbar Omega/2) sigma_+ e^{i(...)} + h.c. and fit the circle radius of the interaction-picture <a>. | Displayed H: at 1/4, populations (0.5, 0, 0, 0.5) and concurrence 0.999999991; at 1/2, product state (0, 0, 0, 1.0), concurrence 1.15e-10. Exact drive: fitted radius/[eta Omega/(2 eps)] -> 1 (0.99474, 0.99868, 0.99917, 0.99980 as eta -> 0), i.e. the sideband coupling is eta Omega/2. | derivation audit 2026-09-04, re-derived in `check_ms_closure.py` |
| 4.4-5: Two ions x two modes with deliberately NON-proportional envelopes (Omega_1 ~ sin^2(pi t/tau), Omega_2 ~ (t/tau) sin^2(pi t/tau)); H is block-diagonal in the sigma_x basis, so get chi exactly from sesolve and compare to 2 K_ij, 2 K_ji and the symmetrized kernel. | Symmetrized kernel exact; the two readings of the printed form err by -18.20% and +18.20% (2 ions) and by ±29.6% / ±21.4% (3 ions). Also assert chi_ij = chi_ji and that the full-square integral of the printed integrand equals K_10 - K_01, the antisymmetric combination. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.4-8: Add a Lindblad interaction-noise channel c_op = sqrt(2k) H_int (Gamma_I = k Omega^2, verified against the carrier-contrast rate) and fit eps_I = A(2 nbar + 1) + B over nbar = 0, 0.5, 1 for (N, K) = (2,1), (3,1), (2,2), (2,3), (3,2). | A/(eta^2 Gamma_I t_g/2) = 0.997-0.999 (the plan's first term is exact); B/[3(N-1)/(8K)] = 1.003, 0.999, 1.007, 1.010, 1.003, against B/plan[(N-1)/4] = 1.505, 1.498, 0.755, 0.505, 0.752. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.4-7: From exact Laguerre sideband elements, check chi(n) = chi_0[1 - eta^2(2n+1)], then compute the thermal gate infidelity twice: with the drive power calibrated at n = 0, and with the power scanned on the thermal ensemble. | ∣M_n∣^2 - ∣M_{n-1}∣^2 = eta^2[1 - eta^2(2n+1)] (ratio 1.0007/1.0020/1.0039 at eta = 0.123 vs 0.955/0.926/0.898 for the naive -eta^2). n=0-calibrated eps/[(pi^2/4) eta^4 nbar(2 nbar + 1)] -> 1 (0.99944 at eta = 0.01, nbar = 1); power-optimised eps/[(pi^2/4) eta^4 nbar(nbar+1)] -> 1 (0.99976). | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.5-1: Build the explicit 24-level 87Rb D2 manifold by ∣m_J, m_I> recoupling (no 6j), feed Steck's Gamma formula the plan's own reduced element, and brute-force Sum_{m,q}∣<J_g m∣d_q∣J_e m'>∣^2 for every excited sublevel; then fit tau from mesolve. | min = max = 3.81097561e7 s^-1 for all 16 excited sublevels, i.e. Gamma_Steck * tau = 1.000000000000 (not 0.5), m'-independent; ∣∣Sum_q L^dag L - (1/tau) P_e∣∣ = 1.5e-8 and tau_fit = 26.2403 ns from every initial sublevel. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.5-4: Compare the plan's 6j + 3j factorization against a brute-force uncoupled-basis triple-CG sum (spectator m_I, no 6j) over (I, J, J') sets spanning I = 0..7/2 and (J,J') = (1/2,1/2), (1/2,3/2), (3/2,3/2), (3/2,5/2); build ∣F m_F> both as ∣(J I) F> and ∣(I J) F>. | 20280 elements, 1760 nonzero, 0 mismatches and max∣diff∣ = 0 exactly for the ∣(J I) F> order; the ∣(I J) F> order flips sign on exactly the cases predicted by (-1)^{2I+J+J'-F-F'} (144 of 370 in the smaller run); 0 selection-rule violations of m_F = m_F' + q. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.5-7: In an 8-level S + P_1/2 + P_3/2 model with sympy CG amplitudes, set Gamma_P1/2 = 1 and Gamma_P3/2 = 3 (unequal), then compare mesolve channel rates to the sqrt(Gamma_e)-inside form and to the Gamma_e-outside form for each choice of Gamma_e. | Raman channel (b = +1/2, q' = 0): mesolve 1.249283e-05, sqrt-inside 1.250000e-05 (ratio 0.9994); Gamma_e-outside gives 1.092122e-06 / 3.276366e-06 / 2.184244e-06 - off by 11.44x, 3.81x, 5.72x. With equal Gamma_e both forms agree to 1.2e-3. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 4.5-8: Quadrature (96x192 Gauss-Legendre) of ∣<D_5/2, m'∣(eps.r)(n.r)∣S_1/2, m>∣ over all 12 allowed pairs, for sigma+ light along B, comparing the recipe with c^(q) = (2/3) b^(q) versus the conjugate duals, and with q = m - m' versus q = Delta m; also check the g sum rule and maxima. | c = (2/3)b with q = m - m': max error 3.9e-16. Conjugate duals with the same q: 2.3e-1. Sum_ij∣c∣^2 = 2/3 for both families (so the norm alone does not discriminate); Sum_q∣g∣^2 = 1/3; maxima ∣g^{±1}∣ = 1/sqrt3, ∣g^0∣ = 1/2, ∣g^{±2}∣ = 1/sqrt6; sigma+ along B requires ∣g^{(-1)}∣ = 1/sqrt3 and ∣g^{(+1)}∣ = 0, driving Delta m = +1. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 6-3: Apply the plan's motional-dephasing L = a^dag a sqrt(2/tau) to a two-ion MS gate at K = 1, 2, 4 (L commutes with the rotating frame, so use one expm per sigma_x block - no ODE tolerance) and extrapolate (1 - F) tau/t_g to t_g/tau -> 0; separately check the Fock coherence law. | alpha_K -> 0.687499 / 0.296875 / 0.136719 = (8K+3)/(16K^2) = 11/16, 19/64, 35/256; alpha_1 is 0.6875, never 0.686. Coherence: rho_{nn'} decays at exactly (n-n')^2/tau (max deviation 1.9e-15, Delta n only), with d<n>/dt = d<n^2>/dt = 0.0 exactly. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 6-2: Diagonalize H/h = A(I.J) + (mu_B/h) B (g_J J_z + g_I I_z) per m_F block for 171Yb+ and for 43Ca+ near 146 G, and report BOTH the coefficient of (delta B)^2 and d^2 nu/dB^2 for each clock qubit. | 171Yb+: (nu(B) - nu(0))/B^2 = 310.7767 Hz/G^2 flat at B = 1, 5, 10 G with no linear term, d^2 nu/dB^2 = 621.5534. 43Ca+ ∣4,0>-∣3,+1> at B* = 146.094 G: coefficient of (dB)^2 = 1207.73 Hz/G^2 = 1.2077 mHz/mG^2, d^2 nu/dB^2 = 2415.46 Hz/G^2 - exactly 2x apart, so the printed 310.8 / 2.4 pair is mixed-convention. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 6-4: Fuzz the 8-dimensional MS-crosstalk model over (chi, phi_beam, theta_13, theta_23) with 4000 samples, comparing F and P_ion3 to the plan's closed forms; then evaluate at theta_13 = theta_23 = pi/2 and at (0.1644, -0.2763). | max∣numeric - plan form∣ = 1.33e-15, independent of both chi and phi_beam; F = 0.900790 and P_ion3 = 0.097217 at the quoted angles (against the printed 0.974422 / 0.025450); at theta_13 = theta_23 = pi/2 the crosstalk unitary reduces to -X1X2, giving P_ion3 = 0 where the halved-argument form gives 0.5. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 8-1: Solve the exact 4-level 171Yb+ F=1 -> F'=0 Lindblad steady state (16-dim Liouvillian, magic-angle polarization, pump << omega_Z << Gamma) over three decades of s_o and compare to both the plan's (Gamma/6, 2/3) form and the (Gamma/18, 2/9) form; also check the saturation ceiling and half-max. | exact/corrected = 0.999991, 0.999284, 0.991954; exact/plan = 0.333478, 0.333243, ... (a flat factor 3). Ceiling Gamma/4 = 30.79/us confirmed; half-max at s_o = 4.5, not 1.5. Sum_m Omega_m^2 = Omega^2/3 for any single-beam polarization; Sum_q∣eps_q∣^{-2} >= 9. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 8-3: Evaluate the literal double-sum P(n;t) of Eq. 8-3 in mpmath (dps 40) against an independent MMPP matrix exponential on the (count, state) lattice at several (R_1, R_2, R_T, t), and sum the printed jump-only branch. | Both agree to <= 1e-30 and Sum_n P(n;t) = 1.000000000000000000; the jump-only branch alone sums to 1 - e^{-R_T t} (0.00995016625083 at R_T t = 0.01), reproducing the missing no-jump branch. The Poisson convolution collapse Sum_k P_p(k; R_1 tau) P_p(n-k; R_2(t-tau)) = P_p(n; R_1 tau + R_2(t-tau)) is exact. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 8-5: Compute eps_geom = (1 - cos(arcsin NA))/2 symbolically and by isotropic Monte Carlo at NA = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9, and compare to the paraxial NA^2/4; also derive the EMCCD excess-noise factor from the cascade recursion. | Closed form = sin^2(theta_max/2) identically; exactly 1/10 at NA = 0.6 (MC 0.099927 ± 0.00015). Paraxial errs -1.0%, -4.2%, -10.0%, -28.2%. F^2 = (2G + p - 1)/(G(1+p)) -> 2 - 1/G -> 2, so QE_eff = QE/F^2 = QE/2 belongs in the variance only, never in the mean rate. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |
| 13-6: Compute the Lamb-Dicke anchor for 171Yb+ at 355 nm counter-propagating (∣Delta k∣ = 3.5398227e7 1/m) and f = 3.045 MHz in mpmath at 40 dps, with m = 171 u exactly and with the ion mass 170.93578 u, for N = 1, 5, 17. | 171 u: 0.1102804189, 0.0493189026, 0.0267469303 (rounds to 0.1103 / 0.0493 / 0.0267). 170.93578 u: 0.1103011324, 0.0493281660, 0.0267519541 (rounds to 0.1103 / 0.0493 / 0.0268). The N = 17 digit needs eta_1 > 0.1102930755, so the anchor must state its mass. | derivation audit 2026-09-04 (the audit agents' scripts live in the run transcript and are not committed; the row is the implementer's target) |

Appendix D.text:
Three multi-agent research runs on 2026-09-03 produced the provenance tags used throughout.

**Run 1** (wf_55100f76-ac4, 111 agents): five web-search angles, 29 primary sources fetched, 145 falsifiable claims extracted with quotes, the top 25 put to a three-voter adversarial panel that fetched the primary PDFs (a claim died on two refuting votes). Result: 15 claims survived, 10 were refuted, mostly on single details (a wrong isotope, an inverted inequality, a dropped digit, a mislabelled mechanism, a superseded record). Those 15 are the **[verified]** facts in Sections 1, 4.1 and 8 that carry vote counts in the companion report "Paul Trap to Fault Tolerance".

**Run 2A** (wf_4eccb03e-072, 295 agents, 23.5 M subagent tokens, 6.9 h) and **Run 2B** (wf_5d918595-430, 398 agents, 32.2 M subagent tokens, 7.5 h): 59 source readings across six topics (trap and motion 8, cooling 8, readout 9, Hamiltonian and single-qubit control 9, two-qubit gates 15, system level 10), chosen by the author rather than found by search, read through ar5iv LaTeX renderings or the PDFs so that equations were transcribed rather than paraphrased. Each source yielded up to six items (equation, definition, parameter, procedure, result or check) with a verbatim quote and location. Every non-tangential item, 354 in total, went to a fidelity verifier instructed to refute on any transcription, convention, condition or numerical error; a refutation or a low-confidence pass escalated to two more verifiers and a majority decision. Outcome by topic at the time of writing:

| Topic | Items | Passed (with flags) | Refuted as stated, corrected | No verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trap, crystal, modes, micromotion, heating | 48 | 34 | 14 | 0 (13 re-run in Run 3) |
| Laser cooling and state preparation | 48 | 32 | 16 | 0 |
| Readout and SPAM | 54 | 27 | 27 | 0 |
| Spin-motion Hamiltonian and single-qubit control | 54 | 40 | 14 | 0 |
| Two-qubit entangling gates | 90 | 56 | 34 | 0 (14 re-run in Run 3) |
| System level: native gates, compilation, calibration, noise | 60 | 33 | 27 | 0 |

**How the tags map.** **[verified]** in Part II means the item passed its fidelity check (one confident pass or a majority of three) and the verifier's flags were folded into the text. **[corrected]** means a majority refuted the item as extracted and the plan states the corrected form; in roughly two thirds of these cases the error was the source's own (a printed typo, a dropped factor, an inconsistent equation), which is precisely why the plan quotes corrected forms with the correction named. **[extracted]** means the item has a verbatim quote but no agent verdict. The 27 items whose verifiers stalled in the original runs were re-run in Run 3: 19 passed with flags and 8 were refuted on a gloss or symbol definition while their equations stood, so no tag now rests on a stalled verification; the tag remains only on a handful of Run 1 statements that were extracted but never put to the vote (a waveguide-crosstalk figure, one budget line from Pino et al., optical-pumping details, a 32-ion mode-frequency pair). The user had confirmed the 27 items independently before Run 3; the agent verdicts agree with that confirmation on every equation and add corrections to seven surrounding statements. **[background]** is the author's textbook physics, added for coherence and never load-bearing without a test.

**What the checking cannot give.** The verifiers established fidelity to the sources and internal consistency, and in many cases recomputed numbers, but they did not re-derive the physics from scratch; a source that is consistently wrong would pass. The convention table of Section 13 is the author's reconciliation across sources, informed by the verifiers' flags but not itself agent-verified. Run 2A's per-topic synthesis stage produced the readout brief but not the trap or cooling briefs: those two synthesis agents exceeded the 64,000-token output cap and were lost, so Run 2A's consolidation ran on the readout brief alone (its findings are folded into Sections 8 and 12). Run 2B produced the Hamiltonian and system-level briefs; its two-qubit brief was lost the same way. Its consolidation, run on those two briefs, listed 47 cross-source inconsistencies and independently recomputed the eight that change a unitary or an error estimate; those results are folded into Sections 6, 7, 9, 12 and 13 with the tag [corrected]. Run 3 recovered the three missing briefs.

**Run 3** (wf_489f7283-103, 65 agents, 6.5 M subagent tokens, 8.2 h, 2026-09-04) recovered what the output cap and the stalled verifiers had cost. The transcripts held no partial output from the three brief agents, only the API error, but they held every input: the 27 stalled checks were re-run from their original prompts with the same escalation (all 8 refutations were unanimous three-vote decisions, each on a gloss or a symbol definition while the transcribed equations stood: the R′ relation, Brownnutt's misprinted Eq. 14 and the Eq. 24 rate, a misattributed α example, Landa's two separate pseudopotential-recovery conditions, Baldwin's clock-qubit encoding in three items and the meaning of Δ_hf), and the three lost briefs were synthesized from the recorded item-plus-verdict inputs in 5, 5 and 8 parts of at most eleven items each, with one assembly agent per topic (trap: 70 model entries, 86 parameters, 97 checks; cooling: 68, 109, 90; two-qubit: 109, 188, 166). One consolidation agent then read all six briefs and both earlier consolidations and produced 20 cross-topic inconsistencies, 17 glossary decisions, 14 components, 22 tests and 20 open issues, folded into Sections 4, 6, 8, 9, 12 and 13. The recovered briefs and the consolidation are stored beside the plan as brief_recovered_<topic>.json and consolidated_C.json. The numerical checks marked "recomputed here" in Sections 7 and 13 were run by the author in the QuTiP environment on 2026-09-03 (Run 2B's unitary checks) and 2026-09-04 (everything else), not by workflow agents.

**Refutation rate as a design input.** Across all three runs about a third of carefully extracted, quoted claims failed a fidelity check, and a substantial fraction of those failures were errors in the published sources themselves. That is the empirical case for Section 9: a simulator built by transcribing formulas would inherit those errors, so the validation suite pins every implemented formula to a checked number.

**Local numerical checks (2026-09-04, this machine, QuTiP 5.3.1, NumPy 2.5.2, SciPy 1.18.1, run under both Python 3.14 and the pinned 3.13.14 with `uv`, with identical outputs and wall times within 10%).** Six scripts, committed to the repository under `validation/scripts/` as the oracle for every number tagged **[recomputed here]**, produced those numbers (`check_recoil2.py` recomputes the Run 4R checks: quadrature identities, the single-kick expectation, the α → 0 floor, the Doppler optimum, Cirac's Fig. 8 minima, the Franck-Condon index, the 40Ca+ Lamb-Dicke parameters and the unit regressions): `bench_numerics.py` (displacement-operator constructions and their unitarity and interior accuracy, ENR construction, right-hand-side evaluation counts in the Schrödinger and interaction pictures; Sections 5.1.1 and 5.2), `bench_ms_timing.py` (wall time of a two-ion Mølmer-Sørensen pulse at joint dimensions 48 to 2048; Section 11.1), `check_atomic.py` (Breit-Rabi against numerical diagonalization, clock points of 43Ca+, 9Be+ and 25Mg+, the 171Yb+ quadratic Zeeman coefficient, Wigner-Eckart branching ratios, Γ to reduced element to I_sat; Sections 4.5 and 9.13) `check_surface_mixed.py` (Laplace residual and boundary values of the gapless-plane electrode potential, the five-wire null height, the mixed-species two-ion mode formula; Sections 4.1.6 and 4.1.7) and `check_recoil.py` (the recoil angular factors 1/5, 2/5, 2/5, 3/10 and 1/3 by quadrature over the dipole emission patterns, and the 171Yb+ recoil-per-photon numbers; Section 4.2.8). The QuTiP interface facts of Section 9.13 were introspected in the same environment. These checks establish internal consistency and agreement with published anchors that earlier runs had verified; they do not replace the source checks, which Run 4 supplies for the transcribed formulas. The third revision (2026-09-04, afternoon and evening) added nine scripts to the same directory, each described in its README and each with its output committed under `outputs/`: `check_ms_closure.py` and `check_c0_floquet.py` (the two derivation-audit corrections the author re-derived independently, Sections 4.4.1 and 4.1.1), `bench_ms_timing_v3.py` (Section 11.1 at the corrected closure), `check_sr_lifetime_quad.py` and `check_sr_lifetime_bbr.py` (Section 4.5.7), and the four topic scripts of Run 5S, `check_comb.py`, `check_composite.py`, `check_constants.py` and `check_transport.py` (Sections 4.3.7, 4.3.5 and 6.9, 8.1 and 4.2.4, 4.6), whose numbers fill Section 9.15; every **[recomputed here]** number added in this revision names its script.

**Run 4Q** (wf_197c5930-856, 46 agents, 4.0 M subagent tokens, 37 min, 2026-09-04): three sources on the electric-quadrupole coupling (James 1998 Secs. 4-5 and Appendix, the Roos 2000 thesis, Schindler et al. 2013) read by one extractor each, 18 items verified with the same escalation as Runs 2-3 (6 passed with flags, 11 refuted as extracted and corrected, 1 split), and one brief of 17 model entries, 33 parameters and 22 checks, folded into Section 4.5.7 and Section 9.14. The refutations were mostly the sources' own: a factor k dropped from a thesis equation, air wavelengths mixed with vacuum ones in one figure, a superseded lifetime, an inverted and squared crosstalk definition, a degenerate angle definition, and node positions off by a factor 2 in a standing-wave construction.

**Run 4R** (wf_7474024c-6e0, 65 agents, 7.1 M subagent tokens, 61 min, 2026-09-04): the recoil follow-up. Run 4's first attempt found Cirac 1992, Marzoli 1994 and Javanainen-Stenholm 1981 paywalled; this run re-attempted them through the publishers' harvest and DOI routes (the first two obtained, the third not) and added Itano and Wineland 1982, Eschner et al. 2003, the recoil chapters of Steck's Quantum and Atom Optics and the cooling chapter of Roos's thesis as open substitutes. Six extractors produced 36 items; 58 verdicts with the same escalation as Runs 2-3 gave 25 items verified with flags and 11 refuted as extracted, where the refutations fell on the extractors' glosses rather than on the sources' equations (a wrong pair of 40Ca+ transitions named as the recoil pair, an invented "extra factor ½", the phrase "recoil floor" for a steady state from which the recoil frequency cancels, three page locators), each resolved in the brief's contested list; one brief of 21 model entries, 24 parameters, 25 checks, a 15-step recipe, 19 conventions, 7 contested points and 12 gaps was read in full and folded into Sections 4.2.2, 4.2.8, 9.3, 13 and 15. Seven printed errors across five sources were identified by recomputation and are listed in Section 4.2.8. The checks the brief reports were recomputed locally (`check_recoil2.py`, Appendix D scripts) before their rows entered Section 9.3.

**Run 4** (wf_0495300f-081, 333 agents, 29.8 M subagent tokens, 6320 tool uses, 162 min, 2026-09-04): four topics that the first three runs had left unsourced, each with its own source set (atomic structure and light-atom coupling, 8 sources; spontaneous-emission recoil and multi-level cooling, 8; surface-electrode trap potentials, 5; mixed-species crystals and the quantized Floquet frame, 6), read by 27 extractors (24 usable), yielding 144 items and 286 verdicts with the same escalation as Runs 2-3 (73 items verified with flags, 65 refuted as extracted, 6 split), 15 chunk syntheses assembled into four briefs (173 model entries, 340 parameters and 320 checks in total) and one cross-topic consolidation (35 glossary entries, 26 inconsistencies, 18 must-implement items, 36 validation rows, 24 open issues). As in Run 3, most refutations fell on the extractors' glosses (page locators, hedges promoted to assertions, mislabelled conventions such as the polarization index) rather than on the sources' equations, but the run also established about twenty printed errors in the sources, listed where they matter in Sections 4.1.6, 4.1.7, 4.2.8 and 4.5, adjudicated two cross-brief conflicts by computation (Nizamani's q ≈ 0.7 is a height-normalized figure of merit 3.2 times the local Mathieu q; two-node Gauss-Legendre returns α = 1/3 for every quadratic emission pattern), found one identity (House's four-wire coefficient, Wesenberg's optimal-quadrupole bound and the numerically observed geometry-independent maximum depth are one number to 10⁻¹⁶), corrected seven of this plan's own citations (Sections 15), and named what it could not source (Section 12). Its results entered the text in two passes: the verdict corrections while the syntheses were still running (Sections 4.1.6, 4.1.7, 4.2.8, 4.5, 9.12, 9.13 and 13), then the briefs and consolidation. One of the plan's own errors was introduced and caught between those passes: the first fold-in labelled the uniform-noise-exempt modes of a reflection-symmetric mixed chain as odd-parity, and the consolidation's parity glossary showed they are the even-parity modes with antisymmetric displacement patterns. The consolidation's statement that "PLAN Section 13 says carrier excluded" quotes the text the critique run had already corrected before the consolidation read it; the two passages now agree.

**Critique run** (wf_7864af35-64f, 4 agents, 0.9 M tokens, 55 min, 2026-09-04): after the Run 4 sections were drafted, four independent critics read the whole rendered plan, each through one lens (trapped-ion experimentalist, light-matter and open-systems theorist, software architect, QuTiP numerics), instructed to report only what an implementer coding from the plan would get wrong or be unable to do, with section anchors. Three reported (67 findings: 12 blocking, 26 major, 29 minor); the experimentalist's report exceeded the 64,000-token output cap and was lost, and that lens was re-run with a capped finding count on the corrected plan. Every blocking and major finding was checked by the author before adoption, twelve of them by direct computation in the QuTiP environment (the Mølmer-Sørensen closure normalization by integrating the displayed Hamiltonian, a check the derivation audit later showed to have integrated the doubled effective form of the second revision's Section 4.4.1 rather than the plan's per-tone drive, the heating-coherence rate with `mesolve`, the EIT limit sign, the 24Mg fixture, the two-GPi2 Euler decomposition, the displacement-element exponent, among others), and the corrections are marked in the text as "caught by the 2026-09-04 critique". Two of them overturned statements that Run 3 had tagged **[corrected]** (the heating-coherence rate, which omitted a term, and the EIT approximate-tuning limit, which carried a sign error), which is the reason this appendix does not describe any tag as final: a **[corrected]** tag records that a source error was found and a corrected form stated, not that the corrected form has been re-derived independently, and the Section 9 tests, not the tags, are the simulator's definition of correctness. The architecture findings (a schedule-calibration import cycle, an undefined calibration bootstrap, a doubly applied readout POVM, a claimed JOINT_EXACT range the plan's own cost model contradicted, the incompatibility of ENR spaces with the mode-factorized kernel, the absence of any interface definition, and milestone estimates the critic judged not credible) are addressed in Sections 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11 and Appendix E.

**Experimentalist re-run** (wf_fd524814-495, 4 agents, 0.67 M tokens, 31 min, 2026-09-04): the lost lens was re-run on the corrected plan as three scouts reading it in thirds (57 candidate problems) and one critic verifying, merging and ranking them into 16 findings (4 blocking, 12 major). Its first blocking finding overturned a number this plan had tagged **[recomputed here]**: the cubic-anharmonicity phase of Section 4.1.4 was arithmetically right and physically wrong, the product g·t where the leading off-resonant effect is second order, and direct integration (`check_anharmonic.py`) confirmed the critic (0.003 to 0.016 rad against 0.89 rad), which is why that tag is now paired with the sanity bound that measured gate errors impose. The other findings added what a laboratory does and the first version of this plan did not: micromotion compensation as a calibrated experiment with the stray field and shims in the device, a measured and stored qubit frequency, calibration age and drift with an optional servo, a qubit-frequency trajectory in the mains band, background-gas collisions with heralded shots, the D-manifold repump path and measurement back-action in readout, the resolved-sideband validity of the Doppler stage, the contribution criterion for frozen spectators, the correct randomized-benchmarking error convention, a realizable two-ion fixture and the correct closure for the timing benchmark, three internally inconsistent pinned numbers (the 171Yb+ linewidth convention, a five-wire height in two width conventions, a trigonometric identity), and a compute budget for the reference suite and the calibration that closes; each is marked in the text as caught by the 2026-09-04 experimentalist critique.

**Errata check** (wf_875da9f3-823, 26 agents, 2.8 M subagent tokens, 1031 tool uses, 45 min, 2026-09-04): one agent per printed source error that this plan corrects on its own authority (25 items across 23 sources), each searching for a published erratum, corrigendum or publisher's note (Crossref update relations, INSPIRE, OpenAlex, PubMed and the journal indices), comparing arXiv versions where they exist, and re-checking the claimed error by recomputation or by the paper's own internal consistency, with one agent tabulating the outcomes. No item has a published erratum. Nineteen claims were confirmed outright, among them Leibfried 2003's Eqs. 10-11 and 67-68, Wineland 1998's Eq. 62 (whose 2aρa† both arXiv versions print correctly, so the journal's stray dagger is a typesetting artifact and the plan matches the authors' own text), Wineland 2003's Eq. 2.5, Berkeland 1998's Eq. 21 (sympy residual exactly zero), Brownnutt 2015's duplicated Eq. 14 dissipator, the three Zhu-Monroe-Duan forms in the published PRL, Leung 2018's Eq. 5 in all four arXiv versions, Blümel 2021's (S6), (S8) and (S9) by numerical evaluation (the printed S6 returns a complex infidelity), Home 2013's seven slips against the LaTeX source, House 2008's Eq. 7 sign (medium confidence, from a mirrored PDF), Mount 2015's PD6 header, Acton 2006's ħ for h (with the Rinton Press errata index as the positive control), Crain 2019's Eq. 3, Landa 2012's undefined downward step, Steck's Eq. 7.132 (still printed in revision 0.16.10 of 27 June 2026), Marzoli 1994's Eq. 4 against Cirac 1992's own half-rate Eq. 41, James 1998's node positions in Sec. 4, Chen et al.'s singular matrix (introduced in the version of record, Quantum 8, 1516 (2024), absent from the 2023 preprint), Schindler 2013's crosstalk definition and Madsen 2004's 2400 against 2694. Five were partly right and changed this plan's wording: Turchette 2000's and Lee 2005's errors are the arXiv preprints' alone, the journal versions being correct (Sections 4.1.5, 4.3.2 and 13 now say so and tag them [corrected: preprint only]); the Ozeri 2007 Table II Yb+ row prints 0.2 × 10⁻⁴ and 2 mW against 0.29 × 10⁻⁴ and 2.9 mW recomputed, the reverse of what the first revision stated (Sections 4.5.5 and 9.13); the Kirchmair and James locators were narrowed; and Brownnutt's Eq. 24 and ladder-operator sub-claims remain unresolved against the published review, which was unreadable. One item refuted the check's own source list rather than the plan (the inverted bright/dark clause belongs to Baldwin 2021, as Section 4.4.4 says, not to Noek 2013, whose text and a 6j check are correct, so Baldwin's clause still rests on the Run 3 verdict), one confirmed the plan's attribution against the check's (the 2400 against 2694 depth is Madsen's, not Chiaverini's), and the check found one bibliographic error, the Zhu-Monroe-Duan arXiv identifier in Section 15, now fixed. APS abstract pages refused every automated fetch, so no publisher erratum panel was read directly; the substitute databases surfaced real errata for other papers in the same queries, which is the evidence that the negatives are meaningful.

**Run 5S** (wf_9734a0eb-744, 360 agents, 30.8 M subagent tokens, 5736 tool uses, 180 min, 2026-09-04): the source-extraction run for the four topics the plan still left unsourced after Run 4, with the same extract-verify-synthesize-consolidate pipeline and escalation rule as Runs 2 to 4: frequency-comb (mode-locked) Raman drives (Hayes 2010, Islam 2014, Inlek 2014, Mizrahi 2013 and 2014, Campbell 2010, Lee 2016), composite pulses and dynamical decoupling with the filter-function formalism (Brown-Harrow-Chuang 2004, Low-Yoder-Chuang 2014, Merrill-Brown 2014, Cummins-Llewellyn-Jones 2003, Kabytayev 2014, Green 2013, Biercuk 2009), the named single-source items (Berkeland-Boshier 2002, Kreuter 2005, Uys 2010, Wineland 2003 Eqs. 2.13-2.18, Ejtemaee-Haljan 2017, Joshi 2020; Letchumanan 2005 was unavailable behind the publisher's access wall), and ion transport, splitting and junctions as a specification for a later milestone (Reichle 2006, Bowler 2012, Walther 2012, Kaufmann 2014, Blakestad 2011, Pino 2021, Sterk 2022). 27 of 28 sources were read (162 items), 308 verdicts gave 89 items verified with flags, 69 refuted as extracted and corrected, and 4 split; 19 chunk syntheses were assembled into four briefs (comb: 63 model entries, 158 parameters, 108 checks; composite: 63, 90, 114; constants: 44, 97, 74; transport: 65, 123, 96) and one consolidation (38 glossary entries, 24 inconsistencies, 18 must-implement components, 34 validation rows, 26 open issues). As in Runs 3 and 4, most refutations fell on the extractors' glosses (locators, hedges promoted to assertions, swapped indices, an invented electrode count), but the run also established printed errors in the sources that Sections 4.3.5, 4.3.7, 4.6, 6.9 and 8.1 list where they matter: a pulse-count-to-Rabi map wrong by (2π)², a Kapitza-Dirac Bessel argument off by 2, a composite-pulse recursion factor and an SK1 sign that make the printed sequences worse than a bare pulse, a splitting equation of motion missing a factor e and a quintic ramp with a global sign error, a heating term whose prose scaling contradicts its own equation, a recoil dissipator with a coherent sum over recoil classes, and a filter-function resummation off by 2 in its exponent. Its consolidation resolved two long-standing factor questions by appeal to this plan's own convention rows (the comb two-photon Rabi frequency Ω = g²/2Δ, with the consequence that a printed π-pulse energy is 2× too small, recorded as derived rather than verified; and the recoil angular factors 1/3, 2/5 and 1/5 being three emission patterns under one definition), and it stated what it could not source (Section 12). The briefs and the consolidation were folded into the text by topic on 2026-09-04, each new number tagged [recomputed here] only where a script under `validation/scripts/` reproduces it (`check_comb.py`, `check_composite.py`, `check_constants.py`, `check_transport.py`). The one unavailable source was reached afterwards by a single agent through the first author's openly hosted PhD thesis (Letchumanan 2004, Chapter 5, which is the published measurement), corroborated by the NIST Sr II compilation and Jiang et al. 2009 and cross-checked against the thesis's own decay-rate table; Section 4.5.7 carries the result and `check_sr_lifetime_quad.py` and `check_sr_lifetime_bbr.py` the numbers.

**Derivation audit** (wf_42fdefe6-fb4, 236 agents, 23.9 M subagent tokens, 3275 tool uses, 249 min, 2026-09-04): the check that no earlier run had made, and the reason this revision exists. Nine harvesters read Sections 4.1 to 4.5, 5, 6, 8 and 13 and listed 126 load-bearing equations with self-contained setups that state the model and conventions but not the result; the 60 highest-ranked (quotas of 4 to 8 per section) went to two derivers each, one analytic and one numerical, forbidden to read the plan or the web and told to derive from the stated conventions and first principles, the numerical one verifying its result in QuTiP, sympy or mpmath; a comparer then judged the plan's form against both derivations (agree, plan wrong, derivations wrong, convention mismatch, undecidable), settling every disagreement by computation, and every non-agree verdict went to two adversarial adjudicators instructed to overturn the comparer, with the majority of three deciding; one agent wrote the report. Eight agents died on the output-length caps of the schemas (five derivers, one adjudicator, two comparers), so two equations, the transverse Hessian of Section 4.1.3 and the emission angular factors of Section 4.2.8, lost their comparison and 58 were audited; four rows rest on a single blind derivation and one on a single adjudicator, and about fifteen derivers reported their setup insufficient, so a few rows rest on a guessed rather than a stated convention. Outcome: 37 equations confirmed as written (re-derivations, not consensus), 16 wrong, 4 convention mismatches (the Ballance thermal infidelity's calibration reference, the R_d and R_b naming, the φ_tone sign convention, the ħ in the displayed master equation) and 1 undecidable (which triangle of the displacement matrix is 'above' the diagonal). Twelve of the sixteen change a simulator result: the micromotion factor on the Lamb-Dicke parameter (Section 4.1.1; the rf-clock artifact behind (1 + q/2)⁻¹), the carrier weight in the sideband-cooling rate coefficients (4.2.2), the modulus in the Laguerre Rabi element (4.3.1), the π/2 between the force axis and the carrier axis (4.3.4), one factor 2 shared by the Mølmer-Sørensen force prefactor, its closure ratio and Roos's Ω_c (4.4.1 and 13, entered when the second revision doubled the per-tone coupling ηΩ/2 into ηΩ and then 'halved on ingest'), the symmetrized two-body kernel (4.4.3), the Steck partial-versus-total rate clause (4.5.6), √Γ_e inside the Kramers-Heisenberg sum (4.5.5), the rank-2 tensor conjugation behind q = m − m′ (4.5.7) and the 171Yb+ bright-state prefactor (8.1, a factor 3 from one missed polarization share); four change a stated number or test target: the Bermudez budget coefficients (4.4.7, up to 8×), the 43Ca+ quadratic Zeeman convention (6.3), α₁ = 11/16 for motional dephasing (6.2) and the pseudopotential amplitude failure note (13). Three of the corrections overturned statements that the 2026-09-04 critique had itself introduced or endorsed (the MS closure, the timing-benchmark fixture and the C₀ regression numbers), and every one of the twelve had carried a **[verified]** or **[corrected]** tag from the source-fidelity runs, which is the empirical content of Appendix D's warning that fidelity to a source is not correctness. The author re-derived two of them independently before adopting any (`check_ms_closure.py`, `check_c0_floquet.py`), re-ran the timing benchmark at the corrected closure (`bench_ms_timing_v3.py`), and applied the rest as the edit batches recorded beside the plan sources, each marked **[corrected: derivation audit, 2026-09-04]** in the text; Section 9.16 carries the audit's thirty discriminating tests. What the audit does not establish is stated in Section 12.

**Run 5C, the four-lens critique of the revised plan (2026-09-04, evening; `wf_0f8efaf8-8c8`).** With the audit, the sources and the errata folded, the revised plan was frozen as a snapshot and read by twenty agents: for each of four lenses (a trapped-ion experimentalist, a light-matter theorist, a software architect, a QuTiP numerics expert) four scouts read the snapshot in quarters and listed candidate problems with line numbers, and one critic per lens re-read every cited passage, discarded candidates the plan already handled, merged duplicates and reported at most sixteen findings with a proposed fix and a confidence; 3.9 M tokens, 482 tool uses, 109 minutes. Three scouts (one theorist, two experimentalist) died on the 64 k output cap of the structured schema, so those quarters reached their critics through the remaining scouts only. Outcome: 64 findings, 10 blocking, all four critics judging the physics layer sound and the seams between sections, the interfaces of Appendix E and the numerics layer not yet fit to code from. Every finding was checked before adoption. The physics ones were recomputed in `check_critique_v3.py` (the sech transform pair behind the comb-tooth convention, the angular rate in I_sat, the dark-state destabilization optimum, the Fock tails of the GHZ fixtures, the zigzag pair, the composite-pulse durations, the Monroe 1995 beam geometry, the Morigi sign map, the Floquet function under the adopted Mathieu sign, the quadratic Zeeman coefficient for four g_J values, the infrared cutoff of the filter function, the order_slope round-off window, the 355 nm second-order weights, the d_m = 8 row of the Section 5.1.1 table, and QuTiP 5.3.1 probes for the Dense `expm`, the ENR `dims` against `shape`, `ptrace` on ENR spaces, `target_tol` without `e_ops` and `steadystate` on a singular kernel), and the numerics critic's benchmark finding was checked by rebuilding the timing benchmark (`bench_ms_timing_v4.py`, Section 11.1). That critic was right that v3 had timed a Dense operator with a non-zero probe printing −1, and the rebuilt measurement showed something the critique had not predicted: the 4.6× excess of v3 over the best construction is not the matrix representation but the coefficient structure, four distinct lambdas making `QobjEvo` apply four dense matrices per evaluation where one shared coefficient function merges them into one, and the CSR construction the critic asked for is 1.8× slower than the merged dense operator at this operator's 50% fill, which changes the cost model of Section 11.2 and confirms that the mode-factorized kernel, not sparsity, is the scaling remedy. Three of the critic's measurements (the `mesolve`/`sesolve` ratio 69.5, the `PicklingError` under `map="parallel"`, the ENR displacement's ⟨n₀⟩ = 2.2412) are adopted from the critique without a committed reproduction and say so in Section 12. Two proposed fixes were replaced rather than adopted: the (2π)³ infrared-cutoff scaling by the 10⁴ measured on the actual free-induction fixture, since the low-frequency estimate does not hold at ω_min T ≈ 1, and the CSR-everywhere recommendation by CSR for `mesolve` (memory) and merged dense for `sesolve` (speed). The fold is edit batches 19a to 19e beside the plan sources, each fix marked **[corrected: critique, 2026-09-04]** where it lands, with Section 9.17 carrying 46 regression targets and Section 12 what the critique left open. Two of the critique's findings overturned statements the derivation audit had just introduced (the u̇(0) = iν(1 − q) sign, written in the RMP's rf phase origin against Section 13's, and the 'η⁴ level' dismissal of C₀), which is the same lesson as the audit's: a correction is a claim like any other and gets its own check.
